body:
## What was wrong

The ingest runner reported success for work that did not finish. When omp's session time limit passes while a tool runs, the pinned omp aborts the tool, ends the session without the model's final answer, and exits 0 (`packages/agent/src/agent-loop.ts:1762-1765` and `packages/coding-agent/src/modes/print-mode.ts:313-318,394` at `v18.12.2-sami.20261026-135627`). The runner passed that 0 on, so a cycle or a maintenance pass cut short by the limit looked done. Per-window markers mean no data was lost, but a deploy step that waits on a maintenance pass read an interrupted pass as a finished one. The same omp also exits 0 when the model keeps answering with nothing past its retries (`packages/coding-agent/src/session/turn-recovery.ts:1081-1131`).

Separately, a maintenance pass whose session the model refused failed at once, while a refused cycle got one fresh session.

## What changed

After each session the runner reads the model's last message from omp's event stream, which it already captures. The session counts as finished only when that message is a final answer, counted the way omp counts one (`session/messages.ts:530-583`, blank meaning blank by JavaScript's `String.trim()`). A maintenance pass must also end its last message with a completion line (`<pass> pass complete`), which the pass's prompt now asks for. Otherwise the runner exits non-zero with one line on standard error that says why. It names the time limit both when omp exits 0 after a tool call and when omp exits 1 because the limit passed while the model answered.

A refused cycle or maintenance pass gets exactly one fresh session, judged the same way. A pass moves no marker and writes a record only to change it, so running it again is safe; the marker is read after each of its sessions, and a pass that moved it gets no retry. A session the limit cut short is not refused, so it is not retried. The deployment doc now lists what each exit status means.

This also fixes a flaky server test that failed CI on this PR's first head with `Directory not empty`: its teardown SIGKILLed the server mid-pass, and because ctx runs each git command in a process group of its own, that git kept writing into the fixture while the test removed it. The test now stops the server with SIGTERM, as Cloud Run does, which waits for the pass.

## Verification

End to end, as root in a container with the pinned omp, a `ctx-agent` user, real `setpriv` and `jq`, every pre-session check passing, a stand-in `ctx` and a scripted model that can stream an Anthropic refusal. For the time-limit runs, a scratch copy of the script lowers the limit to 1 minute and the scripted model asks for a tool that runs for 2 minutes.

| Run | Result |
| --- | --- |
| cycle cut by the limit, current `main` | `exit status 0 after 61s` (the defect) |
| cycle cut by the limit | `exit status 1 after 64s`, `run-cycle: the session stopped at its 1-minute time limit before it finished` |
| maintenance pass cut by the limit | `exit status 1 after 64s`, the same time-limit line |
| cycle that finished | exit 0 |
| cycle whose model answers only `""`, or only U+FEFF | omp exits 0 after its retries; the runner exits 1, `run-cycle: the session exited 0 but did not finish: the model's last message is empty` |
| maintenance pass that ends with its completion line | exit 0 |
| maintenance pass whose report lacks the line | exit 1, `run-cycle: the waiting-on maintenance pass ended without its completion report: …` |
| maintenance pass refused once, current `main` | exit 1 after one session |
| maintenance pass refused once | `starting one fresh session`, then `the second session exited with status 0`; exit 0 |
| maintenance pass refused twice | two sessions, exit 1 |

The pinned omp alone, `--max-time 2s`: a session cut after a tool call exits 0 and its last assistant `message_end` has `stopReason` `toolUse`; one cut while the model answers exits 1 with `stopReason` `aborted` and `errorMessage` `Deadline exceeded`.

The server test's mechanism, shown with a git wrapper that sleeps inside each pull: after SIGKILL the server was gone at `…122.207` and its git went on at `…123.804`; after SIGTERM the git went on at `…130.749` and the server exited after it, at `…130.807`. The test then passed 128 of 128 runs, 32 at a time.

Tests: new tests run the script's own post-session code against omp-shaped events, including a marker that moves during a pass's first or fresh session; on the previous head they fail for each new case. Three new live probes drive the pinned omp past a short limit and into its empty-answer retries (with `""` and with U+FEFF) and feed its real output through the same code. Locally at this head: `cargo test` 738 passed, 0 failed, 8 ignored; `cargo test --test agent_cycle -- --include-ignored` 51 passed; `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check` and `shellcheck` clean.

Consolidate and correct the canonical Condition Builder work from #482, stacked on the guard/child-DocType correction set in #525.

author: zeta-22
body:
Fixes from two Android problem reports: "the home crashes and gets in a loop that shows me the same images", and "I go over one post and it gets back on top of it and makes me scroll all over again", plus stories that open once and then can't be opened again.

## What was wrong
- **The "keep loading" nudge (0.3.0)** fired every 1.5 s while the spinner was on screen, even while a batch was still downloading. With a loader that isn't guarded against a second trigger, that fetches the same batch twice. It also moved the spinner 200000 px *down*, briefly making the page that much longer, so a scroll at the end of the feed ran past the end and snapped back. A scroll-gesture experiment in headless Chrome showed overshoots of up to 190 px with 0.3.0 and none with this version.
- **Home / back arrow on the Following feed** reloaded the whole feed and added a copy of it to the Back history.
- **Hidden reels came back while you were away from the feed.** Opening a story or a post turned off the home-only "Reels in the home feed" rule while Instagram keeps the feed underneath. Every hidden reel grew back to full size, then collapsed again on return, shifting the feed.
- **Hidden reels still loaded their videos** inside their 1-pixel placeholder.
- **The Following page has no stories row.** Its back arrow ("← Seguiti") leads to the main page that has it, but the filter was intercepting that arrow.
- **App:** when Android stopped the WebView's page process (low memory or a crash), the screen stayed frozen until the app was force-closed.

## Changes
- Nudge at most once per batch, only after the batch has arrived and left the spinner on screen. A fallback nudge fires every 10 s if nothing arrives at all. The spinner now moves *up*, so the page never gets longer.
- Home on the Following feed scrolls to the top instead of reloading. Its back arrow is left to Instagram and opens the main page with the stories (`HOME_FEED.backLabels` in `rules.js`).
- When you leave the feed, posts it turned into placeholders are marked so they stay collapsed. The single post of a `/reel/<id>/` page is never touched.
- Nothing inside a placeholder is laid out (`> * { display: none }`).
- App: a fresh WebView opens if the page process dies. If it dies again within a minute, the app shows "Instagram stopped working" with Retry instead of restarting in a loop.
- Problem report: a timeline of the last 80 events (scroll and page-height jumps, posts arriving or leaving, feed list padding, page changes, nudges, Home taps, Blocked screens, switch changes). Numbers and kinds of page only (`src/filter/log.js`).
- Docs: README, CHECKLIST, and the PLAN log (rounds 2 and 3).

## Checks
- `npm test`: 38 pass. 6 new checks, each failing before its fix:
  - a slow, unguarded loader shows no post twice
  - Home on the Following feed doesn't reload
  - the back arrow opens the main page
  - a story leaves hidden reels at 1 px and the feed where it was
  - a hidden reel's video takes no space
  - the report timeline has no names
- `npm run smoke` on the real logged-out instagram.com passes.
- `npx expo-doctor`: 20/20. `npx expo export --platform android` compiles.
- Not verified: logged-in Instagram on the phone. That's the checklist.

- **Android:** needs an update published with `eas update`; merging alone doesn't reach the app.

author: dillionlim
body:
Fixes #695. Fixes #703.

`EditCommandParser` asked three times whether a value held anything, and answered differently each
time. The clearable fields asked `StringUtil.normalizeFieldValue`, which reads every Unicode space
as blank. The ID field test and the two selector sites asked `String.isBlank` and `String.trim`,
which count only the spaces `Character.isWhitespace` recognises — not U+00A0 or U+2007.

All three now ask one named helper, so they cannot drift apart again.

## What changes, measured

Driving the parser directly, with the space shown between the quotes:

| Input | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `edit "<U+00A0>" -p 91234567` | `Index must be a positive integer.` | `Missing required field(s): INDEX or NUS_STUDENT_ID` |
| `edit "<U+00A0>" --target-id A0123456X -p …` | `Multiple targets` — refused | accepted, selects by ID |
| `edit --id "<U+00A0>" -p 91234567` | missing-target **plus** the `--target-id` hint | missing-target alone |
| `edit --id "<U+2007>" -p 91234567` | missing-target **plus** the hint | missing-target alone |
| `edit --id " "` / `"　"` / `""` | missing-target alone | unchanged |
| `edit --id A0123456X -p 91234567` | missing-target plus the hint | unchanged |
| `edit 1 --id "<U+00A0>" -p …` | accepted, clears the ID | unchanged |
| `edit 1 --target-id A0123456X …` | `Multiple targets` | unchanged |

The first row is the worst of the three: it names a kind of value the command does not contain,
since nothing in `"<U+00A0>"` resembles an index and the user typed none. The third is the one #695
was filed about — the sentence was right and only the advice after it was wrong.

## This is not reachable by a user, and that is the point

`CommandTextField.replaceText` converts every character matching `(?U)\s+` to an ASCII space before
the text reaches the parser, quoted values included, and that covers U+3000, U+00A0 and U+2007:

```
typed U+3000 -> box holds [edit 1 -p " "]   codes: ... 0022 0020 0022
typed U+00A0 -> box holds [edit 1 -p " "]
typed U+2007 -> box holds [edit 1 -p " "]
```

So nothing above can be typed or pasted today, and both issues are labelled `type.Task` rather than
`type.Bug` to say so. The reason to fix it anyway is that a file holding three answers to one
question becomes a live defect the moment a second input path appears or that normalization moves.
Settling it costs one helper.

## Why one PR for two issues

Same root cause, same method, one helper. Splitting them would mean two serial branch updates and
two CI runs for a change that is five lines of production code, and would leave the file
half-consistent in between.

## Tests

- `parse_missingTargetWithoutIdField_namesEveryTargetForm` — extended over all four blank-looking
  values; previously only `""`
- `parse_blankLookingTargetWithoutIdField_namesEveryTargetForm` — the selector case from #703
- `parse_blankLookingTargetBesideTargetId_selectsByTargetId` — the `--target-id` case from #703
- `parse_realTargetBesideTargetId_stillRefusesTwoTargets` — a guard, so making the blank selector
  acceptable does not also stop a real second target being refused

The four values are shared as `BLANK_LOOKING_VALUES`: `" "`, `U+3000`, `U+00A0`, `U+2007`. Java
calls the first two whitespace and the last two not, which is exactly what told the two notions
apart.

Confirmed non-vacuous. With `EditCommandParser` reverted to `master` and the tests kept, three fail,
one per site:

```
parse_blankLookingTargetWithoutIdField_namesEveryTargetForm FAILED
    expected: <Missing required field(s): INDEX or NUS_STUDENT_ID>
     but was: <Index must be a positive integer.>
parse_blankLookingTargetBesideTargetId_selectsByTargetId FAILED
parse_missingTargetWithoutIdField_namesEveryTargetForm FAILED
    expected: <Missing required field(s): INDEX or NUS_STUDENT_ID>
     but was: <... NUS_STUDENT_ID. --id (or -i) sets a new NUS Student ID; --target-id ...>
```

The guard passes on both, as it should.

`./gradlew check coverage` passes. `.github/run-checks.sh` exits 0. `src/main` changes by +16/−5 in
one file, inside the v1.6 allowance.

## Documentation

No change. Neither guide describes which spaces count as blank, and no documented behaviour moves —
a user typing spaces between the quotes clears a detail before and after, as `docs/UserGuide.md`
already says. No new DG manual-testing steps, since none of this is reachable from the GUI to test.

## Why

Kyle decided on Oct 31 ([my-waffles#16](https://github.com/thiccolasscage/my-waffles/issues/16)) that logging a bot's own run to the Accuracy Ledger moves from level 5 to level 1. The accuracy-ledger skill requires every scheduled run to log, and at 10 XP a run, level 5 was about 40 unlogged runs away. The issue was filed in my-waffles just as the crew moved here, so it's applied here.

## What changed

- **`config/hooks/level_gate.py`:** at every level, a bot may read any artifact store and may create one new Ledger stretch with `loggedBy: "idle-sweep"`. Every other store write is denied at every level.
- **Tighter than the issue's patch, on purpose:** the issue also allowed `update` and `str_replace` on any stretch. Here only a `set` with no `if_version` passes. That can only create a document, so a bot can't edit or overwrite anyone's past stretch. Writes to any other artifact (the dashboard, for example) are denied too.
- **`config/hooks/test-level-gate.py`:** 74 cases. Result: 74/74 passed. New cases cover replacing an existing stretch, another artifact's `stretches`, task, mark and fix writes, batch, delete, and a stretch written from a file.
- **`crew/levels.md`, `crew/ledge/persona.md`, `crew/CLAUDE_HANDOFF.md`:** logging is now a level 1 ability, and level 5 is open.

Once this merges, step 7 of the "Ledge daily run" prompt changes to "If the Ledger write fails, end with: Couldn't log this run to the Accuracy Ledger from here."

author: jmbarzee
body:
## graph-view: a force-directed graph view with composable axes, extracted from the visualizer

The whole extraction as one change, to be **squash-merged**: main receives a single commit whose tree is the product only. The feature branch `visualizer/composable-dimensions` holds the full per-unit history — 27 stacked pull requests (#158 to #220) merged into it with merge commits — and should be kept, or tagged, as the archive; nothing else from the stack enters main's history.

### What lands

- `tools/graph-view/` — `@temporal-architect/graph-view`: the engine as its own package. A host declares a taxonomy (`createTaxonomy`), builds a `Graph` of nodes carrying values on named axes, and mounts `GraphView`; the view lays out, filters, highlights and tunes the graph without knowing what any of it means. `README.md` is the host's contract; `DESIGN.md` the invariants a maintainer needs; `examples/course-catalog/` the second host, written against the public entry alone.
- `tools/visualizer/` — the first host: the adapter reads parser output into the library's `Graph`, declares the Temporal taxonomy, and bundles the library into its own artifact. Its specs (`spec/`) are aligned to the model.
- CI: typecheck of the library, the host and the catalog; the builds; the pack of both libraries.

### How it was reviewed

Five protected cold reviews of the public surface by a fresh reader, each followed by a run that closed its findings (epics #209 and #217 carry the last two plans and reviews); every unit's review fan-out with its confirmed findings fixed before commit. The verification harness that steered the work — the goldens, probes, ratchet gates and the decision log — was removed by #220 once the work was judged done; its durable decisions are in `DESIGN.md` and the host README.

body:
#1050 は閉じない・#1053 は閉じない（予約済み。公開を確かめたところで閉じる）。#1051 は閉じない・#1052 は閉じない（完成をあやとに見せている段。出したところで閉じる）。#308 は閉じない・#310 は閉じない（コミットに出てくるのは `docs/island-misses.md` の番号）。

## 何をしたか

- イギリスの4本の、あやとの 10/30 の返事を受けた直し
  - ヨーク p2 v6・エディンバラ A v4・B v8: 説明の行の自撮りを、配信でいちばん見せたい画に替えた。B は店内の画を入れ、料理を名指す行に料理を戻した
  - リーズ p3: あやとの書き直しを1字も変えずに本編集（leeds-p3-v3）
  - 浸水 p2（11/3 21:30 JST）とヨーク p2（11/2 21:30 JST）の予約の記録（投稿文・台帳 `posted.json`・`posted.md`）
- 帳面に F-058（自撮りは要るところだけ・いちばん魅力的な画を当てる）と F-059（「要らない」は続きの出来事ごと外す）、F-029・F-055 の追記、`docs/island-misses.md` #310（別のセッションと番号が重なったので #308 から付け直した）、`production.md` 3 の完成を見る表に1行
- 下見の置き場（Firebase Hosting のプレビューチャンネル）が上限 50本で作れなくなっていたのを直した
  - 落ちた理由の字（伏せた形）をログに出す
  - `tools/shorts/preview/channels.py`: 配ったら札を付け、確かめが通ったら同じ回の古い版を消し、配る前に期限切れを消し、上限に近ければ下書き → 古い版の順に消す。下書きは寿命1日
  - 書き出しの道（`remote.py` の report）と `put.py` の道の両方が同じ決まりを通る
  - `put.py list` と `delete --sha256`（いくつも消す）
- 投稿に使う mp4 は、本編集の担当が出す版を決めた場で `fetch --all` で落とす、と `tools/shorts/post/README.md` に書いた（この箱からは下見の置き場が 403）
- 取り込みと書き出しの暗号文（shorts/.work）は外してから入れる

## なぜそうしたか

あやとから「自撮りより魅力的な映像を」「同じ画が続いて飽きる・店内を」と2本続けて言われた。こちらの完成の見直しが「言った物が写っているか」だけで「惹かれるか」を問うていなかったのが根っこなので、帳面と完成を見る表に入れた。
下見は、版を直すたびに7日残るチャンネルが溜まり、50本の上限で 10/31 に2回続けて落ちた（エラーの字 `channel quota reached` で確かめた）。片方の道だけ直すともう片方がまた溜めるので、両方を同じ決まりに通した。

## 確かめたこと

author: proggeramlug
body:
## Problem

A CommonJS module's namespace (`import * as ns from "x.cjs"`) exposed top-level classes that the module never exported. For example, `@aws-sdk/core/dist-cjs/submodules/protocols` gained `SerdeContextConfig` and `UnionSerde` compared with node. The bug is old (0.5.1520 has it too).

## Cause

To keep class identity, the CJS-to-ESM wrap (`cjs_wrap/wrap.rs`) hoists top-level classes out of the wrapper. It then emitted `export { X }` for **every** hoisted class, whether or not the module exports it. The same path caused two more mismatches:
- `module.exports = Class` also exported `Class` by name. Node's namespace is only `default` + `module.exports`.
- `exports.X = wrap(X)` exported the class itself instead of the key's value.

## Fix

A hoisted class is a direct binding export only under a key the module writes, and only when every write of that key stores the class binding: `exports.X = X`, `module.exports = { X }` / `{ X: X }`, or esbuild's `X: () => X`. The binding must also never be reassigned. Every other key is read from `module.exports` through a mangled snapshot (`const __cjsexp_X = _cjs.X; export { __cjsexp_X as X }`), so the module-scope class binding isn't redeclared. `export_key_is_own_binding` and `extract_exports_from_source` now share one export-write scan (`for_each_export_write`), so detecting a key and proving its value come from the same code. Classes are still hoisted, so class identity for real exports is unchanged.

## Tests

- New `cjs_wrap::tests::namespace_exports` (3 tests). Four existing tests that asserted the extra `export { Class }` for `module.exports = Class` now assert that it is absent.
- New gap test `test_gap_cjs_namespace_exports.ts`, checked against node 26.12.1. It covers keys, `in`, the default-import view, the boxed value, and subclassing a default-imported class and a named-imported class. Main fails it (extra keys, wrong `Boxed`, crash); head matches node.
- Sabotage: restoring main's wrap.rs fails 6 tests. Ignoring refuting writes in the proof fails the proof test.
- perry bin 1333/0, perry-hir 1116/0, perry-codegen 3167/0. outputs 22/22 same as main, js-compiled 22/22.
- The aws `protocols` namespace now has the same keys as node.

## Startup (exact callgrind Ir)

hello, commander, commander --help and binary_trees are identical and converge under linkpad. fastify_inject and awfy Richards compile to different user code, because private classes are no longer exported, so linkpad can't equalize their layouts. Unpadded totals: fastify **-669,908 Ir (-0.42%)**, Richards **-38,984 Ir**. The largest drops are in class registration at startup (`registered_class_keys_array`, `js_object_layout_for_class_keys_static`, `class_declaration`, `js_register_class_id`), since fewer exported class objects are built. The +Ir rows are small:
- fastify: canonical-key probe +1.6k and shape intern, from the different class set.
- Richards: mimalloc address rows.

author: gamesbyian
body:
## Additional non-native storage P0 found during #809 review

`CreatedTorrentProvider.publish()` previously called `File.writeBytes()` on a predictable export filename. Repeating a share name truncated an earlier .torrent export. If an internal cache entry had been substituted with a same-UID symlink/hardlink, a pathname reopen could affect foreign data.

**Candidate fix:** validate a single safe `.torrent` filename; require a non-symlink app-private cache directory; use one `FileChannel.open(CREATE_NEW, WRITE, NOFOLLOW_LINKS)` pinned for all writes and `force(true)`, then request parent-directory fsync before announcing a URI. On collision, select a numbered new filename instead of opening the existing object. On ambiguous failure leave the private orphan for review, never perform path-based rollback. The read-only provider refuses symlink-backed export paths. Two focused Robolectric tests check repeated export preserving both versions, existing external symlink and hardlink canaries unchanged, and symlink share read refusal.

**Boundary:** This is app-private export cache, not shared Downloads/SAF. A malicious same-UID actor capable of moving its parent directory could still bypass pathname ownership; full descriptor-pinned parent and process-recovery proof would require further review. This does not touch native/JNI/BitTorrent payload writing and does not resolve ZIP/library #809 or native #568. Exact-head JVM/R8/API35 testing and independent security review required before merge. No external user files intentionally mutated.

## Follow-up acceptance additions
Android instrumentation now includes two real ContentResolver tests for duplicate share requests and occupied foreign-cache filenames. It independently reopens both generated content URIs, verifies bytes, and proves the pre-existing canary remains identical. The creation path also fsyncs the private parent directory when first creating the share folder and caps UTF-8 filename bytes. Latest candidate head: `a98a633c114284ca9bc1578808bbd747268d35be`; its CI has not yet reported acceptance. On-device API29/35 and real power-loss durability remain separate gates.

author: taylorvalton
body:
## Summary

- **The bug (TASK-4292):** `PATCH /api/tasks/{id}` with a `stage` on a cancelled task reopened it in one transaction (`reopenTask`), then applied the rest of the patch in a second one (`patchTask`). When `patchTask` refused the rest, the reopen had already committed. The caller got the error, but the task was back in an open stage with a `task.reopened` event.
- **The fix:** `reopenTask` takes the rest of the patch and applies it with `patchTask` inside the reopen's transaction. Any refusal rolls back the whole request: the stage, the cancellation clear, the activity line and `task.reopened`. Each half still runs the checks it ran alone. `reopenTask` seeds the repo registry on the pool before the transaction opens, as `patchTask` does on its own.
- **Unchanged:** the MCP door. `mc_update_task` never combines `reopen` with other fields, and it already reopens in one transaction.
- **Re-cut of PLX_MC#529.** That PR's two commits lacked the `Agent`, `On-Behalf-Of` and `MC-Checkout` trailers the compliance gate requires on agent commits, and a force-push is not allowed. Its two commits come back here with the trailers and #529's tree byte for byte (`67e4529`), so every check below holds. A third commit, `a6cec59`, adds only a `LESSONS.md` entry about the missing trailers.

## Review links

- Sync module, where the reopen service lives (`src/lib/sync/cancel.ts`): https://github.com/petralabx/PLX_MC/blob/claude/happy-ride-cvtm7f-reopen-one-tx-r2/docs/modules/sync/README.md
- The changed doc, the MCP README's cancel and reopen rules: https://github.com/petralabx/PLX_MC/blob/claude/happy-ride-cvtm7f-reopen-one-tx-r2/docs/modules/mcp/README.md
- Negative check: no screen changes. The task detail's lifecycle rail looks and acts the same; only a refused reopening edit now leaves the task cancelled.

## Workstream

- [x] One-PR change with no workstream. It is a follow-up of STALE S1 (TASK-4265, PLX_MC#528), tracked in the portal's `docs/workstreams/uat-stale-retest.md`.

## Rollback Plan

How to undo: revert this PR with a merge commit. A revert of merged work needs a signed MC merge approval of its exact head. No schema, data, flag or permission change.
Blast radius: one route, `PATCH /api/tasks/{id}`, and only when it moves a cancelled task out of `cancelled`.
After a revert: a refused reopening PATCH leaves the task reopened again, as before this PR.
Verify after rollback: `npx vitest run tests/task-cancellation.test.ts`. The four TASK-4292 refusal tests fail; every other test passes.

## Mission Control

- Accountable human: vince@petrasoap.com
- Task: TASK-4292 (follow-up of TASK-4265, PRJ-UAT-FIX-LOOP, bucket BKT-UFL-P5-MISSION-CONTROL-M)
- MC-Checkout: dsp_mvvnm0jzz1qhpr

## Verification

- **Tests first.** Four tests drive the real route against the in-memory database, which rolls back on a throw. Each covers one refusal of the rest: a repo off the allow-list (422), an agent on a human-only task (409), a project that closes after the route's own check (409), and shared evidence moving into a restricted project (409). All four fail on `main`: the request is refused, but the task is left reopened with a `task.reopened` event. With the fix, the row is unchanged and no event is written.
- **Mutants.** Each of these makes at least one test fail: two transactions again, no registry seed, a seed inside or after the transaction, no `ensureSeeded`, the rest without the session's attribution, and the route without `enforceClosedProject`.
- **Review at effort high:** four reviewers, then a reproducer and a tracer per finding. They found no defect in the fix. A reviewer compared `main` and this head for a reopen whose rest sets every field (each UPDATE's row, dirty fields and attribution, the events, no pool query inside the transaction), for a bare reopen, and for a reopen its own stage gate refuses. The two test-strength findings (P3) are fixed in `87921bb`. The `#528` merge note is below.
- At `87921bb`: `./scripts/preflight.sh --mode pre-commit` passes (13 older lint warnings in other files). The two changed test files pass, 64 tests. At `a6cec59` the pre-commit preflight passes again.
- The pre-push steps, run on `2e4cf31`, whose tree `a5699d3` keeps:
  - pytest: 297 pass.
  - `npm run test`: 328 files and 5,093 tests pass. The 7 `*-postgres.test.ts` files cannot start here, because this container has no Postgres; CI runs them.
  - `npm run build`: passes.
  - Playwright e2e: 473 pass, 5 skip.
  - I skipped `npx playwright install`: this container ships Chromium and forbids reinstalling it, so e2e ran on the preinstalled browser.
  - `87921bb` changes only a test file and a README.

## Interplay with PLX_MC#528

#528 edits the same route block, so whichever PR lands second gets a textual conflict there. A reviewer merged both heads in a scratch repo, and that block was the only conflict. Resolve it like this:
1. Keep #528's echo filter. On a cancelled task that kept `uat:stale`, it removes the echoed label from `rest.labels` before the reopen. Without it, the rest refuses the echo as an add, and the whole reopen now rolls back (S1-08 breaks).
2. Keep #528's pre-check, and reword its comment. The comment says the reopen commits on its own, which is no longer true: `patchTask` refuses the same add inside the reopen's transaction and rolls it back. Suggested wording: "patchTask refuses a uat:stale add inside the reopen's transaction too, which rolls the reopen back; this check answers the same 403 before that transaction opens."
3. Call `const { task } = await reopenTask(id, { stage }, ctx, { patch: rest, ... })`, as this PR does.

Dropping the pre-check is also correct in production. #528's test harness would then need a `withTransaction` that rolls back, as `tests/task-cancellation.test.ts` has. The reviewer ran all three resolutions against nine route and task test files:
- Filter and pre-check kept: 256 of 256 pass, and `tsc` is clean.
- Filter only: one failure, from the harness's missing rollback.
- Neither: S1-08 fails.

## Risk

- Risk: standard, the compliance gate's tier for these paths. One route's transaction scope. No permission, schema, money or workflow change, so no signed MC merge approval.

body:
## Resumen

Atlas De La Participación · Equipo Pumpkin · **Punto 3: diagnóstico de homologación municipal.** Solo documentación y un script de análisis: **no cambia la app**. Las opciones municipales siguen deshabilitadas, como pide la lista del equipo ("mantener deshabilitadas esas opciones mientras falten datos comparables").

El punto 3 completo (homologar municipios, distritos y secciones, con sus estadísticas y cartografía) queda para la siguiente etapa. Este diagnóstico mide con los datos que ya tenemos cuánto cambian los municipios entre 2009 y 2024, para dimensionar ese trabajo.

## Hallazgos

- **2,453 de 2,477 municipios** conservan su clave en las seis elecciones y nunca la intercambian. Reúnen el **99.64 % de la lista nominal de 2024**.
- **19 municipios nuevos** desde 2018, en Chiapas, Campeche, Morelos, Baja California, Guerrero y Sinaloa. Los municipios de los que se separaron también dejan de ser comparables, y para identificarlos hacen falta los decretos de creación.
- **Claves que cambian de municipio:**
  - en Chiapas se reordenaron claves en 2021;
  - Paracho y Parácuaro (Michoacán) intercambian sus claves en 2021 y las recuperan en 2024.

  Unir los datos solo por clave daría series equivocadas.
- **3 municipios sin datos en 2012**, en Chiapas y Oaxaca. Deben tratarse como faltantes, no como cero.
- **40 cambios de nombre**, todos de forma: abreviaturas, nombres largos o cortos y erratas de la fuente.

## Archivos

| Archivo | Contenido |
|---|---|
| `docs/punto3-diagnostico-homologacion.md` | Resumen, hallazgos, qué no cubre (distritos, secciones y cartografía) e implicaciones para la siguiente etapa |

| `docs/punto3_diagnostico_municipal.json` | Detalle municipio por municipio |
| `tests/unit/test_municipal_changes.py` | Casos sintéticos de cada tipo de cambio |

  - **SETTINGS:** DISPLAY, REFLECTIONS, APPEARANCE, LIGHTS, **INTERFACE** (each opens that tab beside the sidebar; the open one is highlighted; search finds them, e.g. "interface"), then CONTROLS.
- CLOSE MODEL sits at the foot. The list scrolls on short windows, and the gamepad focus ring walks it as before.
- The settings (quality profile, eye height, units, and the DISPLAY · REFLECTIONS · APPEARANCE · LIGHTS · INTERFACE tabs) sit beside the sidebar, in one column on narrow windows.

**A cleaner look everywhere**
- Rounded, **anti-aliased** cards, panels, docks, buttons, segmented controls, checkboxes, slider tracks, dropdowns and scrollbars. Segmented controls are now a single track with the choice as a pill.
- About 150 hard-coded panel colours now come from the theme:
  - `UiTheme.Ink(a)` for hover tints and hairlines (dark ink on the light theme);
  - `UiTheme.Shade(a)` behind labels;
  - `UiTheme.Accent(a)` for selections.

  Images, photo tints and marks drawn over the model keep their own colours.

## Implementation notes
- **Core:** `LaunchSettings`: `UiTheme`, `UiAccent`, `UiScale`, `UiTextSize`, `UiFont`, `UiNumbersFont`, `HudLayout`, `HudFade`, all cleaned in `Sanitise`; `UiThemes` and `HudLayouts`.
- **Theme** (`UiTheme`): themed colours become properties set by `UiTheme.Apply(theme, accent)`; the tool colours stay fixed. New `ACCENT_SOFT`, `ON_ACCENT`, `RADIUS`, `RADIUS_SMALL`.
- **Fonts**
  - New `UiFonts`: a `PrivateFontCollection` of `Resources\Fonts`, a list of the installed families, and `Resolve`, which maps each text role (label, body, heading, title, numbers) to a face: the SemiBold / Semibold / Medium face when it exists, else the bold style. Segoe UI / Courier New fill in for any missing face.
  - `FontAtlas` rasterises `UiFonts.Current` at the scale × the text size.
- **Rounded corners:** `FontAtlas` also draws an anti-aliased disc and ring once. `UiBatch.RoundRect` / `RoundOutline` (and `Panel` when `Radius` > 0) draw each corner as a clipped textured quad of one quarter, so curves are smooth with the existing UI shader.
- **`UiBatch`:** `Rebuild` (the atlas again; `Generation` bumps so cached text widths re-measure) and `Opacity` (used for the HUD fade).
  - The scale is Windows' DPI × the interface size.
  - The rebuild runs at the start of the next frame, so a frame never mixes old and new glyphs.
- **Pause menu:** new `GameSession.Interface`:
  - `BuildPauseSidebar` / `SideItem`: immediate-mode, filtered by the search, scrolling; `SideItem(selected:)` marks the open settings tab;
  - `DrawMenuIcon`: small line icons;
  - `BuildInterfaceTab`: the font dropdowns go through the existing overlay system;
  - `UpdateHudFade` and the HUD layout rules in `BuildHud`, `BuildInfoColumn` and `BuildStatusPanel`.
- **Home screen:** `AppShell.ApplyInterface` applies the same settings at start-up and rebuilds after a session changed them.
- **Packaging:** 11 TTF files plus 4 OFL texts (about 4.3 MB) in `Resources\Fonts`, copied by the csproj and checked by `build/publish.ps1`. `THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.txt` gains an "Interface fonts" section.

## Revisions
- **The settings tabs in the sidebar** (5874692): the SETTINGS section showed only CONTROLS, so INTERFACE was easy to miss (it was only a tab in the settings area). The section now lists the five settings tabs first.

## Testing
- `dotnet test tests/BimGo.Core.Tests`: 552 of 553 pass. The one failure is the Linux-only `SunStudyTests.Studies_WriteListReadDelete`, which already failed before this branch.
  - New `LaunchSettingsTests.Interface_DefaultsKeepTheOldLookAndBadValuesAreCleaned`: older settings files read as before; bad themes, colours, sizes, fonts and layouts are cleaned; sizes snap to 5% steps.
- BimGo.App compiles against the `Microsoft.WindowsDesktop.App.Ref` 8.0.0 reference assemblies with 0 errors.
- The bundled fonts' GDI family names were checked from their name tables (e.g. "Inter SemiBold", "Roboto Medium", "Source Sans 3 Semibold").
- **Not run** (no Windows or GPU here). The checklist is under DEVELOPING → Open build (U-A):
  - every theme across the panels, HUD, viewer and home screen;
  - sizes at 75% and 200%;
  - each font;
  - corner smoothness at 100 / 150 / 200%;
  - the sidebar, its settings entries and search;
  - the HUD layouts and fade.

## Docs
- Updated: settings and files (the INTERFACE settings, the new data location), moving around (the new menu), the controls page's pause-menu summary, DEVELOPING (conventions, how it works, open build), HISTORY, and `ai/261031a_Interface_UA` (brief and build notes).
- `docs/images/move-pause-menu.png` should be re-captured with the new menu.

body:
v3.11.0
- Fixed UpdateCurrentMemberAsync sending a whole member object. It now takes UpdateCurrentMemberRequest and can set the bot's own guild nickname, avatar, banner, bio, pronouns and accent color.
- Fixed user profile lookups with a guild ID or mutual friends and guilds requesting a broken URL.
- Fixed RedirectUrls and RequiresCodeGrant on applications always being empty.
- Fixed SocketMessage.GetJumpUrl leaving out /channels/ and linking nowhere.
- Fixed webhook messages with attachments being sent without the files.
- Fixed Webhook.DeleteMessageAsync editing the message instead of deleting it.
- Fixed ExecuteWebhookWaitAsync sending the bot token.
- Added ReferencedMessage to messages, the message a reply replies to.
- Added MentionChannels to messages.
- Added MessageEdited, MessageRemoved, MessagesRemoved, MemberChanged and VoiceStateChanged, handing over the state from before the change. Set MessageCacheSize on FluxerGatewayConfig to keep recent messages for the message events.
- Added SendLazyRequest and SubscribePresences. Fluxer only sends a member's presence updates to sessions that subscribed to that member.
- Added RequestForumUnreads and the ForumUnreadsReceived, GuildMemberListUpdated and ThreadMemberListUpdated events.
- Added UploadAttachmentAsync, uploading large files straight to storage in parts, and a SendMessageAsync overload that sends the uploaded files.
- Added GetInstanceBadgesAsync for the community badge catalog.
- Added avatar, banner, bio, pronouns, accent color, profile flags and mention preference to UpdateGuildMemberRequest, and ProfileFlags and MentionFlags to members.
- Added forum tags, default reaction, sort order, layout, tag matching, thread defaults, content warnings, flags, voice connection limit and peer-to-peer voice to UpdateChannelRequest, and DefaultTagSetting and RtcP2P to channels.
- Added AttachmentIds and EmbedIndices to MessageReferenceRequest for forwarding only some of a message's files.
- Added Cursor to message search requests and results.
- Added Html, HtmlWidth and HtmlHeight to embeds, and VerifyKey to the current application.
- Added AddRolesAsync, RemoveRolesAsync, SetTimeoutAsync with a duration and reason, RemoveTimeoutAsync and GetProfileUrl to members.
- Added GetBanAsync and BanUserAsync with a number of days of messages to delete to guilds.
- Added EnterTypingState to channels, GetJumpUrl to messages, GetUrl to webhooks, EmbedBuilder.FromEmbed and the AllowedMentionsRequest.None, All and Only presets.
- Added SetCustomStatus, CurrentStatus, CurrentCustomStatus and IsConnected to the gateway.
- Renamed opcode 13 to VoiceSignal and opcode 14 to LazyRequest, and added RequestForumUnreads.

> [!WARNING]
> - SetStatus keeps the custom status, online status and mobile flag from the last call when they aren't passed. Use SetCustomStatus(null) to clear the custom status.
> - UpdateCurrentMemberAsync with a GuildMemberJson, FluxerOpCode.CallConnect and FluxerOpCode.GuildSubscriptions are obsolete.

author: predmore
body:
A QA pass on the Thor covered the newest work (All games #336, Folders on/off Home #335, save discovery and Set up saves #332–#334, Eden saves #330) and then a general tour. It found one real bug.

**Fixed: arrow keys stuck in a text field while Gboard is open.** In Settings › Library › RomM › Edit connection, press A on Server, then press Down. Gboard's fullscreen editor took the arrow before the activity saw it, so the caret moved inside Server and the highlight stayed put. The activity-level form interception ran too late. The connection form now catches its vertical keys before the soft keyboard (`onPreInterceptKeyBeforeSoftKeyboard`) and passes them to the existing form dispatcher. It handles both press and release, as the activity's own dispatch does.

On the Thor, Down from Server reaches Client API token, Up from an edited token returns to Server, the Save token row can be reached, typed text is kept, and the bottom display works the same way.

**Local lint blocker:** `:language:lintDebug` failed with `RestrictedApi` on `PanelKeyActivity.dispatchKeyEvent`. AndroidX core's shim marks that public Activity callback as restricted. The suppression covers only that override, with a comment explaining why. CI doesn't run lint, so this only blocked local runs.

These all passed on the Thor with no crash or ANR: All games tabs, Find and Not on Home; folders off Home; save discovery (Azahar is correctly left unbound when it's ambiguous); collections and pins; resuming a running game; sleep and wake; the cursor roaming three columns past the end; data kept across an in-place update. Full report: `docs/qa-thor-2026-10-30.md`.

Not covered: save conflict/write recovery, playing an Eden game and moving its save, streaming, long performance runs. No saves were deleted, and RomM's 30 saves were identical before and after.

Tests: `./gradlew testDebugUnitTest --rerun-tasks` passed (2,026 tests), and so did `:app:assembleDebug :app:lintDebug :language:lintDebug`.

author: jeafatkamano
body:
**Dépend de #63** (lot 3.15b), lui-même empilé sur #62, #61 et #60. Cette branche est empilée dessus : à merger en dernier. Le dernier commit est propre à ce lot (« corrections de relecture » s'il y en a).

## Quoi
- **Classe `app-native`** sur `<html>`, posée par `initialiserNatif()` (`src/lib/natif.ts`) **dans l'application seulement**. Les règles sont sous `.app-native` (`src/styles/index.css`) :
  - pas de surlignage au toucher (`-webkit-tap-highlight-color: transparent`) ;
  - pas de zoom par double toucher (`touch-action: manipulation`) ;
  - `overscroll-behavior-y: none` sur le body ;
  - pas de sélection de texte sur les boutons, la barre de navigation, les en-têtes, les segments et les onglets ; le texte des messages et des annonces reste sélectionnable ;
  - retour visuel au toucher : `:active` à l'échelle 0,97 et à l'opacité 0,85, sur les boutons et les cartes cliquables (liens en bloc). En mouvement réduit, l'échelle reste à 1.
- **Transitions entre pages** :
  - `viewTransition` de React Router 7 sur la barre du bas, les cartes d'annonce, les discussions, les raccourcis de l'accueil, et sur les `navigate` de connexion et d'inscription ;
  - glissement latéral de 200 ms (`::view-transition-old/new(root)`) ;
  - `lib/transitions.ts` renvoie faux sur le site, si `prefers-reduced-motion` est actif, ou si le navigateur ne connaît pas `document.startViewTransition` : la navigation se fait alors sans transition.
- **Bouton retour d'Android** (`src/lib/natif.ts`, `src/lib/fermables.ts`) :
  1. si une feuille du bas (`FeuilleBas`) ou le menu latéral (`Layout`) est ouvert, il le ferme d'abord. Chacun s'inscrit dans une pile à l'ouverture et s'en retire à la fermeture ;
  2. sur l'accueil du rôle (`/tenant/dashboard`, `/owner/dashboard`, `/admin`), sur `/bienvenue` et sur `/login`, il ferme l'application au lieu de revenir en arrière ;
  3. ailleurs, il revient à la page précédente, ou ferme l'application s'il n'y en a pas (comportement d'avant).
- **Vibration légère** (`@capacitor/haptics`, `ImpactStyle.Light`, `lib/vibration.ts`), dans l'application seulement, après :
  - l'envoi d'un message (`ConversationPage`) ;
  - l'envoi d'une candidature (`ListingDetail`) ;
  - la validation d'un code (SMS du numéro, dans le hook partagé par `PhoneVerification` et l'écran qui suit l'inscription ; réinitialisation du mot de passe) ;
  - un paiement confirmé par « Vérifier le paiement » (`RecuPage`, statut `success`).

  Sur le site : rien. Un appareil sans vibreur ou un échec ne change rien.

## Nouvelle dépendance (socle)
- **`@capacitor/haptics` 8.0.2** (épinglée), publiée le 27/03/2026. Plage Capacitor 8, comme `@capacitor/app` 8.1.2.
- **Poids** : 69 kB décompressée dans `node_modules`. Côté web, deux fichiers chargés à la demande, 0,40 kB et 0,51 kB gzip, soit environ 0,9 kB gzip.
- Elle n'est chargée qu'à la demande (`import()` dans l'application seulement) : le site ne la télécharge pas.
- **Android** : la CI lance déjà `npx cap sync android` avant Gradle (`.github/workflows/android-apk.yml`), ce qui enregistre le greffon. Aucun fichier de `android/` n'est modifié ici. Pour un build local sans CI, lancer `npm run android:sync` après le merge.
- Si la dépendance est refusée, cette partie tombe seule : retirer `lib/vibration.ts`, ses appels et la dépendance. Le reste du lot n'en dépend pas.

## Pourquoi
Décision du 30/10 : l'app doit se comporter comme une application, pas comme un site.

## Tests
`cd frontend && npm run lint && npm run typecheck && npm test && npm run build` : tout passe.
- Lint : 0 erreur, 5 avertissements anciens.
- Tests : 368 passent, 1 ignoré. Bundle principal : 52,71 kB gzip (52,14 kB sur #63).

Tests ajoutés :
- `src/lib/sensationNative.test.tsx` (14 tests) :
  - `app-native` posée seulement si `isNativePlatform()` est vrai ;
  - retour Android : les six écrans de départ (dont `/login/`) ferment l'application, même avec une page précédente ; ailleurs, recul ou fermeture ;
  - feuille ou menu ouvert : fermé d'abord, même sur un écran de départ ;
  - `FeuilleBas` s'inscrit et se retire de la pile ; l'écouteur réel suit le chemin courant ;
  - vibration appelée dans l'application seulement, avec `ImpactStyle.Light`, sans erreur sans vibreur ;
  - transitions : site, mouvement réduit, navigateur sans View Transitions.
- `ElementsPage.test.tsx` : menu latéral de `Layout` ouvert, fermé par le bouton retour.
- Les tests existants de `natif.test.ts` passent sans modification.

## Captures
Aucune capture : au repos, les écrans ne changent pas. Les effets (toucher, glissement, vibration, bouton retour) ne se voient que sur l'appareil. À vérifier sur l'APK de la CI : glissement entre deux onglets, `:active` sur une carte, bouton retour sur l'accueil (fermeture), sur une feuille de filtres ouverte (fermeture de la feuille) et sur une annonce (retour).

## Points d'attention
- **Le site ne change pas** : la classe, les règles et les transitions dépendent de `app-native`, qui n'est posée que dans l'application. La vibration vérifie `isNativePlatform()`.
- **Bouton retour sur `/login`** : il ferme l'application, comme demandé, y compris quand on y arrive depuis la présentation. La flèche de l'écran, elle, revient toujours à la présentation.
- **Couloirs** : `src/lib/` (`natif.ts`, `fermables.ts`, `transitions.ts`, `vibration.ts`) et `src/styles/` ne sont attribués à aucun couloir sur `main` (la #59 propose L5) ; `package.json` relève du socle, d'où `[socle]` dans le titre.
- **Aucun changement d'API ni de backend.**
- **Vibration à la réinitialisation du mot de passe** : elle s'y déclenche aussi, au titre de « validation d'un code ». À retirer si tu préfères la réserver au code SMS du numéro.
- **Pile des éléments fermables** : le bouton retour retire l'élément de la pile avant de le fermer. Les deux usages actuels (feuille des filtres, menu latéral) se démontent toujours à la fermeture. Une future feuille qui resterait ouverte après `onFermer` (envoi en cours, par exemple) devra se réinscrire.
- **Tests des points d'appel** : la vibration est testée en elle-même (appli, site, sans vibreur), pas à chacun de ses quatre points d'appel.
- **Relecture `pr-reviewer`** : « OK ». La remarque mineure sur l'ordre des imports de `Layout` est corrigée.

body:
Phase 2, slice 2: the studio's side of a tab shared from the extension's toolbar (slice 1, #213/#214).

**The card** (`SharedTabCard.svelte`, in the chat)
- A share waiting in the extension shows as a card: "You shared a tab on *domain*", with a picker of the person's sessions, the open one first.
- Its note says the agent can read the page while it's on that domain but can't click or type in it, and that what it reads goes to the model provider and into the session's history, which syncs and publishes. When the chosen session holds site grants, it names them and says what's read here can reach them.
- **Share** gives the tab to that session and opens it. **Not now** leaves the tab as it was (`drop`).

**Finding shares** (`shared-tabs.svelte.js`): the studio looks when the port opens, when its tab is shown again, and when its window is focused. The last covers a studio in a window of its own that's in view all along: the toolbar's share only focuses it.

**Giving a tab**
- Site sync's new `tell` makes the extension know the session first: a session with no site grants was never sent, and `take` refuses a session it doesn't know.
- The session's agent gets an inbox note: the tab's id, title and URL, how to read it, and that it's read-only on its site.
- The note has the studio's own frame. The default one is the delegation mechanism's ("treat what follows as evidence"), which doesn't fit. `notes.js` parses the new frame back, so the chat shows the note labelled "shared tab", as it does a delegate's.

**The agent's side**
- `{tabs: true}` marks a shared tab ("shared by the person, read only, on *domain*").
- The tool's description says what a shared tab allows.
- `read-only` and `moved` refusals say what to do instead, for the agent and for a delegate. Code's host object explains them too.
- The browsing skill gets a section on shared tabs (including keeping what's read there in the session), and the primer gets a line.

**Settings:** "Tabs you shared" lists each shared tab with its session, with **Stop sharing** (`unshare`; the tab stays open).

**Checked in a real Chromium**, with the dev extension and this branch's studio on 4173:
- I shared a page as the popup does, and the card came up. Share gave the tab to the open session, and the badge read `on` with its title.
- A scripted turn got the note; then `{tabs: true}`, a read with no grant for the domain, and a refused click all returned what they should.
- Settings listed the tab, and Stop sharing cleared the share and the badge and left the tab open.
- No page errors.

Typecheck, 931 unit tests and 55 extension e2e tests pass.

author: icyleaf
body:
## Summary

Consolidates the duplicated assertion helpers in the standalone QML suites and closes three ways the QML gate could report green while something was broken.

```diff
 tests/
+├── lib/
+│   ├── qmldir                        # registers the singleton
+│   └── Assert.qml                    # check / exitCode / findText / contrast helpers
 ├── tst_theme_color_adaptation.qml    # import "lib" + Qt.exit(Assert.exitCode())
+├── tst_release_notes_markdown.qml    # ditto; its local assert() never failed the run
+├── tst_item_category_subtitle.qml    # ditto
+├── tst_lock_cleanup.qml              # ditto
+├── tst_scope_dropdown.qml            # ditto
+├── tst_scope_filtering.qml           # ditto
-└── tst_*.qml (36 suites, each with its own helper copies)
+└── tst_*.qml (27 suites, still carrying their own helpers; migratable one at a time)
```

- `tests/lib/Assert.qml` exposes `check`, `exitCode`, `findText`, `relativeLuminance`, `contrastRatio`, `compositeOver` and `checkContrast` (the last composites a translucent role wash before measuring, so the assertion sees the color the user actually sees). `tst_theme_color_adaptation.qml` drops its seven local copies and reports through the singleton.
- Five suites defined their own `assert()` that called `Qt.quit()` before throwing, so the throw was discarded by the event loop and the runner saw exit 0. They now report through `Assert` and end with `Qt.exit(Assert.exitCode())`, and the success line is only printed when no assertion failed. No assertion was failing in `tst_item_category_subtitle`, `tst_lock_cleanup`, `tst_scope_dropdown` or `tst_scope_filtering`, so those four only change how a future failure is reported. `tst_release_notes_markdown.qml` had a real one: it expected a hardcoded `#60a5fa` link color, but link colors come from `Commons.Color.accent` now, so the assertion had been failing since the accent token migration while CI stayed green. It derives the expected color from the modal now and gains the PR `href` assertion it was missing.
- `scripts/test-qml.sh` lints one file at a time and reads each exit code together with that file's diagnostics instead of grepping one combined log for `Error:`/`error:`/`fatal:`. Errors fail the build, a file that exits non-zero while printing nothing is reported as a parse failure, and pre-existing warnings are printed without failing. Per-file invocation is what makes the parse failure visible at all: legacy `qmllint` exits non-zero and prints nothing for a file it cannot parse, so a single whole-tree call buries that silence behind every other file's warnings. The script also exports `QT_ASSUME_STDERR_HAS_CONSOLE=1`, because Qt drops QML console output when stderr is a pipe (CI logs, agent tooling), which left a failing suite with an exit code and no diagnostic.
- `scripts/check-hardcoded-colors.py` gains `--summary` and always prints per-file violation counts, so a failing gate names the file to fix instead of dumping every hit.
- `docs/agents/git.md` records the stacked-PR retarget recipe (`rebase --onto origin/develop` → `push --force-with-lease` → REST `PATCH .../pulls/<n>`), including the fact that `gh pr edit --base` fails on this repo's token because it lacks `read:org`.

## Evidence

The release-notes suite before (failing assertion, still exit 0) and after:

```
qml: ASSERTION FAILED: PR link rendered cleanly
qml: Error: Assertion failed: PR link rendered cleanly      exit=0     # before
qml: FAIL: PROBE: deliberately failing check                exit=1     # after
```

The four migrated suites assert the same way and now report through the singleton, each still exiting 0 on a clean run:

```
tst_item_category_subtitle.qml   15 assertions   exit=0
tst_lock_cleanup.qml             30 assertions   exit=0
tst_scope_dropdown.qml           17 assertions   exit=0
tst_scope_filtering.qml          14 assertions   exit=0
```

An injected failure in `tst_scope_filtering.qml` now exits 1 and suppresses its "all tests passed" line:

```
qml: FAIL: PROBE: deliberately failing check      exit=1
```

The first CI run of this branch caught the lint change being too strict — the Ubuntu Qt 6.4 `qmllint` exits non-zero over pre-existing diagnostics:

```
$ gh run view --log-failed | grep -cE "Warning: |Info: "   ->  362
$ gh run view --log-failed | grep -E "Error:"              ->  (none)
```

Now the exit code is read per file. Probes against the real script:

```
components/__probe_broken.qml (syntax error)
  ->  qmllint could not parse components/__probe_broken.qml (exit 255, no diagnostic)!   exit=1
stub: "Error: ..." + exit 1
  ->  qmllint reported errors in <file> (exit 1)!                                        exit=1
stub: no output + exit 255
  ->  qmllint could not parse <file> (exit 255, no diagnostic)!                          exit=1
stub: "Warning: ..." + exit 1
  ->  qmllint passed (warnings and Info diagnostics are reported, not fatal).            exit=0
```

Gate summary on two probe files (2 + 1 violations):

```
Found 3 theme compliance violation(s):

Violations per file:
  components/__probe_a.qml: 2
  components/__probe_b.qml: 1

FAILED (Strict Mode): 3 violation(s) must be resolved.   exit=1
```

Clean tree:

```
$ python3 scripts/check-hardcoded-colors.py
PASSED: 20 QML files scanned cleanly. Zero theme violations found.   exit=0

$ ./scripts/test-qml.sh
=== QML Test Suite Passed Successfully ===   exit=0
```

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way — test tooling, gate script and agent docs only; no runtime QML or Rust behavior changes.

**Blast Radius:** CI-only.

No issue is linked: this follows up on the QML gate retro rather than a filed issue. The 27 remaining suites keep their own `check()`/`failures` helpers rather than the shared singleton, so the migration stays incremental and this PR does not force them; `grep -rn "function assert" tests/` is now empty, so no suite can swallow a failure the same way.

author: bezmoradi
body:
Closes #15.

Fixes for the findings in #15 that hold. They come from three field reports by Claude Code sessions that used knackpack 0.13.2 on other projects. #15 also lists the findings #14 already fixed and the ones left unfixed, with the reason for each.

Version 0.15.0, a MINOR bump: what the hooks print and the names of the reviewers' folders change, and both are public interface under Versioning in `.claude/CLAUDE.md`.

## What changes

### Reviewers' report files (K3, O-4, O-5)

Two of the 37 agents in the reports returned their whole report in their reply instead of saving it. Claude Code 2.1.314 tells subagents "Do NOT Write report/summary/findings/analysis .md files", and its hand-back tool asks for "your full report".

- **The review protocol** now says the caller asked for this file, so that instruction, which is about files nobody asked for, doesn't apply to it. It also says the path-and-verdict reply is what a reviewer hands back as its full report.
- **orchestrate-review** saves a report that comes back in a reply, word for word, as that reviewer's report file.
- **O-5** came from the same inline report. Claude Code flags a hand-back that names `.claude/settings.local.json`, so a reply with only a path and a verdict avoids it.

### The review protocol, in all nine agents

- **A shared machine (K1).**
  - Servers bind to `127.0.0.1`, on a port from the brief or a random free one above 20000.
  - When a port or container name the target fixes is already taken, the check is reported as not run.
  - golangci-lint runs with `--allow-parallel-runners`. Without it, golangci-lint "acquires file lock on start" (`pkg/commands/flagsets.go`), and a second run that can't get the lock exits with an error.
- **The end-of-review check (K14, O-2).**
  - It also compares branches, tags, the stash and worktrees.
  - It lists the repository's files changed since the start with `find -newer`, ignored ones included, such as a binary built in the repository.
  - Tags are safe to compare: in a test with git 2.49, `git fetch origin main`, the protocol's kind of fetch, didn't add new tags.
- **Guidance (K10).** Guidance files are also read in the working tree, since an ignored `CLAUDE.md` is in neither the snapshot nor any revision.
- **A whole code base (K5).** It's reviewed with no base and no diff.
- **Folder names (K13).** Scratch and report folders carry the agent's name: `review-<name>.XXXXXX` and `review-report-<name>.XXXXXX`.
- **What's left behind (K18).** A `Left on this machine:` line lists what the review leaves outside the repository: Docker leftovers, downloaded toolchains or modules, and processes still running.
- **Cost (K6).** A figure that wasn't measured is reported as not measured, never estimated.
- **Agents.**
  - The Go reviewer's golangci-lint command passes `--allow-parallel-runners`.
  - The slop reviewer names the reviewer that covers a defect outside its focus without implying that reviewer ran (K17).
  - The architecture reviewer's draft decision record is the developer's to save, if they want it.

### orchestrate-review (K2, K4, K7 to K12, K19, K-55, O-1, O-3, O-6 to O-8)

- **An empty current change (K4, O-1)** starts no one: Claude asks what to review.
- **The UI reviewer (K7, K8).** Its trigger names HTML and CSS inside server-side or generator templates. The start-up line says when the UI review covers only the code, with no running preview or no Playwright tools.
- **Briefs (K1, K9, K10, O-3).** They add:
  - decisions the user confirmed that reviewers can't read, such as ones in Claude's memory;
  - limits the project documents, such as tests that bill a paid service;
  - a range of 100 ports for each agent;
  - for adjudicators, the absolute path of guidance outside the snapshot.
- **Conditional blocks (K2, O-8).**
  - A block that rests only on a baseline nobody chose, such as the security reviewer's proposed ASVS level, is marked as blocking under that baseline, and adopting the baseline goes under Decision needed.
  - Such an issue is adjudicated only if it's Critical or High or the user asks.
  - Claude says how many adjudications it starts before starting them.
- **Partial refutation (O-7).** When the adjudicator refutes only a claim's consequence or severity, the smaller defect it confirms stays at the severity its evidence supports.
- **Repository state (O-6, K14, O-2).**
  - The state check runs again after the adjudicators, and covers what the protocol's check now covers.
  - A git action the user asks for during the run waits until the last adjudicator reports.
- **Reading reports.** Reports are read with the file-reading tool, in parts when long, since shell output is cut past a size limit.
- **Files it may write (K19).** Reports that came back in a reply, and files the user asks for, join the list.
- **After the report (K11, K12, K-55).**
  - Before replying, Claude checks that the record has the report and each decision.
  - It recommends a review of the fixes once they're in.
  - After the user decides, it moves each decided issue to its new group in the report, and an issue ruled out of scope goes to Won't fix.

### Track intent (K-52, K-53, K-56)

- **Long lines (K-52).** After compaction, a record line past 1,000 bytes is cut at a space, as a Status line past 400 already was, so one long Goal or requirement can't hide every section after it. The skill now says progress belongs in Built, not on the Status line.
- **The newest assumption (K-53).** The reminder cuts the first assumption that doesn't fit, newest first, instead of passing it over for older, shorter ones.
- **Missing files (K-56).** At session start and after compaction, the hook names files on the record's Files line that no longer exist, at most three.

The README describes all of the above.

## Validation

- **`check.sh`.** `dash scripts/check.sh` and `sh scripts/check.sh` pass, version 0.15.0 against 0.14.0.
  - The hook passes under dash, sh and bash, with rules output of 9,770 bytes against the 9,900 cap.
  - track-intent's body is 8,491 characters, against a limit of 8,500.
  - orchestrate-review is 18,580 characters, against 19,000.
- **Three new hook tests in `check.sh`:**
  - a 7,000-byte Goal line;
  - a 900-character assumption behind a 300-character newer one;
  - missing files, with a space and backticks in the paths.

  Run against 0.14.0's hook, each failed under all three shells, and each passes with this one.
- **Hook runs against a test record.** They reproduced K-52 and K-53 on 0.14.0's hook and showed both fixed.
- **Linters.** gitleaks passed. ShellCheck, actionlint, zizmor, codespell, markdownlint-cli2 and lychee aren't installed where this was made, so this pull request's Linux job is their first run on it.

author: philiperiksson
body:
Closes #4571

Part of epic #4560 (whole-app UX consistency). Six small fixes on the account and agent surfaces, from the 2026-10-30 audit.

## What changed

1. **Accounts overview, one account — the tile is gone.** The dashed "Create another account" tile is removed by the owner decision of 2026-10-30; the header's **New account** button stays the one entry point and opens the same dialog. The single account card now takes the full row. The card's hand-rolled chips became `StatusBadge`s on #4563's vocabulary: "Test network" (neutral) and "Default account" (brand), matching `/accounts/<id>`'s meta line. #4021's lowercase "default" is retired with the chip that carried it.
2. **The New account dialog is two sentences, not three paragraphs.** Both #4024 facts are kept, one sentence each: the new account is secured by the passkey just used, and backups are added per account. The third fact ("Nothing is set up on {network} yet …") moved to the dialog's **created** state — the new account's first screen — because `/accounts/<id>` does not say it. CG § Accounts: New account (`docs/product/copy-guidelines.md`) is rewritten to quote the new copy.
3. **Agent Passport: a non-Active standing explains itself.** The title badge ("Issued", from the attestation) and the Standing row ("Suspended"/"Revoked", from the registry) are both true; the row's description now says what that standing means for the agent, so the two stop reading as a contradiction. Badge logic untouched. Tests for `suspended`, `revoked`, `unknown`, and `active` (no description).
4. **The Agents search hint no longer names an internal term.** "by name, description or delegate address" → "by name, description or wallet address" (the copy guidelines' term table maps *Agent delegate address* → *Agent wallet address*). Address search is supported, so the hint was not dropped. The last retired-term occurrence on the design-system demo page is fixed too.
5. **The Settings tab strip at phone width — reproduced and fixed.** At 375×812 dark the tablist painted a vertical scrollbar in its rightmost 8px. Cause: `overflow-x-auto` makes the list a scroll container on **both** axes, and the `-mb-px` underline overlap (1px) plus the 44px `::after` hit area on a 38px tab (2px) overflow it vertically — `clientHeight 37, scrollHeight 40`. Fixed with `overflow-y-hidden` on the tablist; no painted pixel changes. A 375px dark baseline and an overflow assertion guard it.

## Verification (re-run by the reviewer at `87ccd1866`)

- `CI=1 VISUAL_REGRESSION=1 playwright test --project=chromium-desktop --project=chromium-desktop-dark` → **391 passed / 0 failed / 18 skipped** (round 1 of this branch was 8 failed / 383 passed; all 8 are fixed).
- `--project=chromium-mobile` → **62/62**.
- frontend vitest → **311 files / 4851 tests passed**; ui vitest → **17 files / 137 tests passed**.
- `tsc --noEmit` clean for `packages/frontend` and `packages/ui`.
- `node scripts/docs/coupling-gate.mjs --strict` rc 0; `npm run docs:check` rc 0; `npm run lint:copy` rc 0; `npm run lint:deps` rc 0; `scripts/design-lint.mjs` OK.
- Baselines rendered from a CI-shaped prod standalone build (`CI=1` + `next build` with the CI placeholder env + `node .next/standalone/.../server.js`), never `next dev`. Checked for the dev-indicator artifact: 0 dark pixels in the bottom-left 120×120 of the three mobile/desktop captures that could carry it (the 16 dark px in the two desktop captures are the footer label, identical on `dev`).

## Baseline changes

baseline-change: accounts-mobile.png -- the "Create another account" tile is gone (#4571), so the page is shorter and the card spans the full row; the route's text floor was re-derived at 72 characters (was 104 with the tile) and set to 68
baseline-change: accounts-multi-desktop.png -- the two-account card's lowercase `default` chip became the `Default account` StatusBadge stadium (109.0px, up from 52.1px)
baseline-change: balance-freshness-accounts-overview-desktop.png -- the /accounts card's `default` chip became the `Default account` StatusBadge stadium and the tile is gone
baseline-change: currency-sek-accounts-desktop.png -- the /accounts card's `default` chip became the `Default account` StatusBadge stadium and the tile is gone
baseline-change: currency-sek-accounts-mobile.png -- the /accounts card's `default` chip became the `Default account` StatusBadge stadium and the tile is gone
baseline-change: settings-tabs-375-dark.png -- ADDED: the new 375px dark clip of the Settings tablist that guards item 5 (the scrollbar fix)

design-review verdict: approved @ 87ccd1866cba625f8602e31373af7145d7b7b32a -- baselines: accounts-mobile.png, accounts-multi-desktop.png, balance-freshness-accounts-overview-desktop.png, currency-sek-accounts-desktop.png, currency-sek-accounts-mobile.png, settings-tabs-375-dark.png

## Residual risk

- The 375px dark pixel baseline **cannot** catch the scrollbar defect itself: headless Chromium paints overlay scrollbars and they are absent from screenshots (proven by generating the baseline with the fix reverted — byte-identical). The spec's `overflow-y` assertion is the real guard; the PNG catches other changes to the row.
- `ui/Tabs`' documented 44px vertical hit area has never worked: the list is a scroll container, so the `::after`'s 4px above and 2px below are clipped and the effective target is the tab's own 38px box. Measured and documented in `design-system.md` § Tabs and the `Tabs` JSDoc; making it genuinely 44px needs the tab row to grow ~6px on three pages and is a separate design decision, out of this slice.
- Baselines were rendered on this host (Linux, node 22.23.2) rather than GitHub's `ubuntu-latest` runner with node 24; dimensions and content match the CI-shaped standalone build and the pixel gate passes locally, but CI's first run is the authoritative comparison.
- Item 2 keeps the "Signers, in Settings" clause folded into the backups sentence because #4570 owns renaming it; #4570's edit is now a clause edit, not a paragraph edit.

author: lidarbtc
body:
Moves the pinned Iris from v0.32 to [v0.33](https://github.com/dolidolih/Iris/releases/tag/v0.33) and adapts asko to the behavior that changed.

- **Query errors:** v0.33 returns `/query` failures as HTTP 200 with empty `data` and an `error` field. asko used to read that as an empty result. Now it becomes a retryable `Net.Remote_error`, matching how v0.32's HTTP 500 was handled, and the recovery cursor does not advance. The error text is not logged because upstream may include SQL in it.
- **Work directory:** v0.33 copies KakaoTalk databases and extracts SQLCipher into `/data/local/tmp/Iris.work` by default. The launcher now sets `IRIS_WORK_DIR=/data/local/tmp/asko-iris/work`, so these files stay inside the root-owned asko-iris directory.
- **Install/upgrade:** The script pins the v0.33 SHA256 `c4f61523…` (checked against the downloaded release asset). The download cache is now per version, so a cached v0.32 APK no longer fails the new checksum. If the installer replaces a different APK while Iris is running, it stops the old process (waiting up to 30 s) before starting the new one. Previously the old version kept running.

Unchanged: the webhook frame (`msg`, `room`, `sender`, `json`), the `/reply` text request, `/config` fields, and which events are broadcast by default. asko's `chat_logs` and `db2.*` queries still resolve after v0.33 moved KakaoTalk.db to the attached alias `db1`.

Validation: `dune build @all` and `dune runtest` passed (456 checks, plus Python suites with 21, 8, and 16 tests), including a new mock-Iris case for the 200-with-`error` response. They ran on the existing local `asko` opam switch (OCaml 5.4.1) because the `asko-5.5.2` switch is not installed on this PC. The upgrade branch of `iris-install-root.sh` was run on a simulated device tree: when the APK changed, the old process stopped and the start ran; when it was the same, the running process was left alone. This has not been deployed to the phone, and there is no real-device check yet of v0.33 queries, webhook delivery, or replies.

body:
People tracker W4 slice 3 (job 2026-10-30-people-tracker; manager GO, goals area editable): the Goals tab lists the people on each goal, and each name opens that person on /people. Cut from main 18c5031da9; independent of #3432 (no shared files). No schema change, no writes.

## What changes

- `lib/services/goals.ts` `getGoals`: the existing linked-task read also selects each task's `person` (id, name, deletedAt). Each goal gets `people`.
- `lib/services/people/people-on-goal.ts` (new, pure): each live person once, sorted by name; a soft-deleted person is left out. A done task still links its person.
- `components/goals/goal-people-line.tsx` (new): "With <name>, <name>". Each name links to `/people#person-<id>`, the existing hash anchor on /people. Targets are 44 px; it renders nothing when the goal has no people.
- `components/goals/goal-board.tsx`: shows the line under the goal's why, plus one optional field on its local `LifeGoal` type.

Derived from `Task.personId`, which the people tracker fills (W0 links promise tasks at write time).

## Why not the goals snapshot

`buildGoalsSnapshot` feeds the Home card and Nick's command-center state; neither shows people, so it is unchanged.

## Receipts

- Red first: the missing helper module, the missing `people` field, the missing component.
- 18 test files, 263 tests, under TZ=UTC and America/New_York. They include the existing goals service, the goal-board tests, the UI v3 ratchet and the target-floor tests.
- App `tsc` and `tsc -p tsconfig.e2e.json` exit 0.
- Commit hooks: typecheck, eslint (0 errors) and secrets passed. Gitleaks over the range: 0 findings.

## Live check and kill criterion

After merge, a goal with a task linked to a person shows "With <name>" on the Goals tab, and the name opens that person on /people. Kill criterion: if the line appears on no goal after 14 days, fold it into /people instead.

## Self-review (author, hostile)

What I looked for, and what I found:
- **Deleted people:** a soft-deleted person is not listed (test).
- **Done tasks:** they still link their person. That is intended: the person helped with the goal.
- **Duplicates:** one person on two tasks is listed once (test).
- **Snapshot:** `buildGoalsSnapshot` is untouched, because nothing shows people there. I removed my first draft that added it.
- **Consumers:** the extra field on the `getGoals` output breaks no typed fixture (e2e tsc 0).
- **Targets:** 44 px on every link.
- **Found by Codex, not me:**
  - the hash link could not reach a person past /people's first 100 rows (now `?inspect=person:<id>`, which loads the dossier by id);
  - Enter on the link was eaten by the goal row's role=button handler (the link now keeps its own key and click events).

  Both were fixed red-first in 500265ca1d.
- **CI:** the one red run was CI networking ("Could not resolve host: github.com"), re-run.

## Kill criterion and live-check date

- Live check on 2026-10-31: a goal whose task links a person shows "With <name>" on the Goals tab, and the name opens that person's dossier.
- Kill read on 2026-11-14: if the line appears on no goal by then, fold it into /people instead.

## 10x

Relationship health per goal: "2 of the 3 people on this goal have gone quiet", fed by the same picks engine.

## Second reader

Codex: 1 round, 2 findings (P2), fixed and resolved (2 of 2). CI: node re-run after a DNS failure; green expected at 500265ca1d.

author: swayzee20
body: This stacks on #8 (`cursor/iphone-duo-restack-main`), which re-lands #7 → #6 → #5 onto main. It does not merge. #9 now includes #8's deadlock fix (`0905a71`). A new TestFlight build must be cut from this branch (`cursor/iphone-duo-community-workout-b3cc`), not from build 11. ## TestFlight build 11 deadlock Build 11 was killed with `0x8BADF00D`. Main was inside React Native's event beat (`executeNowOnTheSameThread`) waiting on JS, and JS was inside an Expo `SyncFunction` that called `+[EXUtilities performSynchronouslyOnMainThread:]` and `dispatch_sync`'d back to main. The offset `0x190b30` is unsymbolicated (pods are linked into the app binary). The only sync Expo Function our screens call during render that does that hop is `ExpoStatusBar.getVerticalBarEdge`, via `useVerticalBarEdgeIOS()`. That runs on Home, Community, and the Rep in pill, including the first paint and every fold. We no longer call it. `useVerticalBarEdge()` uses the `onVerticalBarEdgeChange` event only. `react-native-reserved-regions` 0.2.0 has no sync JS getter. Its view flush-syncs the first measurement from `layoutSubviews` and watches the hinge, so `extra.reservedRegions` is `false` and that view is not mounted. `@expo/ui` is not a dependency. NativeTabs / Stack.Toolbar were not the sync call. Also on this branch: the community detail sheet is applied on the next turn after a fold, so it is not presented in the same render as the size change. ## What changed Community and Post a workout use `useLayoutMode`, `TwoPane`, `WideColumn`, and the scroll-anchor helper. Compact and wide stay a single column (600 max when wide). **Community** - Left pane: brand header, group selector (drawer stays in the pane), date nav, Community Board, and the feed at pane width. The selected card gets a 2 pt brand outline at `radii.lg`. - Right pane: `WorkoutDetailView` inline. The comment composer is pinned above `insets.bottom`. - Selection is `?post=`. With no param, the newest post of the day is auto-selected. Changing group or day clears back to auto. - Fold: an explicit selection opens `WorkoutDetailModal` after the transition settles and keeps the comment draft. An auto selection shows the feed only. Unfolding closes the sheet without the dismiss animation, sets `?post=`, and restores the pane and draft. - `useCommentDraft(sessionId)` is shared by the sheet and the pane and clears on a successful Post. **Post a workout** - Left: Cancel, eyebrow, title, 7 types in a 2-column grid, 5 effort buttons, Completed row. - Right: photo tile, caption, live `WorkoutSummaryCard`, Log workout pinned, own `KeyboardAvoidingView`. - One screen-level reducer keeps every value across a mode change, including an in-progress photo pick or upload. A focused caption is re-focused. No backend, bundle id, scheme, or EAS project changes. ## Checks On this branch, after the merge: `pnpm lint`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm build:web`, and `pnpm test:layout` (26 passing). ## Unverified - Postgres is not available here, so `pnpm test:security` was not run. - The deadlock fix is from the crash log and the native source. It has not been confirmed on a device yet. ## Device retest A new TestFlight build from this branch is required. - Cold launch shows Home, not a plain background. - Fold and unfold on Home, Community, and Post a workout with no watchdog crash. - Community: tap a post, the right pane updates and the selected card is outlined. Type a comment, fold: the same post opens as a sheet with the draft. Unfold: it is back in the pane. With no post tapped, fold shows only the feed. - Post a workout: fold and unfold with the caption filled. Every value stays, and the caption keyboard comes back. - Side strip: tabs and Rep in stay in the strip. Nothing tappable sits in the fold band. - Split View on both sides, plus dragging the divider: compact layouts work. - Regular iPhone: Community and Post a workout look and behave as before.
