author: carlossalesnaturaltec
body:
Fatia **11** do bloco PRD-05 do `openspec/cronograma-de-fatias.md`. Atende `RF-05-08` e `RF-05-17`, **sem identificador novo** — decisão do fundador de 2026-10-31, pelo precedente de `2026-09-25-temperamento-arena-nas-apps-01-e-05` e de `2026-10-30-carta-em-colunas-e-saldo-para-trocar`.

Change: `openspec/changes/archive/2026-10-31-tela-inicial-da-area-do-guerreiro/`

## O problema

A Área do Guerreiro(a) abria em `definirBloco("coleta")`, e a navegação dos quatro blocos era `cg-area-do-guerreiro__blocos` — classe **sem uma linha de CSS**, com `Botao` empilhados crus. Quem entrava caía na coleta do território e tinha de ir ao menu para chegar à missão, contra quatro lugares normativos:

| Onde | O que diz |
| --- | --- |
| PRD-05 §6.2, `RF-05-08` (essencial) | "Tela inicial abre na próxima missão, com o que fazer e o que ela desbloqueia" |
| PRD-05 §5.2.1 | "A tela inicial abre na **próxima missão**" |
| PRD-05 §10 | "a tela inicial abre na próxima missão **sem exigir navegação por menu**" |
| PRD-05 §12 (aceite) | "**sem que a criança precise procurar em menu**" |

Deriva **preexistente**, não regressão desta fatia. A spec a tolerava porque o cenário estava escopado em "*quando* o Guerreiro(a) abre **o bloco da trilha**"; agora o requisito diz que a **aplicação** abre no bloco da trilha e `NEVER SHALL abrir em outro bloco`.

## O que muda

**Nada se constrói no lado da trilha.** O `Trilha.tsx` já nascia em `tela = "guia"` e o `GuiaDaTrilha` já diz o que fazer e o que a missão desbloqueia — bastou o padrão deixar de ser a coleta.

- Os quatro caminhos viram **cartão com frase**, em **grade 2×2 no celular e 4 em linha a partir do marco de 768 px**, com o **glifo acima do rótulo**. Quatro cartões com frase em coluna dariam ~24 rem e jogariam o guia abaixo da dobra num aparelho de 360×640 — a mesma doença que a §10 quis curar.
- A **ordem** fica fixada em spec, e não é o acaso de quando cada fatia acrescentou o bloco: **minha carteira, Trilha, desafios e equipes, coleta do território**.
- O cartão do bloco aberto é anunciado por `aria-current` e se distingue por **peso de fonte**, nunca por cor. Os cartões são **navegação com item corrente**, não menu de destinos — e por isso a tela inicial não é o menu que o `RF-05-08` proíbe.
- O cartão da Trilha **nomeia a próxima missão**, sem rota nova: `GET /v1/eu/trilhas` já devolvia `proxima_missao_titulo` e `proxima_missao_posicao`.
- `.cg-caminhos`/`.cg-caminho` **sobem** da App 01 à camada comum como **`ListaDeCaminhos`**, com `disposicao` e `caminhoAtual` opcionais. `cg-caminhos__operacao` e `cg-caminhos__grupo` **ficam** na App 01: o `fieldset` "para quem opera o aparelho" é só dela.
- **Três glifos novos** no `Icone` — carteira, desafios e coleta; `trilhas` já existia —, fora do que o arquivo reserva ao escudo da marca (invariante 24), ao círculo da moeda (§9), à estrela da grandeza ponto e às silhuetas de família de badge (§8.3). Daí a **carteira sem moeda dentro**.

**A App 01 fica igual.** O componente serve as duas disposições, e a dela segue em coluna com o glifo ao lado. Do lado dela isto é refatoração: os 310 testes dela passam sem alteração alguma, e acrescentei dois que fixam a disposição.

## Dois achados de passagem

1. **Defeito de acessibilidade real**, que o plano não previa: o nome acessível do cartão da Trilha saía grudado — `TrilhaMissão 3` —, porque rótulo e subtítulo são caixas em linha e o cálculo do nome não inventa separador.
2. **O "nunca acima" do CSS da App 01 estava errado.** O comentário citava o documento 15 §§5 e 11.1, mas o §11.1 só pede o rótulo *junto* do ícone, e a fatia da carta em colunas já pôs símbolo acima do rótulo por decisão do fundador. Comentário corrigido na promoção.

## Specs

Delta em `camada-visual-comum` (3 requisitos novos: a lista de caminhos nas duas disposições, a marcação do caminho corrente sem cor, a reserva que os glifos não invadem) e em `area-do-guerreiro` (1 modificado, 3 novos). Consolidados no arquivamento: `+6, ~1`.

## Documentação

Decisão visual nova tem fonte, pelo precedente da carta em colunas:

- **documento 15 §6.5** (novo) — o cartão de caminho: as duas disposições, o lugar do glifo em cada uma e o caminho corrente
- **documento 09 §1** — a linha em "Já decididos"
- **documento 99** — o assunto na §1 e a linha de rastreabilidade de 15 §6.5
- **`openspec/cronograma-de-fatias.md`** — a fatia 11, implementada

O **PRD-05 não muda**: a fatia põe em efeito o `RF-05-08` como ele já está escrito. A situação do PRD-05 em `docs/prds/index.md` também não muda, e nenhum arquivo nasceu em `docs/`, logo a `nav` do `mkdocs.yml` fica como está.

## Verificação

| Esteira | Resultado |
| --- | --- |
| `vitest run` nos 8 workspaces | **1836 provas**, 0 falhas |
| `tsc -b && vite build` (6 apps) + `astro check` (App 06) | verdes |
| `biome check` e `biome format` | limpos, 719 arquivos |
| `npm run lint` (markdownlint + Prettier) | 0 erros |
| `mkdocs build --strict` | verde |
| `openspec validate --all` | 89 passaram, 0 falharam |

O núcleo **não muda**: nenhuma rota, nenhum modelo, nenhuma migração.

**Merge por merge commit — nunca squash** (CLAUDE.md).

author: bnasraoui
body:
## Problem

The macOS and Windows Test jobs are slow. In full run 41107119596:

- Test (macos-latest) took 69 min: about 32 min to compile and 35 min of tests (nextest suite time 2074 s).
- Test (windows-latest) took 42 min.

Almost all of the test time is trybuild compile-fail tests. They share the serial nextest group `cargo` (`max-threads = 1`), and each one builds its dependencies from nothing, because CI removes the trybuild directories before the cache step.

Trybuild test time in run 41107119596, in seconds:

| Binary | Test | macOS | Windows |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| provenance-http-client::closed_parameters | invented_parameter_values_cannot_compile | 1368 | 817 |
| provenance-core::projection_row_refusals | a_field_named_search_text_is_refused | 1076 | 137 |
| provenance-core::projection_row_refusals | a_tuple_struct_is_refused | 348 | 2 |
| provenance-sdk::compile_fail | type_projection_refusals_hold_at_compile_time | 126 | 232 |
| provenance-store::compile_fail | capability_refusals_hold_at_compile_time | 88 | 680 |
| provenance-store::compile_fail | staged_and_read_only_capabilities_hold_at_compile_time | 2 | 226 |
| provenance-macros::compile_fail | construction_refuses_functions_and_accepts_type_forms | 37 | 61 |
| provenance-core::relation_derive_refusals | relation_declaration_refusals_hold_at_compile_time | 1 | 2 |
| provenance-store::compile_fail | store_has_no_wire_contract | 2 | 2 |
| **Total** | | **3048** | **2159** |

`provenance-cli::cargo_nested_sdk` took 362 s on macOS and 189 s on Windows. It stays on every platform.

## What changed

- The macOS and Windows legs of the Test job exclude the trybuild tests with one nextest filter in the workflow step. The Linux leg runs all of them with coverage, as before, and keeps the `cargo` test group.
- The filter keeps `record_family_catalog_leaves_out_store_only_columns` on every leg. It is a plain test in the store `compile_fail` binary, not a trybuild test.
- `cargo_nested_sdk` still runs on every leg. It runs a real nested Cargo build and tests real paths.
- Two tests are removed (see below). `provenance-http-client` no longer has a trybuild dev-dependency.
- The `enum-parameters` generator test now also checks that no generated Rust client file has a `FromStr`, `TryFrom` or `From` conversion, with or without a path prefix such as `std::convert::`. The operation generation job runs it. Before this change, no CI job ran it.

## Characterization

No test file has `#[cfg]` on the target platform except `provenance-sdk::compile_fail`, which skips the missing-file case on Windows because the diagnostic contains the operating system's own message. The types that the store fixtures use (guards, staged store, repository, read-only section) have no platform-specific code.

History: no commit records a regression that one of these tests caught. Each `.stderr` change followed an intentional API change (store guard and staging refactors) or churn in unrelated output (the `FromStr` implementer list in `invented_side.stderr`).

| Binary / test | Cases | Rule bindings | Refusal it pins | Platform code | Caught a regression | Result |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| core::relation_derive_refusals / relation_declaration_refusals_hold_at_compile_time | bad_field_type, missing_target, unknown_key, undeclared_stable_id | none | `#[derive(Relations)]` refuses a bad field type, a missing target, an unknown key, and a StableId field without `#[relation]` | none | no; `.stderr` files unchanged since 33756075 | keep: no other test proves these refusals, and an undeclared reference field would drop out of the relation graph |
| core::projection_row_refusals / a_field_named_search_text_is_refused | projection_row_search_text | none | `#[derive(ProjectionRow)]` refuses a field that takes the name of the derived `search_text` column | none | no; unchanged since c90bf54d | keep: no other test proves it, and the store cache depends on the column name |
| core::projection_row_refusals / a_tuple_struct_is_refused | projection_row_tuple_struct | none | `#[derive(ProjectionRow)]` refuses a tuple struct | none | no; unchanged since c90bf54d | **removed** |
| http-client::closed_parameters / invented_parameter_values_cannot_compile | invented_direction, invented_side | none | a generated parameter enum has no invented variant and no `FromStr` | none | no; one `.stderr` change in #369 was churn in the list of unrelated `FromStr` types | **removed** |
| macros::compile_fail / construction_refuses_functions_and_accepts_type_forms | construction_on_function, construction_on_test_function, construction_on_struct (pass), construction_on_enum (pass) | none | `#[verifies(..., construction)]` is refused on a function and accepted on a type | none | no; unchanged since 0b8ec6a7 | keep: users write this marker, and no other test proves it |
| sdk::compile_fail / type_projection_refusals_hold_at_compile_time | spec_key_mismatch, implemented_by_missing_file (not on Windows) | none | `provenance_spec!` refuses an identifier that does not spell the spec key; `implemented_by!` refuses a missing file | `#[cfg(not(windows))]` on the missing-file case: diagnostic wording only | no; 5a44f3e8 limited the missing-file case to Unix wording | keep: public SDK macros |
| store::compile_fail / capability_refusals_hold_at_compile_time | forged_guard, guarded_store_outlives_guard, guarded_store_write, guarded_store_wrong_repository, read_after_stamp | rule_store_under_guard_takes_no_second_lock, rule_guarded_reads_use_guard_repository | a guard cannot be forged, a guarded store cannot outlive its guard, write, or use another repository; a read after the stamp does not compile | none in the types used | no; changes follow the guard refactors | keep: Rule evidence |
| store::compile_fail / staged_and_read_only_capabilities_hold_at_compile_time | staged_store_clone, staged_store_outlives_stage, staged_store_returned_from_stage, staged_store_cannot_open_live, layout_store_outside_crate, read_only_section_outside_crate | rule_staged_write_keeps_live_repository_identity, rule_staged_store_lives_only_inside_stage, rule_read_only_section_stays_inside_the_store | a staged store cannot be cloned, escape its stage, or open the live repository; layout stores and read-only sections stay inside the crate | none in the types used | no; changes follow the staging refactor | keep: Rule evidence |
| store::compile_fail / store_has_no_wire_contract | no_wire_contract | rule_store_has_no_wire_contract | `provenance_store::operations::catalog::definitions` does not exist | none | no | keep: Rule evidence; see the decisions below |

## What was removed and why

- `projection_row_refusals::a_tuple_struct_is_refused`: this PR intentionally removes the diagnostic coverage for a tuple struct. The derive requires named fields, and no other test keeps this diagnostic. The test has no Rule binding, and a tuple struct has no field names, so the derive cannot make columns from it. If the derive changes, the diagnostic for a tuple struct can change without a failed test.
- `closed_parameters::invented_parameter_values_cannot_compile`: it has no Rule binding, and the types prove the refusal. A Rust enum has only the variants that it declares, so `Direction::Sideways` cannot compile. The generator test pins the exact variant list of each enum, and now also checks that no generated Rust client file has a `FromStr`, `TryFrom` or `From` conversion. This is evidence about the generator output for a fixture contract. It is not a compile check of the public API of `provenance-http-client`. The operation generation job now runs that test. The removed test was the slowest test on both platforms, and its `invented_side.stderr` lists unrelated `FromStr` types, so it changed when the contract changed.

## Decisions for the owner

- `store_has_no_wire_contract` (bound to `rule_store_has_no_wire_contract`): it proves only that one function name, `operations::catalog::definitions`, is absen

author: etanhey
body:
Size: **S**. 10+/2− hand-written, plus 93 lines of tests. Stacked on #19 (`wf/10-grow-within`); merge that first, then retarget this PR to `wf/integration`.

## Problem

#19 lets a `repeat` grow within one run from its judge's result. Etan, verbatim: "In an inner loop workflow, the workflow grows within. It doesn't need to go out and get to the one who created it." and "the growth within is deterministic upon what the judge ... decides". For agents to use this, two things were still missing:

- `t3_workflow_run` didn't tell them about it.
- The service didn't check template targets before a run started. A template with a bad model would only fail later, mid-run, when the judge grew it.

## Design

- **Up-front checks.** `WorkflowRuns.run` checks every template's target before anything starts, the same way it checks spec agents. That includes refusing `environmentId`.
- **Tool description.** It now mentions `dry?`, `templates?:{name:{task}}`, the judge's `addAgents:[{key, template, input}]` and `rerun:[stage]`, and `{{input.x}}`.
- **Rows for added agents.** They need no change in the service: #19 records each added agent as a launch, so it shows up as a `queued` row with the right `phaseIndex` (its stage) and `attempt` (its round). wf/9-ui-parity draws every phase up front and adds per-agent model and timings; this PR leaves that to wf/9 and only supplies the rows.

## Tests

One service test drives the real orchestrator: `shows a judge's grown agents queued under their phase and round, within 2 KB per update`.

- The judge's round-1 result adds 17 probes and sets `rerun: ["critique"]`, so the run grows to 20 agents.
- When the last added row (`probe-17`) appears, the row's round-2 agents are exactly those 17, all `queued`, phase `draft`, attempt 2, and nothing from round 2 has started yet.
- Each probe gets `{{input.angle}}` filled in.
- The run ends `exit: "accepted"`, and every row update stays within 2 KB.

I wrote this test before the per-update split in #19. Recording all 17 added agents in one update measured 2,439 B, over the cap. That measurement is why #19 records them one per update.

## Bytes

| Budget | Test | Measured |
|---|---|---|
| MCP tool list, cap +1,200 B over upstream | `AgentContextBudget.test.ts` | 46,990 → **47,106 B** (+116 B; after review round 1 it also covers `dry:N` and `addAgents.stage?`). The stack total is +1,199 B over upstream 45,907. |
| Agent instructions | `AgentContextBudget.test.ts` | +0 B: Claude 5,135, Codex 6,865, unchanged |
| Per-update wire, ≤ 2 KB without results | the new service test | largest update **1,436 B** for a run grown to 20 agents |
| Per-update wire, ≤ 2 KB without results | `keeps every workflow row update within 2 KB…` (20 static agents) | largest update **1,465 B**, unchanged |

## Not run

The paid `mcp-tool-use` evals: this worktree has no eval API keys. `evals/mcp-tool-use/run.test.ts`, which tests the grader and its decoding of real specs, passes 411/411.

I didn't add an eval case for growth: the case rule says a new case must be shown to fail on the old text first, and I couldn't run one.

## Demo

`inner-loop-grow-demo.json` in the plan folder is a Haiku haiku inner loop:

- 2 drafters, a reader, and a critic who judges and grows the next round;
- the critic can add critics, red-teamers or rewriters, using the `critic`, `redteam` and `rewriter` templates;
- `dry: 2`, `max: 4`.

`node wf10/decode-demo.mjs` decodes it with the real decoder, then drives the real runner with scripted critic results:

```
decoded: haiku-grow-within, 2 stages, real decoder OK
round 2: … draft.syllable-fix … probe.imagery-critic … probe.cliche-redteam …
loop exit: dry; run: completed
```

- `gate.sh wf/10-grow-within`: green. Lint 3 files, 0 diagnostics; fmt clean; `apps/server` typecheck; `WorkflowRuns.test.ts` 9/9.
- `gate.sh fork/wf/integration` on the stack: green. 6 files linted; `apps/server` and `packages/contracts` typecheck; 31/31 tests.
- `AgentContextBudget`, `McpHttpServer` and `OrchestratorMcpToolkit.integration`: 30/30.

## Merged the updated #19 (with #18) in (`420c7562c5`)

- **`WorkflowRuns.run`.** #18's loop plans each spec agent's target, and this PR's loop checked template targets. Both now run in one loop: templates are checked up front but not planned, because a grown agent's key is only known once the judge picks it.
- **`WorkflowRuns.test.ts`.** I took #19's version and re-inserted this PR's grow-to-20 test as one block (`wf10/restack-test.mjs`). Its assertions now follow #18's layout. At the moment `probe-17` is recorded, the phases are `draft · round 1`, `critique · round 1`, `draft · round 2` and `critique · round 2`. The round-2 rows are the 17 probes plus the planned critic, all queued with no child thread; `rerun: ["critique"]` leaves the poet out.
- **Bytes.** The largest update is now **1,643 B**, up from 1,436 B because #18 adds model and timings to each row; still under 2,048. The tool list is still 47,106 B.

body:
**Goal:** every AST node carries a numeric `id`, and the compiler node-keyed tables key on it, so the compiler no longer needs maps keyed by objects, which Fish does not have. Behaviour is unchanged.

**What it does**
- `id` on every node type. It is not on `Span`, so spreading a span never copies one.
- Fresh ids wherever nodes are made, cloned (`renumber`) or loaded from the std cache, which is stored with ids zeroed so it is the same whichever process writes it.
- `NodeMap`/`NodeSet` and weak versions in `src/nodes.ts` replace about 150 node-keyed tables. They throw if two node objects share an id.

**Evidence**
- Byte-identical IR for all 2387 test programs before and after.
- `tests/nodes.test.ts` checks every node of the compiler own source and the corpus has its own id, and that no node-keyed table remains.
- `bun test`: 6039 pass (builder run). Detached runs had one timing flake each.

**Review:** no crash or output change in normal use. Fixed F-1756 (weak tables never dropped dead entries) and F-1757 (an id-less cached std tree crashed builds). Open: F-1758 (P3: about 2 ms slower `analyze`, and an older leak through type interning).

**Note:** the self-hosting baseline rose from 66 to 67 files, only by the new `src/nodes.ts`. No existing file regressed.

author: lidarbtc
body:
Brings upstream [dolidolih/Iris v0.33](https://github.com/dolidolih/Iris/releases/tag/v0.33) (dolidolih/Iris#131) into the fork. The fork had diverged at `ee1dc978`: upstream rewrote `IrisServer.kt` and changed `KakaoDB.kt` and `KakaoDecrypt.kt`, which conflicted with our query tracing from #1.

Upstream's version is kept for all three files, and only the tracing hooks are reapplied:

- `/query` now goes through `observedQuery`, which handles upstream's single `{query, bind}` and bulk `{queries: [...]}` requests. A query failure uses upstream's HTTP 200 `{ "data": [], "error": ... }` shape. The error contains only `Query failed; request_id=...` and never SQL, bound values, or DB exception messages. Before, the fork returned HTTP 500 with the same lookup ID.
- In upstream, `KakaoDecrypt.decrypt` no longer throws; it counts failures and returns the input unchanged. The optional `onFailure` callback is now invoked on each of those failure paths, so `decrypt_failures` in the query trace remains accurate.
- A bulk request is traced as one request. Each query emits its own `query_parsed` event and stage events. `docs/query-observability.md` is updated to match.

Validation: with JDK 17 and Android SDK 35, `./gradlew :app:testDebugUnitTest :app:assembleDebug` passed: 11 tests, including new bulk and missing-query cases, and the debug APK built. The merged build has not been run on a device. asko currently installs the upstream v0.33 release APK, not this fork build (gosuda/asko branch `lidarbtc/iris-v0.33`).

author: satoryu
body:
## Summary

Speed up the end-to-end tests. The suite now takes **24 s instead of 40 s** locally, with the same 394 tests. Only test code changes.

Most end-to-end tests started and stopped a romad cluster for every test, at about 0.4 s each time. The replication tests also slept for fixed times.

## Start romad once per class
`RomaTestUtils::RomaPerClass`: a test class that extends it starts romad in `startup` and stops it in `shutdown`, instead of once per test.

It is used where the tests only store and read data:
- `ListPluginTest`, `ListPluginTestForceForward`
- `MapPluginTest`, `MapPluginTestForceForward`
- `StorageCommandTest`, `StorageCommandTestForceForward`
- `MapCountPluginTest`
- `ProtocolTest`
- `NewFuncTest`, which already started romad once in its own `class << self` block

Because these tests now share romad, a test must not see data left by another:
- `RomaTestClient` remembers the keys it sent commands for. `delete_used_keys` deletes them, and the classes above call it in `teardown`.
- Without that cleanup, 7 tests failed because of earlier tests' data, such as `test_gets` and `test_map_keys`.
- With it, every file passed 5 runs in `--order=random`.

These still start romad for each test:
- `WriteBehindTest`: each test reads `0.wb`, and the file number grows with every rotation.
- `MHashTest`: stops romad in the middle of a test.
- `CopyDataTest`: starts a fake node for each test.
- `NewFuncChangingClusterTest`: changes the cluster.
- The replication tests: they change the replication state of both clusters.

## Replication tests (13.9 s → about 8.5 s)
- **Before each check of the replica, the tests slept 0.1 s.** They now wait until the value arrives, using `assert_eventually_equal`. The two checks that nothing changes (an `add` that fails and a `replace` of a missing key) keep the short sleep, because there is nothing to wait for.
- **The `expt` and `set_expt` checks each waited for an expiry, about 2 s each.** Both keys now expire together.
- **`test_rc_background_copy_not_overwrite` slept 1 s.** It now waits until the copy of existing data has finished.
- **`test_rc_background_copy_unactivate` slept 1 s.** It now stores a new key and waits until the replica has it. It also checks that no copy of existing data is running, then checks that the old keys were not copied.

## Test plan
- [x] `bundle exec rake test` locally, 3 runs: 394 tests, 0 failures, 0 errors, 0 pendings, about 24 s each
- [x] Each shared-romad file, 5 runs with `--order=random`: no failures
- [x] GitHub Actions (ubuntu-latest, Ruby 4.0): 394 tests, 0 failures, 0 errors, 0 pendings, 29 s (35 s before)

author: kriszyp
body:
![Kyle loads a crowded aisle of crates into a separate trailer that gets hauled away, so the forklifts behind him run fast again](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e431ff43-cecd-4b88-8a61-1baf3f581519)

## ⊙ Problem

`Unit Test` on `main` is red at 39eb2fda1, from two separate causes:

- **`resources-core-a-q` runs past its 7-minute cap.** `enumerableRelationshipPermissions.test.js` leaves about 85 tables in the shared `test` database. Every later file then runs about 45% slower.
- **`tableGetPrimitiveId.test.js` flakes (21 !== 20).** A flush that was already running when the test reset analytics still delivers the old window.

### 🤔 Is the requirement right?

Yes. The second cause is a real gap in [fix(analytics): drop pending actions when analytics is disabled (#3435)](https://github.com/HarperFast/harper/pull/3435): its "a reset leaks no samples" promise missed a running flush. A repo-wide grep finds `setAnalyticsEnabled` called only from unit tests.

## 💡 Solution

- The permissions test keeps its tables in [its own database (`DATABASE = 'enumPerms'`)](https://github.com/HarperFast/harper/pull/3834/changes?w=1#diff-f5417d3feaceabb402c05e9cec89f3624321819d82547e9cc6b7c0e56bde2762R10), which the per-file teardown drops.
- No cap change: [#3824](https://github.com/HarperFast/harper/pull/3824) moved this file to the a-n shard, and its 9-minute cap is 1.57x the slowest leaky run (343 s).
- An analytics reset now also stops a flush that is already running: [`setAnalyticsEnabled` advances `analyticsGeneration`](https://github.com/HarperFast/harper/pull/3834/changes?w=1#diff-f1e47c8ff8e65d10e6aa737a8eb28cf19219efe000ea2890bedc6b013cb955c4R80), and [`flushAnalytics` returns once it changes](https://github.com/HarperFast/harper/pull/3834/changes?w=1#diff-f1e47c8ff8e65d10e6aa737a8eb28cf19219efe000ea2890bedc6b013cb955c4R272). Review the [report delivery checks](https://github.com/HarperFast/harper/pull/3834/changes?w=1#diff-f1e47c8ff8e65d10e6aa737a8eb28cf19219efe000ea2890bedc6b013cb955c4R309) closely.

## ⚖️ Alternatives

<details><summary>Rejected options</summary>

- **Only raise the a-q cap.** This keeps the 45% slowdown, and the next file sorted after `e` uses up the extra time again.
- **Have `perFileDatabaseTeardown` drop tables a file created in kept databases.** `data`, `dev`, `test` and `test2` all alias one storage root, and the teardown only drops databases it can prove the file owns.
- **Stop `resetDatabases` re-opening stores that are already open.** This multiplies costs for apps with many tables. Fixing it requires a storage-layer change and would still leave the leaked tables in place. Recorded as a follow-up.
- **Fix only the analytics test.** The production promise would stay broken, and the regression test below shows the stale window reaches both listeners and the raw-analytics table.

</details>

## 🔧 Changes

- `resources/analytics/write.ts`: `analyticsGeneration` is advanced by `setAnalyticsEnabled` and [captured when the flush rotates its window](https://github.com/HarperFast/harper/pull/3834/changes?w=1#diff-f1e47c8ff8e65d10e6aa737a8eb28cf19219efe000ea2890bedc6b013cb955c4R211). The reset also [calls `getTransactionQueueDepths()`](https://github.com/HarperFast/harper/pull/3834/changes?w=1#diff-f1e47c8ff8e65d10e6aa737a8eb28cf19219efe000ea2890bedc6b013cb955c4R79) so queue-depth peaks reset with the window.
- `unitTests/resources/enumerableRelationshipPermissions.test.js`: every table, permission key and the operations-API schema stub now use one `DATABASE = 'enumPerms'` constant.
- [`resources/analytics/DESIGN.md`](https://github.com/HarperFast/harper/pull/3834/changes?w=1#diff-0ad5fa79cae1d62e772ccbd369b007b89c1e1afa1b2b1355624a2480e7c5f7a5) (indexed on the analytics line of [root `DESIGN.md`](https://github.com/HarperFast/harper/pull/3834/changes?w=1#diff-3dc5dd454e080eb849ee5efaf79df2585fbe0a06804d69249b4c81da05a63875R111)) and [`unitTests/DESIGN.md`](https://github.com/HarperFast/harper/pull/3834/changes?w=1#diff-24e1903dbe32321faf1cfdb6281f89ff08ef1c8cb12ba5f21e6f2ef79a553ddfR15): the reset contract, and the rule that a file creating many tables gives them their own database.

### 🤔 Keep the two comments in `setAnalyticsEnabled`

Kept. The comment on `getTransactionQueueDepths()` is the only sign that a call whose result is thrown away runs for its side effect (it resets the high-water marks); without it the line reads as dead code. The JSDoc gives the exported function's thread scope, which the signature does not show. The comment on `analyticsStart` predates this PR.

### 🤔 `rawReportPaths` matches by path prefix

Kept as is. The prefixes `InFlight`, `Listener` and `Tail` appear only in these three tests: a grep finds no other action path or table name starting with them under `unitTests/`. Filtering by key would guard against a collision that does not exist yet.

## ✅ Verification

The three analytics regression tests fail on base and pass with the fix. Before the rebase, this PR's CI ran the a-q shard in 377 s against 421 s on main at 39eb2fda1, and every unit shard was green. CI on the rebased head measures the a-n shard.

<details><summary>Evidence and runs</summary>

- **Culprit.** a-q step time was 262–355 s on every main commit through d8dbb2aa9. From 3602f3d65 on ([Apply related-table role permissions to @relationship reads (#3316)](https://github.com/HarperFast/harper/pull/3316)) it was 381–425 s against a 420 s cap. Per-suite times from the CI logs (d8dbb2aa9 → 3602f3d65): suites before the new file are unchanged (223 → 219 s on v26, 238 → 222 s on v24). Suites after it went 152 → 232 s and 176 → 244 s.
- **This PR's CI** (head 8c283fb, Node 26; time from mocha start): 421 s → 377 s against main at 39eb2fda1. The new file and everything after it went from 249 s to 202 s. Node 24 total: 370 s. Every unit shard is green. The typestrip a-q shard runs ~250 s of its 7-minute cap, so its cap is unchanged.
- **Profile.** In a local CPU profile of the new file plus three later files, 7.0 s of 14.6 s was rocksdb-js `open` under `resetDatabases → initStores` and `schemaHandler → syncSchemaMetadata`.
- **Local A/B** (new file + `qa-1951…`, `expiresAtAttribute`, `query`, run twice each): user CPU 14.4 s → 7.8 s, wall time 19.7 s → 14.4 s. A full-shard wall-clock A/B could not be trusted: the machine was at load 17/20 with a pinned benchmark. Shard timing on this PR's CI is the end-to-end check.
- **Cleanup probe** (scratch, not committed): run after the new file, it found no `enumPerms` database or directory and no `Enum*` tables in `test`/`data`/`dev`/`test2`. The base version fails the same probe.
- **Analytics regressions** in `aggregationCycle.test.js` ([reset inside the flush](https://github.com/HarperFast/harper/pull/3834/changes?w=1#diff-ec3cb0b12a5282a470c306c9ad54cf979099c98be652a31cb6056bfb81491f28R596), [reset inside a listener](https://github.com/HarperFast/harper/pull/3834/changes?w=1#diff-ec3cb0b12a5282a470c306c9ad54cf979099c98be652a31cb6056bfb81491f28R636), [reset inside the last listener](https://github.com/HarperFast/harper/pull/3834/changes?w=1#diff-ec3cb0b12a5282a470c306c9ad54cf979099c98be652a31cb6056bfb81491f28R663)): one resets from inside the flush (through a function-valued action), one from a listener with another after it, and one from the last listener. All three fail on base and pass with the fix. Each checks the stored raw reports. Each guard has its own pin: removing only the after-yield check (`write.ts:272`) fails the first case, because a later action in the abandoned window runs. Removing only the pre-sink check (`write.ts:312`) fails the third.
- **Rebased head (81fa535).** `test:unit:resources:core:a-n` passed locally (2587 passing). `aggregationCycle`, `tableGetPrimitiveId` and `enumerableRelationshipPermissions` passed. `lint:required`, `check:design-docs` and `check:unit-partition` are clean.
- **Before the rebase.** `test:unit:resources:core:r-z` passed (2194, includes `tableGetPrim

Reduzir o tempo percebido entre abrir a Formação PCH e entrar em um módulo, antecipando o carregamento do componente de detalhe e retirando a geração de PDF do caminho crítico.

body:
## What
A timetable: who teaches which class what, and when. Defaults chosen on the owner's behalf: **the same periods every weekday, double lessons supported, manual placement with conflict checks** (no generation).

- **The school day** (`/timetable/periods`, head only): periods and breaks, set once. A new school is provisioned with a standard day (seven lessons, two breaks) to edit; a school created before this gets a "Use the standard school day" button.
- **By class** (`/timetable`): choose a subject in a cell to place a lesson. Each cell answers for itself (kept, or put back with the reason). A "double lesson" tick fills this period and the next.
- **By teacher**: any teacher's week, printable.
- **A teacher** sees only their own week, from the session's staff id (a `?staff=` in the URL is ignored).

## The design decision to look at
**A lesson stores no teacher.** The teacher is whoever holds the `TeachingAssignment` for that class and subject this year, worked out when the timetable is read. A teacher copied onto the slot would go stale the day an assignment changed and nothing would say so (the repo's rule: never persist a value that changes by itself).

So a clash is not a unique index. It is **refused when a lesson is placed** (one transaction under `pg_advisory_xact_lock` per school and year) and **shown again on every read**, because the clash an assignment edit makes *afterwards* is the one no write refused. The class page marks the cell, the head's page carries a school-wide banner, and the teacher view shows both lessons in one cell.

Also refused before anything is written: another school's class (`ownsClasses`), a subject the class's *level* does not offer, a break, a weekend, a double that would cross a break or whose second period clashes (all or nothing).

## Please look at
- **A teacher is let into a fourth screen** (`/timetable`, read-only, own week). The earlier rule was "exactly three routes plus a read-only `/classes`". `verify:teacher` now lists it and asks for `/timetable/periods` and the slot route by URL.
- Placing a lesson and setting the day are **JSON routes**, not form actions: a form resets its fields when its action returns, and one refused lesson would wipe the others.
- The week grids are added to `verify:design`'s named non-lists (a matrix and an input grid, not lists).

## Before merging (production)
1. `gh workflow run migrate.yml --ref timetable -f action=deploy` (migration `20261031100000_timetable`: two new tables, additive).
2. After merge: `gh workflow run migrate.yml --ref main -f action=rls`, then re-run "Production checks". The tables are unprotected until then.

## Verification
- `verify:timetable` (pure plus the shape of the code, in CI): forced red seven ways. Two of the first runs PASSED because the check matched a substring of the sabotage (`pg_advisory_xact_lock_none`, `if (false && period.isBreak)`); both checks now pin the whole statement.
- `verify:timetable-route` (routes and pages against the database as the head, a teacher and a stranger): all pass; forced red by skipping the clash check, letting teachers edit, and letting the teacher page honour `?staff=` (8 failures). It picks its teacher from the real assignments, because the demo school rotates five teachers over every class.
- Also run against the dev server and pass: `verify:teacher` (50), `verify:parent`, `verify:it-admin` (53), `verify:onboarding` (a new school's `/timetable` opens on a grid). `check:fast` green. Dev database migrated and `db:rls` applied (66 tables).
- Looked at in a browser: empty state, adding the standard day, placing a lesson.
- **Not yet run in CI:** `verify:timetable-route`.

## Not built
Timetable generation; a lessons-per-week target per subject (the line under the grid shows counts, with nothing to compare them to); different days for different weekdays; rooms; a parent's view of a child's class; substitutions; attendance per period.

body:
## Summary

Fixes **SECOPS-21** from security-ops follow-up 9 (#242, live AT30 restore drill run 42396951). After central PostgreSQL was restored to T0 (`nodes.desired_config_generation=11`) while the node kept T1 (`applied_config_generation=14`), `desiredstate.Compiler.Compile` based the next generation on `max(desired_config_generation, max(desired_states.generation))` and ignored the node's applied generation, so the first post-restore offers (12, 13) were rejected by `fvpn-agent` with `ErrStaleGeneration` and the node never stored a new envelope.

- `CompileTx` reads `applied_config_generation` in the same `SELECT … FOR UPDATE` of the `nodes` row that already locks `desired_config_generation`; the next generation is `nextConfigGeneration(desired, applied, maxStored)` — one greater than every one of the three for the current incarnation. Desired 11 / stored 13 / applied 14 compiles to 15 on the first call; the normal row (applied below desired) is unchanged.
- `nodes.applied_config_generation` is the generation the current incarnation reported: `SubmitObservation` refuses a superseded incarnation before writing and sets `applied_config_generation = greatest(applied, reported)` when the observation is not older than `last_observed_at`, so a T1 observation after the restore lands the value `Compile` reads. A new incarnation starts above the previous applied generation until its own observation arrives; a fresh agent accepts any generation.
- The compiled document, release selection, Fair-Use recompile selection, the r13/r14 grace and fence, and lease signing (`nodes.desired_config_generation`) are untouched. No migration, no contract edit.

## Verification

`TestNextConfigGenerationIncludesApplied` (unit: 11/14/13 → 15; 11/10/13 → 14; 11/11/11 → 12; 0/0/0 → 1) and `TestCompiler_RestoreAppliedGenerationAdvancesPastNode` (integration: the restore row compiles to signed generation 15, applied stays 14, the next compile is 16; the normal row compiles to 14; comments cite `node/internal/agentstore/state.go:257`, where 12 and 13 are `ErrStaleGeneration` against accepted 14 and 15 is stored).

Gates exit 0: `go test -tags integration ./internal/desiredstate/`, `make -f mk/policies.mk policies-lint policies-test policies-test-integration policies-build`, `make -f mk/usage.mk usage-lint usage-test usage-test-integration usage-build`, `make -f mk/control.mk control-test-integration control-drift control-lint control-build`, `make go-lint`, `go vet ./...`, `git diff --check`.

`docs/policies/README.md` explains why the applied generation participates after a central restore.

## Routed

- Operator statement for the restore runbook (symptom `ErrStaleGeneration` after a PITR restore; rule; verification: after the first compile `GET /api/v1/admin/nodes/{id}` shows `config_generation.desired` above `config_generation.applied`, e.g. 15 over 14) — handover owner.
- Re-run the AT30 restore drill against this change so SECOPS-21 is measured closed — security-ops owner (follow-up 11; follow-up 10 branched before this merge).

author: satmihir
body:
## Summary

Fixes #204. On Darwin, two Rust commands started at the same moment could leak pipes into each other. A parallel agent's `exec` then reported `output_wait_failed`, and its run ended `effect_unknown` even though the command had succeeded.

**Cause:** Darwin has no `pipe2`, so Rust's std creates a pipe and only then sets close-on-exec. A process started by another thread in that window inherits the write end, and the first command's output doesn't reach EOF until that unrelated process exits. `exec` waits about a second for EOF after the command exits, then gives up. Linux is unaffected because std uses `pipe2(O_CLOEXEC)` there. Go is unaffected because `os/exec` holds `syscall.ForkLock`.

## Change

- **New `rust/src/process.rs`:** a process-wide spawn lock, the equivalent of Go's `ForkLock`.
  - `process::lock()` returns a `SpawnGuard` that creates pipes (`guard.pipe()`) and starts commands (`guard.spawn(...)`) while no other thread can.
  - `process::spawn(...)` is the shortcut for commands whose pipes std creates itself.
- **Every production child process now starts through it:**
  - `exec`, and its `ps`-based process discovery on Darwin;
  - `git_inspect` and the workspace Git probes;
  - `git_do` recipes (guarded pipe plus spawn);
  - `!` shell commands (guarded pipe plus spawn);
  - `/edit` and the login browser launch.
- **`!` shell commands also had their own pipe leak, on every platform.** They created their output pipe with a raw `libc::pipe` and never marked it close-on-exec, so any process started while one ran (for example, an agent's background `exec`) inherited it. That pipe now comes from the guarded std pipe.

The lock is held only while creating a pipe and starting the process, which takes milliseconds. It changes no output.

## Tests

- **`process::tests::concurrent_starts_do_not_inherit_each_others_output_pipes`:** threads released from a barrier together start one command that exits immediately and seven that sleep.
  - **It fails 5/5 with the lock bypassed:** EOF arrives only after about 1s, when a sleeper is killed.
  - **It passes 5/5 with the lock.**
- **`process::tests::guarded_pipes_are_close_on_exec`:** checks that both ends of a guarded pipe have `FD_CLOEXEC` set.
- **The flaky `agents::tests::finish_notices_keep_publication_order_while_results_deliver_lexically`** previously failed about 1 in 36 to 1 in 300 runs on Darwin. With this change it passed **400/400**.

## Verification

Verified at `68de2a0f`, before rebasing onto `main`. The rebase only brought in the test-timeout change from #206.

| Check | Darwin/arm64 | Linux/amd64 |
|---|---|---|
| `cargo build --release --locked` | pass | pass |
| `cargo test --locked` | 438 passed, 0 failed | 439 passed, 0 failed |
| `cargo fmt --check` | pass | pass |
| Full approved parity suite (`e420e346`) | **4,130 passed / 10 pending / 0 failed** | **4,130 passed / 10 pending / 0 failed** |

The suite checkouts were clean before and after both runs.

## CI follow-ups in this PR

macOS CI turned up two more problems while this PR was open:

- **`3640dc4d`, test only.** `pty_plan_choices_require_consent_and_scope_implementation_history` checked the picker's choice lines right after its header arrived. It now waits for the last choice first.
- **`9df32211`, a real input bug in code this PR didn't otherwise touch.** `terminal.rs` `read_turn` took a key from the decoder and then, if the turn had just ended, broke out without applying it. A keystroke typed at that moment vanished from the next prompt's draft: CI showed "draft while shell runs" lose its `n` as a `!` command finished. The key now goes into the draft. Only Ctrl-C and Ctrl-L, which would act on the finished turn, are ignored.
  - **Verified:** `cargo test` 438 passed on Darwin and 439 on Linux; the shell PTY test passed 25/25; the parity CLI/terminal area passed **375/375** on both darwin/arm64 and linux/amd64 with clean suite checkouts.

## Not covered

Some test-only helpers (in `provider/wire_tests.rs`, `git/inspect_tests.rs` and a few inline tests) still start processes directly. They could cause rare test-only flakes, not production failures. Unifying the four separate capture loops into one helper is still open, as #203's process-capture item.

Part of #203.

author: kodokbakar
body:
## Summary & Motivation

Resolves #13.

The simulation runner and IPC subsystem suffered from severe computational, disk I/O, and latency bottlenecks during simulation monitoring and agent interactions:
1. **O(N) Full-Log Re-Parsing Storm on Status Polling:** Client polling triggered sequential calls to `SimulationRunner.get_all_actions()`, which read `actions.jsonl` files from byte 0 to EOF, parsed thousands of JSON lines, and performed full list sorts on every request.
2. **Uncached Discarding of Streamed Actions:** Although the monitor thread incrementally parsed newly appended actions, it discarded actions beyond a 50-item ring buffer, forcing status endpoints to rescan entire multi-megabyte files from disk.
3. **Unconditional Disk Write Churn:** `_save_run_state()` was invoked every 2 seconds unconditionally with non-atomic `json.dump()`, risking race conditions on concurrent reads.
4. **Filesystem Polling Latency in IPC:** `SimulationIPCClient.send_command()` relied on a 500ms `time.sleep(0.5)` polling loop over disk files, introducing an artificial 250ms average latency floor per IPC interaction.

## Changes

1. **Thread-Safe In-Memory Action Cache (`backend/app/services/simulation_runner.py`):**
   - Implemented an in-memory chronological action cache (`_action_cache: Dict[str, List[AgentAction]]`) synchronized with `_action_cache_lock`.
   - Updated `_read_action_log()` to append newly read actions incrementally into the memory cache.
   - Refactored `get_all_actions()` to query the in-memory cache directly with memory-based platform and round filtering and newest-first sorting.
   - Retained transparent cold-cache fallback to disk if the cache is empty or after a server restart.

2. **Dirty-State Checking & Atomic State Persistence (`simulation_runner.py`):**
   - Added dirty-state checking to skip disk writes when simulation run state hasn't changed.
   - Implemented atomic file persistence using a `.tmp` file and `os.replace` under `_state_save_lock` to eliminate JSON read-corruption during concurrent access.

3. **Low-Latency IPC Polling (`backend/app/services/simulation_ipc.py`):**
   - Reduced default IPC polling interval from 500ms to 50ms (`poll_interval=0.05`), cutting average IPC response pickup latency by 90% while preserving timeout semantics.

## Verification & Testing

- Benchmark 1 (Action Fetching, 1,000 actions): 14.528ms (disk) -> 0.329ms (cache) (44.2x speedup, 97.7% latency reduction).
- Benchmark 2 (State Persistence): 0.297ms (disk write) -> 0.0369ms (dirty-check skip) (8.1x speedup, 87.6% I/O reduction).
- Benchmark 3 (IPC Command Delivery): 501.1ms (0.5s poll) -> 50.6ms (0.05s poll) (9.9x speedup, 89.9% latency reduction).
- Full test suite: 611 tests passed (`cd backend && uv run pytest`).
- Added 16 unit and stress tests in `backend/tests/test_simulation_performance.py` covering multi-platform action ingestion, concurrent cache reads/appends, cold-cache recovery, dirty checks, atomic state saves, and rapid concurrent IPC commands.

author: zkasuran
body:
## Blueprint

`flows/kestra-fix-forward-incident-replay.yaml` groups the failed executions of flows labeled `fix-forward: watch` into incidents by error fingerprint. Once the fix is deployed as a new flow revision, it replays every execution of an incident on that revision, each from a restart point computed for that execution: a canary first, then waves with a failure budget, after a person approves the plan. It targets Kestra 2.0 and was tested on 2.0.8.

### Why

A bug usually fails many executions, each with its own inputs or schedule date. Kestra 2.0.8 can bulk-replay them with `POST /executions/replay/by-ids?latestRevision=true`, but that starts every selected execution over from its first task, in one asynchronous operation with no canary, pacing or approval. Measured on 2.0.8: the first task of each execution ran a second time. To restart each one at the right task, you have to replay them one by one and pick the task every time.

Related catalog blueprints solve different problems:
- `kestra-failed-execution-dlq-replay-engine` restarts the failed executions of a namespace behind a `Pause`. It calls `/actions/restart` without its `revision` parameter.
- `auto-resubmit-failed-executions` starts the failed flow again as a `Subflow` 3 seconds after a FAILED or WARNING end. It passes no inputs.

Neither one waits for a fix, picks a restart task, or tracks which executions a bug broke.

### What the flow does

The `action` input picks one of 9 jobs:

| Action | Started by | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `WATCH` | `on_failure` Flow trigger (FAILED executions of flows labeled `fix-forward: watch`) | Fingerprints the failed leaf task and the first line of its first ERROR log, with UUIDs, timestamps, 20 to 24 character ids, hex values and numbers masked. Labels the execution `fix-forward.incident=ff-<12 hex>`. Opens or reopens the incident card in KV and posts it to Slack, once per transition. |
| `SCAN` | `scan` schedule, every 15 minutes | Starts WATCH for failures of the last `adopt_days` that no WATCH labeled. Records a newer flow revision as fix candidate and, with `auto_plan`, starts a PLAN. Marks RESOLVED cards VERIFIED after `verify_hours` without failure. Marks a campaign whose run ended without closing its card INTERRUPTED. Deletes cards and reports closed more than `retention_days` ago. |
| `STATUS` | `weekly_board` schedule, Mondays 08:00 | Writes the board of every incident to the namespace file `fix-forward/STATUS.md`, logs it, posts a summary to Slack. |
| `PLAN` | a person, or SCAN | Dry run of REPLAY. Groups executions into chains (an original and its replays), gives each chain a status, computes the restart point for each revision the candidates failed on, lists the tasks a replay runs again, those that act on another system and the downstream flows, splits the work into waves, and writes `fix-forward/<incident>/plan.md`. |
| `REPLAY` | a person | Builds the plan and stops on a blocker. Takes a KV lease per incident, then waits at a `Pause` whose decision defaults to `REJECT`; the approver can drop executions and change the wave size. Runs the canary (optionally stopped at a breakpoint), then the waves, with `max_failure_percent`, `replay_timeout`, `replay_window` and HALT. When the flow's concurrency behavior is CANCEL or FAIL, waves are capped to the limit and start only when the flow is idle. Writes a report per campaign. |
| `HALT`, `DISMISS`, `MERGE`, `EXPLAIN` | a person | Stop a campaign before its next wave; close an incident with a reason; move the executions of one incident into another and keep the old card as an alias; explain one execution's signature, incident, chain and restart point. |

Each replay is `POST /executions/{id}/actions/replay?revision=<target>&taskRunId=<restart point>`. The restart point is computed again from that execution's own task runs just before it is replayed. The restart rules come from replays measured on 2.0.8:

| What the target revision changes | What a 2.0.8 replay does | What the engine does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| nothing the execution ran up to its failure | fails again | `NO_FIX`, unless `fixed_outside_flow` |
| the failed task | runs the new definition | restart at the failed task |
| a task that ran before the failure | ignores the change unless the replay starts at it | restart at the earliest changed task |
| a new task before the restart point | never runs it, and the replay stays RUNNING | restart at the task before it, or at the flowable that contains it |
| a task that ran is gone | HTTP 409 for a replay from any later task | from the first task, held unless `allow_from_start` |
| the restart point is a `LoopUntil` or inside one | does not run the loop again | from the first task, held unless `allow_from_start` |

An execution is also held when its replay would run again a task that already succeeded and is listed in the `never_rerun` input or in the flow label `fix-forward.never-rerun`.

Other 2.0.8 behaviors the flow is built around, each measured while building it:
- The labels endpoint replaces every label that is not a system label, so labels are merged before each POST. A replay inherits the labels of the execution it replays.
- A `Subflow` cannot start its own flow ("Recursive call"), so SCAN starts WATCH and PLAN runs through `POST /executions/{namespace}/{id}`.
- Replays obey the flow's concurrency limit: with behavior CANCEL, a burst of replays gets cancelled.
- `/dependencies?destinationOnly=true` returns nothing, so the flow reads the full graph and walks it from the watched flow.
- `afterExecution` runs after a kill or a cancel; `finally` does not run after a kill.
- In Pebble, `'
'` in a string literal stays a backslash followed by `n`, and `slice` beyond the end of a list throws. Slack texts and the board excerpt are therefore built in jq.

### What is in the file

- 2,675 lines: 2,414 of flow and 261 of `extend`.
- 30 inputs, 4 flow `checks` (`BLOCK_EXECUTION`, so the API answers HTTP 422 for missing inputs), 1 SLA (`MAX_DURATION` P3D), 31 jq programs in `variables`, 1 `summary` output.
- 213 tasks: 15 top-level, 2 in `errors`, 5 in `afterExecution`, the rest nested. They use 19 task types; with the 2 trigger types that makes 21 plugin types.
- Flowables: 22 `If`, 9 `LoopUntil`, 1 `Parallel`, 1 `Pause`, 4 `Sleep`.
- Triggers: `on_failure` (Flow), `weekly_board` and `scan` (Schedule). All 3 ship `disabled: true`.
- Non-core plugin: `io.kestra.plugin.slack.notifications.SlackIncomingWebhook`, in 13 tasks, sending Block Kit payloads.
- Kestra API calls: `GET /executions/search` (17 tasks), `GET /executions/{id}`, `GET /logs/{id}?minLevel=ERROR`, `GET /flows/{namespace}/{id}` with and without `?revision=`, `GET /flows/{namespace}/{id}/dependencies`, `POST /executions/{id}/actions/labels`, `POST /executions/{id}/actions/replay`, `POST /executions/{namespace}/{id}`.
- State: KV keys `fix-forward.incident.<id>`, `.lease.<id>` (TTL P3D), `.halt.<id>`, `.claim.<id>.<version>` (TTL P7D) and `.scratch.<execution id>`. Namespace files `fix-forward/STATUS.md`, `fix-forward/<id>/plan.md` and `fix-forward/<id>/campaign-<execution id>.md`. Execution labels `fix-forward.incident`, `.campaign`, `.wave`, `.action` and `.for-incident`.

### Tested

Commit `1713c15`, the head of this PR, ran on Kestra 2.0.8 on 31 Oct 2026, with H2, local storage and basic auth. The extra plugin was `plugin-slack` 2.2.3, posting to a local HTTP mock that recorded every payload.
- `POST /api/v1/flows/validate` on the flow part (`extend` stripped with the awk command of `validate-blueprints.yml`) returned no constraint, deprecation, warning or info.
- A harness ran 6 scenarios through the API: 84 checks, 84 passed. Each scenario deploys watched flows, makes them fail, deploys a fix as a new revision and drives the engine.

| Scenario | Checks | Covers |
| --- | --- | --- |
| happy | 29 | adoption by SCAN, 7 failures giving 1 incident and 1 alert, SUPERSEDED after a manual rerun, fix candidate a

| root `devDependencies` | `vitest` | `vitest.config.ts` and 160+ root test files (only health-core declared it) |
| widget-src `devDependencies` | `@testing-library/react` | 71 widget test files |
| widget-src `devDependencies` | `@sentry/core` | 2 widget test files |
| widget-src `devDependencies` | `vitest` | `widget-src/vite-configs.test.ts` and 150+ widget test files |
| health-core `devDependencies` | `esbuild` | `packages/health-core/src/engine-portability.test.ts` |

knip and depcheck flag the first four and the widget ones. If an upgrade of `@sentry/react-router`, `@shopify/shopify-app-session-storage-postgresql` or `discord.js` stopped pulling one of these in, the import would break with no manifest change for a reviewer to see. The resend webhook route would fail at load in production.

## The change
- Each package is declared in the manifest that owns the importing file, at the range of the version already in the lockfile (`@sentry/node ^10.76.2`, `pg ^8.23.1`, `@discordjs/rest ^2.6.3`, `vitest ^4.1.12`, `@testing-library/react ^16.3.2`, `@sentry/core ^10.76.2`, `esbuild ^0.28.2`).
- `package-lock.json`, regenerated with npm 10.9.9 (Node 22's npm): only the three manifest copies inside it change. No `version`, `resolved`, `integrity` or `dev` line moves, so CI, the Docker image and the widget bundles install exactly the same packages.
- New `tests/declared-dependencies.test.ts`: for every tracked `.ts/.tsx/.mts/.mjs/.js/.cjs` file outside `extensions/`, `demo-video/` and `docs/`, it reads the imports with TypeScript's own `preProcessFile` and checks each package is declared in the owning manifest (`widget-src/`, `packages/health-core/`, or the root). `@roadmap/health-core` is exempt: the vitest, vite and tsconfig aliases resolve it to source by design.

Not done here: `@types/pg`, which the audit also suggested, is not in the lockfile, so adding it would be a new dependency. The extra declarations the audit lists (zod at the root and in widget-src, `@types/jsonwebtoken` in `dependencies`) are left alone: the Dockerfile installs from the root manifest alone, so removing the root `zod` needs a Docker build to prove the image still has it.

## Net prod-LOC and what was deleted
+8 in the three manifests (+10/-2, two lines gain a trailing comma). Lockfile +10/-2, the same lines. Nothing deleted. Test: +53.

## How to reproduce
```sh
git checkout 66a66df7
grep -c '"@sentry/node"' package.json        # 0
grep -n "@sentry/node" app/routes/api.resend-webhook.ts   # 2:import * as Sentry from '@sentry/node';
npm ls @sentry/node                           # only under @sentry/react-router
```

## Verification
Node 22.23.4, npm 10.9.9, TZ=UTC.
- RED on `66a66df7`: the new test fails and lists the eight packages above.
- GREEN: 1 passed of 1. `npm ci` accepts the new lockfile. The six test files that import the less common packages (resend webhook, Discord send failure, two widget Sentry tests, the health-core engine test, widget vite configs) pass, 154 of 154.
- Hand mutants, each killed: dropping any one of the eight declarations fails the test.
- `tsc --noEmit` on widget-src, health-core and tsconfig.server.json: 0 errors; the new test type-checks under a scratch config that extends tsconfig.server.json. `git diff --check` clean.
- Full suite: see "Full suite and quality gates" below.

## Behaviour change
None: the same packages at the same versions are installed. Future upgrades now have to keep these declarations in range. The next engine release will warn once that `package.json` and `package-lock.json` changed since the last release (engine-release.yml:144-145).

## Overlap
None with open PRs. Two other prepared fixes from this audit also edit `package.json`: one deletes the dead `lint` script and its packages (and the lockfile), one adds a `typecheck:engine` script. With the lint fix, whichever lands second needs `npm install --package-lock-only` to redo the lockfile.

## Further testing needed
None beyond CI.

Prepared by Bobert, Austin's AI agent.

## Full suite and quality gates
- Full suite (`npm run test:all`, which is `vitest run`; Node 22.23.4, TZ=UTC, CI=1) at the fix head 7134c20e: 9484 passed, 0 failed, 6 skipped (401 files); unchanged main 66a66df7: 9483 passed, 0 failed, 6 skipped.
- Incremental review: no new Medium+. CRAP and mutator do not apply (package manifests only); each of the 8 added declarations removed on its own fails the new test (8/8 killed).
- Based on upstream `66a66df710e3a48c339da08741861df8719b1ece`, the same commit the fix was built and tested on.
Published at Austin's request; maintainer review required.

Found by the 0.3.0 end-to-end run: `redgreen start` refused for unapproved tasks wrote no blocked report, and the Stop gate then re-ran the whole suite at every stop, failing on the tests the agent had written red on purpose. ## Intent

"Fork it under knowttl" ... "Everything in the ledger" ... "Slice it sensibly (bugs first, then reads, then writes)."

This slice is the bugs, from the tool-deficiency ledger for ado-axi 0.4.7:
- TD-059: `work-item list` prints a match count that is four times the limit (`count: 3 of 12` with --limit 3, `5 of 20` with --limit 5), not the number of matching work items; the help line says "Showing 3 of 12 matches". Fix: return the real number of matches from the query result, or drop the "of N" text.
- TD-060: `work-item list --fields` with field reference names (System.AssignedTo, System.CreatedDate, Custom.EventSeverity, Custom.EventType) returns those columns empty for items that hold values, and with the short names the `created` column is empty on every item while assignee, changed and state fill. Fix: accept field reference names in --fields and fill the created column.

author: mrogan
body:
**A drill for the canary (Software Factory's milestone 7, Part C): this makes the shop slower on purpose, so the canary's analysis has a bad release to catch and roll back. Revert it once the drill has run.**

- **What it does:** a product's page (`/products/<slug>`) and the catalogue's drawings (`/assets/drawings/…`) wait for one process-wide lock and hold it for at least 40 ms. Every other page and file is served as before, concurrently and with no hold. The change is in `src/app.ts` alone.
- **Why these two:** product pages are 30 of the 77 requests in the traffic generator's round, the largest group it walks, and drawings are what a browser asks for in bulk (a drawing on every card of a product list, and the "also considered" ones on a product page). So a product page the generator measures ends up waiting behind a browser's queue of drawings.
- **The one thing to check first:** the lock must always be let go. The turn is taken before anything is awaited, and released when the response closes, whether it was sent or its client went, even while still waiting. A request whose client has gone is not answered.

Where the lock sits in the request handler:

```text
handler(req, res)
  turn = queues(path) ? oneAtATime() : none     // before the first await
  res.once('close') → release the turn          // sent, or client gone
  await flag set's revision
  /health, /version                             // answered without waiting
  if turn: await turn; sleep 40 ms; if res.destroyed, stop
  asset or page, as before
```

<details open>
<summary>

## How the canary should catch it

</summary>

- **What does not see it:** the concurrency tests from #69 serve their own routes (`/quick`, `/slow`, `/page`, `/a.css`), none of which takes the lock, so they pass unchanged; no test is changed or removed. One product page alone is about 40 ms slower, and the probes and the crawler allow seconds. The generator asks only for pages, never their files, and at a 25% canary sends it about one request every 800 ms, so its product pages hardly ever queue behind each other.
- **What does:** the journeys the canary's analysis runs every 3 minutes, and at the end of each step, open product lists and product pages in up to four browsers at once. Their requests are not measured, but they take the lock, and the generator's product pages, which are measured, wait behind them. The analysis fails the canary when its p99 is more than 25% and more than 100 ms above the baseline's.

</details>

<details>
<summary>

## Tests

</summary>

The base and this change side by side on a laptop. The generator's walk was sent at 5 req/s, 3 requests to the base for every 1 to the change, as a 25% split. The journeys gate, from the pinned `factory-browser` image, ran against both 90 s into each 3-minute window. The figures are the apps' own times for the generator's requests, over 3-minute windows.

| | requests | p50 | p99 | max | over 100 ms |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| base, traffic and journeys | 706 | 2 ms | 23 to 24 ms | 29 ms | 0 |
| change, traffic only | 235 | 12 ms | 49 ms | 50 ms | 0 |
| change, traffic and journeys | 235 | 3 to 10 ms | 142 to 235 ms | 279 ms | 5 to 8 |

- On the change, product pages alone have a median of 46 to 47 ms with traffic only, at most 50 ms; on the base, 4 to 5 ms.
- With the base's p99 at 24 ms, the limit is about 124 ms. Traffic alone stays under it; with the journeys, both windows go over. Prometheus works the p99 out from the histogram's buckets, which puts the lower window nearer 180 ms.
- Both journeys runs found nothing that passes on the base and fails on the change (167 checks). The slowest single answer was 279 ms; the crawler calls an answer slow at 2 s.
- `make check` passes.

</details>

<details open>
<summary>

## What should happen

</summary>

1. Martin merges this, then its deploy pull request.
2. Released, the canary's analysis judges it bad on latency and rolls it back, with nobody touching anything.
3. Martin retries it from the console with auto-rollback off. The analysis fails it again, and this time the release pauses for him; he aborts it.
4. He retries it a third time, and Stop the line aborts that canary.
5. Martin reverts this by hand, and the revert's release should promote.

</details>

author: f-wunderlich
body:
V4.1 rendering currently drops reasoning from every non-prefix assistant message when no tool prompt is rendered. In a history ending with `user q2 -> assistant(reasoning, tool call) -> tool result`, that assistant message belongs to the unfinished current turn. The checkpoint reference keeps its reasoning even when this request omits tool definitions or sets `tool_choice=none`.

This is the current-turn reasoning part of https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/46348.

Track the latest actual user or mid-conversation system message. Without a tool prompt, drop reasoning only before that boundary; tool results do not start a new turn. Existing behavior with active tool definitions and V4 rendering is preserved.

Tests cover a tool-result continuation without definitions and with disabled tool choice, complete prompt equality against DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017's reference `encoding.py`, removal of earlier-turn reasoning, and a mid-conversation system boundary.

Validation on Rust 1.97.1:

- The unmodified implementation fails both new regression tests (14 pass, two fail).
- Fixed implementation: all 18 core tests and all 16 encoding tests pass.
- `cargo fmt --all --check` passes.
- `cargo clippy --locked -p deepseek-recipe-encoding --all-targets -- -D warnings` passes.

Namespace identity is tracked separately at https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-recipe/issues/59. This PR changes the V4.1 prompt renderer; it introduces no protocol fields or sampling changes.

author: hanzamas
body:
Closes #561

AUD1-DT-15-R1: the four minor findings of the read-only review of PR 551 (AUD1-DT-15, #497, merged). Each finding was checked against the code of integration first. All four are real, and each has a fix with a test. The change touches no C source and no file under `src/`, `proto/` or `cmake/`: it is one CI script (`first-test.ps1`, which the job `first test` runs), two docs pages, comments in two Go files, four new Go tests and one extended Go test.

## Acceptance criteria

| # | Criterion of #561 | What changed | Test or job | Result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | The restore of the allowlist in `first-test.ps1` runs also when the read-back or a later step of that block fails | `.github/scripts/first-test.ps1`, step `certificate`: the add of 203.0.113.77 and its checks are in a `try`, and the call that puts the list back is in its `finally`, before any later line of the block | the jobs `first test (x64)` and `first test (arm64)` of `windows.yml` (the way that succeeds: the logs still say `the allowlist is as it was: ...`), and `TestTheFirstTestPutsTheAllowlistBackWhenItsCheckFails` (controller/cmd/ranz, reads the script and holds the restore to the `finally`) | met: `first test (x64)` and `first test (arm64)` are success in run 41189349067, and their logs show the add of 203.0.113.77 and then `the allowlist is as it was: ...`; the Go test passed in `ranz (Linux)` and `ranz (Windows x64)` of run 41189349001 |
| 2 | A viewer does not read the name of an expired token in the audit, or the docs of the roles say that it does, and a test or a docs check shows which | the docs say it: AP-5 and AP-8 of `docs/threat-model.md`; the comments of `api/audit.go` and `api/auditexpired.go` give the true reason | `TestAViewerReadsTheNamesOfTheTokensInTheAuditLog` (controller conformance: a viewer reads the record under `token:leaked`, filters by it, and is refused `GET /api/v1/tokens` with 403) and `TestDocsSayThatAViewerReadsTheNamesOfTheTokensInTheAuditLog` (controller/cmd/ranz: both rows, the two ADR sentences they rest on, and that the tests the row names exist) | met: both tests passed in `ranz (Linux)` and `ranz (Windows x64)` of run 41189349001 |
| 3 | The text on a router that translates addresses names SNAT and a proxy, and says that a plain DNAT keeps the public source | step 5 of `docs/first-test.md` and AP-3 of `docs/threat-model.md` | `TestDocsSayWhereTheDefaultAllowlistIsTooWideAndTooNarrow` (controller/cmd/ranz, reads both pages for the new text and for the absence of the old) | met: the test passed in `ranz (Linux)` and `ranz (Windows x64)` of run 41189349001 |
| 4 | Two deletes and two role changes of admin tokens at the same time leave at least one admin token that has not expired | `controller/internal/rbac/lastadmin_concurrent_test.go` | `TestTwoChangesOfAdminTokensAtOnceLeaveOneThatHasNotExpired` (rbac, on a real rqlite, run by `ranz (Linux)` with `-race`) | met: the test passed in `ranz (Linux)` and `ranz (Windows x64)` of run 41189349001 |
| 5 | No gate relaxed | no gate, floor, baseline or exempt line is touched | the fast set green, and the full set, which runs because `docs/first-test.md` and `first-test.ps1` are paths of SENSITIVE in `ci-plan.py` | met: the diff touches no file of `.github/quality`, no workflow, no `go.mod` or `go.sum`, and not `.github/move-only-waivers.txt`; every run of the head is completed and success, the full set included (the section CI below) |

## The four findings, checked in the code

1. **Real.** On integration the block was `Assert-AllowlistHolds '203.0.113.77'`, then the `set` of `$before`, then `$script:allowlistEvents++`, plain statements one after the other. `Assert-AllowlistHolds` reads the list back after its `set` and throws when the address or an old entry is missing, which is after the address is in the list, so the address stayed. The rerun on a machine whose data directory persists then fails at `set <held> 203.0.113.77`: `intent.ParseSources` refuses an entry that is listed twice (`source ... is listed twice`, `intent/sources.go`) and a bare address is its `/32` (`parseSource`). A restore call that itself fails cannot be saved by the same call in a `finally`; that stays an error of the step, as before, and the job is red. A runner keeps nothing, so the finding is for a machine that does.
2. **Real, and the decision is to say it.** The code does what the ADRs say: `GET /api/v1/audit` needs the role viewer (ADR-0031, "stay with the viewer"; ADR-0030, "It needs the role viewer, since the API gives every read that role; keeping the audit log from viewers needs a rule in the Guard"). The log already named the tokens before PR 551: `AuditCalls` records every change under `token:NAME` (`rbac.Token.Actor`), and each read of the tokens, the audit log or the licence under the name of its caller, and existing tests have a viewer read those records (`TestAuditTargetsAndRetentionAreManagedThroughTheAPI` is one: a viewer reads the eight operations under `token:admin-2`). What PR 551 added is the name of a token that only reads, which no record named before, once its secret is tried after its end, with when it ended and from where. The reason that PR gave, "the audit log is the operator's", is not in any ADR. What was wrong was that the pages did not say it.
3. **Real.** Step 5 of `docs/first-test.md` said "a router that translates addresses (masquerading, NAT)" and AP-3 "a masquerading (NAT) router". A router makes every caller look private only when it rewrites the source address of what it passes on (source NAT, which masquerading is), or when it is a proxy or a load balancer. A plain port forward (destination NAT) keeps the public source of the caller, and the default list refuses it with 403, so the text warned too much, in the safe direction.
4. **Real.** `grep` finds no test of `store` or `rbac` that runs two changes of admin tokens together. The existing concurrent tests are `TestTokensAreUsedConcurrently` (the last use), `TestSetFirstAdminSourcesOfMembersThatStartTogether` (the allowlist) and the conformance tests of #497, which call one change after the other.

## Decisions

- **Finding 2: say it, do not hide it.** Reason: hiding the name from a viewer is a rule in the Guard for `GET /api/v1/audit` that no ADR has (ADR-0030 says so in as many words). To be of use it would have to hide the actor of every record, since a viewer reads `token:NAME` under every change today, which is a redesign of the log and not the fix of one record; and it would take the name out of the record that criterion 2 of #497 asks for ("audited under the token"). The name is no secret and no secret comes into the log. AP-5 and AP-8 now say that the audit log names the API tokens, that a viewer reads those names and can filter by one, and that the list of the tokens stays the admin's. `TestAViewerReadsTheNamesOfTheTokensInTheAuditLog` makes a token that only reads (so no record names it) expire, tries its secret, and has a viewer read the record. A later change that hides the names fails that test and the docs test until the pages follow.
- **Finding 1: the `finally` swallows an error of its own call, after it has printed it.** Reason: a failure of the restore, the Controller not answering for one, must not hide the error that is in flight, which says what failed first; the read back after the block fails the step when the list is not as it was, so no failure of the restore passes.
- **Finding 1: a Go test reads the script.** Reason: the job `first test` runs the script where nothing throws, so it cannot show the way that fails. `TestTheFirstTestPutsTheAllowlistBackWhenItsCheckFails` holds the call that puts the list back to the `finally`, and the read back to after it, as `notice_test.go` reads the fetch scripts.
- **Finding 4: ten rounds of three pairs, with an admin token that has expired beside them.** Reason: a check made in Go before the write is passed by both changes only when their reads come before both w

body: ## Problem `--no-mount` installs (the default for `cargo xtask build`) build the image's whole tree in a staging directory before archiving it into RedoxFS. The directory was hardcoded as `/tmp/redox_installer_`. Building the COSMIC image, about 10 GB of packages with debug info, failed partway through on a host where `/tmp` is a RAM-backed tmpfs with user quotas: ``` installer: failed to install: cannot extract package cosmic-term 0: Disk quota exceeded (os error 122) (None) "Copying and hashing file" ``` That is the host's `EDQUOT`, not a RedoxFS error, but it reads like one. ## Solution Stage the tree beside the output image as `..staging`, on the filesystem that has to hold the image anyway. A tree left there by an interrupted install is removed first. `with_redoxfs_ar_owned` already takes a staging path and removes it afterwards; `install_inner` now passes one. ## Testing The full COSMIC image/build and headless-login evidence refers to the initial bring-up snapshot before review follow-ups. Validation of the current combined stack is still in progress; the focused checks below are identified separately. - New unit test: the staging path sits beside the image, an interrupted run's leftover tree is cleared, and an image path with no file name is an error. - `cargo test -p redox_installer`: all pass. - The COSMIC `wayland` image then installed and booted headless to `redox login:`. ## AI assistance Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5) found the cause while building the COSMIC image and wrote the change and test. ## Checklist - [x] I understand this change in full and will respond to review. - [x] My commits are signed off under the Developer Certificate of Origin (`git commit -s`). - [x] I have built and tested this change. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) ---

author: naokihamada
body:
Inductive skeleton risk formulas previously covered a single simplex or product cell. Derive and prove the formula for any finite assembled simploidal set with compatible positive degrees, including shared and self-identified faces, degenerate boundary maps, disconnected domains and nonuniform evaluation weights.

The new chapter expresses propagation as a finite polynomial in a block triangular matrix, derives cell/group allocation optima, and compares joint fitting using the global proper-control count. It recovers the existing simplex/product formulas and gives exact quadratic chain and loop examples. The public skeleton APIs retain their documented single-cell scope; the general estimator is verified with successive public constrained fits.

## Validation

- 41 new reference tests: exact rational moments and propagation versus independent public-basis quadrature and constrained least squares, across ten assembled domains.
- Full pytest: 2,739 passed, 41 skipped, 54 subtests passed.
- Mypy: 86 files; pre-commit and changed-file typos: passed.
- Strict Sphinx HTML and doctest builds: passed, 287 examples.
- Independent mutation checks reject uniformized evaluation weights and an incorrect squared group multiplicity.
- No package source changes; diff coverage has no changed executable package lines.

## Local review

Aspects: requirements, design, correctness, edge cases, tests, documentation, conventions, readability, numerics and framework integration (10 reviewers, 3 rounds). Final round has no findings.

| Severity | Found | Fixed | Rejected | Deferred |
|----------|-------|-------|----------|----------|
| blocker | 1 | 1 | 0 | 0 |
| major | 2 | 2 | 0 | 0 |
| minor | 2 | 2 | 0 | 0 |

Fixed: explicitly require mutually independent noise independent of design rows; evaluate weighted risks by independent chart integration; compare grouped allocations with the original cell objective; derive numerical tolerance budgets from roundoff, operation counts and conditioning; distinguish zero-trace cells from zero-coefficient groups in singular-evaluation allocation limits. Duplicate reviewer findings are counted once.
