author: po4yka
body:
Phase 8.1 of the redesign plan (`docs/redesign/PLAN.md`, "S1. Hero" and "Phase 8", item 8.1): split the hero, set the name as the display moment (rule A9, `--step-6`), and a CSS-only boot reveal. 8.2 (decode) to 8.6 (pointer) follow as separate PRs.

## What changed
- **Static, bilingual hero:** `src/components/Hero.tsx` (one `client:load` island whose text came from the locale store, so the server HTML was always English) becomes `src/components/Hero/`: `HeroText.tsx` and `HeroWhois.tsx` are server-only React rendered by `Hero.astro`, with all text through `<T>` like the Phase 3 sections. A Russian visitor gets Russian from the first paint and no script sits in front of the name. `BuildStats` is static too. Only `ActivitySparkline` (`client:only`, because it computes date labels at render time) and `LatestReleasePanel` (`client:visible`, with a placeholder so it has something to observe) still hydrate. The whois `$ cd ~/po4yka && cat identity.md` line is plain text now (it was a click-to-copy button that needs hydration).
- **The name (rule A9):** two lines, the given name at weight 300 and the family name at 650 on Geist's `wght` axis, in `.display-name`. `--step-6: clamp(3rem, 24.5cqi, 7.5rem)` sizes it to the identity column (an `@container`): the longest line, "Pochaev" at 650, is 3.91em, so it fills the column with about 4% to spare. Measured: 67px at 320, 80px at 375, 120px from 768; fits and no horizontal scroll at 320, 375, 768, 1024, 1280 and 1440 in EN and RU. The h1 still reads "Nikita Pochaev" / "Никита Почаев" for copy and screen readers.
- **Boot reveal:** the label, subtitle, meta strip, CTAs and whois column fade in with `Reveal` (CSS `@starting-style`, stagger up to 240 ms, none under reduced motion). The name and the intro paragraph do not fade: either can be the LCP element, and a fade delays LCP.
- `DESIGN.md`: rule A9, `--step-6` in the type scale, the hero description. `docs/Guidelines.md` and the PLAN `--step-6` row follow.

## Deviations from PLAN
1. The hero becomes static server markup (like the Phase 3 sections), not a split `client:load` island. Only the two GitHub-fed panels hydrate.
2. "300 at rest and 650 on the emphasised letters" is a two-line name: given name 300, family name 650.
3. `--step-6` uses container units instead of a `vw` + `rem` clamp, because the name must fill a column whose width is not a fixed share of the viewport. The 3rem floor and 7.5rem cap are rem; browser zoom keeps the name inside its column.

## Verification
- `npm run lint`, `tsc` (TS7), `tsc6`, `npm test` (39 files, 378 tests, new `hero-text.test.ts`), `npm run build`, `npm run validate:skills`: pass. `astro check` runs in CI.
- Chromium e2e against this build: 89/89, including `language.spec.ts` (the stored RU locale shows "Никита Почаев" from the first paint; the switcher changes it in place; no reveal on the h1; no horizontal overflow at 320 and 375 in both locales), `cls.spec.ts` and `hydration.spec.ts`.
- **LCP element (acceptance):** Lighthouse names `h1#hero-heading > span > span.block` ("Pochaev") as the LCP element on mobile and desktop. Before, it was the intro paragraph.
- **LCP value:** desktop 0.6 to 0.7 s (Phase 0: 726 ms). Mobile 2.7 to 2.9 s over three runs, CLS 0, TBT 0. Phase 0 measured 2.46 s, so I measured current `main` the same way on the same machine: 2.9 s, 2.9 s, 2.9 s (FCP 2.3 to 2.4 s on both). This PR does not move mobile LCP; the drift since Phase 0 is shared by every page: the render-blocking stylesheet is now 73 KB and Lighthouse charges about 0.9 s to it.
- Screenshots: 1280 EN and 375 RU checked by eye.
- **Not run locally:** WebKit and Firefox (not installed here; CI runs them).
- **Visual baselines:** the home baselines at 375 and 1280 change (the name, the reveal order is not captured since visual runs use reduced motion). I will refresh them from this PR's CI artifact after checking the images.

author: lucas-albers-lz4
body:
Refs #385

## Problem
`properties/generated/aidevops_encodable_fraction.json` carried `measurement_status: historical_pre_615_shell_extractor` with a note saying it predates the #615 shell extractor expansion guard and is **not** issue-closure evidence. It also recorded 63 unclassified parse-error rows.

## Approach
- Materialized `marcusquinn/aidevops` at pin `8666b6c6c52472b5535aa295f2df593918152cb1` and re-ran `scripts/measure-corpus-fraction.py --corpus aidevops --assert-determinism` with the current extractor.
- Result: **10,198 / 11,422 = 0.8928**, `complete_run=true`, two runs byte-identical, compiler fingerprint `35ea1f238a9e`. The extractor now finds 11,422 site instances versus 11,330, so the earlier 10,212/11,330 figure is superseded.
- Parse-error rows drop from 63 to 28. Sampled rows show the extractor stopped mid-character-class (`^[[:space:`, `^#[[:space:`), so they are extraction truncations rather than corpus patterns. They stay in the `parse-error` bucket and are not counted as encodable.
- Removed the historical status from the fraction and smith decision, updated the reason with the current numbers, and documented the measurement and parse-error disposition in `batch/corpora/aidevops/README.md`.
- Regenerated `conversion-ledger.json/.md` via `scripts/conversion-ledger.py`: aidevops is no longer excluded from the inventory aggregates (`non-current ... none`), and the encodable/extracted and excluding-YARA rates are recomputed.

## Tests
- `python3 -m pytest -q tests/test_aidevops_gate_batch.py tests/test_conversion_ledger.py tests/test_intervals.py` — 48 passed.
- `ruff check --fix tests/test_aidevops_gate_batch.py` then `ruff check` — clean.
- Ledger regeneration run twice — byte-identical.

## Risk
The ledger headline rates move because a previously excluded corpus is now counted; that is the intended consequence of a current measurement, and the exclusion note now reads `none`. No saturation claim and no product property is made from this corpus.

## Exclusions
No change to `WAVE_CORPORA`, scoring, disclosure handling, or any other corpus. This PR does not merge or affect the status of #385.

author: roboomp
body:
## Repro
In an unattended session, queue a steering message while `ask` awaits a dialog answer (including plan mode). The message stays behind the dialog until someone answers or cancels it. Before the fix, `bun test packages/coding-agent/test/tools/ask.test.ts -t 'delivers queued steering while ask is open'` failed when the safety abort fired instead of delivering the steer.

## Cause
`AskTool` in `packages/coding-agent/src/tools/ask.ts` was exclusive but not interruptible. `executeToolCalls` in `packages/agent/src/agent-loop.ts` therefore passed the external-only signal, not its queued-steering interrupt signal; the dialog could not close on steering.

## Fix
- Made `AskTool` interruptible; queued interruption releases the dialog without calling `context.abort()`, while user cancellation still aborts the turn.
- Added an agent-loop regression for queued delivery and retained question context in plan mode, plus fallback-selector interruption coverage.
- Documented the user-visible change in the coding-agent changelog.

## Verification
`bun test packages/coding-agent/test/tools/ask.test.ts packages/coding-agent/test/agent-loop-wait-interrupt.test.ts packages/coding-agent/test/agent-session-queued-steer-delivery.test.ts` — 132 passed. `bun check` — passed. The regression drives the actual agent loop through a pending rich dialog. Skipped the PR pre-publish gate: `bun run test` fails on clean `main` with a permission error in `packages/utils/test/dirs-xdg.test.ts`; separate runs on clean `main` reproduce the same offline PlusCal grammar, session-lease, and usage-banner failures seen in the branch's full-suite run. The default-branch checkout was generated from `origin/main` into `/tmp/omp-17537-main` because `/work/.tree` is unavailable in this environment.

Fixes #17537

author: k-macao
body:
## 结论

DeepSeek key **已经在生效了** —— 线上 05 节现在显示：

> ◆ DeepSeek 检索兜底 **已启用 · 本轮救回 6 源 · 剩余额度 14**

救回来的是 WSJ 经济 / Seeking Alpha / Kitco / FXStreet / 汇通网 等以前长期 403 的源。
整体可用源从 **18/49 (37%) → 45/49 (92%)**，01/04 的数据覆盖从 **94% → 99%**。

但剩下 4 个「未获取」不是网络抖动，逐个查过后是两类**机制缺陷**，这个 PR 修掉它们。

## 剩下 4 源的真实原因

| 源 | 原因 | 本次处理 |
|---|---|---|
| **福布斯市场** (#18) | 单端点 `forbes.com/markets/feed/` 已 **404**，且**根本没有配 `deepseek_fallback`** —— key 再好也救不回来 | 补兜底 |
| **福布斯商业** (#10) | 同样是单端点（`/business/feed/`，暂时 200，改版即死） | 补兜底 |
| **DailyFX** (#36) | 有兜底，但检索词 `forex market news` 在 `site:dailyfx.com` 约束下 **0 结果** | 收敛为 `forex analysis` |
| **QuantStart** (#48) | 同上，`quantitative trading algorithms` → 0 结果 | 收敛为 `quantitative trading` |
| 雪球 (#23) | 4 个公共 RSSHub 实例全是 antiCrawler（403/超时） | 补第三条路由；检索兜底仍是主力 |

核心认知：检索式是 `site:<站点> <query> lang/x after:<日期>`。**站点体量小 + query 超过 4 个词 =
几乎必然 0 结果** —— 这就是「有兜底却救不回」的隐形坑。

## 新增回归（加严，不是放宽）

- `test_every_source_that_can_realistically_die_has_a_fallback`
  单端点源**必须**显式配兜底；确实只有唯一公开出口的（CNBC / IBD / FOOL / OILPRICE /
  COINTELEGRAPH / BITCOINMAG / PROJECT_SYNDICATE / CNINFO / OAKTREE）要在
  `KNOWN_SINGLE_ENDPOINT` 里**点名并说明理由**。以后新增单端点源，测试会强制做一次判断。
- `test_fallback_queries_stay_broad_enough`
  检索词 ≤ 4 个词，防止再次写窄。

这两条正是从「FORBES_MKT 明明有 key 却永远救不回」和「DailyFX 有兜底但 0 结果」两个真实故障反推出来的。

## 验证

- `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests` → **361 OK (skipped=1)**
- `python3 rss_feeds.py --catalog-md docs/rss-49-feeds.md` 已重新生成（测试要求文档与目录一致）
- `python3 build_site.py --check` → 126 个占位符全部可解析、无残留
- 兜底源数量：10 → **11**

## 合并后预期

下一轮构建里，福布斯市场 / DailyFX / QuantStart 若能被检索救回，可用源会进一步接近 48–49/49；
救不回也会**如实标注**（会显示 `DeepSeek 检索: ValueError: 检索无结果` 而不是含糊的未获取）。

author: thejackshelton
body:
TLDR: the dead-controls probe's load pass now reads each page until two reads a few frames apart agree. A width whose layout never holds still is reported incomplete instead of compared. Same build, two runs: Chromium's load-pass findings reproduced 48% of the time (box 313/650, hit-region 77/178, missing-at-width 111/212), against 100% in WebKit.

Why the runs differed:
- `ready()` waited at most 1 s for fonts, and the settles cap at 300 to 700 ms. On a loaded runner a late font or layout pass lands after the read, and the box is read mid-change.
- Chromium shards served the original from 3 `next start` copies while it was not frozen. Each copy regenerated its stale ISR pages on its own, so loads differed by copy. WebKit used one copy. #467 freezes the original.

What changed (scripts/probe/dead-controls.mjs, src/dev/findings.ts):
- `stableRead(page, fn)`: up to `STABLE_READS` (8) reads, each after two frames and 150 ms. It returns the first read equal to the one before it, and undefined if none is. The load pass reads the original's controls and region grid, and the port's controls, this way.
- A side that never holds still at a width adds `{ width, side, why }` to the route's `incomplete`, and that width's boxes, hit points and controls are not compared there.
- `ready()` waits up to 10 s for `document.fonts.ready`, not 1 s.
- `dev`'s run diff prints `INCOMPLETE` lines, and a load-pass finding at an incomplete width is not counted as fixed.

How it was checked:
- Locally, the original against itself (frozen copy) at CONCURRENCY=2 on `/docs/components/aria/kbd` and `/docs/monorepo`: 0 findings and nothing incomplete, at 130 s and 206 s.
- `test/dev.test.ts` covers the incomplete diff.
- The CI receipt needs two probe runs on one build. I'll queue it once the shadcn deploy has the runners back; the coordinator has capped us at one GitHub run at a time.

author: adityakharbikar
body:
PR #15 merged only its first two commits (`f260994`, `62d1f68`). These two landed after that merge and **main does not have them**. Each fixes a bug that is currently live on main.

## 1. `Invalid Date` on every alert — `reporting.py`
`get_alerts()` selects `a.ts` but emitted the output key as `created_at`; `AlertCard.jsx:30` reads `alert.ts`. Now emits both. Reported by @ayaan.

```
before: ts=None          -> "Invalid Date"
after : ts=2026-10-31T07:00:25.691863+00:00
```

## 2. SLA drift — `tickets.py`
Mine was `{critical:4, high:24, medium:72, low:168}`; `contract/db.md` says **4/12/48/72**. This is the 23.4h showing on tickets. Now imports `app.constants.SLA_HOURS` (Ayaan's A3, now on main) with that same table as fallback, so the two cannot drift again. Existing auto-tickets backfilled 24h → 12h.

## 3. Ticket evidence never rendered — `tickets.py`
`TicketDrawer.jsx:71` gates on `evidence.explanation`; I only wrote structured fields. The ticket now carries the detector's own sentence:

```
TK-9001 [spike]      Lab 102 is using 2.3× its normal Saturday 12:00 load (7.9 kW vs 3.5 kW expected).
TK-9003 [night_leak] Hostel Room 103 is drawing 1.9 l/min of water at 00:00 — steady flow with nobody there points to a leak.
```

## 4. What-if returns 422 — `router.py` / `reporting.py`
`client.js runWhatIf` posts `{actions: [...]}` and reads `{baseline, scenario, savings, per_building}`. My route took `{action: str}` and returned `{projected, saving, by_building}`. A hard 422 on the what-if demo beat.

- accepts `action` (single) or `actions` (list, combined)
- multiple actions compound, so four at once gives 96%, never negative
- response carries both key spellings so neither side breaks while we settle on one

## Verified live on the shared Supabase
```
alerts ts parses        : 31 Oct 07:00
auto-ticket SLA         : 12.0h (high)
evidence.explanation    : present on TK-9001..9006
whatif {actions:[led,ac]}: 200, 53.2%, ₹341,982/mo
whatif bad action       : 400
```

## Correction on my PR #15 review comment
I claimed `/api/equipment/{id}` lacked `prediction`. **That was wrong** — it has returned it since A2 (PR #14). The real caveat is that `predictions` is derived: a fresh `app.seed` has 0 rows until `POST /api/insights/run` runs, so `AssetCard`'s prediction block is invisible on the README happy path until someone hits run once.

## Still open, not mine
`frontend/src/pages/Insights.jsx` and `Reports.jsx` are 5-line placeholders (@harshavi) — the what-if and report demo beats have no UI yet, though the endpoints are ready.

body:
## Samenvatting

PR 7.6 uit `docs/pr-7.6-plan.md` (besluiten §H goedgekeurd door de eigenaar op 2026-10-31): corrigeren van een afgeronde wedstrijd werkt nu ook in cloudmodus. Dit is de gebundelde PR van het plan (#135), 7.6a (#136), 7.6b (#137) en 7.6c (#138), inclusief de bevindingen uit de Opus-review. Staat op `main` na de merge van PR 7.5 (#132).

**Wat de gebruiker krijgt (cloudmodus)**
- Coach, admin en owner kunnen een segment corrigeren; de gebruiker-ID wordt als corrector vastgelegd (lokaal blijft `null`). Viewer en scorer niet.
- Per wedstrijd één statusindicator: Wacht op synchronisatie, Gesynchroniseerd, Actie nodig of Conflict, met een knop "Opnieuw proberen" bij Actie nodig.
- Bij een conflict of bij Actie nodig kan de gebruiker de eigen lokale versie verwerpen, met een bevestigingsscherm dat uitlegt wat verloren gaat. Dit verwijdert alleen de lokale kopie; de cloud wordt niet aangeraakt, het is geen tombstone, en zonder bevestigde cloudkopie kan het niet.
- Corrigeren staat uit zolang de afronding nog niet server-bevestigd is (met uitleg); een wedstrijd die alleen in de cloud staat mag wel gecorrigeerd worden.
- Alle nieuwe tekst bestaat in NL en EN.

**Niet gewijzigd:** Firestore Rules, datacontract, statistiekfuncties, CSV-contract, localStorage-keys. Geen deploy.

## Review-bevindingen die zijn opgelost
- Na een correctie van een cloud-only wedstrijd bleef het apparaat op "Lokaal beschikbaar" staan en was verdere correctie geblokkeerd (`hasConfirmedCloudCopy`, met tests voor het pad lokale kopie zonder checkpoint plus bevestigde cloudkopie).
- Een tweede gebruiker op hetzelfde apparaat kon vastzitten in "Actie nodig": verwerpen is nu ook daar mogelijk.
- Verwerpen weigert bij een eigen, onbevestigde cloudwrite; focus na verwerpen valt niet meer op `body`; de knop "Opnieuw proberen" verschijnt alleen als er iets te herstellen valt.

## Tests
- `v2/`: `tsc -b`, `eslint .` en `prettier -c .` schoon; `vitest run`: 162 bestanden, 2325 tests geslaagd.
- Emulator Suite (lokaal): nieuwe spec voor twee apparaten, 8 scenario's, 3 keer herhaald: 24/24 geslaagd (zonder `test.fail()`); volledige auth-suite 143 geslaagd; gewone e2e-suite 146 geslaagd (inclusief één bestaande, ongewijzigde `test.fail()`).
- Deze branch is inhoudelijk identiek aan de lokaal geteste stand; de CI van GitHub draait hier voor het eerst op.

## Voor het mergen
1. Publiceer de Firestore Rules uit PR 7.5 vóór clients met cloudcorrecties; een Netlify-build doet dat niet. Zonder de Rules faalt het uploaden veilig met "Actie nodig".
2. Test op staging één correctie met fictieve data en controleer dat de status "Gesynchroniseerd" wordt.
3. Gebruikers die vóór de publicatie corrigeerden, zien na een herstart "Actie nodig" en moeten bewust "Opnieuw proberen" kiezen.

## Open punten
- Een offline gemaakte correctie wordt niet meegeteld door de waarschuwing voor niet-gesynchroniseerd werk bij uitloggen op een onvertrouwd apparaat; eigen vervolg-PR.
- Een Rules-test met een groot logboek (50 correcties, veel segmenten) ontbreekt; de emulator logde "maximum of 1000 expressions" bij geweigerde correcties.
- Echte-apparaat- en staging-verificatie is niet gedaan; geen e2e voor "Opnieuw proberen" in de browser of twee gebruikers op één apparaat (unit-tests dekken dat).
- `by` mag in de cloud `null` blijven; cloudmigratie van gecorrigeerde wedstrijden blijft geblokkeerd.

author: cryptohivekeeper
body:
## Description

BLAKE3 tail and tree-reduction work on the SIMD tiers:

- A 9..15 chunk tail runs in a single 16-lane AVX-512 pass, and its chaining values are written out through an 8-row un-transpose.
- Partial-batch CVs (2..15 chunks) are reduced with the 8-wide parent kernel and pushed as complete subtrees instead of chunk by chunk.
- Single parent compressions take an SSSE3 path without a staging buffer.
- On hosts without AVX512VL the 8-lane AVX2 kernels no longer spill on every rotate: three of the 'a' words wait in spare rows of the message buffer, so the 16 state words leave a scratch register for the shift-or rotates. The stepped kernel is now selected on AVX512VL rather than AVX512F.

With this, BLAKE3 is back at parity with the other implementations for inputs between a few KB and just under 16 KB. On an AVX2-only run (`DOTNET_EnableAVX512=0`) the AVX2 tier is also faster from 3 KB up, about a quarter faster at 1 MB and beyond, and the 8-lane XOF squeeze is an order of magnitude faster at 128 KB.

The benchmark docs now note that the SSSE3 and AVX2 rows of a run on an AVX-512 host still use its 32-register file and single-instruction rotates, so they overstate real SSSE3- or AVX2-only hardware.

Also included: comment corrections across the BLAKE3 tiers, `Debug.Assert`s on the chunk counts each partial kernel serves, code-analysis cleanups (braces, pattern checks, CA1822 suppressions on TFM-conditioned members) and named hash-size constants in `Streebog`.

## Type of change

- [ ] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [ ] ✨ New feature / algorithm (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [ ] 💥 Breaking change (fix or feature that changes existing public API or behavior)
- [ ] 📝 Documentation
- [ ] 🏗️ Build / CI / tooling
- [x] ♻️ Refactor / performance (no functional change)

## Affected package(s)

- see auto labels

## Checklist

- [x] The solution builds clean with `TreatWarningsAsErrors=true`.
- [ ] `dotnet format "CryptoHives .NET Foundation.sln"` changes are committed.
- [x] `dotnet test "CryptoHives .NET Foundation.sln"` passes across the target frameworks.
- [ ] I added or updated tests covering the change.
- [x] Public API changes are documented (XML docs, package `README.md`, and/or docfx).
- [x] The code stays AOT-safe for the .NET 8+ targets (no new trim/AOT warnings).
- [x] Every commit is signed off (`git commit -s`), see [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/CryptoHives/Foundation/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#sign-off-your-commits).

## Notes for reviewers

The new BLAKE3 paths are covered by the existing known-answer and cross-validation tests. `Streebog` gains two public constants, `HashSizeBytes256` and `HashSizeBytes512`.

## Summary

Closes #3507.

- Give OpenCode 1.x and 2.x one `SurfacedBatch` owner for surface, native-prompt injection, acknowledgment and abandonment.
- Refuse native-prompt injection while a batch is open, preserving the active batch and leaving queued messages pending for a later eligible turn. Keep the existing receive-key holds, success/Stop acknowledgments, error release and 2.x execution-event guards.
- Preserve the existing `computeInjection` export. Add real-broker regression cases to the maintained adapter suite, await native hook completion and bind those fixture brokers explicitly to loopback.
- Update the user documentation and comments naming the old helper, adapt the existing cooperative-teardown fixture recipe to the new method names, and include a patch changeset for both touched connector packages.

## Verification

author: yuminn-k
body:
Fixes #2803

**Description**

During consolidation, Karpenter simulates rescheduling the pods on a candidate node. `VolumeTopology.getRequirements` adds the node affinity of each pod's bound PV, so a pod with a generic ephemeral volume was pinned to the zone of its current volume. That PVC is owned by the pod and is deleted with it. The replacement pod gets a new PVC, so the old PV's zone does not apply to it. Because of the pin, the node could not be consolidated whenever the pod had to move to another zone, and Karpenter reported the pod as not schedulable (`Unconsolidatable`, with the zone narrowed to the volume's zone in the topology spread message).

This PR skips the bound PV's node affinity for ephemeral volumes on pods that are already bound to a node (`spec.nodeName` set). It then falls through to the StorageClass `allowedTopologies`, which still limits where the new volume can be provisioned. This addresses the concern @jmdeal raised on the issue about `Immediate` binding: whatever the binding mode, the new PVC is provisioned within the StorageClass topology, and the old PV no longer exists. Pending pods, and regular PVCs on any pod, still use the bound PV's requirements as before.

This builds on #2907 by @moko-poi, which used the same bound-pod condition but returned no requirements for these volumes, so it also dropped the StorageClass topology. That PR was closed as rotten. The commit credits them with `Co-authored-by`.

**How was this change tested?**

- New table test in `pkg/controllers/disruption/consolidation_test.go` (`Delete` context). There are two nodes in different zones, and a pod on the second node has a volume bound to a PV in that node's zone:
  - ephemeral volume: the node is deleted and the pod fits on the other node. This fails without the fix (no command).
  - regular PVC: the node is kept. This passes before and after the fix and guards the scope.
- `go test -race ./pkg/controllers/disruption/... ./pkg/controllers/provisioning/...` passes (`disruption`, `provisioning`, `provisioning/scheduling`).
- `gofmt`, `go vet`, and `golangci-lint-kube-api-linter run` on the touched packages: clean.

```release-note
Fixed consolidation treating pods with generic ephemeral volumes as pinned to the zone of their current volume, which blocked consolidation when the pod had to move to another zone.
```

### المرحلة 0 (خادم)

body:
## What

**1. Installable app (PWA)**
- Adds a manifest, icons (192 px, 512 px, maskable, Apple touch icon), a service worker and an offline page.
- **Android Chrome, Edge, Samsung Internet:** an "Install app" button appears in the footer.
- **iPhone:** the same button explains Share → Add to Home Screen.
- **Installed:** the app opens full-screen with the Coffee Lab icon.

**2. Receipts no longer slow down checkout**
- Checkout saves the order and answers right away with receipt status `pending`.
- `services/receiptQueue.js` builds the PDF and image afterwards:
  - two at a time, up to 3 attempts each
  - repeated requests for one order collapse into one build
  - a request that arrives mid-build (cash collected → "PAID") reruns the build afterwards
- A sweeper runs every 5 minutes and re-queues receipts left `pending` by a restart (signed-in orders from the last 24 hours, not cancelled).
- The tracking page says "Preparing your receipt…" and checks back after 3 s and 8 s. After a minute without a receipt it offers the existing "Generate receipt" button.

**3.** The footer's Facebook link now points to the real profile.

## Why the service worker is conservative
- **Pages and `/api`:** never served from the cache.
  - A deploy is live on the next load, so the app never runs old JavaScript against a new server.
  - No order, session or receipt is ever stale.
- **CSS, JS and icons:** fetched from the network first; the cache is used only when the phone is offline.
- **Navigation while offline:** shows `offline.html`.

## Risks
- **Service workers stay installed in browsers.** If one ever misbehaves, bumping the `CACHE` name or shipping a `sw.js` that unregisters itself fixes it. Its scope is deliberately small.
- **The receipt queue lives in memory.** It assumes one server instance; a restart is covered by the sweeper. With several instances, a receipt might be built twice (harmless: the last upload wins). Moving to a database-backed queue (pg-boss) is the next step at that size.
- **Customers see `pending` for about 1–3 s after ordering**, where before they saw the receipt immediately.

## Checks
- **Lint:** passes; the service worker is linted with service-worker globals.
- **Tests (135 pass):**
  - The new `test/receiptQueue.test.js` covers dedupe, rerun mid-build, retries then giving up, and the sweeper's filters.
  - `api.test.js` now checks that the manifest (its content type, maskable icon, every icon URL), `/sw.js` (it must skip `/api`) and `offline.html` are served.

Stacked on #43.

author: thorstenhornung1
body:
Follow-up to #1. It addresses the code review of the adaptive temperature step
(upstream issue `fredrike/pydaikin#168`).

## Review findings and fixes

| Finding | Fix |
|---|---|
| P1: HTTP 404 on a strict write counted as success | A strict request raises on 404; reads keep the old `{}` behaviour |
| P1: a failed read-back after `ret=OK` left the requested value cached | The read-back is part of the transaction and must report a numeric `stemp`. After an unknown outcome (timeout, HTTP error, cancellation, `ret=NG`, missing `stemp`) the requested `stemp` is removed from the cache and the resource invalidated |
| P1/P2: tenacity could repeat a write up to 3 times | Retries are limited to reads; pydaikin sends every write once |
| P2: a confirmed 0.5 °C device could be downgraded by a range error | No fallback once `confirmed`, or outside 18–30 °C |
| P2: retry accepted but read back differently re-raised the original rejection | New `DaikinVerificationError(requested, actual)`; the cache shows the read-back value |
| P2: accepted half degree with a different read-back was only logged | Raises `DaikinVerificationError` as well |
| P3: free-form status string | The setter only accepts `unknown` / `confirmed` / `inferred` |

Additional finding: aiohttp itself resends an idempotent GET once when a reused
keep-alive connection drops without an answer (RFC 9112). It is the identical
request, never a different setpoint. pydaikin cannot disable it on a session it
does not own, so the behaviour is documented and tested.

P3 items that are left as open questions for the maintainer: the optimistic 0.5
on BRP072C (only tested offline), and the polling lock scope (kept simple: with
`MAX_CONCURRENT_REQUESTS = 1` requests were serialised anyway; cancellation
releasing the lock is tested).

## Tests

```
$ pytest -q tests/test_brp069_temperature_step.py
62 passed                      (10 repeated runs, all green)
$ pytest -q
423 passed, 5 skipped          (baseline on master: 361 passed, 5 skipped)
$ pre-commit run --files <changed files>
ruff / ruff format / pylint: Passed
```

GitHub Actions are disabled on this fork; these are local results.

## Real device check (Stylish 0FC1, adapter 4_2_303, unit off, guarded writes)

22.5 was accepted and confirmed. 22.2 was rejected with `PARAM NG` and not
retried. A simulated whole-degree adapter fell back to 23 and was inferred.
With the fallback disabled, the rejection was raised. A simulated rejection
after a confirmed 0.5 °C was raised without any fallback. Afterwards the
original state was restored with no difference.

author: y1o1
body:
Code-quality fixes from the architectural reviewer's batch 2a (foundation), for records, store, keys, secret-hash and mail. Behaviour is unchanged: every module's tests pass as they were, and no public name, setting or output changes. No notice row.

## Per module (one commit each)
- **records:**
  - R1: the resend until the store answers is now `untilAnswered`, so `settled` means only a keyed set's member.
  - R2: the pauses' start and cap are `firstPauseMs` (50) and `longestPauseMs` (1000).
  - R3: `rewrite`, `create`, `remove` and `changeRecords` try again through one helper, `retried`. An attempt answers `again` where it lost a race or confirmed nothing; past `attempts` the answer is unavailable, as before.
  - R4: `pairedRecordsAcross` splits reads and results by place through a typed `byPlace<F, S>`, so its three `as unknown as` casts are gone. Each place's decided changes are taken by `take`.
- **store:**
  - S1: `batch` and `batchAcross` apply through one `applyBatch(conditions, writes, now)`.
  - S3: `defaultAttempts` (8).
  - S4: `largestLimit` (1,000,000,000).
  - S2 is left as it is: `guarded` keeps a late answer under the mark and `guardedAcross` does not. So a different request reusing that mark answers `reused` from one and `late` from the other, and making them one would change an answer.
- **keys:**
  - KY1: `rsaModulusFloor` (2048 bits, RFC 7518 §3.3) and `hs256SecretFloor` (32 bytes, RFC 7518 §3.2), beside the settings they bound.
  - KY2 stays, as the review found.
- **secret-hash:** SH1 names the floors and sizes in the card's words:
  - `bcryptCostFloor` (4);
  - `scryptLnFloor` (10);
  - `nodeLnPerR` (16, Node's own limit);
  - `scryptMostP` (2);
  - `saltBytes` (16–64) and `keyBytes` (32–64);
  - `scryptMemoryBase` (128, the 128 in 128·N·r).
- **mail:** M1 names the address limits:
  - `longestAddress` (254) and `longestLocalPart` (64), from RFC 5321 §4.5.3.1;
  - `longestDomain` (253) and `longestLabel` (63), the text form DNS holds (RFC 1035 §2.3.4).

author: naiches
body:
## Summary

| # | Fix | Area |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Camera-roll backup under "Selected photos" access explains itself and stops looping | Backup engine, Settings |
| 2 | Files-app uploads are ~2.5× faster and survive a dropped chunk request | File Provider extension |
| 3 | Photo previews you choose (size and format), stored once in your account, opened instantly on any device | Photos viewer, Settings, native module, server |
| 4 | Grid thumbnails: two fixed WebP sizes (384 / 768 px) instead of a quality setting | Thumbnails, Photos grid, backup engine |
| 5 | Photo viewer fills the screen; no black bars, no jump when the controls hide | Photos viewer |

Gate results (whole branch, re-run after every fix):
- `bun run test`: `isolated: 3818 pass, 0 fail across 382 files`
- `bunx tsc --noEmit`: exit 0
- `bash scripts/swift-ci/run-swift-tests.sh`: `swift-tests: 1594 assertions across 28 files, 0 failed`
- iOS simulator Debug build: `** BUILD SUCCEEDED **`

Not part of this PR: local `pod install` byproducts in `ios/Podfile.lock` / `project.pbxproj`.

---

## 1. Camera-roll backup under "Selected photos" access

### Problem

With iOS photo access set to **Selected photos**, camera-roll backup could sit at "Waiting for first scan" or "Preparing backup – 2 of 11 items" forever, retrying in a loop and never telling the user why.

Reproduced on the simulator: backup ran with full access, then access was narrowed to 0 selected photos. The 9 photos still queued were no longer readable. Each one came back "missing locally", was counted as a **failure**, and every 5 of them parked the drain for 60 s. The few shared photos sat behind that skip → pause → skip loop. With nothing selected from the start, Settings showed "Waiting for first scan" with no hint that the photo permission was the cause.

### Root causes

1. **The scan never scoped the manifest to the limited selection.** Rows for photos the user stopped sharing stayed `pending_upload`.
2. **The library observer only inserts.** Unsharing a photo in the limited picker never removed it from the queue.
3. **A missing/unshared photo counted as a failure** in `processBatch` and fed the 5-in-a-row → 60 s backoff.
4. **Settings and Backup status counted photos with a call that always throws.** In expo-media-library 57, `getAssetsAsync` from the main entry point throws at runtime; only `expo-media-library/legacy` still has it. `SettingsScreen` and `BackupInsightsScreen` still imported the main entry and swallowed the throw, so the on-device count was always 0 (or stale). The other screens had already moved to `/legacy`.
5. **No UI for limited or revoked access.**

### Changes

**Engine (`NativeBackupEngine.swift`)**
- Scan: under `.limited`, scope the manifest to the fetched photos using the existing album-selection mechanism (`selected_for_backup`). Unshared photos leave the queue and the counts, and come back on the first scan after access widens.
- `photoLibraryDidChange`: under `.limited`, do a full rescan (as with an album selection), so unsharing is picked up.
- `processBatch`: the task group returns `uploaded` / `skipped` / `failed`. A photo marked `local_missing` is **skipped** and no longer touches `consecutiveFailures` or the 60 s backoff.
- `local_missing` copy: "Photo no longer on this iPhone or no longer shared with Beebeeb" (was "Photo removed from this iPhone before backup completed").

**UI**
- `photoAccessNotice()` in `src/lib/photo-permissions.ts` decides what to say for limited / revoked access.
- Backups & files: the camera-roll line reads "Paused · no photos shared with Beebeeb" or "Paused · no access to Photos" in place of a progress line that cannot move. A second line explains the cause and offers **Choose photos** / **Change** (the iOS limited-library picker) or **Open Settings**.
- The screen refreshes on photo-library changes (`MediaLibrary.addListener`), so a new selection shows straight away.
- `SettingsScreen` and `BackupInsightsScreen` import `expo-media-library/legacy`.

### Tests

- New `src/lib/limited-photo-access-backup.guard.test.ts`: pins the three engine rules against the Swift source.
- New `src/lib/media-library-legacy-import.guard.test.ts`: fails when a file calls a legacy-only media-library function through the main entry point. It was red on `SettingsScreen` and `BackupInsightsScreen` before the fix.
- `src/lib/photo-permissions.test.ts`: `photoAccessNotice` cases (full, limited with none / one / many, denied, unknown).
- Updated pinned shapes in `native-backup-manifest-wiring.test.ts` (task group type) and `native-backup-write-fence.test.ts` (rescan reason). What they guard is unchanged.

### Manual QA (simulator, iOS 26.3)

| Step | Result |
|---|---|
| Backup on, access narrowed to 0 selected mid-backup | Unshared rows deselected; drain idle; no 60 s backoff; line reads "Paused · no photos shared with Beebeeb" + **Choose photos** |
| **Choose photos** → select 2 → confirm | Engine rescans and uploads both straight away; no "missing" loop |
| Back on Backups & files | "3 of 3 items · 6 MB", green bar, "Only 3 selected photos are shared with Beebeeb. **Change**" |

### Not done

- No device run yet.
- iOS still shows its own "Select More Photos / Keep Current Selection" alert on every launch under limited access, because `PHPhotoLibraryPreventAutomaticLimitedAccessAlert` is not set. Candidate for a later section of this PR.

---

## 2. Files-app uploads: faster, and a dropped chunk no longer restarts the upload

### Problem

Copying a large file into the Beebeeb location in the iOS Files app uploaded at about 2.5–3 MB/s on a fast Mac link (a 500 MB video took ~3 minutes on the simulator, far longer on a phone). One failed chunk request failed the whole upload, and Files started it again from the first byte.

### Root causes

1. **The File Provider extension hardcoded 1 MiB chunks**, below the core ladder's own 4 MiB minimum. A 500 MB file took 478 PUTs, each paying a full request round trip.
2. **No retry per chunk.** `streamUpload` let any chunk error fail `createItem`. The app's own uploader (`NativeManualUploader`) retries each chunk up to 4 times.

### Changes (`targets/file-provider/FileProviderExtension.swift`)

- The chunk size comes from the core (`planChunks(…, profile: "mobile")`), capped at 4 MiB for the extension's ~50 MB memory budget, the same size the extension's download path already decrypts.
- `uploadChunkWithRetry`: a timeout, dropped connection, 429 or 5xx is retried with backoff (1, 2, 4 s), up to 4 attempts. Auth errors, account mismatch, other 4xx and cancellation fail at once.
- Chunks stay one at a time. With two PUTs in flight to the same upload session, the server left 2 of 77 requests unanswered until they timed out (61 s); one at a time ran 0 of 119. That looks like a server-side issue with concurrent chunk writes to one session and should be followed up there.

### Tests

- New `src/lib/file-provider-upload-throughput.guard.test.ts`: chunk size planned by the core and capped, no literal 1 MiB, one chunk at a time, every PUT through the retry wrapper with the right errors retryable. Red on the previous source (0/3), green now (3/3).
- `src/lib/file-provider-extension-behaviour.test.ts` (runs the shipped extension sources):
  - New `chunk-retry` scenario: a timed-out chunk is sent again without restarting the upload and the create completes; a 400 fails at once with one attempt. Red on the previous source (create failed `-2005`), green now.
  - The harness gains a `planChunks` stand-in that mirrors the core ladder (4 MiB floor, 32-chunk target, `mobile` cap 32 MiB).

### Manual QA (simulator, 500 MB H.264 video copied into the Beebeeb location)

| Variant | Chunks | Time | Speed | Unanswered requests |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Before: 1 MiB, one at a time | 478 | ~3 min | 2.5–3 MB/s | 0 |
| 4 MiB, two in flight (rejected) | 77 of 119 | did not finish | ~8 MB/s | 2 → upload failed and restarted |
| **After: 4 MiB, one at a time, retry** | **1

author: forrestlinfeng
body:
## Why

dsh (web profile, plugin 1.0.1) still injected nothing for a Xiaohongshu operations question after evomap-hub#4022/#4023 shipped. The Hub returned two on-topic genes judged against the task, and the plugin's local relevance gate dropped both:

| asset | words shared with the prompt | score | bar |
|---|---|---|---|

author: haowjy
body:
## Changelog

- Fixed: a deploy no longer interrupts scans uploading on Run on new scans; the page moves to the new app once they finish.

## Why

Since #373 an open tab reloads onto a new deploy when an API response no longer matches its schema. On Run on new scans that reload aborted any scan still uploading (and, before it, the browser's "Leave site?" prompt from the page's `beforeunload` guard would pop up on its own). A start pressed during uploads ("Start now and it begins once the upload finishes") was dropped too, or its `createStudy` cut off mid-request, so the person couldn't tell whether the study started. Deploys must never need a human click or lose work.

## Design decisions

1. **One hold API in `shell/deploys.ts`.** `holdLeave()` counts a hold and returns its release (idempotent); the deploy's reload, or the move Home after a write's mismatch, waits until the last hold is released and no pointer is held, then goes one task later. Work that a reload would lose takes a hold; the deploy code doesn't need to know what it is. Ruled out: the deploy code inspecting upload state (reaches into a feature), or a deadline (a 5 GB scan can take longer than any sensible deadline).
2. **Holds live in effects, so they can't leak.** `useUploads` takes its hold in the effect that already adds the `beforeunload` warning, keyed on "a scan is waiting, uploading or finishing": finishing, failing, removing the last scan and leaving the page all release it through the effect's cleanup. The page holds while a start is armed (effect on `armed`) and around `createStudy` (`try/finally` in the mutation).
3. **Under a hold, a write's mismatch fails; reads still hang.** Since #373 a call whose response mismatches never settles while the tab is about to leave, so no error flashes. Held work waits only on writes (`createUpload`, `completeUpload`, `createStudy`, all POSTs), and a hanging write would keep its hold forever, so under a hold a write throws its `ContractError`: the upload shows its error, ends, releases, and the tab leaves. Reads keep hanging: a failing `getMe` on refocus would otherwise put up the router's error screen and unmount the page, aborting the uploads. Ruled out: failing every call under a hold (the first version of this PR; review found the `getMe` path).
4. **A missing chunk waits for holds too.** Dropping a sample sheet loads `./xlsx` lazily; after a deploy that chunk can be gone. Under a hold the import fails as it would without the handler (the sheet can't be read) and the reload is queued behind the holds, instead of reloading through the uploads' "Leave site?" prompt.
5. **The feature imports `shell/deploys`.** `features/study` importing `../../shell/deploys` is a first: features don't import each other, and this is the shell's API, with no cycle (deploys imports only `@voluma/api-client`). Recorded in `decisions.md` as the one shell API features may import. Ruled out: putting the hold in `@voluma/api-client` (it isn't about the API); passing it through outlet context (more wiring for one function).

## Walkthrough

### A deploy waits for an upload

1. Setup: this branch, `OBJECT_STORE_DIRECTORY=<scratch dir> pnpm dev` (local store, no R2 writes), temporary edits reverted afterwards: let a guest upload (`inputs.ts` member check, `new-page.tsx` `canUpload`/`guest`), delay each storage PUT 15 s (`index.ts` storage mount) so the upload lasts, and rename `runs` to `items` in `GET /run/runs` to make the mismatch.
2. Open `/new`, intercept `/` to return `<script type="module" src="/assets/index-NEWDEPLOY.js">` (a new deploy), drop the real `OA6-1RK.zip` (452 MB).
3. While it uploads, switch away and back (refetches the runs list: mismatch).
4. Expect: main reloads at once and aborts the upload. This branch: the deploy is found (sessionStorage key set), the upload carries on, and the reload comes right after it completes.

![uploading, deploy found](https://github.com/voluma-bio/voluma/blob/3b2535f81e9102fbadd20b0af07ffe2dd23c3671/.github/pr-assets/jimyao/upload-hold/1-uploading-deploy-found.png?raw=true)

Recorded in the page (seconds): `77.9 Uploading`, `80.7 mismatch`, `94.1 Finishing the upload…`, `94.6 PAGEHIDE` (the reload). Both scans uploaded this way are `ready` in the database. With no upload, the same mismatch reloads at once.

The same with `GET /api/auth/me` mismatching instead (rename `kind`), triggered by refocus during the upload: `32.1 Uploading`, `34.0 mismatch`, `48.3 Finishing the upload`, `49.0 PAGEHIDE`. No error screen at any point; the upload completed first.

### A start waiting on uploads isn't dropped

1. Same setup; drop the scan, press Start run ("Waiting for uploads…"), trigger the mismatch.
2. Expect: the upload completes, `POST /api/run/studies` goes out and is answered, then the tab reloads. In this run it was answered 403, because the temporary guest-upload edit doesn't make a guest allowed to start on Voluma's keys; the order is what's checked here: the reload came after the answer.

Read in this order: `apps/web/src/shell/deploys.ts` (`holdLeave`, `busy`, `recheck`, `whenIdle`, `hang`), `apps/web/src/features/study/uploads.ts` (the `beforeunload` effect), `apps/web/src/features/study/new-page.tsx` (`start`, the armed hold).

## What changed

- **`shell/deploys.ts`** gains `holdLeave()` and module-level wait state (holds, held pointer, the pending leave) in place of `trackPointer().whenIdle`'s per-call listeners; `recheck` runs after pointer release, visibility change and every release.
- **`features/study/uploads.ts`**: the busy effect also holds.
- **`features/study/new-page.tsx`**: holds while armed and while `createStudy` runs.

## Risk and where to look

- Breaks or changes: a tab with uploads under way stays on the old app until they end; during that time mismatching reads hang (last good data stays) and mismatching writes show their errors. If the deploy changed the upload contract itself, `completeUpload` shows "Couldn't finish the upload" although the server completed it (the scan is listed after the reload), and an armed start is then disarmed and the tab goes Home: the start is dropped, visibly. A `createUpload` mismatch leaves an open upload until it expires. The released reload still drops the form's rows and study name (scans stay under "Or use a scan you uploaded before"). A forgotten release would keep a tab on the old app until it closes; every hold here is released by an effect cleanup or a `finally`. Undo: revert this PR.
- Where to look: `hang` and the `found` path in `followDeploys`; the `vite:preloadError` branch under a hold; the order in `new-page.tsx` where the armed effect fires `start.mutate()` and the uploads' hold is released in the same commit (the mutation's hold is taken in a microtask, before the release's `setTimeout` recheck).

## Knowledge layers, docs and deletions

- **Docs:** `apps/api/.context/deploy.md`: the reload waits for holds, a write's mismatch fails under one, a missing chunk waits too. `AGENTS.md` "Contract changes": "no work holds it (`holdLeave`)". `.context/decisions.md`: `holdLeave` is the one shell API features may import. `apps/web/src/features/study/.context/CONTEXT.md`: which page work holds.
- **Deleted:** `trackPointer`'s returned `whenIdle` and its per-wait document listeners, replaced by one module-level `recheck`.

## Contract changes

None. `packages/contracts` is untouched.

## Verification

- Ran: `pnpm check --skip-nx-cache` (passes, nothing cached). The browser runs in Walkthrough with the real OA6-1RK zip at 1440×900.
- Saw: upload then reload, in that order (14 s apart, the PUT delay); both uploads `ready`; a `getMe` mismatch during an upload: no error screen, reload after the upload; no-upload mismatch reloads at once; an armed start's `createStudy` answered before the reload. Not seen: a member's successful start followed by the reload (no member session locally), the missing-chunk path (needs a production build).
- Review: a fresh reviewe

author: zhanglue
body:
### Summary
Add a reusable HTTP layer with managed clients, application-owned responses and exceptions, shared configuration, and logging.
- Introduce AsyncHttpClientsManager to explicitly create, retrieve, and close named clients.
- Wrap HTTPX with AsyncHttpClient, exposing async GET, POST, and request methods.
- Return HttpResponse for 2xx responses and raise typed exceptions for HTTP status, timeout, connection, and transport failures.
- Add layered TOML/CLI configuration and a shared logger with stderr output, optional rotating files, and millisecond timestamps.
- Add DEBUG request diagnostics with bounded response previews and credential redaction.
- Define the shared daybreak Conda environment and document development commands.

### Validation
- All 36 automated tests pass in the daybreak environment.
- Live httpbin GET and POST requests returned 200 with the expected echoed data.
- A live 404 response raised HttpStatusError and produced the expected logs.
- Client shutdown and git diff --check pass.
Scope and limitations
Requests do not retry or follow redirects automatically. Responses are fully buffered. The Manager closes clients at application shutdown. DEBUG response previews may contain application data despite credential redaction.

Garmin access, authentication flows, and MCP integration are outside this PR.

author: pmnmalo
body:
Fixes #2226

**The defect.** The hold check of two flip-flops (`pads().hold`, `packages/silinx-fpga/src/fpga/timing.js`) used the inputs' hold time (−1.018 ns, `model.clock.hold`) and `minScale` for every flip-flop. Its slack came out 0.57–0.79 ns more optimistic than trce's, so a real hold violation was reported as met: trce gives −0.659 ns on blinky with 12 clock pins off the global lines, and Silinx said +0.143, met.

**The change.**
- **Earliest delays as trce's.** `model.clock.minLogic` = 0.80 of the model's logic delays, the same in every logic arc trce's hold paths show (clock-to-out, LUT, carry, block RAM clock-to-out). `minNet` = 0.784 of the wires', fitted on 4 410 connections with an rms error of 0.053 ns.
- **Each end's own hold margin.** It is the third element of a setup arc (`instArcs`, `timing-arcs.js`), trce's (−Th):
  - through the slice: `minLogic` × the way to X / Y, less `Tckdx` 0.047 ns;
  - BX: `Tckdi` 0.093 / 0.134 ns (SLICEL / SLICEM);
  - BY: `Tckdy` 0.135 / 0.152 ns;
  - CE: `Tckce` 0.069 ns;
  - SR: `Tcksr` 0.491 ns.
- **Clock skew.** The skew of #2224 stays counted.
- **Not given.** A model without `minNet` (the Spartan-6's) keeps the old formula. An end trce's reports did not show (an IOB's, a block RAM's, a multiplier's, a SLICEM memory's) has a margin of 0.
- **Fit script.** `research/s3e-route/ff-hold.mjs` reads trce's hold paths, the same `trce -v 2000 -fastpaths` reports of the nine routings of #2224, so no new ISE run was needed.

**Against trce** (worst hold path, same pair of flip-flops):

| routing | trce | before | now |
|---|---|---|---|
| blinky, 12 clock pins moved | −0.659 | +0.143 | −0.547 |
| blinky, 3 moved | −0.106 | +0.454 | +0.009 |
| blinky, nextpnr v0.6.0 | +0.032 | +0.732 | −0.014 |
| blinky, nextpnr v0.9.1 | +1.202 | +1.776 | +1.162 |
| blinky, Silinx | +0.984 | +1.772 | +0.937 |
| stopwatch, 12 moved | −0.580 | +0.150 | −0.455 |
| stopwatch, nextpnr v0.6.0 | −0.073 | +0.662 | −0.167 |
| stopwatch, nextpnr v0.9.1 | +0.927 | +1.762 | +0.915 |
| stopwatch, Silinx | +0.917 | +1.775 | +0.915 |

The new slacks are within −0.09 / +0.13 ns of trce's. Two borderline routings come out with the opposite verdict from trce's:
- blinky nextpnr v0.6.0: trce +0.032 (met), Silinx −0.014 (not met);
- blinky with 3 pins moved: trce −0.106 (not met), Silinx +0.009 (met).

The periods and the pads' paths are unchanged on all nine routings.

**Tests.**
- `test/fpga-ff-hold.test.js` fails on the old code. Its fixture is `blinky-hold-violation`, with trce's worst hold path; the #2224 fixture's JSON gets its hold path too. It checks trce's pair, the slack within 0.15 ns, and the exact NOT MET report line.
- Updated for the new arc element and hold formula: `fpga-timing`, `timing-parts`, and `fpga-clock-skew` (its hold line now reads −0.014 ns, NOT MET, against trce's +0.032).
- `node scripts/related-tests.mjs origin/main HEAD`: 460 of 462 passed. The `timing-parts` assertion has been fixed since, and that file passes alone. `third-party.test.js` fails because `npm ls` reports the `silinx-fpga` workspace link missing in this worktree's incomplete `node_modules`.

author: erikzet-oss
habibium
body:
Adds a config file for output defaults and SearXNG settings.

hodis reads `hodis/config.toml` in the user's config directory (`~/.config` on Linux and macOS, `%APPDATA%` on Windows), or the file `HODIS_CONFIG` names. Every key is optional:

```toml
format = "json"      # pretty | json | markdown | plain | urls
color = "never"      # auto | always | never
timeout = 10         # seconds per search request

[searxng]
url = "https://searx.example.org/"
embedded = true      # fall back to hodis's own SearXNG if url doesn't answer
```

- `--format` and `--color` override the file, and `hodis --help` ends with the config file's path
- A misspelled key gets a warning and is otherwise ignored; an invalid value stops hodis with the file, the line and the allowed values. A file named by `HODIS_CONFIG` must exist
- `url` must be http or https (a bare `localhost:8888` is rejected), and a missing trailing slash is added so endpoints land under it
- `embedded` stays on by default but turns off once `url` is set, so an instance that's down gives an error rather than a surprise local install
- `color` in the file overrides `NO_COLOR`, as no-color.org advises for config files; at the default `auto`, `NO_COLOR` still applies

Paths now come from etcetera instead of dirs. Linux and Windows paths don't change. On macOS the data directory moves from `~/Library/Application Support/hodis` to `~/.local/share/hodis`, so an embedded engine set up there before is installed again once.

## Testing

- `cargo test`: 82 passed, 2 ignored (66 before); every commit builds and passes on its own
- Config parsing is tested through the library, and the binary is run with `HODIS_CONFIG` for the help footer, a missing file and an invalid value, all of which exit before any search
- Checked live against a local SearXNG: defaults without a config file, `format` and a misspelled key from a config, `color = "always"` while piped, and a dead `url` failing at once without setting up the embedded engine


author: jerryfromkenya
body:
This PR picks the storage for the context space, specifies how its two memory agents work, and records that P0 has started.

**Storage (decision 1).** There is one `items` header carrying owner, audience, provenance, lifecycle and a context line, and each kind keeps its own detail table keyed by `item_id`.
- Today's `memory_fragments`, `sessions`/`session_messages`, `context_items` and `suggestion_queue` become those detail tables. P1 adds an `item_id` and a header row to each instead of moving the data.
- A guard test fails the build when a kind names no detail table or no lifecycle.

**Contextual extraction** (section 7.3, the Conversation agent):
- The extraction call sees who is speaking, the date, how the message came in, the conversation so far, and the items it already holds at the speaker's scope.
- It writes one context line for each fact (who, when, what "it" refers to). That line is embedded and keyword-indexed with the fact, and it costs no extra call.
- The write gate stays in code: `fact_defect`, the subject gate and banding by vector. The owner comes from the principal, never from the model's output.

**Adversarial consolidation** (section 7.3, the Consolidation agent):
- The existing Proposer, Adversary and Judge (`three_stage_consolidator.rs`) become the default; today they are off.
- The Adversary adds three challenges:
  - *unsupported*: the result says more than its sources do;
  - *scope*: a private fact would widen to the household, or two members' facts would merge;
  - *planted*: a fact rests only on untrusted content that instructs the assistant or makes claims about a member.
- `apply_actions` refuses any widening of scope and keeps every source's evidence.
- A fact whose only evidence is untrusted is labelled, and Profile and Proposal wait until a consolidation run has passed it.

**P3 gate.** P3's gate gains two tests:
- contextualised recall beats plain recall on the reachability fixture, on the Orin;
- a planted set leaves no unflagged fact that a turn or an agent would act on.

**Elsewhere.** The PAI checklist gets a dated note, the docs index row is updated, and decision 10 asks for adversarial consolidation to be the default once P3 shows it fits the Orin's quiet hours.

The change is docs only. `every_pai_row_states_its_verification` reads only the checklist's requirement rows, and this PR touches none.

author: zbennour
body:
## Summary
Implements AUDIT.md §4.8 item 4: the 0D tier replaces the lumped thermal update with a real-gas control-volume energy balance. Bumps the version to **1.4.0**, because default 0D thermal results change.

$m u - m_{old} u_{old} = \Delta m^+ \bar h_{in} + \Delta m^- \bar h + \Delta t\, m c_v (T_{rock} - T)/\tau$

- Injected gas enters at the new `injection_temperature` (default: reservoir T). Produced gas leaves at the in-place state, and flow enthalpies are trapezoidal.
- Wall heat transfer is implicit and uses the existing relaxation time τ.
- New `enthalpy_molar` / `internal_energy_molar` (Peng-Robinson departure + closed-form Shomate). For pure H2 they are consistent with the JT coefficient. ΔH/ΔU match CoolProp within ~5 J/mol with Peneloux.
- `thermal_model="lumped"` keeps the old behaviour; sorbent stores use it automatically.

### Validation (adiabatic 70 000 m³ cavern, CoolProp energy-balance reference)
| Case | CoolProp | energy balance | old lumped |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Fill 40→120 bar, H2 in at 293 K | +70.8 K | +70.5 K | +110.1 K |
| Discharge 120→40 bar (6 h steps) | −81.2 K | −79.4 K | −80.5 K |

The old model treated filling as isentropic compression of the whole inventory and overstated heating by 55 %.

### Also
- The 0D Newton solver now bisects when it stalls at the saturated-rate kink. A step starting exactly at the BHP target previously exhausted its iterations.
- Canonical scenarios:
  - Teesside working gas is unchanged; its peak temperature falls from 99 °C to 74 °C.
  - Porous working gas is 1.2–1.3 % lower.
  - Run time is 3–5× the lumped model (Teesside 0.6 s → 2.9 s), after closed-form ideal enthalpy and warm starts.

## Test plan
- [x] `pytest`: 67 passed (+ enthalpy/energy vs CoolProp, cavern fill/discharge, sorbent fallback)
- [x] `ruff check` / `ruff format --check` clean
- [ ] CI

## AA4-BBOINV — independent inverse proof of B/B-overlap six-source-ID path multiplicity

Scientific Draft stacked on [#676](https://github.com/definitely-stable/Mathlab/pull/676), frozen base `613d5f8bbdd3e99b6086bf4c9f1fe32ab8f9295d`. No changes to parent scientific PRs, main or root state.

### New rigorous all-h ORIGINAL sixset -> physical path inverse theorem

Fix EVERY dyadic s=2^h on the genuine original W(3,s), and EVERY complete separately globally injected arbitrarily correlated f,g. Start with one EXACT historical accepted GF5 **B/B-overlap sixset Q of six different ORIGINAL incidence IDs** (not a synthetic projection), *without enumerating physical paths*.

**Canonical inverse from original source IDs**:
1. B/B original factor multiplicity uniquely determines repeated ORIGINAL point p and repeated ORIGINAL line ell; the B/B-overlap ORIGINAL incidence (p,ell) occurs ONCE. Therefore the three original source anchor flag IDs `(q,ell),(p,ell),(p,r)` and the three complementary original path flag IDs are uniquely determined by Q, independent of any physical 3-walk enumeration. GQ no-4-cycle forces q,r nonincident and the original forward projection anchor is uniquely this triple.
2. On the LEFT side, the four non-repeated original point pair labels form a *simple physical C4*, vertex-disjoint from f(p). Removing the f(q) edge yields a unique physical 3-edge P4 chain labeled by the THREE actual remaining ORIGINAL flag IDs, with precisely two reversals. On the RIGHT side, do the same with four non-repeated source line pair labels and delete g(r); another uniquely original-ID-labeled P4 results, with precisely two reversals.
3. A physical grid 3-path exists iff LEFT and RIGHT P4 edge sequences have the SAME THREE ORIGINAL source flag IDs in the same order (up to reversing the paths). Therefore EXACTLY ZERO or TWO DIRECTED paths correspond to any such accepted source sixset. The two survivors are exact reversals; they use two diagonals of the SAME true ORIGINAL source flag support and are physical-coordinate-proper on both sides. Their two physical endpoints decode the exact unique original nonincident (q,r) projection.
4. For ANY ORIGINAL core I and deleted original flag set Z, both paths survive precisely when all THREE non-anchor original IDs belong to I, NO flag of Q's SIX original IDs belongs to Z, and the two source-ID order chains align. Anchor IDs may be OUTSIDE I; six-ID verification is never reduced to only three path IDs.

**Thus** the forward #672/#673 original valid path->original accepted B/B-overlap sixset map has exact TWO preimages **onto its image**. It is intentionally NOT claimed surjective onto all historically accepted B/B-overlap sixsets: some may have incompatible source-ID orders and yield ZERO paths. This independently certifies the critical original-sixset normalization factor 1/2 used for Branch A, without reusing its physical walk count or original source projection enumerator.

### Proof and independent source-native falsifiers

[Detailed independent all-h inverse proof](docs/research/HYP-105-BBO-INVERSE-ORIGINAL-SOURCE-BRIDGE.md); `research/hyp105_BBo_inverse_source_bridge.py` (build inverse only from source ORIGINAL sixset and the two physical labels); `research/test_hyp105_BBo_inverse_source_bridge.py` (full historical W32 BBo source census by existing GF5 classifier for **five legal globally reassigned right g maps**, independent inverse-vs-forward original sixset image EQUALITY, verify every inverse edge's original provenance; W32 sparse original cores and original flag deletion; true W34 sparse cores including projection anchor flags OUTSIDE the retained core and actual deleted flags, B/B-disjoint counterexamples, invalid source ID rejection); hosted independent fail-closed workflow `.github/workflows/hyp105-bbo-inverse-source-bridge.yml`.

**Scientific STOP:** this is a genuinely all-h *local inverse multiplicity theorem*, but not a new proof of global all-map Branch A or total R3. External mathematical referee for #672/#673/#674 and mixed full/core remains mandatory; root #230 OPEN_WITH_FORMAL_BLOCKER. All code/tests on a separate stacked Draft, no merge.

### Independent negative/non-surjectivity discovery and final exact-head verification

An originally written negative-control test improperly selected the *first* historical original B/B-overlap sixset and expected exactly two physical paths. The independent inverse found that this particular genuine historically accepted source sixset has **ZERO** compatible left/right three-original-ID orders. That is **not** a contradiction of the theorem; it establishes why this theorem states **ZERO OR TWO** and why the forward construction is NOT surjective onto the whole historical positive B/B-overlap class.

The revised test requires distinct genuine ORIGINAL historical source witnesses of BOTH kinds:
- \`BBo inverse = ZERO\` (still accepted by the exact historical GF5 class classifier; no aligned physical source-backed grid P4);
- \`BBo inverse = TWO\` (a pair of exact reversed physical paths, whose three provenance IDs match both physical coordinate chains).
It additionally checks actual B/B-DISJOINT original source sextuples are correctly excluded, and rejects malformed original IDs. The full five-map W32 historical census is exactly equal as a SET to the independently forward-produced physical-path image, with every source sextuple counted precisely twice; sparse true W32/W34 cores and original Z flags maintain this property, including projection anchor flags **outside** the retained core. This is stronger than re-running the same forward physical 3-walk count.

**Final exact source/test HEAD** \`a2b982b003c9349ea172216ecf799ec037a38c2b\`. Dedicated [CI #41193038777](https://github.com/definitely-stable/Mathlab/actions/runs/41193038777) **SUCCESS**, INDEX [#41193038775](https://github.com/definitely-stable/Mathlab/actions/runs/41193038775) **SUCCESS**, Research [#41193038860](https://github.com/definitely-stable/Mathlab/actions/runs/41193038860) running at this update. author: dale1996-code
body:
## Summary

Column-aware verification of Ask claims (F4): a figure in a table that prints its column header once must now name the column its cell sits under, checked against the cell's position in the cited chunk's row. **Draft. Three independent reviews are done; merge needs the owner's explicit approval.**

**What the record says about its own history:** two reviews found real problems in earlier commits (the first commit newly accepted incorrect claims; the second contained a rule that rejected a legitimate torque specification). Both are fixed. Numbers below are for the final tree (head `70a835c`).

## The problem, as it turned out to be

PR #169 left one limit open: Front/Rear-style tables could not have a figure verified (chunk #236, document 109, page 2). The verifier had **no column concept at all**, and Experiment L's recorded diagnosis was partly wrong:

- With the header and the whole row in the quote, the right claim **and the wrong-column claim** were both accepted ("the rear height is 310 mm" against a cell under Front), as was a swapped two-figure claim. Same on a real accelerator-pedal data list.
- A claim naming no column was accepted when the quote left the header out, including a label-less quote of cells starting at a later cell or at a first cell two rows share.
- The only right claim rejected was on a quote cut after the first cell, for an unrelated reason (the chunk's own full row became a "sibling", and its label sentence runs back through unrelated words).

## What changed

`columnHeaderRun`, `quoteRowCells` (exported for tests), `columnReading` and `possibleColumnRow` read a column by position from the cited **chunk's** row: a clean header and one cell per column. Each figure is placed under its cell's column; the claim must name that column and the quote must print the word. `row_mismatch` details, no new reason or client string: `wrong_column`, `column_unstated`, `column_unresolved` (figures under different columns). A quote tied to no single chunk row that prints a clean column row's cells is `possible`: no column is attributed, but a claim naming none is `column_unstated`. A row whose cell count does not match its header is **not read**.

**The change can only add rejections.** It deletes five lines from the verifier and adds early `return` branches at the top of `judgeFigureRow`; the body after them is byte-identical to `origin/main`. Everything the final verifier accepts, the old one accepted too, for any input (confirmed independently in reviews 2 and 3).

## F2 scope: what was approved and what shipped

The label-less-quote rule (F2) was **authorized in-session, but the shipped rule is broader than the wording the owner was shown, and the widening was not separately approved.**

- *Chronology.* After review 1 the owner chose "Fix the docs, defer behavior" for F2 and also instructed that F2 be investigated separately and any tradeoff explained rather than silently weakened. I investigated, stopped, and asked again with a measured prototype footprint (rule: a quote's values at a **cell boundary** inside a clean column row and the claim names no column; 33 claims newly rejected in the two real column tables, 12 in the vehicle-height table's later rows, 0 in unrelated tables). The owner then chose "Implement it". So the earlier "defer" was superseded by that second answer.
- *What went beyond that wording.* The shipped rule uses token-bounded **containment**, not a cell-boundary start, and applies to any quote tied to no single row, labelled or not. So (1) a quote that starts **inside a cell** (at the alternate unit) is also caught: **120 claims in 27 chunks / 13 docs plus 36 claims in 6 chunks / 4 docs**, the same two tables, none in unrelated tables, none newly accepted; and (2) a labelled row the chunk prints twice is caught (0 corpus instances; one invented false reject). The 33 + 12 + 0 figure covers only boundary-aligned quotes. I reported the footprint as unchanged without flagging these differences; that was an omission.
- *Decision for the owner.* Keep as shipped, or narrow the rule back to the cell-boundary wording. Narrowing is a small code change plus re-validation.

## Correct claims this change can now reject (introduced; the safe direction)

These are correct, well-qualified claims the old verifier accepted. They lose an answer; none lets a wrong figure through. "0 correct claims newly rejected" in the fuzz holds **only inside the fuzz's own claim vocabulary**.

- **A column word anywhere in the figure's clause counts as naming that column, negated or not.** With 0.6 to 1.2 V under "Fully Released" (invented table), "The sensor alpha voltage with the pedal **not depressed** is 0.6 to 1.2 V" gets `wrong_column`; so does "…and it rises as the pedal is depressed". The same shape was reproduced on the real accelerator-pedal data list (chunk #6218). A claim naming only the figure's own column is accepted. **Not pinned by a test.**
- A claim naming no column against any quote that lands inside a column row, including a later cell, the inside of a cell, and a first cell two rows share (the F2 rule above; the intended no-column rule).
- A labelled row printed twice beside a column table, when the claim names no column (invented; 0 corpus instances; not pinned).
- An alternate unit printed without parentheses is counted as a second cell, so a correct claim for the first column gets `wrong_column` (invented; not pinned).
- A part name holding both words of a group ("Rear … x Front …"), when the row prints as many numbers as columns (pinned `F4-L3`; 0 corpus instances).

Not an introduced loss: a cut quote of the vehicle-height row, whose label carries an unrelated condition word, is rejected by the old verifier too (`F4-C1`).

## What the earlier commits got wrong

1. **First commit** let a cut quote's own full row stop counting as a sibling; that row was also the only thing that saw a condition the quote left out ("Minimum", "Reused", "without", a trailing "or less"). Review 1 found it; five invented rows (`F4-S1`..`S5`) were written red first. A narrowed version still leaked (72 of 120,744 fuzz cases), so the exclusion was removed. **Cost:** a cut quote on a label with an unrelated condition word is rejected again, which includes the real vehicle-height table.
2. **Second commit** rejected any claim naming a column of a header whose cells did not line up. Review 2 showed it newly rejected the correct 2ZR-FE engine-mount insulator torque (real chunk #18768: a part name "Rear … x Front …" read as a header, then three bare numbers). My "0 claims on this corpus" had skipped bare-number rows. Full population of header rows with two or more cells: 27 aligned unit-bearing rows (two real tables), 3 aligned wiring rows, 3 unaligned rows (**1 legitimate torque row**). One spec lost, none protected, so it was removed.

## Testing (free; no paid call of any kind)

| | Final tree |
|---|---|
| Oracle | 60 `F4` rows: 23 fix a verdict, 32 controls, 5 pinned limits (`todo`); table 114 → 174. Written first, run red each time. On the `origin/main` verifier **21 rows fail** (18 fix rows, 3 controls). 34 tests in `columnAwareClaims.test.js`. No pre-existing test or oracle row removed or edited |
| Mutation checks | **28 mutants, 28 killed, 0 survivors** (re-run independently in review 3). Review 3's own extra mutants left 3 surviving: `endsWith` → `includes` in the row match, an equivalent filter, and the overlap merge in cell grouping (fewer readings only) |
| Fuzz, **402,384** invented cases | **0 incorrect claims newly accepted** (also guaranteed by the diff argument); 0 correct claims newly rejected **within the fuzz vocabulary only**; 8,824 incorrect claims newly rejected. The first commit newly accepted **4,754** |
| `eval:replay`, 8 files | **8 of 8 byte-identical** to `origin/main` |
| Corpus differential | **0 claims newly accepted anywhere.** 27 unit-bearing column rows: 105 wrong-column and 54 no-column synthetic claims

author: 3ru
body:
The rule can warn about APIs a program doesn't use. For example, an ordinary `request.caller` property is treated as a Function API, and a custom `getContext()` method can be treated as a canvas option. A typed `Range` can also inherit the newer Baseline date of `AbstractRange` despite having its own older compatibility entry.

Resolve the API receiver and its closest compatibility entry before applying the configured target. This removes those false warnings and keeps real Function, canvas, and WebGL uses tied to their own feature IDs.

| Case | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `request.caller` or `request.arguments` on an ordinary object | Warns about Function APIs | No warning. Proven function receivers still report |
| Typed `Range.collapsed` and `StaticRange.collapsed` at a Baseline 2020 target | Warns with the newer `AbstractRange` status from 2021 | Uses the exact Range 2015 and StaticRange 2020 entries. No warning at this target |
| Custom `getContext(...)`, `getExtension(...)`, or `getSupportedExtensions().includes(...)` calls | Can trigger Canvas or WebGL warnings from matching names and arguments | No warning for custom receivers |
| Canvas context options and WebGL extension arguments without type information | Guesses API identity from names and arguments | Skips these checks without types. Existing native patterns remain covered with type information |

Canvas and WebGL argument checks now require type information. In safe mode, unproven member calls stay silent. Enable the type-aware preset and TypeScript parser services to check these options. Function checks use a bounded scope check and skip aliases or values whose identity is unknown.

body:
## Intent

[Image: the captain's Codex test] Bilibi asked to approve the company/customer plan first, then said "I can't include Kam Pui Yue's affiliation or the office address yet: those steps need the new company's ID, which is assigned only after the company/customer plan commits", and asked for a second approval for the contact and address plan.

drain the PRs and issues faster; use your judgment when the change is low risk but benefits are significant.

Context: Bilibi's plan engine (apps/base/agent_api, src/plans.rs) accepts 1-20 ordered operations per plan, but a later operation cannot refer to a record an earlier operation in the same plan will create, so the person must approve several times for one real-world task (create a company, then its contact person and their affiliation, then its address).

## What Changed

- Adds one-based same-plan references from later inputs to records created by earlier steps, resolving real IDs during the atomic commit.
- Enables linked Company, Person, Affiliation, relationship, and Address operations while retaining owner validation and authorization checks.
- Extends the editable review card and agent guidance to edit, preview, and approve mixed dependent steps as one plan.

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: The change is bounded by prior-step owner declarations, fail-closed dependent previews, concrete-input revalidation, and atomic owner commits; the fix-round secret scrub is minimal and complete.

## Testing

Targeted live validation used a fresh PostgreSQL 18 database, exact-origin Bilibi Dev server, browser sign-in/OAuth, the shipped MCP review card, adversarial MCP calls, screenshots, and persisted database/audit readback. All scenarios passed. Repository-wide tests, lint, formatting, and static analysis were intentionally not run in this assigned Test phase.

body:
Cele sase bifatoare ale motorului (Style Raw, Seamless Tile, Refiner, Hires Fix, Face Restoration) primeau **doua etichete**: una generata automat deasupra (`label for=id`) si una lipita de bifa, care este si suprafata pe care se apasa.

## Ce era gresit, masurat la 320px

- **Numele accesibil iesea dublu**: `['Style Mode', 'Style Raw (photographic)']`. Un cititor de ecran citea „Style Mode, Style Raw (photographic), bifa, nebifata”.
- Captura de deasupra ramanea o **tinta separata de 34px**, sub pragul de 44px, care ducea la acelasi loc: o a doua tinta mica pentru un control care avea deja una de 50px.

## Reparat

La bifatoare, captura este acum un `<span class="setting-caption">` (stil identic cu `label`, dar nu se apasa); eticheta ramane doar cea lipita de bifa. La celelalte tipuri de campuri ramane `<label for>`, ca inainte.

## Verificat la 320 si 390px

author: oorabona
body:
The 0.15.1 Store submission passed certification, then sat in Partner Center as "ready to publish" until someone clicked **Publish now**. `msstore publish --noCommit` builds each draft by copying the previous submission, publish mode included. The product was switched to manual publication for 0.14.3, so every submission the `store` job has made since inherits manual mode. Decision: from now on, a submission goes live as soon as it is certified.

## Change

- `scripts/store-listing.ts`: new `publishOnceCertified(submission)`. It sets `targetPublishMode` to `Immediate`. `main` runs it on the submission after `applyListings`, so the `updated.json` the workflow sends with `msstore submission update` carries it. It finds the key with `keyOf` whatever its case. When the payload has no such key, it adds `targetPublishMode` in the API's casing instead of failing. `targetPublishDate` is not changed: the API reads it only for `SpecificDate`.
- `.github/workflows/release.yml` (`store` job, step "Submit to the Store"): a comment explaining the mode, and the step summary now says the release goes live once certified. No command changes.
- `packages/clients/desktop/msix/README.md` ("Releasing to the Microsoft Store"): describes the publish mode. A draft left waiting for its What's new (exit code 3) is never updated, so it keeps the previous submission's mode. The README now says to check that mode before submitting such a draft by hand.

No Store news fragment: nothing changes in the app.

## Field name and casing

- Microsoft Learn, [Manage app submissions › App submission resource](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/uwp/monetize/manage-app-submissions#app-submission-resource) (updated 2026-03-10): `targetPublishMode` is a string, one of `Immediate`, `Manual` or `SpecificDate`. `targetPublishDate` applies "if the *targetPublishMode* is set to SpecificDate".
- MSStoreCLI v0.4.3, the version the job pins: `DevCenterSubmission` has `string? TargetPublishMode`. `submission get` prints with an upper-case naming policy, so the key it prints is `TargetPublishMode`. `submission update` reads the payload with `PropertyNameCaseInsensitive = true`, so either casing reaches the API and the value goes through as a string.

## Tests

- `scripts/store-listing.spec.ts`: 4 new cases, 28 pass in total.
  - A `Manual` mode (in the CLI's PascalCase) becomes `Immediate`. No second key in another case is added, the date and the other fields are kept, and the input object is not modified.
  - A `SpecificDate` mode becomes `Immediate`, and its date is left as it was.
  - A payload with no mode gets `targetPublishMode: "Immediate"`.
  - `main` with a submission file: the output carries both the What's new and `Immediate`.
- `pnpm lint` and `pnpm typecheck` pass. `node scripts/store-listing.ts 0.15.2 <sample submission>`, run with plain Node type stripping as the workflow runs it, prints `"TargetPublishMode": "Immediate"`.
