author: notonlywhite
body:
Stacked on #5 (`claude/m1-08-fabric-half`). Retarget it before #5 merges.

## What

**The generated CI now runs the end-to-end tests.**
- `ci.yml` gains an `e2e` job when a pack fills the new slot `ci.e2e-steps`. Without one, there is no job.
- The react pack fills it with `.github/scripts/e2e.sh`. The script:
  1. starts the AppHost the way a developer does;
  2. waits for the web app;
  3. runs Playwright;
  4. stops everything again.
- The sign-in test now runs this script instead of its own AppHost harness, so the test exercises the CI step itself.

**Profile CI in this repo.**
- `build/profile-ci.sh <profile>` generates the profile with the CLI from the real packs, no stand-ins, and adds a module.
- It then runs the generated project's CI steps:
  - backend build and every test project;
  - `pnpm install`, `build`, `lint` and `test`;
  - the end-to-end tests.
- It runs in its own job, `profile-saas-standard-react`, in parallel with `build`.

### What Aspire 13.6 does when it stops

Making `e2e.sh` stop cleanly meant finding out how Aspire 13.6 behaves:

- `dotnet run` hands the AppHost to Aspire's CLI. The CLI starts the **Debug** build whatever `-c` says, so `-c Release --no-build` fails with "No such file or directory" when only Release was built. It also does not pass Ctrl+C on.
- When the AppHost is signalled through the CLI, its shutdown is cut short. The orchestrator (DCP) then outlives it and restarts the host and the Vite server.
- So the script signals the AppHost process itself and waits until the containers it started have been removed. It then stops DCP and anything still running from the project.
  - Two script runs in a row each took about 50 s.
  - Afterwards there were no DCP processes, no containers and no project processes left.

## Tests observed failing

The new structural test, before the job existed:

```
failed Fabric.Packs.Tests.FrontendTests.The_generated_ci_runs_the_end_to_end_tests_against_the_running_application
  Shouldly.ShouldAssertException : ci
      should contain (case insensitive comparison)
  "
  "
```

The sign-in test, before the script existed:

```
failed Fabric.Packs.Tests.SignInTests.A_user_signs_in_through_keycloak_and_sees_a_modules_data (1m 19s 283ms)
  Shouldly.ShouldAssertException : e2eExitCode
      should be
      bash: .github/scripts/e2e.sh: No such file or directory
```

## Verification

Local runs:

- Core: 186 passed.
- CLI: 19 passed.
- Packs: 38 passed, including the Docker, Aspire and Playwright tests.
- `build/profiles.sh`: green.
- `build/profile-ci.sh saas-standard-react`: green. Architecture 13, integration 7, Billing module 1, web 3, Playwright 1 passed.

The new CI job has not yet run on GitHub; this PR is its first run.

body:
## Summary

Extend the existing "Remember aspect ratio" preference to include regular video zoom, supporting both shared settings and independent per-video settings.

When enabled:
- Apply the default aspect ratio across all videos.
- Apply the default custom aspect ratio when configured.
- Remember regular zoom adjustments and reuse the last saved zoom across videos.

When disabled:
- Restore each video's previously saved aspect ratio.
- Restore its custom aspect ratio, when configured.
- Restore its individual zoom level.

Previously saved per-video visual settings are preserved while shared mode is enabled, so switching the preference off restores those settings instead of losing them.

## Changes

### `PlayerActivity.kt`
- Removed the separate late default-zoom application after track selection.
- Aspect ratio and regular zoom are now restored together through the playback-state restoration flow.
- Prevents the late zoom application from overriding the values already restored for the current video.

### `PlayerViewModel.kt`
- Updated `resetVisualPreferences()` to prepare pan and advanced zoom settings without prematurely overriding regular zoom restoration.
- Added `restoreAspectAndZoom()` to apply the selected aspect ratio, custom aspect ratio, and regular zoom together.
- Updated `reapplyCurrentVisualPreferences()` to reapply regular zoom alongside the aspect ratio.
- Extended `setVideoZoom()` with an optional persistence flag.
- Regular zoom adjustments now update the shared default zoom when "Remember aspect ratio" is enabled.
- Restoration can update MPV and UI state without accidentally overwriting shared preferences.

### `PlayerPlaybackStateController.kt`
- Added shared-mode tracking for visual preferences.
- Added centralized aspect ratio and zoom restoration through `restoreVideoAspectAndZoom()`.
- Shared mode restores the global aspect ratio, custom ratio, and default zoom.
- Per-video mode restores the corresponding values from the saved playback state.
- Moved visual restoration ahead of the existing track-restoration process to avoid delaying aspect ratio and zoom application.
- Preserves previously stored per-video aspect ratio, custom ratio, and zoom while shared mode is active.
- Avoids overwriting saved visual settings when playback state has not finished loading.

## Testing

- Build successful.
- Tested shared aspect ratio and zoom across different videos.
- Tested independent per-video aspect ratio and zoom restoration.
- Verified that previously saved per-video settings are retained when shared mode is enabled and restored after disabling it.
- Playback and visual restoration worked as expected.

3.21.3 release run 41189667887 attempt 2 uploaded and verified the four immutable bottles. ARM verification passed, while both Intel legs failed trying to reinstall a candidate bottle into the old 3.21.2 keg.

The helper action puts `.release-venv/bin` first on PATH. Its `gh-address-cr` is 3.21.3, so the unqualified baseline probe reported the helper's version instead of the installed 3.21.2 Homebrew CLI. _Requested by **Dimitar** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01R2NUAYajJj9sUdYxmEReBu?thread=cmsg_01R2NUAYajJj9sUdYxmEReBu6JBFv1KkeuN3EPYPvr9VKm)_

Closes #2161. Dimitar picked "COW per mono clone".

## Changes

- **`hir/cow.rs` `cow_ty`:** after the checker's substitution, a type parameter counts as a copy-on-write type. Generic bodies now get the same share / unique ops as the same code over a concrete type.
  - Before, `Cell<T>::get()` never shared its result. A write through it changed the stored object, and a counter closure over `Cell<Box>` returned 1, 2, 2, 2.
- **Per-type clones** run on the clone's ground types:
  - At a class or array type (`Cell::get$inst$Box`), the clone keeps the ops.
  - At `int`, MIR passes the word through with no op. `Cell::get$inst$int` has no `Cow`, so a scalar is never read as a pointer.
  - A two-word value (a pair type) passes through as it is.
- **Shared generic bodies** (`mir/from_hir.rs`): a type parameter's word is opaque there, so `Cow` on it passes through. It is also not a "type variable read" refusal. This is written up in `docs/internals/limitations.md`.
- **Warnings:** E0141 / E0142 are not given on a bare type parameter. Otherwise every program would get warnings from `core` (`Option::map` and similar).
- **Two tests changed to value semantics.** Both wrote through a generic alias, which now behaves like the concrete code:
  - `tests/data/generic_class_cell.hy`: `outer.get().set(6)` now changes a temporary copy, as `.get().set()` on a concrete class already did.
  - `tests/generics/generic_rest_readonly_vec_spread.hy`: `all` uses `for mut r in rest`.

  I checked the concrete equivalents: a plain `for r in rest { r.reset() }` and `o.get().set(6)` drop the write, and `for mut` keeps it.
- New test: `tests/memory/cow_generic_bodies.hy`. It covers a getter, a setter, a free generic, the call through a shared body, the counter closure, and an `int` cell. 4 of its 6 cases failed on main.

> 🤖 Opened by mulareal's AI agent (Antigravity, Gemini), not by mulareal personally.

## What
- Entity shadows are no longer visible from below when looking upward through terrain in Spectator Mode.

## Why
- `RenderPipelines.ENTITY_SHADOW` and `RenderPipelines.OIT_ENTITY_SHADOW` inherit `RenderPipeline.Builder.build`'s default `cull = true` in vanilla, culling the underside of the upward-facing (`+Y`) shadow quads emitted by `ShadowFeatureRenderer.prepare`.

author: maxkongerskov
body: ## Root cause The File menu, title-bar Export button, and export sheet already treated an audio clip as enough to enable Export (`hasVideo || hasMusic`). The encode still failed for a playlist with no picture. `rebuildComposition` always added a video track (persistent id 1) even when every clip was audio. That empty track makes `AVPlayerItem` fail to open, so `player.currentItem` stays nil. `beginExport` returned immediately in that case, before the save panel, which is why Export looked dead. A video container (MP4/MOV/M4V, GIF, X-Loop) then went through the video writer, which requires a real picture track and failed instead of mixing the audio. ## Fix - Export stays enabled for any timeline that has picture or sound, including audio-only. The menu, title-bar button, and sheet share `canExport`. - The composition gets a video track only when a picture sample is actually inserted. Audio-only timelines are audio assets. - If the chosen mode needs video and the timeline has none, the export becomes an audio mixdown (WAV by default) and the file extension follows. A project that has video still exports video. - If the composition never becomes playable, export reports an error instead of returning quietly. ## Tests `AudioExportTests` covers: - audio-only timelines enable Export and rewrite a video/MP4 choice to WAV - an audio-only playlist rebuilds with audio tracks and no video track, and the mixdown is a playable WAV - a video container on an audio-only timeline writes that WAV rather than an MP4 - a mixed timeline still keeps its video track and video export settings This environment is Linux and has no Swift toolchain. The package imports AppKit, SwiftUI, and AVFoundation, so it could not be built or tested here.

Commands now report success only after the targeted AC relays confirm their requested state. The web dashboard retains real-strip control and existing measurements while adding a neutral light/dark interface and persistent per-outlet consumption history.

## Changes

- Harden device sessions and HTTP command validation, handle offline devices and command deadlines, and show pending, confirmed, and failed states in web and Android clients.
- Redesign the responsive web dashboard with individual outlet switches, explicit All on / All off actions, live summaries, preserved keyboard focus, and documented UI guidelines enforced by automated checks. History selects explain bucket granularity, strip identity, and outlet scope, with progressive desktop enhancement and native touch pickers.
- Record AC outlet readings in SQLite every 30 seconds by default. Add filtered history summaries, UTC buckets, recorder health, and CSV export for later analytics. Baselines, counter resets, gaps, and intervals crossing bucket boundaries are handled explicitly.
- Identify both USB charging ports on the verified stock firmware and explain that USB switching and separate consumption readings are not verified. Totals and history remain explicitly AC-only; unknown USB readings are not presented as zero.
- Add Python, web interaction/design, and Android CI checks; update English/Arabic documentation and Android connection/error handling and backup settings.

author: jamessnaps
body:
**Stacked: merge #37, then #38, then this.** This PR's own commit is the last one.

## What

The game now has real sound to match the visuals: 26 sounds and music tracks made once with ElevenLabs and bundled with the game (about 4 MB).

- **Moments:**
  - touchdowns for jets, props and helicopters, at the moment the wheels touch
  - chimes for shift start, cleared and failed
  - a collision, a divert, and a radio call when a route locks onto a runway
  - a wind gust for wind shifts
- **Flap board:** real clacks, one per tile step with varied pitch, and a rattle when the board opens.
- **Backgrounds:** one 20-second loop per landscape (meadow, coast, desert, snow, night).
- **Engines:** a loop per aircraft family that gets louder with more aircraft in the air and pans to where they are.
- **Music:** 1960s jet-age lounge jazz. A board theme, then a calm and a busy track on shift. It turns busy when the sky is 70% full or two aircraft are in conflict, and calms down again after 10 quiet seconds.
- **Music toggle** on the board beside Sound.

## How

- `tools/final_approach_sounds.py` holds every sound's prompt and remakes any of them by name. The key is in `~/.config/elevenlabs/env` on the dev VM: restricted to sound effects and music, with a credit cap, and never in the repo. The game never calls ElevenLabs; it only plays the bundled files.
- `game.py` lists the files present, and the page gets their cache-busted URLs. Anything missing or still loading falls back to the old synth. Effects preload on the first tap; backgrounds, engines and music load when first needed.
- Loops cross-fade each repeat, because MP3's padding would click if the buffer looped directly.
- `tools/` is kept out of the server image.

## Checks

- `pytest tests -q`: 748 passed. New tests check that the files and the generator's list match, that the page lists every sound, and that the total stays under 6 MB.
- Headless Chromium against a local hub:
  - all 26 files decode at their intended lengths
  - in play, the background, the engine loop for the aircraft in the air, and the calm music start
  - a staged conflict switches the music to busy, and it holds there after the conflict clears
  - the Music toggle works and is saved
  - the route handles still work
  - no console errors
- **Nobody has listened to it yet.** The sounds were judged only on decoding and length, so any that don't land need re-prompting.

## Licence

The playbook records an open question: which ElevenLabs plan the sounds were made on. On the free plan the terms don't allow commercial use and ask for attribution, and this repo is public.

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Client-side Final Approach assets and simulation only; no auth, records, or shared server game state changes beyond listing static audio files.
> 
> **Overview**
> Ships **Final Approach v1.20.0** with bundled ElevenLabs audio (~26 MP3s) instead of synth-only feedback, plus the **v1.19.0** feel fixes that land in the same tree (route handles, arrival markers, storm-safe spawns).
> 
> **Sound:** The server discovers MP3s under `static/final-approach/audio/` and injects cache-busted URLs as `window.FA_AUDIO`. The client runs a **WebAudio soundscape** on four buses (effects, landscape bed, engine loops, music): one-shots with synth fallback, **cross-faded loop repeats** to avoid MP3 click, engines that scale and pan with traffic, and **calm vs busy music** driven by conflicts and airspace fill. A **Music** toggle on the board persists beside mute; conflict alerts stay synthesised. Playback is named **`playSound`** so it cannot shadow shift **`play()`**.
> 
> **Gameplay (v1.19):** Arrivals use **screen-pixel** markers and route-end **handles** (`pickAt` continues a route from its end). **`queueArrival`** rejects paths that intersect storms during the warning plus five seconds of straight flight; markers avoid HUD plates. Early levels get a **3s warning** in `levels.js`.
> 
> **Tooling & deploy:** New `tools/final_approach_sounds.py` (prompts + ElevenLabs generation); `tools/` excluded from the Docker image. Tests lock generator ↔ files, page URLs, total size under 6 MB, and warning bounds. Playbook and `CLAUDE.md` document the audio pipeline and expanded roadmap.

TL;DR: native docx ships every font pack

## Summary
- `@betteroffice/docx-native` now depends on `@betteroffice/fonts-latin`, `@betteroffice/fonts-intl` and `@betteroffice/fonts-cjk` next to `@betteroffice/fonts`, and keeps all four external in its build, like `@betteroffice/pptx-native`.
- Default fonts already load through `@betteroffice/fonts`, which reads pack assets from the installed package files on Node.js, Bun and Deno and decodes them with the native engine. With the packs installed, every Latin, international and CJK face loads from disk on first use; nothing is fetched. Before, `fonts-intl` and `fonts-cjk` were not part of a native install, so international and CJK text had no bundled face.
- README: the optional-peer sentence becomes one line that default fonts need no setup.
- Browsers are unchanged: `@betteroffice/docx` keeps fetching faces on demand.

## Repro
- `bindings/docx-native/index.test.ts`: the manifest case requires the three packs (fails on the base manifest), and a new case loads Carlito, Noto Sans Devanagari and Noto Sans JP through `@betteroffice/fonts` with the package's own `decodeFontFace` while `fetch` rejects, checking each face's exact byte length.

## Evidence
- Packed install (VM): `npm pack` of fonts, fonts-latin, fonts-intl, fonts-cjk and docx-native (workspace ranges pinned by `scripts/rewrite-workspace-deps.ts`), `npm install` of the tarballs into an empty directory, then with `fetch` throwing: Carlito 632,084 B, Noto Sans Devanagari 243,520 B, Noto Sans JP 4,533,028 B and Noto Serif SC 11,625,800 B read and decoded locally, and the `./yrs` entry imports, on Node.js 24, Node.js 20.16, Node.js 22.3 and Deno 2.9.

- Red: the manifest test fails on the base `package.json`.
- Wire size: browser packages unchanged (no source change).

- [x] Packed tarball install reads all packs with no fetch (Node.js 20.16, 22.3, 24, Deno 2.9)

author: fagci
body:
Этап 4: звук. Микрофон узла Phone sensors идёт мимо аудио-цепочки WebView / Chrome (getUserMedia), которая на ряде телефонов даёт провал в спектре (например 8–14 кГц) и пересэмплирует.

- **Источник** (`micSrc`): `auto` (UNPROCESSED, если телефон умеет, иначе MIC) / `unprocessed` / `mic` / `camcorder` / `voice_recognition` / `voice_comm` / `performance`. Недоступный источник → MIC с пометкой.
- **Частота** (`micHz`) до 192 кГц; не открылась — ближайшая стандартная, в записи `sr` реальная. Раньше потолок был 48 кГц, а по умолчанию 16 кГц (выше 8 кГц сигнала не бывает).
- **Обработка**: шумодав, АРУ и эхоподавитель принудительно выключаются на сессии входа.
- **Устройство** (`micDev`): usb / wired / bluetooth / builtin через `setPreferredDevice`. В записи `ms` (источник) и `dev` (устройство).
- **С root** («Allow root features»): источники, закрытые приложениям, — `voice_call`, `downlink` (собеседник), `uplink` (свой голос), `submix` (что играет телефон). Помощник `RootAudio` запускается через `su` + `app_process` (root обходит проверку `CAPTURE_AUDIO_OUTPUT`), PCM идёт через stdout, ошибки `ERR:` — в статус; при остановке процесс убивается. Зависит от аудио-HAL телефона.
- Страница: параметры `micSrc` / `micDev` / расширенный `micHz`, сообщение подписки; пресет *Phone App: Wideband Microphone — Raw Source, up to 192 kHz, USB, Call Audio (root)*; тесты `test-termux.mjs`, `MicTest.kt`; README (корень и `tools/android`).

Не проверено на телефоне: пропадает ли провал 8–14 кГц; какие источники и частоты отдаёт конкретная модель; работает ли `RootAudio` на конкретном ROM (Android 12+ создаёт `AudioRecord` через `AttributionSource`, в голом процессе без пакета это может отказать — тогда причина будет в статусе).

author: shaoxier
body:
第二轮冲刺第 8 项：隔离检查补 DNS、Docker 接口、项目边界三类探针，每类都带正向对照，计数改对。对应会议第 8 条和 todo 清单第 8 项（P0-4）的最小版本。

## 改了什么

- **对照**：每项结果多了“对照”列表，用来证明探针本身看得到问题。任何一项对照不成立，“通过”一律改判“无法验证”。这条规则在宿主统一执行。
- **DNS 查询外传**：替换原来那项永远判不了“通过”的检查。
  - 在沙箱的出网网络上临时起一个金丝雀 DNS，代表“虚拟机以外”。
  - 三个对照：出网侧容器直接发送、经 Docker 内嵌 DNS 转发都必须被记到；虚拟机本身能解析公网域名。
  - 一个反例：内部网络上 DNS 指向金丝雀的探针，查询不能被记到。
  - Agent 另外测公网 DNS、TCP 53、DoT、IPv6、网关和门卫上的 DNS，并解析一次 example.com。
  - 再核对 Docker 设置：Agent 只接内部网络、DNS 上游只有 127.0.0.1。
- **Docker 接口**：
  - 扫描环境变量、挂载、socket 文件和 2375/2376 端口；
  - 两个阳性样本：Agent 容器里的假接口；把假接口挂到 `/var/run/docker.sock` 的对照容器。
- **项目边界**：
  - 读 Agent 的挂载表，共享目录只能挂项目本身且路径正确；
  - 哨兵放在 `~/CageWorkspace` 下、与项目并列的测试目录里，虚拟机能读到它才算对照成立，Agent 从哪个挂载点都看不到才算通过；
  - 同时检查上级目录。
- **直连数据库**：改连出网侧解析出的地址。原来 Agent 里没有 DNS，这一项永远“无法验证”。
- **新增“绕过网关直连远程 MCP”**：不带凭据逐个请求，只有门卫在请求发出前就拒绝才算通过。
- **计数**：运行状态页从“x/y 项通过”改成按状态计数；检查对话框逐项列出对照。
- **临时容器与清理**：
  - 用 Agent 的镜像和同样的限制，带沙箱标签，不挂项目、home 卷或 Docker socket，用完即删；
  - 出网侧的只运行 Python 标准库；
  - 运行状态采样跳过它们；
  - 检查开始、停止、删除或重置沙箱时，清理遗留的探针。
- **检查脚本**：全部改用 `python3 -I -S`，项目里的 `json.py` 不再能顶替标准库。同一沙箱同时只跑一次检查。

## 验证

详见 `docs/validation/2026-10-31-isolation-checks.md`，脱敏结果在 `docs/validation/assets/2026-10-31-isolation-checks.json`。

- **自动测试**：`make check`、`make test`（含竞态检查）、前端 `node --test` 都通过。新增：
  - 对照规则；
  - DNS 23 种判定情形；
  - 用伪造的挂载表直接运行项目边界脚本；
  - Docker 接口和项目边界的判定；
  - 远程 MCP 多服务判定；
  - 运行状态跳过探针；
  - 探针容器的限制。
  - 三处关键修复都确认过：去掉后对应测试失败。
- **真机**（测试沙箱 `uat-isolation`：Codex→xapi，DeepWiki 远程 MCP，演示数据库）：
  - 9 项全部“通过”，所有对照成立，整轮约 2.8 秒；
  - 用临时容器扮演五种配错的 Agent，五项都报“发现问题”：接在出网网络上、挂了 Docker socket、共享了整个工作区、把工作区挂成项目目录、另挂一份工作区；
  - 检查期间运行状态一直正常；
  - 结束后没有残留的探针容器、卷或测试目录。
- **界面**（模拟后端，数据取自真机结果）：对照的成立/不成立显示，计数文字。
- **独立复查**：子代理复查了一轮并在真机上复现，报了 1 个高、3 个中、7 个低，都已修复，逐条记录在验收文档。
  - 最重要的一条：项目边界原来只在原路径找哨兵，把整个工作区挂成项目目录或另挂一份都会判“通过”；现在改读挂载表。
  - 修复后没有再请子代理复查，用自动测试、变异验证和真机测试确认。

## 顺带发现（没改）

- Agent 能 TCP 连上内部网关上虚拟机的 22 端口（sshd）。colima 的私钥不在共享目录里，现在登录不进去，但多了一个可达的系统服务。
- 实验确认，内部网络加 `com.docker.network.bridge.inhibit_ipv4=true` 可以去掉这条路径，容器之间照常互通。
- 已有沙箱要重建网络，单独处理。

## 限制

- **没做的探针**：IPv6 正向对照与公网 IPv6、管理面、跨沙箱、宿主回环。DNS 没做团队自有域名的外部对照；虚拟机断网时 DNS 一项只能判“无法验证”。
- **出网侧探针的剩余风险**：用的是 Agent 镜像里的 Python。镜像在构建时被投毒的风险没有单独处理。
- **Agent 能干扰检查**：检查脚本在 Agent 容器里以 Agent 用户运行，已被控制的 Agent 能干扰结果。检查验证的是配置。
- **结果不落盘**：结果仍只在应用内存里；验收 JSON 由测试命令导出。

## 合并

本 PR 基于最新的 main，不依赖其他未合并的 PR；与第 9 项（终端文件栏）的分支互不冲突。按约定用 merge commit 合并。

author: yia-mw-agent
body:
## Summary

The versioned Mintlify site only had four hand-written qualification pages. This publishes the SDK's own guides for each release and a component catalog, and adds the checks and the procedure to keep them correct.

## What changes

- `docs/releases/VERSION/release.json` records, per release, the published packages, the pinned source revision, the guides taken from it, every `docs` file that is left out with a reason, and the catalog components.
- `scripts/docs-release.ts` generates the guide pages and the catalog from that revision with `git show`. It refuses to rewrite a committed release. `check` needs only committed files (navigation, labels, one stable default, links, anchors, fences, catalog against the release record). `routes` prints every route and where each component is documented. `verify-source` regenerates a release in memory and reports drift.
- 0.7.6 (stable, default) publishes the two guides that describe its published packages. Guides that describe the Lit packages (first published at 0.7.7-rc.1) or that state no 0.7.x package exists are excluded, each with its reason. 0.11.0-rc.1 (prerelease) publishes the user guides. Contributor and maintainer documents are excluded in both.
- Each release has a component catalog read from the package manifests and entry points at the pinned revision: FaithfulCard and ActionButton in both, SagaAttribution in the prerelease only. A package without a registry release at that version is marked as such. Each component page shows a static demonstration copied from a maintained source file, its exports, usage guides and the evidence the guides record, with their limits.
- `docs/connect/assistants.mdx` explains the documentation MCP address, client steps, naming a release and the Markdown and index files the site serves.
- The probe gains `pages` (every navigation page is served and its code blocks equal the committed ones) and, when the search tool has a `version` argument, repeats each question with it. It now reads a search result by its `Link` and `Page` lines, so a page whose text quotes another release's path is not counted as a result from that release.
- `docs/mintlify.md` documents the release, update and rollback procedure.

## Verification

Source, at head `aa877cc`:

- `npx vitest run scripts/docs-release.test.ts scripts/docs-probe.test.ts` (67 tests), `npx tsc -p tsconfig.json`, `npm run test:docs`, `scripts/check-test-discovery.ts`, `format:check` and `scripts/mw-version.py check` pass.
- `docs-release.ts check` and `verify-source` pass: every committed page is reproduced exactly from its pinned revision, and every code fence of every published guide equals the source's. A test also fails if a `docs` file of the revision is neither published nor excluded.
- `npx mint validate` and `npx mint broken-links` pass.
- The heading ids that `mint dev` renders for every page under `docs/releases` match the anchor rule the generator uses (Mintlify keeps `@`, `/`, `+` and an apostrophe, and numbers repeats from 2, unlike GitHub). An earlier version used GitHub's rule; one link (`#alexa`, rendered as `alexa+`) differed and was corrected.

Preview (`https://saga-a2ui-automation-tracked-017cee831271.mintlify.site`), at head `aa877cc`. These show what the preview served; the production site still serves the four earlier pages until this merges.

- `docs-probe.ts pages`: all 30 pages are served as Markdown and their fenced code blocks equal the committed ones (the platform adds ` theme={null}` to info strings, which the check ignores).
- `docs-probe.ts mcp`: initialize, `tools/list` (`search_saga_a2ui`, `query_docs_filesystem_saga_a2ui`, `submit_feedback`), then for each release a search, a version-filtered search and a read of its `server-entry-points` page. Both releases pass: the requested release's page ranks first, its retrieved content states that release's export facts and not the other's, and the filtered search returns only that release's pages (plus the shared assistants page). Unfiltered search also returns the other release's pages, listed by path.
- The site serves `/llms.txt` (default release pages only), `/sitemap.xml`, `/.well-known/mcp.json`, `.md` for each page, and `components/catalog.json` for each release. `/llms-full.txt` returned 404 on the preview and 200 on production before this content; confirm it after merging.
- Update and rollback on non-production content: after a baseline snapshot of the 30 pages, commit `b23ceb1` appended one sentence to `docs/releases/0.11.0-rc.1/server-entry-points.mdx`. About a minute after the push the preview served it, and `compare` listed that page as the only change; the other 29 pages, including all of 0.7.6, were unchanged. Reverting it (`dfc4bfb`) returned every hash to the baseline (`changed: []`). The four production pages were unchanged by both. The net diff against `main` has no change to that page.

## Limits

Documentation only; no package version changes and no publication. This does not activate `docs.saga-a2ui.dev` or change DNS. Previews and the analytics reports depend on the Mintlify plan; nothing here relies on them after merge. The static demonstrations are copies of source lines, not live renderings, and the component evidence is limited to what the linked guides record: a local fixture result for FaithfulCard rendering and the bounded ChatGPT web, Claude web and Alexa+ simulator observations for the flows named there, not a complete host matrix.

author: 404khai
body:
## Summary
Sets up the Graft Cargo workspace, a `graft` CLI with `--version`, `--help` and `doctor`, a `graftd` stub, and CI for Linux and macOS. Includes a privileged job that checks reflink detection on real ext4, btrfs and XFS filesystems.

## Why
Every later phase needs a consistent crate layout, lint policy and CI before real code lands. `graft doctor` also answers the first question about a Root: can its filesystem share blocks with grafts (reflinks), or will grafts have to copy files?

## What changed
- **repo**: workspace with all 12 crates from §5, toolchain pinned to 1.99.0, workspace lints (`clippy::pedantic`, `unwrap_used`/`expect_used` outside tests, `missing_docs`, `print_*` in libraries), `deny.toml`, `.editorconfig`, `.gitignore`.
- **graft-core**: `GraftId`/`RootId` (16 bytes) and `BlobHash` (32 bytes, blake3-sized) newtypes with one canonical lowercase-hex form (serde included); `GraftError`; `$GRAFT_HOME` resolution (env override must be absolute, XDG on Linux, `~/Library/Application Support` on macOS) with the environment injected so tests never mutate the process env; optional `config.toml` (`[log] filter`) that rejects unknown keys.
- **graft-fs**: `filesystem_type` (statfs magic / `f_fstypename`), `probe_reflink` (clones a scratch file with `FICLONE` / `clonefile(2)`, see ADR 0001), `same_filesystem`, FUSE and NFS client checks. `#![deny(unsafe_code)]` at the root; all `unsafe` sits in the private `sys` module, each block with a `SAFETY` comment.
- **graft-cli**: clap skeleton; `graft doctor [PATH]` finds the repo top, probes inside `.git` so `git status` never sees scratch files, and reports `$GRAFT_HOME` without creating it, whether it shares a filesystem with the repo, config status, FUSE and NFS. It exits non-zero only for problems that stop Graft working.
- **graft-daemon**: `graftd` binary that handles `--version`/`--help` and otherwise exits with "not implemented".
- **tests/e2e**: built as graft-cli's `e2e` test target, so Cargo builds the binary for it. Covers the CLI and doctor, and enforces repo policy: `forbid(unsafe_code)` on non-FS crates, crate docs, workspace lints.
- **ci**: fmt; clippy, test, cargo-deny and rustdoc (`-D warnings`) on ubuntu-latest and macos-latest; a privileged Linux job (`scripts/mount-test-filesystems.sh`) that loop-mounts ext4, btrfs and XFS.
- **docs**: `docs/STATUS.md` (every phase's criteria), `docs/architecture.md` (§1–§5), ADR 0001, README.

Example output (macOS, APFS):
```
platform      macos aarch64
repository    /Users/admin/Developer/graft
  filesystem  apfs
  reflink     supported (clonefile)
graft home    /Users/admin/Library/Application Support/graft (default, not created yet)
  filesystem  apfs
  same fs     yes
config        /Users/admin/Library/Application Support/graft/config.toml (not present, using defaults)
fuse          unavailable (macFUSE not installed; not needed, Graft uses NFS loopback on macOS)
nfs client    available (/sbin/mount_nfs)
```

## How to test
```sh
cargo fmt --all --check
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings
cargo test --workspace
cargo deny check
cargo run -p graft-cli -- doctor
# Linux, as root, for btrfs/XFS/ext4:
sudo scripts/mount-test-filesystems.sh /tmp/graft-fs "$(id -u):$(id -g)"
GRAFT_TEST_FS_MOUNTS=ext4=/tmp/graft-fs/mnt/ext4,btrfs=/tmp/graft-fs/mnt/btrfs,xfs=/tmp/graft-fs/mnt/xfs \
  cargo test -p graft-fs --features privileged-tests --test privileged
```

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] Build, test, clippy, fmt and deny pass in CI on Linux and macOS: all 10 jobs green in [run 41192910428](https://github.com/404khai/graft/actions/runs/41192910428).
- [x] `graft doctor` reports reflink support correctly, as shown in the CI logs: APFS supported (clonefile, macOS runner); ext4 not supported (Ubuntu runner and loop mount); btrfs and XFS supported (FICLONE, loop mounts in the privileged job).
- [x] forbid(unsafe_code) on all non-FS crates, enforced by `repo_policy::unsafe_code_is_forbidden_outside_fs_and_sandbox`. `graft-sandbox` uses `deny` so it can allow `unsafe` per module later, as §6 permits.

## Benchmarks
n/a

## New dependencies
All MIT or Apache-2.0 (dual), widely used, actively maintained; `cargo deny check` passes.

| Crate | Version | Where | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| clap (derive) | 4.6.7 | cli, daemon | Mandated by §4 |
| anyhow | 1.0.104 | cli | Binary errors, §4 |
| thiserror | 2.0.21 | core | Library errors, §4 |
| serde (derive) | 1.0.229 | core | Config and ID serialisation, §4 |
| toml | 1.1.8 | core | `config.toml`, §4 |
| tracing | 0.1.44 | fs, cli | Logging, §4 |
| tracing-subscriber (env-filter) | 0.3.23 | cli | `$GRAFT_LOG` / config filter |
| libc | 0.2.191 | fs | `statfs`, `clonefile`, `FICLONE`. std has no wrappers; `rustix` lacks `clonefile` |
| tempfile | 3.27.0 | fs (+ dev everywhere) | Probe scratch dir with guaranteed cleanup; test isolation |
| assert_cmd | 2.2.2 | dev | E2E CLI tests, §4 |
| predicates | 3.1.4 | dev | Output assertions for assert_cmd |

I did not add `dirs`: `$GRAFT_HOME` resolution is about 30 lines of std and easier to test with an injected environment.

## Not in this PR
- `docs/on-disk-format.md`, ID generation and `RootId` derivation: Root registry (`feat/root-registry`).
- `graft.toml` (dogfooding Blueprint): its schema arrives with the layer cache.
- `FsBackend` trait and the reflink backend: reflink grafts.
- Project license: owner's decision. Workspace crates are `publish = false` until one is chosen.
- `main` was bootstrapped with a single commit containing only `AGENTS.md`, because the repository was empty and a PR needs a base branch. Everything else is in this PR.

## Contexte

Lot 2, tâche 2.1 : le cœur de l'évaluation, en fonctions pures, sans IA (ADR 0005).

## Changements

- **`parcourir`** : chaque nœud de l'arbre est désigné par son chemin (`"0.1"`), sans identifiant à écrire dans le contenu.
- **`evaluer(arbre, cités, niveaux)`** :
  - un nœud compte s'il est cité **et que son parent compte** — chaîne continue jusqu'à la racine ;
  - les nœuds cités sans cette chaîne sont des **orphelins** : premier signal de récitation sans raisonnement ;
  - détail couche par couche, et **niveau atteint** (le plus exigeant parmi les nœuds valides, dans l'ordre du domaine ; les orphelins ne comptent pas).
- **`normaliser`** : minuscules, sans accents ni ligatures, ponctuation remplacée par des espaces, espaces réduites.
- **`reperer(arbre, réponse)`** : propose les nœuds cités dans une réponse libre — mot, synonymes et alternatives, comparés sur des mots entiers. C'est une proposition, que l'utilisateur corrigera à la révélation (2.4).

## Vérification

`make check` : 63 tests dans `core`, dont 22 pour ce module, sur le domaine de cuisine.

author: agourakis82
body:
**Defect.** Madaros ignored every declared user effect. `checker_collect_item_inplace` (the `*mut` collect spine, which the modular compiler runs) had no `ItemEffect` arm, so the user-effect registry stayed empty. It is the third gap of this kind, after `ItemAlgebra` (09-01) and `ItemUnit` (09-09). A three-line file shows it, and lean_single accepts the same file:

```
effect HostT {}
fn f(x: i64) -> i64 with HostT { x + 1 }   // E246: unknown effect 'HostT' … not a declared user effect
```

This defect is why **Loom Coordination** is red on main (since 2026-10-27, and on #3384): `stdlib/coordination/loom_continuity.sio` declares `pub effect LoomHostTrust {}`. It is not a regression of #3383, because the previous prebuilt behaves the same.

**Fix**
1. `checker_collect_effect_def_inplace` mirrors the by-value `collect_item_effect` (id = 100 + index, ops with their return type lowered) and writes the registry in place.
2. An effects-first pre-pass runs over every module in `check_modules_verdict_boot4_with_visibility`, and over each item list. A `with X` is resolved while its signature is collected, and an importer is collected before the module it imports. With the arm alone, `use m::{HostT}` + `with HostT` was still E246 (that was a miss in my first prediction, fixed by this pass). Registration is idempotent by name.
3. A selective import resolves effect names, so `use m::{X}` no longer gives E-USE-ITEM.
4. `loom_continuity_typestate_gate.sh`: the visibility sabotage accepts only linear codes (E039/E040) and fails on any other code. Before, it only required that E039 appear somewhere in the log.
5. The prebuilt is refreshed from this branch (run 41191247601, sha256 `9f97b209…`), with a receipt from `madaros_full_gate` (pass), verified.

**Prediction vs. observation** (build 1 = arm only, build 2 = arm + pre-pass)

| case | prediction | build 1 | build 2 |
|---|---|---|---|
| single file (3 shapes) | clean | clean | clean |
| `use m::{HostT}` + `with HostT` | clean | **E246** (miss) | clean |
| `run-pass/user_effect_declared_madaros` | `USER_EFFECT_OK 42` | ✓ | ✓ |
| `compile-fail/user_effect_missing_in_caller_madaros` | E035 | ✓ | ✓ |
| `run-pass/user_effect_import_{a,main}` | pass | **fail E246** (witness discriminates) | pass |
| 4 Loom gates (causal_receipt, fleet_transaction, loom_continuity, loom_obligation) | PASS | loom_continuity FAIL | **4/4 PASS** |

---

**Second defect, in the same PR (one prebuilt refresh covers both).** `ExprHandle` had no arm in `checker_check_expr_inplace`. The fallback `checker_check_expr_mut` refuses whatever expression kind it receives, so every `handle<E> { .. } with { .. }` failed `--check` with "expression kind was not checked in place". Both prebuilts, the current one and the previous one, fail this way. The 6 `#830` fixtures fail on the current-source job, which is red on #3384. Fix: an in-place transcription of `check_handle_expr`: the effect is held only for the body and released before the handler, and the result has the body's type.

| case | prediction | build 2 | build 3 |
|---|---|---|---|
| `handle_*` (11 `.sio`) | 11/11 | 6 fail ("dispatch missed") | **11/11** |
| effect witnesses + 4 Loom gates | unchanged | pass | pass |

The prebuilt is now build 3 (run 41193671900, sha256 `0ff69d86…`, source `0ed977cec`). Its receipt comes from `madaros_full_gate` (pass) and has been verified.

<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"lilseyi"} -->
Requested by **Dev2** · project thread

## Problem
In production, the real run of "Tex notes into their objects" refused every note with `STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE`, so nothing moved. Refused rows are left exactly as they were, and the bucket stays authoritative, so no note was lost or changed.

The cause is in the routing check. `withTexRouting` allows only `person:<binding.workspaceId>`, but a credential the control plane opens (`S3GatewayCredential`) carries no workspace. Every Tex key that reached a console store therefore read as another workspace's.

Those console stores are the migration, Download as folders, the trash's emptying and collaboration filing. So the notes already born in the Durable Object since #2506 could not be exported from the console either.

The gateway's own binding does carry `workspaceId`, so turns were never affected. The door test built its binding with a `workspaceId`, which is why the gap passed review.

## Fix
- `storeForBinding` takes `texWorkspaceId`, and that takes precedence over `binding.workspaceId`.
- `consoleTexRouting(ctx, workspaceId)` returns `{texStore, texWorkspaceId}` together, so a caller cannot pass one without the other. All four console callers spread it.
- The image-upload job's store (`storeForOpenedBinding`) now routes Tex keys too.

## Tests
- The door test now builds its binding the way the control plane opens one, with no workspace. Without the fix it fails; with the fix it passes.
- Results:
  - Convex door and migration tests: 21 pass.
  - Gateway suite: all 7 entry points pass.
  - `convex typecheck` passes.
  - `pnpm architecture`: 0 errors.
  - Path gates: OK.

Once this is live, I'll rerun the move.

author: zeecm
body:
Fixes from an independent phone and renovation test of zeecm/dream-home-designer#14 and zeecm/dream-home-designer#15.

## Renovation carry-over
- **Field-by-field merge.** Carrying an edit to the renovation now merges each record field by field (`merge` in `renovation.ts`):
  - the edit's fields go over where the renovation's are unchanged;
  - the renovation keeps fields it changed itself, such as paint or height.

  Before, any renovation change to a wall (even paint) blocked trace fixes at its corners. Since most renovations repaint most walls, most later fixes were held back.
- **Still held back:**
  - a field both versions changed differently;
  - a record one version removed and the other changed;
  - the renovation's own door on a wall whose ends the edit moves;
  - anything that would leave the result inconsistent.
- **Whole-drag rollback.** A drag held back at any step now takes back its steps already carried, leaving the renovation as the drag found it (`restore`, passed from the store). Before, the moves stayed but the final settle didn't, which left a wall end resting unjoined on another wall.
- **Room clash notice.** Renaming or refinishing in Before a room the renovation also changed now shows the hold-back notice instead of skipping silently.

## Panning on a phone
- **No coast after a pinch.** Coasting needs 40 px of real panning first. Before, a finger lifting a frame after the other at the end of a pinch made the zoomed spot slide 140–240 px away.
- **Coast stays on screen.** It stops before the plan's middle leaves the screen. A swipe could otherwise throw the whole flat off a phone screen.
- **Other view changes win.** Fit, or anything else that moves the view, stops a coast instead of being overridden by it.
- **Tap just stops.** A tap that stops a coast does nothing else, as on phone lists and maps. Before, it also selected a room, or set a wall's first corner.

## Furniture
- **Tabletop pieces only.** Only pieces under 1.2 m (lamps, the succulent, the TV) stand on the piece under them. A wall cabinet keeps its 1.45 m instead of dropping onto the counter.
- **Same-level selection.** A click selects a piece only when it's on the same level as the one picked (floor, raised or ceiling). So with a table lamp picked, a click under a pendant places the lamp instead of selecting the pendant.

## Walk view
- **Honest label.** The View label shows the angle actually in effect: 74° on a phone held upright, where it used to read 70°.
- **Saved choice kept.** Moving the slider to its end on a tall view no longer overwrites a wider choice made on a wider screen.

## Checks
- Core: 216 tests pass. New ones cover splitting a repainted wall (paint kept), both versions changing a field (held back), and a drag's carried steps taken back.
- Web unit tests: 36 pass.
- e2e: all 58 pass. New phone checks cover a tap during a coast (stops it, selects nothing) and the swipe coast.
- Lint and typecheck pass.

- `.python-version` is the only place the Python version lives. The `sync-python-version` prek hook rewrites the Dockerfile's `ARG PYTHON_VERSION` default from it, the same pattern Airflow uses for its Dockerfile `ARG`s. Dependabot can't update a `FROM` line that uses an `ARG`, so Python bumps are a one-line edit to `.python-version`.
- `python -m app` reads `HOST` and `PORT` from `Settings`. `HOST` defaults to `127.0.0.1` and the image sets `HOST=0.0.0.0`. I checked the image: it runs as uid 10001, `/v1/liveness` returns ok, and `-e PORT=9002` serves on 9002. `uv run pytest`: 7 passed.

author: theglitching
body:
## Why The false news this audience meets arrives as a WhatsApp chain or a two-line Facebook post, and Squiggle refused all of it: under 200 characters the site said « Collez le texte complet de l'article », the extension refused a page under 200 words, and the article grid would have judged a rumour on sourcing and structure it can never have. A short message now has its own analysis mode, answering four questions: what it is about, who says it, what is known, what is missing. ## How the mode is chosen A text of at most 1 200 characters (`MAX_MESSAGE_CHARS`, `shared/src/engine/message.ts`) is a message, read from the length of the text itself, as the video mode is read from the address. No client flag can choose it, so the text fingerprint that keys the cache also fixes the instructions. A YouTube transcript stays a transcript however short. 1 200 characters sits at the extension's own article floor (200 words), so no article the extension reads falls under it; a press brief that does is read well by the four questions anyway. ## The message instructions (`MESSAGE_SYSTEM_PROMPT`, `prompts.ts`) Same JSON, same five domains read for a message, so scoring, research, the panel and the site's report work unchanged: - the summary is four lines: **De quoi parle-t-on / Qui l'affirme / Ce qu'on en sait / Ce qui manque**; - the audit never says true or false from memory (a rumour is often recent, local or invented): the main claim always goes to research as an `affirmation-non-etayee` with its `checkableClaim`, and what is known comes back with sources; - the signs that usually come with a false message are findings when they are in the text, named as signs, never as a verdict: no or anonymous source (`source-absente`), urgency, fear and calls to forward (`cadrage`), a figure without an origin, an authority without a name, « on vous le cache » (`sophisme`); - an ordinary personal message gets one `point-fort` and nothing invented; practical news of general interest (a date, a measure) is still checked; - the language of a message typed on a phone is not judged (5/5). `PROMPT_VERSION` goes to **1.2.0**: texts of 200 to 1 200 characters were analysed under the article prompt before, and their cached reports must not be served under the new one. ## Where it is wired - **Site** (`/analyser`): a text from 20 characters (`MIN_MESSAGE_CHARS`) is accepted; the counter says « analysé comme un message » up to 1 200; a hint invites a WhatsApp or Facebook message; a lone address pasted as text is refused with its own sentence (nothing would be fetched). A one-line share **without a link** is the text, not the title; « headline https://… » from a paper's app is still a title. The report names a « Message problématique / solide… » and shows the summary one question per line. - **Android app**: on top of #157 (a text without a link already opens `/analyser#text=…&via=appli` and starts at once), a text that carries a link but more than a headline around it (≥ 200 characters, a chain with a link) is now a message too, instead of opening the link. The « trop court » sentence now only covers a text under 20 characters. - **Extension**: a passage the reader selected in the page, between 20 and 1 200 characters, is analysed instead of the page (`src/content/selection.ts`), and highlighted by its words; a longer selection is ignored. A short X post (social thread) is no longer refused by the 200-word paywall rule. The panel says how, under the button. - **Server**: a message read by the extension is never served by link alone (`read_by_extension` stays false: a post on the page is not the page's article). Counter `run_started_message` (no migration: counters are rows by name), shown in Pilotage as « dont messages courts ». ## Quota and price Unchanged: one analysis, one credit, same daily limits. Measured on the production model (`deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash` via OpenRouter, the server's own stages run in process, billed `usage.cost` read from each OpenRouter answer): **$0.0009 to $0.034 per message, $0.019 on average**, against the $0.15-0.27 worst case of an article (cost-guard PR). Nothing in the cost argues for a different price. ## The 12 messages, live Ten typical French rumours, one true practical message and one ordinary personal message, each through the real hosted stages (`createWorker` with the production model, signed-in web session), on the final prompt. Corpus and harness kept outside the repository. | Message | Nature | Car. | Note | Constats | Recherche | Coût | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `caf-apl` | chaîne WhatsApp (annexe A.1 de l'étude) | 125 | 34 problematique | 4 | non vérifiable | $0.0211 | | `whatsapp-payant` | chaîne WhatsApp | 268 | 11 problematique | 5 | non vérifiable | $0.0214 | | `camionnette-blanche` | publication Facebook locale | 257 | 25 problematique | 5 | non vérifiable | $0.0164 | | `citron-cancer` | chaîne santé | 270 | 16 problematique | 4 | douteuse | $0.0150 | | `ibuprofene` | message vocal transcrit / chaîne | 273 | 27 problematique | 4 | douteuse | $0.0226 | | `appel-225` | SMS d'alerte | 210 | 23 problematique | 4 | non vérifiable | $0.0237 | | `radar-telephone` | publication Facebook | 186 | 47 problematique | 3 | douteuse | $0.0225 | | `aides-migrants` | publication Facebook | 219 | 18 problematique | 5 | douteuse, non vérifiable | $0.0344 | | `coupure-electricite` | chaîne WhatsApp | 232 | 25 problematique | 4 | non vérifiable | $0.0219 | | `vaccin-adn` | chaîne santé | 187 | 21 problematique | 4 | non vérifiable | $0.0142 | | `changement-heure` | message vrai (contrôle positif) | 144 | 87 solide | 1 | vérifiée | $0.0160 | | `anniversaire` | message anodin (contrôle) | 144 | 100 solide | 1 | - | $0.0009 |
caf-apl (chaîne WhatsApp (annexe A.1 de l'étude)) : 34/100, problematique Message : ``` URGENT ⚠️ à partir du 1er novembre la CAF supprime les APL pour les retraités propriétaires. Transférez à tous vos contacts ! ``` Synthèse : - De quoi parle-t-on : le message affirme que la CAF supprimerait les APL des retraités propriétaires à partir du 1er novembre, et demande de le transférer à tous ses contacts. - Qui l'affirme : aucune source n'est donnée ; ni la CAF, ni un média, ni un document ne sont cités. - Ce qu'on en sait : le texte ne fournit qu'une date (« 1er novembre ») et un organisme (la CAF), sans aucun élément vérifiable ; l'affirmation principale est soumise à la recherche présentée sous ce message. - Ce qui manque : une source nommée et retrouvable (communiqué de la CAF, texte officiel), une année précise pour la date, et l'absence des signaux d'alerte relevés (URGENT, ⚠️, appel à faire suivre). Constats : - **Affirmation non étayée, Affirmation principale sans source** (« à partir du 1er novembre la CAF supprime les APL pour les retraités propriétaires ») : Le message annonce une suppression de prestation par la CAF, mais ne cite aucun communiqué, texte officiel ou média. Rien dans le texte ne permet de vérifier cette affirmation : c'est la recherche associée qui dira ce qu'on en sait. - **Cadrage, Ton d'urgence et symbole d'alerte** (« URGENT ⚠️ ») : La mention « URGENT » et le symbole ⚠️ visent à provoquer une réaction immédiate plutôt qu'une vérification. Ce sont des indices qui invitent à la prudence, sans prouver que le contenu est faux. - **Cadrage, Appel à faire suivre** (« Transférez à tous vos contacts ! ») : L'injonction à transférer largement est un procédé fréquent des messages non vérifiés : elle fait circuler l'affirmation avant tout contrôle. Elle ne démontre pas que le message est faux, mais invite à ne pas relayer sans vérifier. - **Source absente, Source absente** (« la CAF supprime les APL pour les retraités propriétaires ») : Aucune source n'est nommée : ni la CAF elle-même, ni un média, ni un document officiel. Une affirmation d'intérêt général sur une prestation sociale devrait pouvoir être rattachée à une source retrouvable.

Problem: kubernetes-axi had no installed public read path to verify its approved package and identity-isolation contract.
Consequence: selected identity, managed kubectl and expected version/pod results had no executable product evidence.

Fix: implement **Plan task B1.1**, Package one read with an isolated identity.
The strict TypeScript package ships one credential schema, SecretRefs, an isolated kubeconfig/process runner, digest-checked kubectl, compact TOON output and a public packaged verifier.
Pod reads use real kubectl discovery followed by one bounded raw GET through kubectl, preserving continuation state.
Native get follows continuation tokens even when chunking is disabled.

Scope: standalone server version and pod list only.
All verification used a verified loopback TLS fake, synthetic identities and real pinned kubectl.
No real clusters, real credentials, pending live probes, cluster changes, deployment or release were used.
Artium integration and native Windows commissioning remain pending B1.2/B1.3 work.
Stage and release prerequisites never count as passes.
Retained sanitized fixtures and the credential-standard capture are copied byte-for-byte and checked against manifest hashes.
No code was copied from the reference implementation.

kubectl pin v1.32.2 - captain-delegated (overnight), plan-named selection; revisit at commissioning.
Both official linux/amd64 and windows/amd64 binaries were verified against their published SHA-256 values.
The supported-server range v1.31-v1.33 remains observational until live commissioning.
The recorded toolchain is Node 24.14.0, npm 11.9.0, Python 3.12.3 and OpenSSL 3.0.13; npm dependencies are exact and locked.

Validation: no-mistakes passed review, installed-product tests, documentation and lint, and pushed head 96d6d69026f7258bd6a9dbb56224d3ecf6c69b92.
The B1.1 verifier passed 21 installed-package tests, with ten supplemental public-interface scenarios checked against the TLS fake.
The actual TOON decoder verified output, identity selection, pre-request rejection, binary selection, redaction and continuation state.
Review fixes moved redaction before serialization, kept the redaction fixture schema-valid, distinguished unavailable prerequisites from failures, and removed the optional JSON output mode as directed.

Negative-control evidence: `python3 scripts/verify.py task B1.1 --mode offline --pack evidence --negative-control` returned exit 1 and outcome failure after the review fixes.

CI was intentionally skipped for this offline-only run.
Native Windows execution, real Artium integration and live commissioning remain unrun.

author: weirdyang
body:
The Development-only certificate bypass applied whenever the site ran in Development, including against real Exchange Online, so a developer's machine never verified Microsoft's certificate.

## Change

- New setting `OAUTH_Email_M365:AllowInvalidCertificate`, off by default. It's on `OAuthSmtpOptions`, so any future provider gets it too.
- The check is skipped only when the setting is `true` **and** the site runs in Development (`OAuthSmtpClient.SkipsCertificateValidation`).
- Outside Development the setting is ignored and a warning is logged once. In Development with it on, a warning says the certificate isn't checked.
- The Microsoft 365 status tab shows a warning while the setting is on.
- The README has a "Testing locally with smtp4dev" section.

For local smtp4dev testing, add `"AllowInvalidCertificate": true` to `OAUTH_Email_M365` in `samples/Sushi.OC.Web/appsettings.Development.json`.

## Testing

- 8 new tests: every combination of the setting and the environment, no environment, off by default, and binding from configuration. All tests pass.
- Sent through a real smtp4dev with its self-signed certificate:

| `AllowInvalidCertificate` | Environment | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `false` | Development | Refused (`SslHandshakeException`) |
| `true` | Production | Refused (`SslHandshakeException`) |
| `true` | Development | Sent; appeared in smtp4dev |

Independent of #1; they touch different files.

author: imran-basha-data
body:
## Summary

Terraform for the Azure platform the Kubernetes manifests in imran-basha-data/cloud-platform-automation#2 target. **Nothing has been applied to Azure, and no paid resources have been provisioned.**

- **Modules:** `network`, `monitoring` (Log Analytics with an ingestion cap), `container_registry`, `key_vault`, `aks` (system pool reserved for add-ons plus an autoscaled `apps` user pool).
- **Identities created before the cluster:** user-assigned control-plane, kubelet and workload identities. The control plane gets Managed Identity Operator and Network Contributor *before* AKS exists, the kubelet gets AcrPull, and the `platform-api` workload identity gets Key Vault Secrets User via a **federated credential** for `system:serviceaccount:platform-<env>:platform-api`.
- **Secure defaults:** AKS local accounts disabled with Entra ID + Azure RBAC; workload identity; Azure Policy; network policy; encryption at host; automatic patch upgrades; authorised API ranges. ACR has no admin user or anonymous pull. Key Vault uses RBAC, purge protection and a deny-by-default firewall (AKS subnet service endpoint plus operator IPs).
- **Environment separation:** one root module, `environments/{dev,prod}.tfvars`, separate backend state files.
- **Guardrails:** plan-time preconditions reject prod without authorised IP ranges or the Standard (SLA) tier, and unordered autoscaler bounds. Validation covers environment, region allow-list, CIDRs, names and subnet size.

## Evidence

**CI: all 7 jobs green:**
- `terraform fmt -check`, `init -backend=false`, `validate`: pass (Terraform 1.9.8, azurerm ~> 4.0)
- `terraform test`: **14 passed, 0 failed**. Plan and mock-apply runs against a mocked azurerm provider; the "Planning failed" lines in the log come from the `expect_failures` runs, which are meant to fail.
- Checkov: Terraform **32 passed / 0 failed / 11 suppressed in code with reasons**; rendered Kubernetes **180 / 0 / 6**; Dockerfile 97 / 0
- All earlier jobs (app, container + Trivy, manifests, **kind reliability scenarios**) still green

**Three CI failures before green, each fixed at its cause:**
1. `terraform test`: `kubelet_identity[0]` was an empty list under the mocked plan. Rather than masking it with `try()`, I moved to **pre-created user-assigned identities**, which also removes the create-then-grant race against real Azure (`326ef59`).
2. Mocked teardown failed because the mock generated random strings as resource IDs, and the provider parses NSG IDs when planning the destroy. I gave every referenced resource a well-formed mock Azure ID (`e23cb01`).
3. The provider reported `enable_rbac_authorization` as deprecated and renamed, so I switched to `rbac_authorization_enabled` (`f38ecfb`).

**Limits:** `registry.terraform.io` is blocked in my local sandbox (HTTP 403), so validate and test ran only in CI. Mocked tests prove configuration logic, not that Azure accepts every combination (quotas, feature registration, regional SKUs). Only a real plan against a subscription can show that, and `terraform/README.md` says so.

body:
## Linear

- Issue: PIN-196 (child of PIN-23). Follow-up for the rest: PIN-201.

## Requirements

- Satisfies: `docs/11-studio.md` section(s) 5.1 (Policy owns limits), 5.2 (errors map to friendly typed responses), plus `docs/18-i18n.md` (updated here: new "Server errors" section).

## What changed

User-facing server errors now carry a catalog key + values instead of English text. `errorResponse` translates them into the request's language, so none of its ~25 call sites change. Error `code`s and statuses are unchanged; `.message` keeps the English for logs.

- **Mechanism** (`src/i18n/user-message.ts`): `userMessage(key, values)`, `englishText`, `localizedErrorText`, `isMessageKey`. `BoardApiError`, `PhotoIntakeError`, `SceneJobRequestError` and `BoardPlusError` accept `UserMessage | string` and expose `userMessage`. A `SceneJobRequestError` rethrown as `BoardApiError` keeps its key.
- **`errorResponse` design** (`src/app/api/boards/shared.ts`): the signature stays **sync** because `creditErrorResponse` in the checkout route (owned by PIN-197) is typed `NextResponse` and returns `errorResponse(...)`, so an async variant would not typecheck without editing that route. New `localizedErrorJson`:
  - **English only (the default `UI_LOCALES`):** builds the same `NextResponse.json` body as before, right away, and never reads the request.
  - **More than one language:** the body is a one-chunk `ReadableStream`. Its `start()` runs synchronously inside the `errorResponse` call, so `getLocale()` reads this request's cookie and headers. If the lookup fails, the body falls back to English, so it never becomes a 500.
  - `plusErrorResponse` uses the same helper and keeps `code`.
- **Literals → keys:** a new `error.*` group in `en.json`, placed right after `ai.*`, with the English kept word for word. Converted: `board-api.ts`, `board-session.ts`, `photo-intake.ts`, `scene-job.ts`, `board-plus.ts`, plus the existing `t("en", …)` calls in `board-api.ts`, `board-plus.ts`, `scene-job.ts` and `decompose-job.ts`. The 404 "not found" lines stay plain text (the uniform 404 hides them).
- **Stored English:** a refused scene now stores `refusalReason: "ai.refused"` (the key). `publicScene` / `publicSceneJob` leave a key out, so the client shows its own `ai.refused` line in the reader's language. **Old docs that already hold English pass through as-is (no migration, per the stop condition).**
- **Tap fallback label (decision, deviates from the issue text):** "My thing" stays stored as English, via `tapFallbackLabel()`. Storing a key would mean translating at every label reader: `publicElement`, the activity strip, my-pins, the library copy, and the scene prompt/chips AI inputs. That is a broad change for one fallback, and thing names stay English for now per docs/18 "Stays English". The follow-up and the decision are in PIN-201, together with PIN-200.
- **Policy:** new `displayNameMaxChars` (default 30, board-overridable) replaces the hard-coded 30 in `normalizeDisplayName` (AGENTS rule 4).
- **en-only-files:** the PIN-196 block now lists only `decorators.ts` and `dictation.ts`, which move to PIN-201.

**Split (AGENTS rule 9):** the full change was 585 lines, so this PR has the mechanism and the biggest files (463 changed lines, 332 without tests). PIN-201 covers: gateway refusal lines + dictation, `user-session.ts`, `scene-chips.ts`, `my-pins.ts`, `CreditCheckoutError` (its route mapping belongs to PIN-197; the client already maps by `code`), the tap-label key, and `auth-ui.ts` `defaultJoinName`'s literal 30.

## Test evidence

- [x] Bugbot review finished and every finding triaged (fix / follow-up PIN / justified dismissal in-thread): Cursor Bugbot completed `success` on head `50a4c7c` with 0 findings (0 review threads); `check` and `gitleaks (full history)` also `success` on that head.
- [x] Unit / contract tests (after merging the latest `origin/dev`):
  - `npm run typecheck` → clean
  - `AI_MOCK=1 npm test` (vitest run) → 129 files passed / 1 skipped; 1409 tests passed / 1 skipped
  - `npm run build` → exit 0
  - New `src/app/api/boards/shared.test.ts` (fr.json stubbed with `vi.mock`, never edited) checks:
    - a French request gets French when the key is translated, English when it isn't;
    - an English request gets English;
    - English-only config builds the old body and never calls `getLocale`;
    - a failed lookup still returns the 4xx in English;
    - the uniform 404 and generic 500 are unchanged;
    - Plus errors keep `code`.
  - `board-session.test.ts`: the display-name cap comes from Policy and the message names it. `scene-job.test.ts`: the stored refusal is the key, the view leaves it out, and a legacy English doc passes through.
  - **Live check** with `next dev`, `UI_LOCALES=en,fr`, `AI_MOCK=1` and a temporary uncommitted fr key, sending `POST /api/boards` with body `[]`:
    - cookie `pinneds_locale=fr` → `{"error":"<fr text>"} 400 application/json`
    - `Accept-Language: fr-FR` → French
    - cookie `pinneds_locale=en` → `{"error":"Give your board a title."}`

    This confirms the streamed body reads the request's language in a real route.
- [x] Preview click-through (phone viewport) for UI changes: N/A (server only; response bodies are byte-identical under the default English-only config)
- [x] Screenshots attached (UI changes): N/A

## AI / cost impact

None. No prompts, models or calls changed.

## Safety & privacy

- [x] No secrets, `.env`, or real player photos in this diff
- [x] Originals-never-persisted invariant intact (or N/A — say why): N/A, no storage paths touched
- [x] Prompt safety rules untouched, or eval pass noted above: untouched

## Rollback

Revert this PR. Scenes refused while it was live store `"ai.refused"`; after a revert, the view would send that key as the text. To avoid that, keep `refusalReasonView` or map that one value back to the English line.

author: mishkaten
body:
Investigation of order #3's mill test certificate (31 table columns, 7 portrait pages, headers broken letter by letter): the content was right, the Word file's layout was not. The converter always wrote A4 portrait, 2 cm margins, 11 pt, with equal column widths, and Claude's HTML has no way to ask for another page.

- `html_to_docx(..., layout=PageLayout(landscape, size, margin_cm))`: landscape A4, margins, type size (headings follow), and table columns sized to their content (fixed layout, narrow cell margins). Without `layout` nothing changes, so Suliko Translate and the Word editor are unaffected. `widest_table()` counts columns. The API copy is the same file.
- Worker: a table of 10+ columns, or a first line `<!--page: landscape-->` written by Claude, gets a landscape page. With LibreOffice installed and the original's page count known (PDF pages, 1 for a picture), the page is tightened step by step until the Word file is no longer than the original: margins first, then size (ordinary text to 10 pt, a wide table to 8 pt). Without LibreOffice a wide table still gets landscape and one fixed size.
- Rules file and CLAUDE.md tell Claude about the landscape comment and that sizes are not its job.

Not verified: page counts by LibreOffice (not installed on this machine), and this certificate itself. Tests cover the layout, widths, the directive, the fitting loop with a stubbed page counter, and an end-to-end landscape job.

Deploy on the Claude Code server: `winget install TheDocumentFoundation.LibreOffice`, pull, `pip install -r requirements.txt` with the worker venv (adds pypdf), copy `claude_worker.py`, `translation_docx.py`, `translation-rules.md` and `requirements.txt` to `C:\claude-worker`, restart the service. author: fontanf
body:
## Summary

The reduction uses its own timer (`ReductionParameters::timer`), which has no time limit unless `--reduction-time-limit` is set. It ignored the time limit of the algorithm, so a run could take far longer than `--time-limit`: on `gecco2020/AC_02_cover.txt`, the reduction takes about 16 s (mostly dominated sets removal), so `-a large-neighborhood-search -t 3` ran for more than 16 s.

`solve_reduced_instance` now runs the reduction with a copy of its timer, restarted at the start of the reduction, whose time limit is the minimum of the remaining time of the reduction timer and the remaining time of the algorithm timer.

If the reduction uses all the time, the algorithm still has no time left on the reduced instance and returns the solution with all sets, as before. Only the duration of the run changes.

## Tests

`-a large-neighborhood-search` on `gecco2020/AC_02_cover.txt` (full reduction: about 16 s):

| Options | Wall time | Value |
|---|---|---|
| `-t 3` | 3.2 s | all sets of the partially reduced instance |
| `-t 8` | 8.2 s | all sets of the partially reduced instance |
| `-t 30 --reduction-time-limit 1` | 30.3 s | 4 |
| `-t 3 --reduction-time-limit 10` | 3.6 s | all sets of the partially reduced instance |
| no time limit | unchanged (full reduction) | 4 |

The reduction only checks its timer in some loops, so it can exceed the limit by a fraction of a second (0.6 s in the `-t 3 --reduction-time-limit 10` run).

- **[다시 확인]이 시작할 수 있는 명세로 돌아옵니다.** ai-companion-voice-agent `memory-owned-recall-decision` 은 구조 개선(rework) 명세인데, 조사 모델이 성능 가설(`hypothesis`)을 "성능 개선은 주장하지 않는다" 는 내용으로 채우고 측정 명령(`measure`)은 두지 않았습니다. author: teamleaderleo
body: Leo, 2026-10-25: "session summary on top right flickers when im scrolling thru the chat" Leo, 2026-10-22: "did we get this top right side summary fixed yet? also the initial load is kinda slow it like flickers the initial thing/paints and renders it..." (This PR covers the summary half. The initial-load and black-screen half belongs to another lane.) ## Cause Scrolling over rows that are already loaded changes nothing in the card; base is steady there, and the browser test shows it. The flicker comes from scrolling **up**. Attach sends only a chat's newest records. As the reader scrolls up, `direct.ts` `loadOlder` pages in older history, and each page changes `snapshot.rows`, which the Summary card and Session Info read. Page after page, mid-gesture, the card: - slid in from its reserved column; - flipped the header toggle's `aria-pressed`; - added head and body sections; - grew. Session Info went from 74 px to 275 px tall. ## Fix `summary/heldWhileScrolling.ts`: one page-wide `ReaderScroll` flag. It is set by the reader's own scrolls (`onScroll` when the scroll is not programmatic) and by the reader's input (wheel, keys, touch, pointer). Input counts because wheeling at the very top of the loaded rows fires no scroll event while the older page lands. - `useHeldWhileScrolling(snapshot.rows, shownSessionId)` gives the Summary card, its content flag and Session Info the rows as they stood when the scroll began. - They take what the scroll paged in **once**, `ScrollPacing.settleMs` (250 ms) after the last reader input. - A streamed reply that keeps the view at its end, Jump to latest's glide and every live update outside a reader scroll still land at once. - Another chat takes its own rows at once. **Timer:** one `setTimeout`, re-armed on each reader event, so only one is ever pending. - **Stop condition:** it fires 250 ms after the last reader event and is not re-armed. - **Cleanup:** `releaseReaderScroll` clears it. It runs from a `useEffect` cleanup keyed on `shownSessionId`, so on a chat change and on unmount. The flag notifies twice per gesture (on, then off), never once per scroll event. No new work runs per scroll frame or per token. ## Performance Harness: `test/summary-scroll-steady.test.ts`, run in real Chromium and WebKit on fast-checks. It watches 100 painted frames of wheel scrolling over a 60-turn chat whose attach sends 40 turns, so older history pages in under the scroll. Unit harness: `test/summary-held-while-scrolling.test.tsx`. | metric | before (91684367) | after (5adcbd7) | delta | harness or run link | |---|---|---|---|---| | DOM changes in the inline Summary card and toggle while history pages in (100 frames, Chromium) | 15 | 0 | -15 | [before](https://github.com/manaflow-ai/cmux/actions/runs/41180639428), [after](https://github.com/manaflow-ai/cmux/actions/runs/41191863690) | | Session Info boxes seen while history pages in (Chromium) | 2 (74 → 275 px tall) | 1 | -1 | same | | Card re-renders with new rows during a 100-event scroll with 10 pages landing (unit) | 10 | 0 (1 on settle) | -10 | `summary-held-while-scrolling.test.tsx` | | DOM changes over 100 frames of plain scrolling (inline, popover, Session Info) | 0 | 0 | 0 | same browser test | ## Before / after Filmstrips are being captured (they follow in an edit). ## Tests - **Red at 91684367, green at the head:** `cd webviews && CMUX_BROWSER_TESTS=1 bun test test/summary-scroll-steady.test.ts`. 10 tests across Chromium and WebKit. The two "while older history pages in" cases fail at 91684367 and pass at the head. The plain-scroll cases pass at both. - `bun test test/summary-held-while-scrolling.test.tsx`: the flag notifies twice per gesture. The card is handed the same rows through 100 scroll events while 10 history pages land, takes them once on settle, and another chat's rows land at once. - `bun run check` passes at the head, in the same fast-checks run ([41191863690](https://github.com/manaflow-ai/cmux/actions/runs/41191863690)), together with both test files. **Observed:** the fast-checks runs above (Linux, headless Chromium and WebKit, the stand-in acpmux from `test/support/papercutChat.ts`). **Not run:** the native app on a Mac. The change is webview-only. ## Design The rule is added to the Session Info spec (`design/session-panel.md`) in leo-workspace: the right-hand card never changes under the reader's own scroll. This PR is a behaviour fix with no visual design choice, so it has no gallery variants. Risk: normal. Webview-only, and it touches only what the right-hand card reads. Worst case, the card shows new content 250 ms after a reader scroll ends instead of mid-scroll. Agent session: [agent session](https://cmux.com/deeplink/agent?id=aid-92fa78a91e29868c5eaa) 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need. --- ## Summary by cubic Fixes the Summary card, Session Info, and the card's Changes list flickering while scrolling through a long chat. Scrolling up pages older history in, and each page that landed mid-gesture changed the card: it slid in, flipped the header toggle, added sections, and grew. The card now reads the chat's rows as they stood when the scroll began and takes what the scroll paged in once, 250 ms after the last reader scroll or input. The Changes list is held the same way, so an older edit paged in under a scroll no longer changes a showing card mid-gesture. Streamed replies, Jump to latest, and live updates outside a reader scroll still land immediately, and another chat's rows land at once. **Tests** - Browser tests in real Chromium and WebKit watch 100 painted frames of wheel scrolling and assert no DOM changes in the card, including while older history pages in and an older edit pages in under a showing card. - Unit tests cover the hold flag notifying twice per gesture and the settle timer with a manual clock. Written for commit 5ba22fa6f5c057d4cc73e37353a01718219950bd. Summary will update on new commits.

author: jfwooten4
body: ## opener-0855 — §13.3 Process security **Requirement:** Restrict the scanner's filesystem access where feasible. ### Implementation and rationale - Confine the **actual Built-in ClamAV scan process**, not just the optional Maximum analyzer, with a macOS Seatbelt deny-by-default profile. - Allow document contents only for the specific validated file or application bundle, the installed signature database, the resolved scanner executable, and OS/Homebrew runtime paths. Give extraction files a separate per-invocation private scratch directory; block other user documents and writes outside that scratch. - Constrain ClamAV `--version` subprocesses as well; on macOS, missing sandbox support fails closed rather than launching unconfined. Retain original scanner flags, explicit argument separation, existing 30-minute/3-minute timeouts, cancellation, native scan concurrency, signatures, cache, quarantine and selected destinations. - No sandbox constraint is imposed on the trusted parent opener process; file-integrity verification and user preferences remain unaffected. ### Tests and checks - Add deterministic policy and error-path tests, including exact argv preservation on Linux, missing sandbox refusal, symlink rejection, private scratch lifecycle and sanitized errors. - Add real macOS Seatbelt probes that allow reading the selected document and private scratch writes, but deny reading an adjacent private file and writing outside scratch. - Add a dedicated Actions workflow with Linux regression tests and macOS kernel enforcement, in addition to the repository's existing required CI. ### Coordination - Started from verified `origin/main` `1bd5f132eb147887be7a2f4d2964168f38593729` on isolated branch `g4-berrypunch-scanfs`; no applicable `AGENTS.md` files exist in the tracked tree. - Existing process-security PRs #590, #594 and #595 address executable admission, subprocess deadlines and concurrency, respectively. This PR addresses only **scanner-child filesystem confinement**. PR #595 also touches scanner version execution; integrate without losing its concurrency checks if it merges first. - Four relevant files changed; no secret-bearing files accessed. Do not squash-merge until required checks pass.

author: marcocondrache
body:
Adds a `steering` skill that decides where an instruction for a coding agent should live and at what scope. It draws on Anthropic's article [Steering Claude Code](https://claude.com/resources/articles/steering-claude-code-skills-hooks-rules-subagents-and-more), rewritten as decision rules in this repo's voice.

- Decision rules: "always" goes in a hook, "never" goes in a hook or permission, procedures go in skills, file constraints go in path-scoped rules, noisy side tasks go to subagents, tone goes in the system prompt.
- A table comparing each mechanism on when it loads, what happens after compaction, context cost, and what it's good for.
- Guidance on steering file size, ownership, and pruning, plus hook output, the output-style pitfall, and bundling a setup into a plugin.
- Mechanism names are generic, per the harness-agnostic rule in `AGENTS.md`.
- `retro` now points at `steering` when it chooses where a fix goes. The README credits the source, and the plugin version goes to 0.11.0.

Not tested with a fresh agent yet.
