author: wackeyssl
body:
Row P96 of `docs/plans/2026-10-22-phase-3.md` (lane H, release-engineer): "ci: `PERF bases` lines in the job summary", estimated at 20 lines, after P93 (#248, merged as f1798b2). The verify job's job summary now shows the two base-arena perf lines that P93 prints, under a heading of their own, the way it shows the `PERF sim` lines. Base: main 81c9b61. One commit: 694eb29.

## What changed
- **`.github/workflows/ci.yml`** (verify job, step "Job summary", +10): after the `PERF sim` block the step now writes a blank line, the heading `### PERF bases (the base arena, report only)`, a blank line, and a fenced block with
  `grep -a -E '^PERF bases (units=|impl=native units=)' "$RUNNER_TEMP/verify.log"`.
  - If no line matches, or there is no log, the block says `no PERF bases line (the base arena perf suite did not run)`, like the `PERF sim` block's fallback.
  - Without the SimKernels library the suite prints a plain note in place of the native line (it does not start with `PERF `), so only the GDScript line shows. This is the same as for `PERF sim`.
  - A comment above the step names P96 and says nothing gates on the lines.
  - The `PERF sim` command, its fallback text and its position are untouched. The step still runs with `if: always()`.
- **`tests/project/test_ci_workflow.gd`** (+51 −3): the existing `test_verify_job_summary_copies_the_two_perf_lines` now also calls a new private helper, `_assert_perf_bases_summary`. The helper checks:
  - the heading line and the `PERF bases` grep line are in the step, in that order, after the `PERF sim` grep line;
  - the `PERF bases` selector picks both base-arena lines;
  - it picks no `PERF sim` line, and the `PERF sim` selector picks no `PERF bases` line;
  - it skips the plain note without the library, both `WATCH ... hash_bytes` lines and an indented `PERF bases` line.
  `_perf_selected` takes an optional pattern (default: the `PERF sim` one).

## Deviations from the plan
- **No `WATCH bases hash_bytes` line in the summary.** P96's request says to add it only if `WATCH sim hash_bytes` is in the summary. It is not: the job summary selects only `^PERF sim (units=|impl=native)` today, and every `WATCH` line stays in the verify log. So the base-arena watch line stays in the log too, and P93's test comment ("the line starts with `WATCH`, not `PERF `, so the job summary does not select it") still holds. Adding a `WATCH` line to the summary is a separate decision.
- The heading is on the new block only. The `PERF sim` block keeps no heading, because the row says its lines must show as before.
- Test change: the new checks sit in a private helper called from the existing test, not in a new test case. `test_ci_workflow.gd` already has 20 public functions, gdlint's maximum (`max-public-methods`), so a 21st failed lint. The helper also keeps the test name that `docs/plans/2026-10-11-phase-2.md` references (line 4942).

## Not in this PR
- A `WATCH` line in the summary (see Deviations).
- Any gate on the `PERF bases` lines: they stay report-only. P93b calibrates `[bases]` in `budget.cfg` from CI numbers.
- No change to the `PERF sim` selector, the other jobs' summaries (the Android jobs have their own "Job summary" steps) or any script.

Size: 10 production lines by `git diff --numstat 81c9b61` (`ci.yml` +10 −0), against the row's 20. The test is `tests/project/test_ci_workflow.gd` +51 −3; 64 changed lines in all.

## How it was verified
```
===== VERIFY SUMMARY =====
godot:  4.7.2.stable.official.ed1daf0bf
commit: 694eb29
FAILED: unit tests (gdUnit4)
```
- **Why it is red:** 1 of 3467 test cases failed (0 errors, 0 orphans): `res://tests/perf/test_sim_perf.gd:219`, "mean_ms 0.459 is above the budget 0.4575", the perf arena's native wall-clock mean, 0.3 % over. It ran while two other lanes ran Godot suites on the same machine. P96 does not touch that suite, and CI judges timings. Every other step passed: native build, gdformat, gdlint, import, clang-format and the sim smoke (3 matches of 1800 ticks, no dropped commands). The golden hash is 21ef133c89e9a99f, the base arena's a294900896cc6438, and the web export is OK.
- **Lane:** `bash scripts/run-tests.sh -a res://tests/project/test_ci_workflow.gd`: 20 of 20 passed, 0 orphans. The same suite fails (3 failures, one of them the summary test) against the old `ci.yml`, so it does pin the change.
- `gdformat --check` and `gdlint` are clean on the test file. `ci.yml` parses with `yaml.safe_load`.
- The two selectors, copied from `ci.yml`, were run with `grep -a -E` against an inline sample log holding both `PERF sim` lines, both `PERF bases` lines, the plain "no PERF bases impl=native line" note, both `WATCH ... hash_bytes` lines and an indented `PERF bases` line. The sim selector printed exactly the two `PERF sim` lines and the bases selector exactly the two `PERF bases` lines. The fallback text printed for a log without bases lines and for a missing log.
- Not checked in the session: the rendered summary. It is seen only on this PR's CI run. No timing or AI-vs-AI runs in the session.
- **Review (2 lenses, contract and shell/test correctness, on 694eb29):** no blocking finding. The contract lens matched the selector against the lines `perf_report.gd` and `test_base_arena_perf.gd` really print (also without the native library) and confirmed the `PERF sim` output is unchanged byte for byte; the shell lens traced `bash -eo pipefail` with no match, no log and a match. CI judges timings (no timing runs in a session). A read-only interaction review found no bug that appears only in the combination.

body:
# Gated batch integration — agent-infra, 2026-10-31

> **This PR is the batch's evidence and its landing unit.** It is not a hand-merge: it goes through the
> rail (`scripts/atomic-land.sh`), which requires a clean review recorded at THIS PR's head. What the
> rail lands is the tree the matrix already passed.

**Branch:** `integration/batch-20261031-16`
**Base:** `origin/main` at cut time — **unchanged** while the batch was assembled and tested (0 commits
behind at the last check), so the tested tree is the tree that will land.
**Decision record:** #3131. **Owner doctrine:** tortoise#10399 / `docs/ops/batch-integration.md`.
**Method:** one `--no-ff` merge per PR, ascending, each at its **live head**; the branch's own history
is the manifest — `git log --oneline origin/main..integration/batch-20261031-16` reads as one
`train: land #<N>` commit per constituent.

## The invariant

> `main` only ever receives a tree that has already passed the full suite.

The batch **is** the gate. A constituent PR's own CI was not consulted — eligibility was a **clean
review recorded at its live head** (`~/.pi/agent/reviews/daniel-ospina-agent-infra-<N>.json`,
`head_sha` == live `headRefOid`), verified per PR, and then the composition was audited after assembly
(merged sha == live head == recorded `head_sha`, verdict `clean`).

## Constituents — 15 PRs (16 merges; #3099 is two, its live head was merged after review)

| PR | reviewed head | what it does |
|---|---|---|
| #3040 | `a7dfc668e` | a private temp root per runner INSTANCE (#7815) |
| #3059 | `e86b34784` | — |
| #3095 | `11b1b3b69` | — |
| #3096 | `084434ce6` | reclaim an ORPHANED mergeclaim lock that names no pid |
| #3097 | `cb8d853c7` | re-pin the deploy-harness arms a rename and a deletion left stale |
| #3099 | `91a43d66e` | the shard list lived on STDIN; `</dev/null` + array materialisation (§ reviewed delta: `say`→`note`) |
| #3101 | `ae746e979` | grade the research contract by EFFECT |
| #3108 | `57065e33b` | deliver the uv cache+link-mode pin on every box |
| #3118 | `9f7d97460` | stop suppressing the dispatches a capped listing cannot answer for |
| #3122 | `3be41e425` | re-cut the sanctioned-script pin |
| #3129 | `680f53516` | re-run the required check when the ISSUE it reads changes |
| #3130 | `f6fd85cb9` | — |
| #3132 | `53fef58c8` | pin that tracker/report writes are NOT the dispatch floor |
| #3133 | `bbf93274a` | a LOST pin is UNKNOWN, and drift the farm cannot deliver is not a pass |
| #3139 | `a74fdca09` | run the full matrix on `integration/**`; keep the failure-filing job on `main` only |

## What the batch caught that per-PR review did not

- **#3114 was REVERTED OUT of the batch** (it was eligible at review time; the matrix, not the review, found this) after the matrix failed `sigpipe-grep-guard` (green on
  `main`): its new `scripts/check-portability-traps.test.sh` trips the repo's own
  `check-no-sigpipe-grep.sh` at four `printf … | grep -q` sites under `pipefail` — the #841/#861
  false-negative class, inside a guard asserting a guard. Doctrine says a culprit is **dropped, never
  fixed inside the batch**, so the revert is on the branch and the diagnosis is on the PR
  (issuecomment-6541878481).
- One composition conflict only: `MEMORY.md` at #3101, an **append-only** file where both sides added
  bullets → resolved as the UNION. A verifier then caught that the first splice had merged two entries
  onto one line and that a stray `|||||||` diff3 residual was carried in the file; both fixed and
  re-verified.

## The gate

- **Baseline, measured first** (doctrine Phase 1): `main`'s own completed ci-main run `41181932786`
  fails **`script-validate`** and **`extension-tests / unit-test`** → `BASELINE(script-validate,
  extension-tests/unit-test)`. Those two convict nobody in the batch; anything else is a new failure and
  does.
- **The matrix**: the `CI on main` workflow on this branch (its `integration/**` trigger is #3139, and is
  itself part of the batch — the batch supplies its own gate).
- **Verdict:** `BATCH-GREEN` / `BATCH-GREEN(BASELINE(ids))` / `BATCH-RED(ids)`. A carve-out-only run is
  never green.

## Landing

After this PR's own clean review record at its head: `scripts/atomic-land.sh <this PR>`. Then the 15
constituents are closed by `scripts/close-train-constituents.sh --apply BATCH_PR=<this PR>`, each comment
naming this PR and this branch. No raw push to `main`, no `--admin` bypass.

author: nomanali95
body:
**Problem** — When message-broker's pending setup runs on a new node (moving the broker), or on a reinstall or upgrade, it can overwrite the RabbitMQ credentials stored in Consul KV. `consul kv get` exits 1 both for a missing key and for any Consul error (403, agent unreachable, timeout). The setup script treated both as "no credentials". It created a new password, wrote it over the stored one when the write went through, and applied it to RabbitMQ even when the write failed. Components that cache the old password, such as videoserver, files and ws-collaboration, then cannot authenticate until they are restarted.

**Solution** — A password is only ever created in Consul KV, never overwritten, and a failed Consul write stops the setup before RabbitMQ is changed.

- `carbonio-message-broker-setup-users` writes a new password with `consul kv put -cas -modify-index=0`, so Consul only accepts it when the key does not exist yet
- any failed KV write exits 1 before calling `rabbitmqctl`, so the pending setup stays pending and can be rerun
- `setup_user` simplified in a separate commit, with no behaviour change

Tested on k3d against the current script: fresh install, broker move/reinstall, upgrade re-run, RabbitMQ/KV password drift, partial KV, Consul 403 or unreachable, failed KV read with a working KV write, and two concurrent runs. Stored credentials are never replaced, and consumers reconnect after a broker move without a restart.

**Impact** — Moving, reinstalling or upgrading message-broker keeps the existing credentials, so videoserver and the other consumers keep working. If Consul cannot be read or written, the pending setup now fails with "Cannot store a new password … aborting" instead of rotating the credentials silently. Rerun it once Consul is reachable.

author: pierreraybaut
body:
Closes #472.

### Problem

Since guidata and PlotPy icons are SVG files (#471), several DataLab icons were replaced by library icons with the same name: the delete icon of the object list (inline action) and of the history panel, the signal/image object icons, the Image panel icon, Edit, Rename, Histogram, Create > Square (PlotPy square marker instead of the square wave). `get_image_file_path` returned the first match in registration order, and libraries register their image paths before DataLab. Moreover, **Processing > Resize** already showed guidata's column resizing icon in DataLab 1.3.

### Fix

Relies on guidata 3.17.1 (PlotPyStack/guidata#132, PlotPyStack/guidata#134, merged into `develop`): the image paths registered last take precedence, ambiguous names emit an `ImageNameConflictWarning`, and `"module:filename"` (or `"package:path"`) designates an image explicitly. Also relies on DataLab-Platform/SigimaX#55 (merged into `develop`), which provides the HDF5 browser, signal/image and memory status icons.

- **Explicit designation** of ambiguous icons: `"datalab:delete.svg"`, `"datalab:edit.svg"`, `"datalab:rename.svg"`, `"datalab:resize.svg"`, `"datalab:histogram.svg"`, `"sigimax:image.svg"`, `"sigimax:signal.svg"`, `"sigimax:apply.svg"`, `"guidata:export.svg"` (including the dynamic panel icons of the welcome page)
- `create/square.svg` renamed to `square_wave.svg` (unrelated to PlotPy's square marker)
- **No more copies of SigimaX icons** (30 files): the 5 copies used by the documentation are moved to `doc/images/icons/` and the `.rst` files updated
- **Plugin icons** (`get_plugin_icon`: `PluginInfo.icon`, tools, welcome tiles) also accept `"module:filename"` images registered with guidata (e.g. `"datalab:delete.svg"`), consistently with guidata's image names; `doc/features/advanced/plugins.rst` (+ French translation) updated. The `datalab.plugins` contract modules (mirrored by DataLab-Web) are unchanged.
- **Tests**: `ImageNameConflictWarning` is an error in the test suite (`filterwarnings`); new `icons_unit_test.py`: icons requested by DataLab exist and are unambiguous, DataLab image file names are unique, no copy of guidata/PlotPy/SigimaX icons, explicit designations; `applications_dialog_test.py`: plugin icons with `"module:filename"`
- Release notes 1.4 (+ French translation)

### Tests

Full suite: 1300 passed, 3 skipped (with `ImageNameConflictWarning` as error). Resolved icons checked visually.

### Notes

As usual, the minimum versions (guidata ≥ 3.17.1, PlotPy ≥ 2.12.1, SigimaX ≥ 1.1.0) will be raised once these releases are published.

author: matthiasgrandl
body:
Refs #3971. This is the main cause of the app's CPU use while an agent is running, found while measuring #8378.

## Problem

The native status ring (`components/status-ring`) is the spinning indicator in the composer's "N working" pill, on agent status icons and in sidebar rows. It got its rotation from a UI-thread `requestAnimationFrame` clock that wrote a new value **every frame** while any ring was visible. With Reanimated on the new architecture, each write goes through `cloneShadowTreeWithNewProps` → commit → Yoga layout. So for as long as an agent works, the app re-commits and re-lays-out its shadow tree at the display's refresh rate.

A `sample` of the simulator app while an agent worked and nothing visible changed showed the non-idle time spent in `reanimated::cloneShadowTreeWithNewPropsRecursive`, Yoga pixel-grid rounding, `calculateShadowViewMutations` and Core Animation layer updates.

## Change

- `clock.native.ts` (moved from `clock.ts`, which now re-exports it, following the `text-input` pattern): each ring rotates with RN `Animated` and `useNativeDriver: true`. That updates the view's transform natively, with no React commit or layout per frame.
- **Phase sync preserved:** a ring starts at the shared wall-clock phase (`Date.now() % STATUS_RING_PERIOD_MS`) and loops one full turn from there, so rings that mount mid-flight are in step and the loop restart is seamless.
- **Hidden retained panels:** still don't animate. The loop only starts while `useRetainedPanelActive()` is true and stops on unmount.
- Web (`clock.web.ts` / `index.web.tsx`) is untouched.

## Measurements

Setup:
- iOS Simulator (iPhone 18 Pro, iOS 27.0), Release build (Hermes, no dev mode).
- The app was opened on a real, live orchestration agent session showing "1 working" and the composer spinner.
- Each run reinstalled the app, waited 30 s, then measured the process's cumulative CPU time over 180 s.
- Runs were interleaved so changes in the agent's activity show up as noise.

| Build | App CPU (% of one core) |
|---|---|
| `main` | 18.5 |
| `main`, ring and `SyncedLoader` clocks disabled | 1.2 |
| `main` again | 18.8 |
| `main`, only the ring clock disabled | 1.9 |
| **This PR (before file move)** | **5.2** |
| **This PR (final)** | **5.2** |
| `main` again | 19.9 |

So the ring accounted for about 17 of ~19 points. This PR cuts the app's CPU while an agent works by about 72%. The remaining ~3 points above a static ring is the native driver's per-frame tick. Moving the loop to Core Animation would cost about as much as a static ring, but it needs native code or global Reanimated flags (`IOS_CSS_CORE_ANIMATION` / `IOS_SYNCHRONOUSLY_UPDATE_UI_PROPS`), so I left it out.

I checked rotation by comparing two crops of the ring taken a moment apart: the arc had moved.

## Tests

- `clock.native.test.tsx` (new):
  - the ring uses the native driver, starting at the wall-clock phase and turning one period;
  - the loop stops on unmount;
  - a hidden retained ring never starts an animation.
- These tests target the new hook (`useStatusRingProgress`), so on `main` they fail because the hook doesn't exist, not on an assertion.
- `e2e/mobile/status-ring` (manual Android harness): the probe now counts native-driver updates through an `Animated` listener instead of a Reanimated reaction. The phase checks allow a 15° tolerance, because each ring now takes the phase at its own start instead of reading one shared value. **I could not run this harness** (it needs an Android emulator and `agent-device`).

```
npx vitest run --project unit src    # in packages/app
 Test Files  644 passed (644)
      Tests  6287 passed (6287)
```
Typecheck, oxlint, oxfmt and the lefthook pre-commit checks pass.

## Not tested

- **Physical devices:** no physical iPhone (no developer account) and no Android device or emulator. Absolute numbers are from Apple Silicon simulator hardware.
- **Android behaviour:** the native driver works the same way there, but it's unverified.
- **Battery:** not measured. CPU time is the proxy.

body:
Agents with **Let the AI greet** now always open the first reply of a conversation with a short welcome. Before, the greeting was only a line in the prompt, and later rules won ("Lead with the answer; no filler", "Open with a one-sentence answer", and "Skip pleasantries" for the Short tone), so the fast direct-answer model answered straight away. This showed up on a live agent right after #177 was released.

## Closes

- Bug in the greeting from yoshovski/chatwoot#177 (Huly CWAI-135).

## What changed

- On the first AI reply of a conversation with `greeting_mode: ai`, the reply schema gets a required `welcome` string ("one short, warm welcome sentence in the customer's language…; the response parts must not greet again"). Every other reply keeps the same schema as today.
- `ResponseParts.from_response` puts the welcome first, so it opens the first bubble (as its own paragraph) and is kept in the conversation history. It has no citations.
- The composer shifts `separate_parts` indexes by one when a welcome is present.
- The greeting prompt line now points at the `welcome` field.
- The direct route reuses the runner's reply schema instead of building its own copy, and `ResponseSchema.for` takes its flags as keyword options.

The fixed-message greeting already posted its own bubble from code and isn't affected.

## No migration

## How to test

1. Agent with Behavior → Conversation → Greeting: **Let the AI greet**.
2. New widget conversation, first message a real question (for example "How do I integrate your API with my server?") → the first bubble starts with a one-sentence welcome, then the answer.
3. Second question in the same conversation → no welcome.
4. Greeting **Off** → answers start directly, as before.

## Not verified

- No live model run; covered by specs (schema only on the first AI reply, welcome first in the parts and the bubble, `separate_parts` offset).

Automated re-pin of this repo's `skills.lock`, opened by
`scripts/bump-consumer-locks.sh` in [`Adam-S-Daniel/_agent-guidance`](https://github.com/Adam-S-Daniel/_agent-guidance).

**What moved:** `Adam-S-Daniel/adam-agentskills` —
`466d22e` → `4755ca0`.

**This pull request merges itself.** A later run of the same bumper sweeps it
and merges it with a merge commit once every check on it has concluded green —
or straight away where this repo runs no checks at all. It is not waiting for a
reviewer, so review it now if you mean to. It refuses to merge itself if
anything but `skills.lock` appears in the diff: push a second file onto this
branch and it becomes yours. Closing it is not a way to say no — the next run
proposes the same change again. See `docs/decisions/0006`.

The bundle content at the old ref no longer matches the registry's tree, which
is why this PR exists: a lock is not wrong for being old, but a lock pinned
before a skill changed delivers the older skill to every ephemeral session and
reports `OK` while doing it. `--check-current` says the two have diverged:

```
FAILED: the bundle has moved on since 466d22eb6166c5a085c1d9ec5b0d47ff85be97e8, which skills.lock still pins — nothing added or changed since then reaches an ephemeral surface. Re-pin it (after committing the content) with:
  python3 scripts/generate_skills_lock.py --repin -o skills.lock
  (Seeing this on a freshly merged branch usually means the re-pin was cut
  before another commit touched a locked skill: the lock is still faithful
  to the ref it pins — that ref just is not the bundle. Same fix, re-pin.)
  - changed: 'adam-coding-anywhere/skills-doctor' differs from its content at 466d22eb6166c5a085c1d9ec5b0d47ff85be97e8
```

**Every digest here is re-derived from the newly pinned commit**, materialized
with `git archive` — never from anyone's working tree — so the lock describes
bytes that are actually published at `4755ca0`.

This lock has no federated sources.

**Generated, never hand-edited.** The whole change is
`generate_skills_lock.py --repin`'s output. That command inherits this repo's own `registry`, `bundles` and `sources` from
the lock already committed here and re-resolves only `ref`; it cannot be told to change any of
them. Nothing
in `_agent-guidance` composes a lock of its own — see its
`docs/decisions/0005` and `docs/decisions/0009`.

author: axiomiccoreness
body:
**Depends on #166. Merge after #166.** This branch is based on `feat/llm-markdown-latex` (head `aed929c7`), so until #166 lands the diff against `main` also shows #166's two commits (`cddc77c`, `aed929c`). This PR adds only the last two commits (`9447615`, `501d2ec`). After #166 merges, the diff shrinks to those two.

## What it does
`HISTORY_BACKEND=jsonl` (the default) works exactly as before. `HISTORY_BACKEND=sqlite` stores the `/llm` history in SQLite (`src/llm_history_sqlite.py`):

- **Schema** (`PRAGMA user_version = 1`):
  - `sessions(id TEXT PK, name, created_at, updated_at, archived_at NULL)`, plus a unique index that allows one live row per name.
  - `messages(id INTEGER PK, session_id FK→sessions.id, role CHECK IN (user, assistant, system), content, format, thinking, model_label, ts, dedupe_key UNIQUE)`.
  - An index on `messages(session_id, id)`.
  - Timestamps are ISO 8601 in UTC with `+00:00`, the same as the JSONL `ts`.
- **Pragmas** on every connection: `journal_mode=WAL`, `foreign_keys=ON`, `busy_timeout` (`LLM_HISTORY_DB_BUSY_MS`, default 5000).
- **Same semantics as JSONL:**
  - The user turn is saved only together with a successful assistant reply, now in one `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` transaction.
  - The window still goes through `trim_history`, with the same `LLM_HISTORY_MAX_TOKENS` result.
  - `/llm reset` sets `archived_at` and deletes nothing. A new live session then starts under the same name.
  - `/llm status` gains a final history line with the backend and counts. This applies to JSONL too.
  - `thinking` is never sent back to the model.
- **Never exits.** Each call opens a connection under a per-file lock and closes it before returning, so an idle bridge holds no handle. If the DB is locked or deleted, that one call logs a warning and returns empty, the reply is still shown, and the next message reopens the file (recreating the schema if needed). There is no `sys.exit` or `os._exit`, and a test checks for that.
- **Importer:** `python -m src.history_import --from jsonl --to sqlite [--src] [--db] [--skip-stubs] [--json]`.
  - Runs as one transaction and is idempotent: the dedupe key is sha256 of session + ts + role + content, so a rerun inserts nothing, even after a reset.
  - Never writes the source; it checks the source's sha256 before and after.
  - Imports everything by default. With `--skip-stubs` it skips the complete `what is the brain doing?` / `Lane L3 is busiest.` stub pairs.
- **Docs:** new `serving/HISTORY_BACKENDS.md` (not `serving/README.md`, because #163 edits that file). It also notes that a MariaDB backend can implement the same `load` / `append_pair` / `archive` / `stats` / `import_rows` interface later.

## Existing SQLite reused
`rg -n "sqlite3|\.sqlite|\.db\b"` finds only `mesh_modal.py` and `witness_compiler.py`, plus the `witness_chain.db` ledger file. None of them relates to the bridge or chat. Their patterns are reused here:
- From `mesh_modal.py`: an env-var path override, a `threading.Lock` with a short-lived connection per call, `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` on first use, and soft failure.
- From `witness_compiler.py`: `FOREIGN KEY` and ISO text timestamps.

WAL, busy_timeout and user_version are new. Neither existing module uses them.

## Enable
```bash
cd sovereign-irc-bridge
python -m src.history_import --from jsonl --to sqlite \
  --src /workspace/bridge-serving/llm_history.jsonl --db /workspace/bridge-serving/llm_history.sqlite3
HISTORY_BACKEND=sqlite LLM_HISTORY_DB=/workspace/bridge-serving/llm_history.sqlite3  # then restart the bridge
```
The running bridge was **not** switched.

## Tests
`src/test_llm_history_sqlite.py` has 19 offline tests, all under `tmp_path`. They cover:
- the window (matching JSONL trimming at several budgets)
- separate sessions
- reset/archive
- status
- atomicity when the model fails and when the assistant insert fails mid-pair (via a trigger)
- a locked DB, which fails softly and recovers
- a deleted DB, which is recreated
- an unopenable path, which never raises
- refusing a newer schema
- idempotent import, including after a reset, with the source sha unchanged
- `--skip-stubs`
- the CLI under `python -I`
- a Unicode and LaTeX round trip

The autouse fixture reuses #166's tripwire on `DEFAULT_HISTORY_PATH` and its `.sqlite3` sibling. It also asserts that the live JSONL and DB mtimes are unchanged.

The existing fixtures in `test_llm_chat.py` and `test_llm_backend.py` now also clear `HISTORY_BACKEND` and `LLM_HISTORY_DB`. `test_deepinfer_status`'s `/llm status` test now points history at `tmp_path` and expects the one extra history line, still checked as an exact list match.

Dry run on a copy of the live JSONL (210 rows, 84 stub pairs): 210 inserted by default, 0 on rerun (210 duplicates), and 42 with `--skip-stubs`.

Signed-off-by: Clarke Yoursa Tee <mrteanotcoffee@gmail.com>

body:
Milestone 7 (docs/ARCHITECTURE.md section 13): the review screen, corrections, line-item add and delete, live re-check, check ticks, approval, reopen, type change, the document's history, the phone layout and single-document delete.

Closes #32

## What changed

**Migration** `supabase/migrations/20261031131351_review.sql` (new; no existing migration edited):
- `check_ticks` table: RLS on, `revoke all`, select for members, no client writes.
- `extraction_fields`: column grant `update (corrected_value)` to `authenticated`, policy `extraction_fields_update` (member, document `needs_review`), trigger `set_correction_audit()` (sets `corrected_by`/`corrected_at`; cuts a corrected `card_last4`/`account_number_last4`/`iban_last4` to four characters, OQ-29).
- Client RPCs, each `security definer`, `search_path = ''`, execute for `authenticated` only: `add_line_item(document_id, after_position)`, `delete_line_item(document_id, line_position)` (named `line_position` because `position` is a reserved word; ARCHITECTURE.md updated), `set_check_ticked`, `reopen_document`, `change_document_type`, `get_amount_tolerance`.
- Service-role functions (invoker): `approve_document(document_id, actor, result)` and `delete_document(document_id)`.
- Helpers with no grants, called by the RPCs as their owner: `line_item_fields`, `line_item_count`, `shift_line_items`, `lock_document_for_review`.
- `document_events.kind` check widened to add `extracted` (drop and re-add of the check constraint, a strict superset); `record_extraction` replaced with the same signature and one added insert of an `extracted` event; existing extracted documents get the event of their last extraction. The history needs it (criterion 7); the upload entry is the document row itself.
- Lead ruling 1: `change_document_type` clears `duplicate_key` and `duplicate_of`. Ruling 2: `approve_document` re-runs U1 against the database with the corrected key and updates both.

**Edge Function** `supabase/functions/approve-document/` (new): `approve.ts` (pure steps behind deps, unit-tested), `index.ts`, `deno.json`. Re-runs the type's checks on the corrected values with `recheck` from the new `shared/doctypes/review.ts` (the same function the browser runs), then `approve_document` does U1, the upserts and the approval in one transaction, refusing with 409 naming unticked failures, and refusing if a value changed meanwhile. Non-member: 404.

**Next.js**
- `DELETE /api/documents/[id]` (`src/app/api/documents/[id]/route.ts`, logic in `src/lib/documents/delete.ts`), as ARCHITECTURE 6.2: RLS read as the caller (404 otherwise, 401 signed out), Storage removal, then `delete_document`.
- `src/lib/supabase/server.ts`: `createServiceRoleClient()`, throws when `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` is unset (server-only module).
- Review route `src/app/(app)/documents/[id]/`: `page.tsx` (server read, not-found for non-members / missing / deleted documents, a short notice for Queued, Waiting, Processing and Failed per ruling 3), `not-found.tsx`, `review-screen.tsx`, `document-viewer.tsx`.
- `src/lib/documents/review.ts` (corrections model, live re-check with U1 kept as stored, flag order and reasons, labels), `src/lib/documents/load-review.ts`.
- Document list: the file name links to the review screen for Needs review, Approved and Not supported; each row has an icon-only delete button with a confirmation naming the file (`delete-document.tsx`). The button sits in the Pages cell so every cell's text and the name cell's accessible name stay exactly as the existing specs read them.
- `src/components/ui/checkbox.tsx`: shadcn/ui's checkbox, written by hand.
- `src/types/pdfjs-worker.d.ts`: a module declaration for pdf.js's worker module, which ships no types.

**New dependency**: `pdfjs-dist` 4.10.38, pinned exactly. It draws every page of a PDF on a canvas so all pages are shown and zoomable (US-5.1 AC-1); headless Chromium has no built-in PDF viewer, and an iframe could neither show nor prove every page. It runs on the main thread (importing its worker module sets `globalThis.pdfjsWorker`), so no worker file is served; a document has at most 10 pages. Its lockfile entries include the optional `@napi-rs/canvas`, which is only for Node and is not used. `npm audit` shows the same 16 moderate findings as on main.

**Tests and mock**
- `tests/access/review.test.ts` (31 tests), `tests/access/functions.test.ts` (every new function's security mode, search path and exact grants; `check_ticks` has RLS; the correction trigger).
- Unit: `shared/doctypes/review.test.ts`, `src/lib/documents/review.test.ts`, `supabase/functions/approve-document/approve.test.ts`, plus cases in `src/lib/documents/upload.test.ts` (`isReviewable`) and `src/lib/supabase/server.test.ts` (service-role client).
- Playwright: `e2e/review.spec.ts` (each flow at 360px and on a desktop) with `e2e/support/review.ts`, which stores documents as `record_extraction` leaves them; two type-change tests added to `e2e/extraction.spec.ts` (they need the pipeline, so they run in the extraction project). `e2e/mock-claude/`: a document `Scanned slip.png` that is Not supported when detected, plus an `asChosen` answer per tool, so a request that sends only `record_receipt` gets the receipt fixture whatever the call order.

**Docs**: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md (sections 3, 4.1, 4.2, 5, 6.1, 6.2) and docs/go-live.md (a "Review, approval and delete" section: deploying `approve-document` with JWT verification, the delete route's use of `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY`, and checks to run in production).

## How it was tested

Locally, on a fresh `npx supabase db reset` (every migration replays):
- `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`: clean.
- `npm test`: 30 files, 383 tests passed.
- `npm run test:access`: 16 files, 257 tests passed.
- `npm run build`: passed.
- `npm run test:e2e`: 84 tests passed (all specs, both projects).
- `~/work/ai-hq/scripts/agent-ready.sh .`: AGENT-READY.

Each new test was seen failing first:
- Unit: with the new modules removed and main's `upload.ts` and `server.ts`, all 5 files fail.
- Access: with the new migration removed and the database reset to main's migrations, 29 of the 31 review access tests and the 28 new function-rule rows fail (the 2 that pass assert refusals that already hold on main, such as no client update of `extracted_value`).
- Playwright: with main's `src/app/(app)/documents` and no `src/app/api`, all 15 tests in `e2e/review.spec.ts` fail, and the type-change test in `e2e/extraction.spec.ts` fails at the link to the review screen.

## Noticed, not changed

- **Pages of a type-changed Needs review document.** Its pages stay counted (`pages_reserved` true) and no further pages are counted, as the issue says. But if its new extraction then fails, `record_extraction` releases them, and if it is deleted while queued, `delete_document` releases them: either way pages that a successful extraction had counted are refunded. The issue does not cover this; it may want a ruling.
- **The review screen does not subscribe to Realtime.** It reads again after each approval, reopen or refused change; a change another member makes meanwhile is caught by the RPCs' status checks and by `approve_document` comparing the values it checked. ARCHITECTURE.md section 3 now says so.
- **A correction made at the same instant as an approval.** The update policy reads the document's status without locking it, so a correction committed in the moment after `approve_document` commits could land on an approved document. The window is a single concurrent transaction.
- **Local edge runtime.** After a function's files change, or after `supabase db reset`, the local edge runtime can answer 503 `BOOT_ERROR` until `npx supabase stop` and `npx supabase start`. Local only; CI starts the stack fresh.
- The PR title came from the branch name, because `--fill` with several commits takes it from there.

author: danialrostamani
body:
Replaces the GitHub-token install from #21 with an **install password** the owner chooses.

## How it works
- **Private:** the source repository and its releases.
- **Public:** [`drnetwork-dist`](https://github.com/Danialrostamani/drnetwork-dist), which holds per release:
  - `s-ui-linux-amd64.tar.gz.enc`: the archive encrypted with the install password (AES-256-CBC, PBKDF2-SHA256, 600000 rounds, salted);
  - `password-check.enc`: a known short text encrypted the same way, so a wrong password is rejected before the large download;
  - `SHA256SUMS` of the plain archive, which `install.sh` now requires and checks after decrypting;
  - `install.sh` and `s-ui.sh`.

  Anyone can download these; nothing installs without the password.

**Release workflow:** the `publish` job encrypts and publishes to the dist repository after the private release is uploaded. It fails with a clear error if `DRN_INSTALL_PASSWORD` is not set.

**`install.sh`:**
- Finds the latest tag from the `/releases/latest` redirect (no API, no rate limit).
- Gets the password from `DRN_PASSWORD`, the saved file, or a hidden prompt (three tries on a terminal; unattended runs use only the saved one).
- `openssl` reads the password from a file descriptor, never from its arguments.
- Saves the password root-only in `/etc/drnetwork/install-password`.

**`s-ui.sh`:** downloads from the dist repository. `s-ui password` replaces the saved password after the check file accepts it.

**Panel update:** looks the release up in the dist repository and runs that release's `install.sh` unattended, which decrypts with the saved password.

**Panel, node and README commands:** download the script to a file and run it: `(f=$(mktemp) && curl -fsSL -o "$f" …/drnetwork-dist/releases/latest/download/install.sh && bash "$f" …)`.

## Checked locally
- Encrypting with the workflow's settings and decrypting with `install.sh`'s round-trips byte for byte.
- A local stand-in for the dist repository (redirect included): `latest_tag`, the password from `DRN_PASSWORD` and from the saved file, the decrypted archive passing its checksum, the saved file `0600`.
- A wrong password, unattended, exits 1 with "Wrong install password".
- On a pty, a wrong then a right password is accepted on the second try without echoing.
- Frontend: lint, `vue-tsc`, 238 tests, build.

## Before the first release
1. Create the public repository `Danialrostamani/drnetwork-dist`, initialized with a README so it has a branch.
2. Add repository secrets here:
   - `DRN_INSTALL_PASSWORD`: the install password;
   - `DIST_TOKEN`: a fine-grained token with Contents read and write on `drnetwork-dist` only. GitHub uses it when publishing; servers never see it.

author: andig
body:
Fix #35621

On plain H3 (H3_SET, FW Master 2.23) hold failed with `exception '2' (illegal data address), function '16'`. The only function 16 write in the hold sequence is Remote Active Power (44002), which this firmware rejects.

Hold now mirrors the `fox-ess-h3-smart` approach (#34363):
- hold: Remote Enable (44000) = 0, Work Mode (41000) = Self Use, max discharge current (41008) = 0
- normal and charge: restore 41008 from the new `maxdischargecurrent` param (A, default 26 = H3 factory setting)

Using plain Self Use with a discharge limit also avoids the PV curtailment seen on H3-Pro/Smart with a 0 W remote target.

Not changed: charge mode still uses remote control (44002). On H3_SET it likely fails the same way, but whether grid charge is possible at all on this firmware is still open in the issue.

Untested on hardware. @eichler82 offered to test, please verify that 41008 = 0 stops discharge on FW 2.23.

author: jposluns
body:
On main, the Verify section of workflow-orchestrators.md is one block that pastes the `ss` inventory and the Prefect, Dagster, Airflow, Temporal, Flower, Flower socket, Argo and direct-origin checks together. Every part ends in a labelled `|| echo`, so the block always reports status 0, including after a finding, a failed command or a guard refusal. This change splits it into nine blocks, one per product or vantage, because the parts are independent and one product's result should never hide another's.

Each block now runs in one outer subshell that turns errexit off, records every classified result and every failed command in it, and exits once under CONTRIBUTING.md rule 6. The statuses are 0 for a pass or for an observation the block says it cannot classify, 1 for a finding, 2 for a guard refusal and 3 for a failed or inconclusive check. A finding outranks an inconclusive result, which outranks a refusal, and each block's last line says what it leaves for the reader to judge.

The 2026-10-31 status rulings, which rule 6 records since #1106, are applied. The Prefect, Airflow and Argo credential helpers now give status 2 when `python3` is missing or the reader's input is empty or, for Argo, not a valid token. A prompt that fails after those checks gives status 3; its existing "credential helper failed; not probing" message is kept. The inventory checks that `ss` is installed before it runs and, if it is not, prints `ss is not installed here; not listing sockets` and exits 2; an `ss` that runs and fails still gives 3.

The Prefect, Airflow, Flower and Argo blocks parse each JSON answer with `python3` and check the shape or field their discriminator names, instead of matching substrings. Legal JSON whitespace, such as a list followed by a newline, is accepted, and a malformed or unexpected body, including one from an authorized positive control, is inconclusive. If `python3` is missing when an answer needs parsing, that answer is not classified and the block records 2.

- Inventory: `ss -tlnp` is read and judged; the block exits 3 if `ss` fails and 2 if `ss` is not installed.

- Prefect: the anonymous call passes on 401 and is a finding when it returns a JSON list. The authorized call must return a JSON list of flow objects, and any other answer is inconclusive.

- Dagster: an anonymous RepositoryConnection read is a finding, a PythonError or GraphQL error is inconclusive, and any other answer, such as a proxy's 401, is left for the reader. Against the origin it reports 0 only for an answer it cannot classify: an isolated origin exits 3 and a reachable Dagster answers the query, since it has no login; sent to the proxy URL, a 401 or login redirect exits 0 and is left for the reader.

- Airflow: the host guard keeps its refusals, and if `tr` fails while lowercasing the host name, the block says so and exits 3 before any probe. A nonempty access_token for the documented airflow/airflow account is a finding, the valid-account comparison must obtain a nonempty access_token or the block records 3, and the anonymous pools read is left for the reader.

- Temporal: a listing without credentials is a finding and any error is inconclusive. The block says it cannot report 0, because a rejection and a TLS or namespace error both make `temporal` exit nonzero.

- Flower: an anonymous dashboard (2xx) or worker list, a JSON object whose values are worker objects, is a finding; 401 is the pass, and a 302 is left for the reader to follow into the login flow.

- Flower socket directory: a mode that grants anything to other, or a named user: or group: access entry whose permissions include x, is a finding. The directory gets its own `stat`, so a missing socket records 3 without skipping the directory's mode check. Owners, numeric IDs and the socket's own mode are left for the reader.

- Argo: the anonymous call passes on 401 and is a finding when it returns a workflow list, a JSON object with a metadata object and an items list or null; a 403, redirect, 404 or 5xx is inconclusive. The authorized call must return HTTP 200 with a workflow list.

- Direct origin: any HTTP answer is a finding, read from the HTTP code curl reports rather than from its exit status, so a transfer that fails after the response, such as curl exit 18, is still a finding. With no HTTP response the block records 3, and it says it cannot report 0, because from the untrusted vantage the fixed state and a local DNS, TLS or connection failure look the same.

Captured output and statuses are held in positional parameters. Statuses are taken through `if` conditions and `||` lists or, after each nested credential subshell and in the Airflow token and getfacl checks, read from `$?` on the next line with errexit off, so an inherited `readonly` or `declare -i` variable or `set -e` cannot change a result. The five `) || echo "<label>: block exit $?; continuing"` lines are removed, and every other existing printed message is kept, except the two Airflow token responses, which can carry an issued access token, so those requests now print only curl's write-out line, and only after curl exits 0. The kept messages include the eleven `exited nonzero; continuing` messages; flower-stat's now follows either of its two `stat` calls. The new lines are the FINDING, inconclusive, unclassified-observation, "credential input refused", "python3 not found", `ss is not installed here; not listing sockets`, Airflow host-check failure and `block exit` lines.

Each block has its own REASONED declaration: the paragraph before it, or for the origin block the paragraph after it. The claim-registry `verify` lists move from `[1]` to `[1]` through `[9]`, one claim per block, with every claim's text unchanged. The Verify introduction keeps its earlier run records, says they covered single-block forms, and says the current form is covered by the gate's bash -n and ShellCheck passes and by stub runs of every block made while drafting. It also says that the Airflow token print lines, which show only curl's write-out line after curl exits 0 and otherwise a fixed message, and the Airflow block's opening trap reset and `set +x +a +e` changed after those runs and are covered by the gate passes and by later stub runs. This closes the workflow-orchestrators.md part of follow-up row 11. The guide has no entry in `tools/bracket_ranges_allow.txt` or `tools/verify_marking_baseline.txt`.

`VERSION` and `plugin/plugin.json` are bumped to this pull request's number unless main is already higher, in which case they stay at main's value.

Both Airflow token requests now print only curl's write-out line, because each response body can carry an issued access token, and the Airflow block clears inherited traps and turns tracing off before either token is captured. If curl exits nonzero, including when it stops before writing that line, the request prints a fixed inconclusive message that names curl's exit status and shows none of the response, then its existing exited-nonzero message, and records 3 without lowering a finding. If curl exits 0 without that line, the request prints a fixed no-write-out message instead and records 3 in the same way.

Checks: `tools/run_all_checks.sh` passed on staged tree e1a0911c, the tree committed as 9db14682, with only the two advisory SKIPs (local Python 3.14.4 against CI's pinned 3.14.7, and AIQT hooks not activated).

author: johnhck
body:
## V0.3 V3, phase V3b: new entries, changes, third-party ACL and processes after the plan

Tests and docs only. **No change in `src/` or `tools/`.** The four gates stay `$false`. B1, RECENT and eligibility are
unchanged. No real ACL or machine setting is touched.

### Mechanism (same as V3a)
- The CI-only harness runs against the installed engine with the real lock, the real T1 log file, and the real
  revalidation and runtime evidence.
- **Windows of the attack:**
  - before the plan;
  - in the harness's own confirmation reader, before the final phrase;
  - in `-BeforeDeleteHook`, before the revalidation;
  - in the deleter wrapper, which calls the real `AtmDeleter` with the engine's own arguments: either before the call,
    or inside `afterPinning` (J1).
- **Each case asserts:** its code for its leg, the log read back from the file, the number of `intent` records, and
  that nothing outside the planned root and the declared attack changed. The new roots are planted with the V3a ones,
  so the phase snapshot covers them.
- **Process churn:** if new processes on the runner cause a refusal before the attack ran, the case is retried and the
  retry is explained, as in V2 and V3a.

### Cases (contract sections 4.3 and 4.4)
| Case | Window | Expected |
|---|---|---|
| N1 file added | preview → clean | `ALTERADO_DESDE_O_PREVIEW`, both legs |
| N2 file added | plan → final confirmation | `PLAN_CHANGED_BEFORE_EXECUTION`, the new file intact |
| N3 | confirmation → revalidation | V2's P8 (already integrated) |
| N4 file added | revalidation → deleter | `PLAN_DIFFERS_FROM_VALIDATED_MEASUREMENT`, `REFUSED`, nothing attempted |
| N5 file created in a pinned folder | inside the deleter | measured: {created → `PARTIAL` (`DELETE_DIR_FAILED`), the file intact; refused → `COMPLETE`} |
| N6 planned file changed | inside the deleter | `FILE_CHANGED_AFTER_PLANNING`, `PARTIAL`, the changed file intact |
| N7 write keeping every statistic | — | `NOT_TESTED` by design (no content hash), declared as a case |
| N8 hard link to a sentinel outside the root | before the plan | `COMPLETE`; the sentinel intact (same SHA-256); the link count is not checked |
| A1 write for `Users` on the root | before clean | `ESCRITA_CONCEDIDA_A_TERCEIROS` in **both** legs (see note) |
| A2 the same | plan → final confirmation | `PLAN_CHANGED_BEFORE_EXECUTION` (statistics unchanged; the gate refuses) |
| A3 the same | confirmation → revalidation | `REVALIDATION_REFUSED` (ACL; in leg A also `B1_EXCEPTION_NO_LONGER_APPLIES`) |
| A4 the same | inside the deleter | measured: `COMPLETE`. **Limit proven:** the ACL is not read again once pinned (SECURITY-MODEL) |
| P1 process of this account naming the root | confirmation → revalidation | `REVALIDATION_REFUSED` (use observed) |
| P2 process of another account (leg A) | confirmation → revalidation | `REVALIDATION_REFUSED` with `B1_EXCEPTION_NEW_UNINSPECTABLE_PROCESS` |
| P3 the same (leg A) | plan → final confirmation | `PLAN_CHANGED_BEFORE_EXECUTION` |

**Correction to the contract (A1):** the contract expected "A: B1 itself". In fact the V0.1 ACL gate runs before the B1
gate and is not cut short the way the lock probe is, so leg A shows `ESCRITA_CONCEDIDA_A_TERCEIROS` too. The case asserts
the code observed in the code path.

**ACE (J4):** the only ACE added is one explicit, non-inherited ACE for `Users`, on a root planted in that run. The
function checks the planted root and its nonce first. A4 adds the same ACE on the root that the deleter has pinned.

**P2/P3:** before leg A, the e2e starts a watcher of the runner account. Its script lives in the runner's temp folder,
which the test user cannot change. Leg A asks through a file in a signal folder. The watcher then starts one fixed
command (`Start-Sleep 40`), confirms it, and the command ends by itself. The watcher itself ends on a stop file or a
45-minute deadline. Nothing is ever terminated.

### Suite
A new static case checks that:
- the cases are present and inside the phase snapshot;
- the ACE is added only after the planted-root check, and `Set-Acl` appears nowhere else;
- the watcher runs only its fixed command, has a bounded lifetime, never terminates a process, never reads the
  content of a request, and keeps its script outside the test user's folder.

### Docs
- `TESTING.md`: new V3b section.
- `ROADMAP.md` and `CHANGELOG.md`.
- `SECURITY-MODEL.md`: ACL after pinning, and hard links.

### CI results
Run 41207636280 (head `488eedb`, code and tests): every job passed (16/16), CodeQL included.

**Leg A** (the summary counts every V3 case, V3a and V3b):
- **5 of the 6 `install e2e` jobs:** V3 37 PASS / 0 FAIL / 1 NOT_TESTED. The NOT_TESTED case is N7, by design.
- **windows-11-arm/powershell:** 36 PASS / 2 NOT_TESTED. A4 was also NOT_TESTED there: process churn of the runner
  refused all 3 attempts before the attack ran, each explained by new identities, and nothing was deleted.

**Leg B:** V3 10 PASS / 28 NOT_TESTED. The coverage measured incomplete, so ELIGIBLE was unreachable. N1 and A1 passed in
leg B as well.

**Suite:** 319 PASS / 0 FAIL / 3 NAO_TESTADO on PowerShell 5.1, pwsh and ARM64 powershell; 303 / 0 / 3 on the ARM64
pwsh subset. The new V3b static case passed everywhere.

**Measured, with the same result on every image:**
- N5: the file **was created** in the pinned folder, and the run stopped as `PARTIAL` (`DELETE_DIR_FAILED`) with the new
  file intact.
- A4: the ACE **was applied** inside the deleter and the deletion completed (`COMPLETE`). This proves the limit; see
  SECURITY-MODEL.
- P2/P3: the watcher confirmed the process of another account each time, which gave
  `B1_EXCEPTION_NEW_UNINSPECTABLE_PROCESS` and `PLAN_CHANGED_BEFORE_EXECUTION`.
- P1: `ACTIVE_EVIDENCE` plus `B1_EXCEPTION_NO_LONGER_APPLIES`.

A follow-up commit (`8d61787`) labels the V3 counts by phase (`V3 (V3a+V3b)`) and records the N5 outcome in TESTING. Its
run is linked in the checks.

### NOT_TESTED and limits
- N7, by design.
- Leg B in-deleter cases, and P2/P3 in leg B: its coverage is incomplete, and P2/P3 are a leg A case.
- N5 and A4 measure the Windows behaviour of the runner image.
- V3c (deleter outcomes, log, interruption, concurrency, shared bases) is next.

author: bwbensonjr
body:
## Summary

Elo treated the higher score as the winner in every sport. In cross country the lower score wins, and golf mixes stroke play (lower wins) with match play and points formats (higher wins), varying by conference. Those ratings rewarded losses: girls cross country ranked Framingham first with a 0-10 record.

- **`SCORE_ORDER`** in `high_school_elo.py` sets which score wins per sport:
  - `higher` (default): home minus visitor score; every other sport is unchanged.
  - `lower`: cross country.
  - `outcome`: golf. The scores don't reveal the format, so the recorded `home_outcome` decides.

  Rating updates and `actual_point_spread` use this home margin.
- **`Elo(margin_of_victory=False)`** and `update_ratings_margin`: golf margins can't be compared across formats, so golf is rated on wins and losses only and `pred_point_spread` is NaN.
- **Calibration** uses the same margins. Recalibration results:
  - Boys cross country: `home_field` 20, refit spread.
  - Boys golf: `k`=100, `home_field`=50, `season_regression`=0.1; holdout log loss 0.543 → 0.487.
  - Girls cross country: keeps its current values, which still win on the corrected data.
- **Reports** leave a missing spread blank instead of printing `nan`.
- **Site** verdict tags orient each margin by the recorded winner.
- Cross country and golf results are regenerated.

### Data note

Across about 60,000 games in the other sports there is one record where the score and the recorded outcome disagree: Hanover 0, Plymouth South 1 in field hockey on 2026-10-21, recorded as a Hanover win. Elo keeps using the score for higher-wins sports. The site bolds the winner from the outcome, and its verdict now agrees with that.

## Results (2026 season games)

| Sport | Games | Log loss | Picked winner |
|---|---|---|---|
| Boys cross country | 334 | 1.400 → 0.518 | 25.7% → 74.0% |
| Girls cross country | 311 | 1.695 → 0.419 | 18.3% → 81.0% |
| Boys golf | 1,455 | 1.076 → 0.495 | 39.0% → 76.6% |
| Girls golf | 70 | 0.544 → 0.580 | 75.7% → 74.3% |

Girls cross country is now led by Billerica (10-0).

## Test plan

- [x] Field hockey, boys soccer, and football regenerated: game-level results files are byte-identical
- [x] Site verdict tags match an independent calculation for cross country, field hockey, and golf (no verdicts)
- [x] Existing 35 Playwright site checks pass
- [ ] After merge: Deploy Site succeeds and live cross country rankings show the corrected order

author: programadorkevinsvega-sys
body:
## Summary

Implement Phase 6.7.3 as an independent, experimental MongoDB document mapper / ODM over RustFlow's existing MongoDB adapter. The implementation is accepted by CI on the exact final PR head `659f1750d611e57315263216167d43375da23574` (2026-10-31). This PR remains Draft, open and unmerged; it does not close the global Phase 6.7 maturity gate.

## Architecture and boundaries

- ADR 0021 selects an explicit Serde/BSON Data Mapper using the `DocumentModel` trait and typed `DocumentField<T>` descriptors.
- Reuses `MongoDatabase`, the existing official `mongodb = 3.6.0` client and its BSON re-export. No second client/pool, external ODM, DNS SRV resolver, or SeaORM dependency is added.
- MongoDB remains document-oriented: BSON documents, `_id`, MongoDB-native filters/updates, indexes, embedded documents, explicit references and MongoDB session/transaction behavior.
- No SQL joins, SQL migrations, SeaORM entities, lazy reference loading, implicit cascades or global identity map.

## Implemented API

- `DocumentModel`, `DocumentField<T>`, `DocumentRepository<M>`, `DocumentFilter`, `DocumentQuery`, `DocumentUpdate` and typed operation outcomes.
- CRUD, bounded ordered/unordered insert-many, upsert, count/exists, replace/update/delete operations, typed projections and aggregation outputs.
- BSON filters/operators with field-path and overlapping-update validation; updates to immutable `_id` paths are rejected before sending the operation.
- ID consistency checks, safe generated-`ObjectId` compatibility validation, and explicit custom-ID behavior.
- Index bootstrap verification compares declared index names, ordered key documents and uniqueness. Other index options are not claimed.
- Explicit session-aware insert/find/update/delete methods; MongoDB transaction commit ambiguity remains identifiable through `MongoError::is_unknown_transaction_commit_result()`.
- Safe public error mapping and bounded operation behavior while preserving the driver's native collection API as an escape hatch.

## Integration evidence

MongoDB 7.0.45 CI coverage runs against both:
- A single-node replica set for real transaction commit and abort.
- A standalone server to verify rejection of multi-document transaction writes.

The suite also covers CRUD/bulk behavior, filters and updates, projections and aggregation, generated/custom IDs, duplicate keys, partial bulk failures, missing/null/default semantics, embedded documents, nested dotted-path filters and nested projection DTOs.

## Acceptance record — 2026-10-31

All required workflows passed on the exact final PR head `659f1750d611e57315263216167d43375da23574`:
- Rust checks (1.85): format, Clippy, workspace tests, MySQL/MariaDB integration, MongoDB integration, CLI smoke, benchmark smoke, Rustdoc/documentation build.
- Rust checks (stable): the same checks, all successful.
- WebAssembly target check.
- Browser E2E and bundle-size check.
- Documentation site build.
- Governance checks.
- Dependency review.

The roadmap, README, ADR 0020/0021, technical database reference and public website guides/status pages record the accepted subphase and its experimental boundaries.

## Deliberate limitations

- `DocumentModel` is trait-based; this PR does not claim a procedural model derive.
- The application maintains the mapping between `DocumentField<T>` paths and Serde field names.
- The typed index surface currently manages ordered keys and uniqueness only; TTL, sparse, partial, collation and other options are not claimed.
- Session-aware methods cover a documented subset; not every repository operation has a session variant.
- Bulk writes are not all-or-nothing; driver errors may describe partial application. A caller timeout does not prove a write was not applied.
- The API remains experimental and pre-1.0.

## Remaining global Phase 6.7 work

Phase 6.7.3 is accepted, but the global phase remains open. The advanced SQL relation/loading extensions in 6.7.4, generated CRUD application in 6.7.5, and global quality/compatibility gate in 6.7.6 remain separate work. Phase 6.7.2 is already merged in `main` through PR #59.

author: kingleosgold
body:
Found by the Claude review of the whole batch since 99331f8 (#141 to #153), which came back clean in 1 round with this one P3. The P3 was already in 99331f8.

## The bug
A sync that finds no row for a queued holding marks it rowless, and Sign Out's unsent count then treats that delete as settled. A list delete that was still out (a lookup that throws, a send that errors, or an earlier add it outwaited) went back on the queue unsent. But it only cleared the holding's marks when its first queue write had failed. A mark the sync set in the meantime stayed, so Sign Out didn't ask, the queue was cleared, and the holding could come back if its row landed later.

## The fix
`sendListDelete` now clears the holding's rowless marks (same user, metal and local id) whenever the delete ends up queued. That includes the case where the retry write fails but the first one stands. Clearing a mark can only raise Sign Out's count, so the worst case is an extra prompt. A delete that can't be queued at all still puts the holding back and leaves the marks alone. The App.js comment on the count now says so.

## Tests
Three new tests in listDelete.test.mjs, one for each path: the earlier-writes timeout, a failed send whose retry write fails, and a lookup that throws. In each one a sync marks the holding while the delete is out. All three fail on main. `npm test`: 666 pass.

## Claude review
Clean after 3 rounds.
- Round 1 was clean. Its first P3 was the same bug through a failed retry write, so the clear moved under `if (queued)`, and a findRow-throws test was added.
- Round 2 was clean but found that one new test never made its retry write fail. That test was rewritten to go through a failed send, and the App.js comment was updated.
- Round 3 was clean.

Filed as follow-ups:
- (P3, pre-existing) The sync's `withoutDeletes(queue, rowlessDone)` can still take off an entry that a list delete re-queued after the sync marked it.
- (P3) No `sameAccount()` recheck after the re-queue write. That only makes Sign Out over-count.
- (P3) The comment at listDelete.js:79-83 doesn't yet mention the re-queue clear.

author: mbryantms
body:
## Summary

The bottom tab bar's **Search** tab navigated to `/search`, which with nothing typed was eight "Awaiting query" rails and an input iOS will not focus on arrival. Desktop has the topbar field and the ⌘K modal; the phone now gets the same modal.

- **Search tab opens `SearchModal`** as a sheet from the top edge: full width, under the status-bar inset, input focused, live results and recent searches one tap away. A **Cancel** sits beside the input (no Escape key on a phone; the backdrop is under the keyboard). The sheet's height follows the visual viewport so the list ends above the keyboard. The tab reads active while the sheet is open and on `/search`.
- `globals.css` makes every dialog a bottom sheet on phones with a doubled `data-slot` selector; the search sheet opts into the top edge via `data-search-sheet` with the same specificity, later in the file. A search's input must not move as the result count changes.
- The bottom bar warms the modal's lazy chunk on phones so the first tap opens it inside the gesture (desktop still loads it on the first ⌘K).
- **Stray X fixed**: the vendored `DialogContent` renders its close button at `top-4 right-4`, which landed over the input's right end (measured x 912–944 against an input ending at 951 at 1344px). The modal passes `showCloseButton={false}`; Escape, the backdrop and the phone's Cancel close it.
- **`/search` empty state**: recent searches (the chips now live in `components/search/RecentSearches.tsx`, shared with the modal) or one line on what the page covers, instead of the placeholder rails. A 1-character query keeps the rails so the page does not collapse and regrow per keystroke. The page is still the full-results destination from the sheet's footer and deep links.
- `docs/dev/phone-layout.md` rules 0 and 4 updated.

## Verification

- In-app browser at 375px: tap Search → sheet at top 0, input focused, Cancel visible, `aria-expanded` on the tab; with `--safe-top` forced to 59px the sheet pads to 59 so the input clears the status bar. Typing shows grouped results; "View top results" lands on `/search?q=…`; `/search` with nothing typed shows the recent chip.
- Desktop at 1344px: ⌘K modal has no corner close button; Cancel is `display: none` from `sm` up.
- `tests/dom/phone-one-bar.test.tsx`: the tab is a button that opens the modal and reads active; source guards for `showCloseButton={false}`, the `data-search-sheet` rule (inset, visual-viewport height, status-bar padding, slide from top, ordered after the bottom-sheet rule) and the chunk warm-up. Full web suite: 1450 passing.
- Not verified on a real iPhone: that the keyboard appears on the first tap, and the sheet above the keyboard.

author: qaqp980520-prog
body:
## Run 73 — two development tracks

### New playable Godot 4 game: KROLL Neon Climber M0.1
- Three-sector side-scrolling platformer: Maintenance Shaft, Reactor Scaffold and Signal Tower.
- Double jump, short dash with cooldown, three data-core pickups, checkpoint respawn, laser hazards and locked/unlocked exits.
- Keyboard and on-screen touch controls; no external assets, plugins, audio or network dependencies.
- Standalone project, root-project nested path mirrors, rules tests and runtime smoke test.
- Registered in the root Survival Test Hub; root smoke checks the 18 launch buttons and instantiates Neon Climber.

### Existing system: all-nine surface terrain patch lifecycle
- Added `tests/production_surface_world_terrain_patch_all_chunks_reload_test.gd`.
- Uses the real SurfaceWorld/controller to edit all nine patches in the active 3×3 surface window with distinct state/revision patterns.
- Serializes all nine stable IDs, streams to a disjoint window, verifies old nodes/proxies are released and registry states retained, returns to the origin window, and verifies fresh patch/proxy instances restore each independent state.
- Performs a schema-1 save/restore roundtrip for the nine-patch set.
- All-nine regression verifies BoxShape3D collision height and grounded offset after edits, chunk reload and schema-1 restore for every patch.
- World-save schema remains version 1; no terrain runtime code or save format changed in this regression-only expansion.

### Game correctness and regression fixes
- Checkpoint anchors: Maintenance Shaft `(760,368)`, Reactor Scaffold `(820,278)`, Signal Tower `(940,268)`.
- Reactor checkpoint was moved away from the laser at x=870..940, y=275..295.
- Added hazard-aware `Rules.is_checkpoint_supported(position, platforms, hazards)`; level validation rejects invalid hazard rectangles and checkpoint anchors that are unsupported or overlap a hazard.
- Runtime activation validates checkpoint ID, exact authored position, platform support and hazard clearance before mutating progress.
- Rules/runtime tests cover embedded-position rejection, laser-overlap rejection, grounded respawn, and the Reactor checkpoint.
- Smoke test reacquires the player node after next-level/reset rebuilds the level root, avoiding stale-player assertions.
- Root and standalone `main.gd`/`rules.gd` mirrors remain byte-identical.

### Run #825 failure and correction
- Run #825 passed all prior steps and all Neon Climber tests, then failed in the all-nine terrain unload test at line 71: it attempted to cast a freed object reference after the controller had correctly unloaded the chunk.
- Updated the test to capture WeakRef handles before unload and verify `get_ref() == null`, avoiding casts of freed nodes. Fresh instance IDs and restored geometry/state remain checked.
- Fix commit: `80e5d71f26eaffaaceabd970af7147cf9fd96490`.

### Validation
- Latest candidate HEAD: `80e5d71f26eaffaaceabd970af7147cf9fd96490`.
- Run #825: failed at the all-nine terrain unload assertion; this is not accepted as a pass.
- Exact-head Godot 4.3 Run #826 is queued: https://github.com/qaqp980520-prog/2126-Survival/actions/runs/41209679698
- Do not merge until #826 completes all steps and cleanup with zero failures/skips.
- No local Godot executable is available. No local GUI/GPU/iPhone QA.
- Known limits: fixed authored platforms, three short sectors, no progression persistence, audio or animation.

author: drkiyira-dev
body:
A clean Sites checkout could reuse installed dependencies without running upstream's `postinstall`, leaving nine browser libraries out of the release archive. Existing local output masked this until production startup failed. This change makes the normal build regenerate those libraries and rejects incomplete delivery artifacts before release.

## Changes

- Reuse upstream `vendor()` and its file list on every build. Require all nine browser libraries (including Three), clear generated `dist/`, and fail with an installation hint when dependencies are unavailable. Upstream sources/rules are unchanged.
- Validate HTML/import-map references and hashed client/worker entries; generate an independent file-size/SHA-256 manifest.
- Add `npm run check:dist` and `npm run check:artifact -- /absolute/site.tar.gz`. The archive gate streams a real tar.gz with Python's standard library, verifies every file and hosting configuration, and rejects missing/altered/extra files, links, directory substitutions, duplicates, unsafe paths, truncated gzip data and appended archives.
- CI installs upstream dependencies with hooks disabled, builds, runs tests, verifies a real static archive, then runs the existing browser suites serially. CI has no deployment step and only read permissions.
- Update both English and Chinese README instructions. Preserve all licences, upstream credit and the genuine Codex co-author trailer.

## Validation

All local tests were run serially on macOS with Node.js 26.7.0, Python 3.14.3 and Chrome 156.0.8078.47:

- `npm run build` and `npm run check:dist`: passed.
- Final `npm test`: **103/103 passed**, including **28 new regression checks**. An isolated source checkout has no generated vendor directory and reuses installed dependencies; stale output is removed, and missing installs/Three cannot borrow stale libraries.
- `npm run test:browser`: **all eight suites passed** (reliability, terminal, kit loader, branding/mobile simulation, audio, maps, scenes and static scene imports). Existing offline/fixture modes were used; no new external-art availability claim is made.
- Official Sites `package-site.mjs` local-only output: **860 files**, final archive gate passed. No source sync, version save or deployment was performed.
- Compared against the retained v9 release archive: **all 859 existing files are byte-identical; the only addition is `dist/artifact-manifest.json`**.
- The actual failed v8 archive was rejected with exit 1 and all nine missing vendor paths identified. A temporary extra file also caused `check:dist` to exit 1.
- `git diff --check`: passed.
- GitHub CI: **passed** for both [pull request](https://github.com/drkiyira-dev/stronghold-protocol-personal/actions/runs/41207639114) and [branch push](https://github.com/drkiyira-dev/stronghold-protocol-personal/actions/runs/41207584481). The clean Linux runner passed hook-disabled dependency installation, build, the full test suite, 860-file archive verification, all eight serial Chromium browser suites and evidence upload.

## Limitations and rollback

Archive validation and its regression tests require Python 3.8+ on PATH, with no pip dependencies. Hash checks prove completeness relative to the separately verified local build, not external URL availability or gameplay correctness. Native Safari, a fresh nine-round campaign and physical mobile testing were not rerun for this packaging-only change; the existing runtime is byte-identical to v9.

**Sites v9 remains Public and unchanged. Do not merge or deploy automatically.** Production deployment still requires separate explicit maintainer approval. Revert this commit to restore the previous build workflow if necessary; no save migration, game-rule rollback or production access change is involved.

author: andygout
body:
The `CALL` subquery syntax used by many Cypher queries is deprecated, an issue highlighted by the Neo4j Desktop 2 app when entering the queries into the Query feature.

For example, when I enter the Cypher query from this [file](https://github.com/andygout/dramatis-api/blob/4db35dc3cb370177f99f4dcbf13ab516f229dbdd/src/neo4j/cypher-queries/time/show/show.js), it displays:

> CALL subquery without a variable scope clause is deprecated. Use CALL (time) { … }

This PR updates the queries to the current accepted syntax.
