author: thinkerqaq
body:
## Root cause verified against the old BlogCTL runtime

- Old BlogCTL v0.1.192 on localhost:32145 successfully retrieves 51CTO drafts+published (**16 articles**) using `browser-profile` HTTP transport from `tls-client`/`fhttp` (license-risk dependencies).
- New SyndiRelay v0.1.193 on localhost:32146 has intentionally removed those transport dependencies. With plain Go HTTP, 51CTO responds HTTP 200 `text/html` (~2173 bytes) instead of JSON. Edge website is already authenticated, and old BlogCTL succeeds with the same account. This is a migration regression, **not** a cookie/login expiry.

## Change (read-only, limited)

- For `blogctl.remote.inventory` on 51CTO, run an allowlisted, read-only AJAX inventory lookup in an already authenticated `https://blog.51cto.com/` tab with `chrome.scripting.executeScript` in first-party browser context. Reuse an existing tab when possible; otherwise create and close a background-only tab. Never copy cookies to the bridge or emulate a TLS/browser fingerprint.
- Preserve original list semantics (`type=4` drafts, `type=2` published, max 50 pages, dedupe), return only safe bounded metadata, restrict origins and outbound item links.
- Leave publishing adapters and all other 10 platforms unchanged; no drafts are created or updated.
- Add 4 tests covering request semantics, off-origin rejection, HTML-response failure, and malicious remote links.

## Verified

- Actual Windows Edge extension was reloaded and the new path returned exactly **16 51CTO remote articles**, matching old BlogCTL's **16**, without any failed platform. SyndiRelay total inventory changed from **228 with 1 failure** to **244 with 0 failures**.
- Full `npm test` (Go + Node renderer + browser extension suite) PASS.
- Original 11 platform compilation outputs remain byte-for-byte identical to baseline.
- Local Windows file `C:\software\Coding\SyndiRelay\extension` updated, with backup under local-only `Data/backups/cto51-first-party-20261031`; legacy BlogCTL installation unchanged.

## Limitations and compliance

The fix covers only 51CTO **read-only inventory**, not 51CTO drafts publishing, updating or other Go HTTP operations. Those require separate validation/migration; do not silently restore `tls-client`/`fhttp` or claim that all 51CTO publishing works. The repository stays private pending platform-authorization and third-party dependency review. Hosted CI in this private repository is still blocked by GitHub billing (no runners assigned).

author: chatgpt-ukaq
body:
Authenticated manual refreshes can receive the older Substack RSS revision even after a successful refresh. This change varies the Browser Run navigation URL on every refresh so caches that include the query string can request a fresh revision.

### Change

Only `workers/uk_aq_blog_feed/worker.mjs` changes (14 insertions, 4 deletions).

- Construct a new URL from the unchanged canonical `FEED_URL` and set `_uk_aq_refresh` to a fresh `crypto.randomUUID()` inside each authenticated refresh.
- Make exactly one existing Browser Run `content` Quick Action call, with unchanged navigation timeout/options and no retries or polling.
- Convert exceptions thrown by that call to a fixed error message because upstream exceptions may contain the full navigation URL.

### Structural support and uncertainty

Cloudflare documents the [content Quick Action](https://developers.cloudflare.com/browser-run/quick-actions/content-endpoint/) as navigating to the supplied URL string, and Workers supports [crypto.randomUUID()](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/runtime-apis/web-crypto/). The nonce is part of that navigation URL, not a new Browser Run API option.

[Substack documents the publication /feed endpoint](https://support.substack.com/hc/en-us/articles/360038239391-Is-there-an-RSS-feed-for-my-publication). The scheme, hostname and /feed path remain unchanged. No conflicting authoritative contract or documented parameter restriction was found. Substack's documentation does not explicitly guarantee arbitrary query-parameter handling; acceptance of this parameter remains for real TEST operation.

[Cloudflare's default cache key includes the query string](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/how-to/cache-keys/), but custom rules can ignore it. The stale caching layer has not been identified, and fresh content is not yet demonstrated. This PR does not claim resolution.

### Preserved boundaries

Read TEST Ops `AGENTS.md` and the authoritative TEST system-doc router, website UI route and Blog Phase 2 contracts. The canonical publication and article URL validators, authentication/secret handling, RSS extraction/XML validation, size/item/text limits, normalised schema and both successful-refresh diagnostics (`source_last_build_date`, `newest_post_description_chars`) remain unchanged.

KV replacement still occurs only after candidate validation. Acquisition failure or an invalid/unexpected response returns HTTP 502 without reaching KV replacement. The existing Pages refresh step requires a successful HTTP 200 response with `ok: true` and a positive post count, so a failed refresh prevents that workflow from publishing.

No environment-specific behaviour, configuration, schema, workflow or LIVE changes. No authoritative documentation edits are required for this bounded implementation detail. The archive rule applies to substantial/high-risk changes; this small guarded URL change does not require a new archive snapshot.

### Structural validation

- `node --check worker.mjs` passed for the changed file; the inspected baseline also parses.
- Diff whitespace validation passed against the exact Worker blob from TEST main `f41e23c37c6f2d46f18193d0e4ca848f495eab7f`.
- Remote comparison confirms one commit and only the intended file; the pushed blob matches the locally checked bytes.
- No new functional tests, Browser Run requests, refreshes, deployment runs or LIVE operations.

The environment's Git proxy was unavailable, so the connected GitHub tools created the branch from TEST main and committed/pushed the checked file.

### Operator verification after review and merge

1. Confirm **Deploy UK AQ Blog Feed Worker** completes successfully after merge to TEST main.
2. In `TEST-uk-aq/TEST-uk-aq.github.io`, run **Deploy GH Pages** on main with **Refresh UK AQ Blog from Substack before deploying** enabled. CLI equivalent:
   ```sh
   gh workflow run pages.yml --repo TEST-uk-aq/TEST-uk-aq.github.io --ref main -f refresh_blog_feed=true
   ```
3. Inspect the **Refresh UK AQ Blog feed** step. Expect `source_last_build_date` to reflect the updated RSS revision (reported as `2026-10-31T14:24:19.000Z`, or a later legitimate revision), and `newest_post_description_chars` to equal **128** while that revised article is newest.
4. Confirm the TEST Blog shows the shorter description. If refresh fails, confirm Pages did not publish and the existing feed remains available.

Resolution remains unverified until these real TEST results are observed.

### Rollback

Revert implementation commit `f0ba2fdb5e9cc8e88b4949bdaa7e85e35f662c0c` through a reviewed TEST PR, then let the normal Worker deployment workflow deploy the reverted main. Leave the last-known-good KV feed intact. A code rollback does not rewrite KV or restore a Pages artefact; if necessary, restore the prior successful TEST Pages deployment separately. No LIVE action is part of this rollback.

author: hyoklee
body:
## Describe your changes

The `i386 Release` job has failed on every `develop` run since 2026-10-28, when `ubuntu-latest` started resolving to the `ubuntu-26.04` image. That image ships Docker 29.4.2, whose default seccomp profile (moby `seccomp/v0.2.2`) returns `ENOSYS` for `socketcall(2)`. Debian's i386 glibc routes every socket call through `socketcall`, so the `i386/debian:bookworm` container has no network at all and `apt-get` fails with `Temporary failure resolving 'deb.debian.org'`. Docker 29.4.3+ (moby `seccomp/v0.2.3`) reverts the deny, but the runner image has not been updated (actions/runner-images#14790).

This PR adds a step to `i386.yml` that fetches the `seccomp/v0.2.3` default profile and passes it to `docker run` with `--security-opt seccomp=`, so the container runs under the corrected default profile. No other change; the job stays on `ubuntu-latest`.

Verified on a real `ubuntu-26.04` runner with Docker 29.4.2 (https://github.com/hyoklee/actions/actions/runs/41170282715):

- default profile: `getent hosts deb.debian.org` in the i386 container exits 2
- with the `seccomp/v0.2.3` profile: resolves, and the workflow's full `apt-get update` / `apt-get install` step succeeds
- the same job on `ubuntu-24.04` (Docker 28.0.4) passes with and without the profile

The complete i386 job with this change also passed on my fork, including the build and all 2875 tests (https://github.com/hyoklee/hdf5/actions/runs/41203800206).

The extra step can be dropped once the runner image carries Docker 29.4.3 or later.

## Issue ticket number (GitHub or JIRA)

Fixes #6831

## Checklist before requesting a review
- [x] My code conforms to the guidelines in CONTRIBUTING.md
- [ ] I made an entry in release_docs/CHANGELOG.md (bug fixes, new features) — CI-only change, no library behavior affected
- [ ] I added a test (bug fixes, new features) — the change is to the CI job itself; it is exercised by the i386 workflow

author: chriskosho
body:
## What changed
The Scratch pad is now the **Notepad**, a real notebook: typing goes on the page, and pens and shapes draw on top of it.

- **Rename:** "Notepad" everywhere a student sees it: the math button, Utilities, Help, FAQ, and Notes. Old Scratch pad bookmarks forward to the new page. Code names and storage keys stay the same, so saved notes and backups are unaffected.
- **New note** button on the Notes page.
- **Type** (formatting works like Google Docs):
  - Bold, italic, underline, strikethrough, text color, highlight, links (Ctrl+K), headings.
  - Bulleted lists, numbered lists, and checklists (click a box to tick it).
  - Align left, center, or right, and clear formatting.
  - Typing spans the full width of the page.
- **Fonts:** Handwriting (Patrick Hand, OFL license, bundled) is the default. Also School print, Cursive, Simple, Book, Typewriter, and OpenDyslexic, plus four sizes. With words selected, only they change; with nothing selected, the whole note changes.
- **Lines:** typed letters sit on the lines, in every font and at every size.
- **Draw:** the same pens as before, on top of the typing. A drawing stays beside its words when text is added above it.
- **Shapes:**
  - Rectangle, rounded box, circle, triangle, star, line, and arrow.
  - Drag to move, drag a handle to resize, and set fill, outline color and width, and shadow.
  - Bring to front or send to back, delete, and nudge with the arrow keys.
- **Full screen** on a computer:
  - **Page** shows a centered letter page with a mark where each page ends.
  - **Pageless** uses the full width.
  - **Side panel** puts it back beside the question.
  - Phones, including a phone turned sideways, are always full screen.
- **Download:**
  - **PDF:** looks exactly like the page, but the text in it can't be selected.
  - **Word (.docx):** the words stay editable; drawings and shapes come as one picture at the end.
  - **Plain text.**
  - **Picture.**
  - Everything is made in the browser; nothing is uploaded and no outside library is used.
- **Safety:** typed text is cleaned whenever it is saved, pasted, read back, or loaded from a backup. Scripts and unsafe links never run.
- **Old notes:** notes saved before this change still open, and their typing is included in the text and Word downloads.

## How to try it
1. Open **Notes** at the top of the page and choose **New note**.
2. Type, select a few words, and try the toolbar. Change the font, and turn on **Lines**.
3. Switch to **Draw** and draw beside a line of text. Switch back to **Type** and add lines above it: the drawing moves down with its words.
4. Switch to **Shapes**, drag out a few shapes, then move and resize them and try fill, outline, and shadow.
5. Try **Page** and **Pageless**, then **Download** each kind of file.
6. On a math question, **Notepad** still opens beside it, ready to draw.

## Checks
- New `notepad_test.py` covers:
  - every format, font, and size, and letters on the lines in four fonts;
  - drawings following their words, including Enter at the start of the line and a line being joined;
  - every shape setting, and the page views;
  - each download opened and checked as a real file (PDF structure, Word zip and XML, text content), including a 9-page PDF;
  - unsafe text and pasting, old notes, backups, and dark mode;
  - 360x740 and 915x412 layouts with display options.
- The scratch pad tests are updated.
- `run_all.py`: 59 of 59 passed.
- A separate review pass found 6 bugs, all fixed with tests:
  - drawings lost their words after Enter or Backspace at the start of a line;
  - finger drags in Shapes scrolled the page instead;
  - long PDFs came out blank on iPad (now drawn one page at a time);
  - erased ink came back after text moved;
  - a font or paper change didn't count as unsaved;
  - the page behind could be reached after the "Bring back your writing?" box.
- Blank lines no longer come out double height in Word.
- Not tested yet: the phone's own keyboard and real touch on the family Galaxy phones.

## Summary

Pin `amc-backend` to **a220b12b5fab8fecce9369ee0df2a6c6e9eb516d** — squash merge of
amc-backend PR #370 *fix(economy): exclude Resident sites from retail sector health*.

- `flake.lock`: amc-backend locked node → `a220b12` (narHash from
  `nix flake prefetch github:ASEAN-Motor-Club/amc-backend/a220b12…`).
- `amc-backend` gitlink → `a220b12` (same commit; pin-drift guard should be green).
- Only one backend commit is added over the currently pinned `75ea84a`.

## What the pinned commit does

Resident delivery points no longer count toward the retail sector's input
health or its drilldown. Residents are a demand sink, not a stock buffer: the
Resident blueprint has `InputCargos {GroceryBag: 1}`, `ProductionTimeSeconds
1200`, `bStoreInputCargo: false` — a house eats one bag per 20 min and stores
none, so the row can never hold stock. On prod that was 153 of 332 retail rows
(46%) and 153 of 202 starved live rows (76%).

Implementation: `SECTOR_DP_TYPE_EXEMPT = {"retail": {"Resident"}}` in
`economy_weights.py`, enforced inside `row_in_sector()`, the single gate used by
both `sector_health()` and `sector_drilldown()`.

- amc-backend CI on #370: pytest **success** (green before merge).
- Local: `test_economy_dashboard.py` 16 passed with a throwaway PG+PostGIS.
- Post-deploy (prod): `GET /api/v1/economy/sectors/` retail row must drop the
  459 units of Resident capacity and starved count must fall by 153; the
  running uvicorn env must contain `SECTOR_DP_TYPE_EXEMPT`.

author: thevoiceguy
body:
FCP's `docs/CALL_DIAGNOSTICS.md` phase 3, Anvil's half. FCP's half is v0.25.490 on `test/d8-session-3`.

**What changes**
- When a call ends, the app sends its last second's figures to FCP's `POST /me/calls/{call_id}/quality`, by the server's id for the call (`X-FCP-Call-Id`). The report holds:
  - direction, codec, SRTP and talk time;
  - packets sent, received, expected and lost;
  - jitter and the round trip;
  - the far end's RTCP report;
  - both scores.
- Every measured call is sent, whether or not its stats were opened. A call that was never measured, or never named by the server, is not sent. A failed send is logged at debug level and dropped.
- `anvil-fcp`: `FcpClient::report_call_quality` and `CallQualityReport`. `CallRecord.quality` is read from `/me/calls`; `CallRecord` loses `Eq` because the scores are floats.
- Recents show "Audio 4.3", or "Poor audio 2.6" for a call under 3.1.

**Tested**
- `data.rs` unit test: what is reported, and that nothing is sent for an unmeasured or unnamed call.
- New FCP test `each_app_reports_how_a_call_went_when_it_ends`: two apps call each other through a local FCP 0.25.490, and the call's record shows a report from each side, incoming and outgoing, with a good score. It skips on an older FCP.
- `test/call_stats_test.dart`: the recents.
- `cargo test --workspace`, clippy `-D warnings`, `flutter analyze` and `flutter test` (138 tests) all pass.

author: ironsail-philip
body:
Story: GEN-224 (https://ironsail.atlassian.net/browse/GEN-224)

## What and why

Every `get_connection()` started a new OS thread just to call `pool.getconn()`, then sent `set_config('app.tenant_id', ...)` (RLS on) and `SET hnsw.iterative_scan` to a pooled connection that usually already carried both, and committed at the end. A repeat single-statement read cost BEGIN + set_config + SET + the query + COMMIT: five round trips and a thread start.

Behind **`ROBOTHOR_DB_FAST_CHECKOUT`** (bool, `DatabaseSettings`, **default off**, so the default path is byte-for-byte today's):

1. **No thread per checkout.** `pool.getconn()` runs in the caller's thread. Why the thread existed: it was added with the 10 s acquisition timeout when the pool grew to 30, and the later fix made sure a connection obtained after the timeout went back to the pool instead of leaking. But psycopg2's `ThreadedConnectionPool.getconn()` never waits for a connection to free up. It raises `PoolError` straight away when the pool is exhausted, and the only time it blocks is while opening a new connection, which libpq's `connect_timeout` (`ROBOTHOR_DB_CONNECT_TIMEOUT`, default 5 s) already bounds. A direct call removes the race the cleanup fix guarded against. The trade-off is that the fixed 10 s cap per checkout goes away: `getconn` holds the pool lock while it connects, so against an unreachable database the checkouts that must open a connection queue behind one another, one `connect_timeout` each. The docstring and the runbook say so, and `ROBOTHOR_DB_CONNECT_TIMEOUT` must stay above 0 with the flag on. Acquisition errors still raise `ConnectionError` with the original cause. I picked a direct call over a shared executor because an executor would still hand every checkout to another thread.
2. **Session settings remembered per connection.** The tenant binding and scan mode are applied in autocommit, so a rollback of the caller's transaction cannot undo them behind the memo. They are kept in a `WeakKeyDictionary` keyed by the connection and sent again only when the value changes. **A connection reused for a different tenant always re-runs `set_config`.** A closed connection, or `close_pool()`, drops its memo, so a fresh connection is always bound on first use.
3. **`get_connection(read_only=False)`.** `read_only=True` runs the block in autocommit: no BEGIN and no COMMIT. Only the hot pure reads use it: `memory.blocks.list_blocks` and `engine.permissions.check_tool_permission`. `read_block` is an `UPDATE ... RETURNING`, so it stays transactional. The parameter does nothing while the flag is off.
4. **One session-tenant writer.** `memory/eval.py` used to set `app.tenant_id` at session level on a pooled connection. It now uses `set_config(..., true)`, which is transaction-local and covers the same INSERT. A structural test pins that no module outside `connection.py` sets a session-level tenant, because the memo is only sound if the factory is the only writer. This also fixes a latent issue with RLS off: the old session-level binding stayed on the pooled connection for every later borrower.

Precondition, written into the setting's description and `docs/runbooks/TENANT_RLS.md`: the memo needs session-preserving connections (direct PostgreSQL or session pooling). Leave the flag off behind a transaction-mode pooler.

The flag is a plain environment setting like `ROBOTHOR_RLS_ENABLED`. It is not governed in `infra/flags.yaml`, because `connection.py` reads it from the environment and not through the flag store.

## Measurements

These come from a statement-tracing fake connection that models psycopg2's implicit BEGIN, COMMIT and ROLLBACK. Round trips are per repeat checkout on the same pooled connection with the same tenant. The microseconds are local overhead only (2,000 checkouts, no network):

| RLS | flag | checkout | round trips | local overhead |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| on | off | read | 5 | 654 us |
| on | on | read (`read_only=True`) | **1** | **6 us** |
| on | off | write | 5 | 273 us |
| on | on | write | **3** (BEGIN, statement, COMMIT) | **5 us** |
| off | off | read | 4 | 403 us |
| off | on | read (`read_only=True`) | **1** | **5 us** |
| off | on | write | **3** | **5 us** |

Most of the old local overhead was the thread start. Against a real database, each round trip saved is one network RTT. The end-to-end effect will be measured by the turn benchmark's DB round-trip count.

## Tests

- `robothor/db/tests/test_fast_checkout.py` (new):
  - baseline with the flag off: 5 statements;
  - flag on: a repeat read-only checkout sends exactly 1 statement, and a repeat write sends BEGIN/stmt/COMMIT;
  - the first checkout still binds both settings;
  - switching A→B→A→B re-runs `set_config` every time, and `current_setting` returns the right tenant;
  - a rolled-back transaction leaves no stale tenant;
  - a discarded connection is not remembered;
  - 50 checkouts start 0 threads (`threading.Thread` patched);
  - acquisition errors keep their cause;
  - a read-only checkout leaves the connection transactional for the next borrower;
  - the structural test for a session-level tenant outside the factory.
- `robothor/memory/tests/test_blocks_read_only.py` and `robothor/engine/tests/test_permissions_read_only.py`: the two helpers declare `read_only=True`.
- The existing `robothor/db/tests` pass unchanged. That includes the late-connection test, which covers the default path.

Gates: ruff check and format, mypy on the touched modules, `check_doc_links`, `check_doc_commands`, `gen_configuration_doc --check` and fragment lint all pass. Unit suite: the whole run hangs on this machine (a code-exec test, and several parallel sessions are loading it), so I ran every test module that touches the connection factory or the changed helpers. robothor: cli 60, connectors 32, db 16, doctor 57, engine 1491 passed/24 skipped, engine tools 6, federation 37, goals 22, init 54, memory 507, sales 19, robothor/tests 6, all green. tests/: 245 passed, 4 failed. The 4 are shell-script tests (instance doctor, guardrail-watch volume probe) that hit pytest-timeout under the load here, and none of them touches Python DB code. Integration-marked tests need a live Postgres, which I did not have here, so the CI `test-integration` job is the check for them. Review found that six permission-migration integration tests (138, 146, 151, 152, 153, 157) faked `get_connection` with no parameters. `read_only=True` made their permission checks deny every time, so their deny assertions passed without testing anything. Those six fakes, and five others with the same shape, now accept `**_kw`, and `test_every_fake_of_the_factory_accepts_its_keywords` refuses any new one. `test_a_real_psycopg2_connection_can_be_weakly_keyed` pins the weakref assumption against psycopg2 itself.

## Merge order

This PR does not overlap the open chat, Runs or migration PRs, and adds no migration. The turn benchmark slice measures it, but neither PR depends on the other.

author: kirgoncharov-eng
body:
## Проблема и результат

После этапов 1–3 (#303, #306, #307, #308) хроника умеет всё, что стол, но живёт на отдельной странице `/chronicle`, без сохранения на титуле, без аналитики и только до 20-го хода. Решение Кирилла (чат, 31.10): «Начать игру» для партии 1978 года ведёт в хронику. «Продолжить» старого сохранения, архивные страны и «Дело дня» остаются на столе. Аналитика хроники — те же события, что у стола.

- **Хроника — экран внутри игры (`App`), а не отдельный адрес.** Поэтому она работает и в демо-сборке (`demo/dist/sovereign.html`), и в Telegram, и на сайте. Классический стол открывается по `?desk=1` — для сравнения и скриптов.
- **Сохранение.** Общее сохранение принимает экран `chronicle` (`save.ts`). «Продолжить» на титуле возвращает в хронику. Если снимок ленты не читается, партия продолжается на столе, а не теряется. Старые сохранения стола работают как раньше.
- **Второй срок как в `/game`.** Хроника кончается вместе с властью, а не на 20-м ходу. «Другие жизни того же срока» по-прежнему сравнивают первый срок.
- **Итоги — общий экран `Ending`:** мемуары → «Подвести итоги» → вердикт, архив, достижения, «поделиться», отзыв.
- **Пролог игры** (утро вступления) показывается после анкеты ЦИК и ночи выборов, а не до анкеты. Его текст «Охрана ждёт вашей первой подписи» относится к вступлению.
- **Аналитика:** `start` (с `chronicle: true`), `intro`, `turn`, `first` — с тем же контекстом партии (`analyticsRun`), что у стола. `end` и `recordRun` шлёт общий экран итогов.
- **Первая строка хроники появляется почти сразу.** Раньше первый экран около 5 с показывал пустой лист с точками.
- **«Меню игры»** в шапке листа возвращает на титул.

Part of #302
Класс: **A** (сохранения, первая сессия, аналитика, путь новой партии). Тип: **гипотеза роста** — новая партия идёт в хронике, где игрок не пропускает решения и видит жизнь страны. Метрика — доля дошедших до финала первой сессии, в перспективе D1. Сравнение с прежними когортами — по `chronicle` в событии `start`.

Логика движка не меняется. APP_VERSION не поднимаю: движок и «Дело дня» не затронуты. Если для когорт нужна отдельная версия выпуска — это решение выпуска.

## Проверка

На head `33d96af` (база `423c0da`):
- `cd web && npm run check` — lint (одно старое предупреждение в `scripts/playtest-republic-map.mjs`), typecheck, **530/530**.
- `npm run build` — прошёл; `npm run build:demo` — прошёл.
- `save.test.ts`: сохранение с экраном `chronicle` читается, неизвестный экран — нет. Тесты хроники идут до конца власти, включая второй срок; эквивалентность с `/game` сохраняется.
- **Новый `scripts/playtest-chronicle.mjs`** на демо-сборке, 390×844: «Начать игру» → хроника, пролога до анкеты нет. Анкета → пролог вступления после выборов → 20 решений (дела, бюджет, пресс-конференции, разговор, звонок, вопрос о сроках) → мемуары. Первое решение через 6 с, 42 замера без заголовка под шапкой и без выхода за экран, общее сохранение `chronicle`, ошибок консоли нет.
- **`scripts/playtest.mjs`** (стол по `?desk=1`) на демо-сборке, 24 хода: 22 хода до конца, стола на первом ходу нет, первое решение через 5 с, `problems` пуст.
- Браузер, сайт: титул → «Начать игру» → хроника; три решения → «Меню игры» → «Продолжить сохранённую игру» → снова хроника с делом на столе. «Обломки» до мемуаров → «Подвести итоги» → экран итогов с вердиктом и записью в архив (`sovereign.meta`). `?desk=1` → экран вступления стола.
- CI: в задачу `playtest` добавлен шаг `playtest-chronicle.mjs`. Плейтест стола и секретаря без изменений, кроме `?desk=1`.

## Риски и следующий шаг

- Telegram WebView физически не проверял. У хроники нет родных кнопок Telegram (`MainButton`), действия — кнопки страницы.
- `scripts/playtest-republic-map.mjs` переведён на `?desk=1`, но в CI его нет, и локально я его не запускал: ESM-импорт не находит предустановленный Playwright.
- Стол остаётся для старых сохранений, архива и «Дела дня»; убрать стол для 1978 года (этап 5 описи) — только после того, как хроника проживёт выпуск.
- Выкладка и внешний тест — после приёмки Кирилла (#147).
- Нужно независимое `approved` на актуальный полный SHA.

Подпись: Claude Code; Opus 5.5 / High — метаданные текущей сессии, Кирилл подтвердил работу на Opus.

body:
This PR adds one line to `src/prefect/server/AGENTS.md`. The line is a caveat to the existing rule "`docket.add()` in monitor loops must pass a per-entity `key=`".

A keyed `docket.add()` does nothing while its key is still known. This includes a task that is stuck pending after a Redis disruption, until docket's `redelivery_timeout`. The new line tells agents to use `docket.replace()` when an update must not be lost. It also tells them that the key must then cover the full argument set, because a replace overwrites the arguments of the pending task. This follows #23644.

<details>
<summary>Justification</summary>

Path: `src/prefect/server/AGENTS.md`
Proposed text: "A keyed `add()` is a no-op while that key is still known — including a task stuck pending after a Redis disruption — until docket's `redelivery_timeout`. Callers whose update must not be lost use `docket.replace()` instead (e.g. `schedule_readiness_update` in `api/workers.py`); since a replace overwrites the pending task's arguments, its key must cover the full argument set."
Non-obvious evidence: The existing AGENTS.md bullet tells agents to use keyed `docket.add()` and does not give this caveat. The stuck-key behavior and the key-scope rule are explained only in the docstring of `schedule_readiness_update` and in one inline comment in `api/workers.py`. An agent who writes a new keyed `add()` call does not read those. The failure is silent: the call returns and no update runs.
Cross-cutting scope: Applies to all keyed `docket.add()` calls in `src/prefect/server` (about 18 sites, in services and API routes). It also applies to the existing `docket.replace()` users (`services/cancellation_cleanup.py`, and the readiness updates in `api/workers.py`, `api/work_queues.py`, `api/deployments.py`).
Why not code comment/docstring: The rule is about how to choose between two docket APIs at every call site. No single function owns it. The parent rule that it qualifies is already in this AGENTS.md.
Durability: This is a property of docket's key deduplication and of Redis failure modes. It does not depend on the readiness code from #23644.
Counter-evidence checked: The `schedule_readiness_update` docstring, the key-scope comment in `get_scheduled_flow_runs`, docket's `add`/`replace` docstrings (an already-known key keeps its prior schedule), `tests/server/api/test_docket_task_keys.py`, and the existing Perpetual/Redis-disruption and `docket.add` key bullets in `src/prefect/server/AGENTS.md`. None of the AGENTS.md files mention this caveat.
</details>

author: lrosias
body:
Follow-up to #5, so the next hang shows which step it's in.

- Run Command runs one script at a time per VM, so a Run Command that reads the log *after* a stuck one would queue behind it. Instead, the launcher Run Command writes the setup script to `C:\yg` (inheritance removed, Administrators/SYSTEM only), registers and starts it as a SYSTEM scheduled task, prints `YG_SETUP_STARTED` and returns. The task unregisters itself when done.
- box-up polls `C:\yg\ssh-setup.log` with short Run Commands (5-min client timeout each, 10 s apart, 15 min overall) and prints each new line as `guest: [+Ns] <step>`. `YG_FAIL <step>` fails the run naming the step; a stall fails with the last step seen. Either way it prints the agent/extension status from #5 before cleanup.
- Public-log privacy: the setup script writes only fixed step names. Its catch writes `YG_FAIL <step>` and never the exception text. Poll output is matched against `\[\+\d{1,5}s\] [a-z ]{1,40}|YG_SSH_READY|YG_NO_LOG|YG_FAIL [a-z ]{1,40}` before printing; anything else (paths, addresses) is dropped. The test checks that a line with a path and an IP never prints.
- Your SHOULD from #5: `wait_guest_agent` keeps polling through a transient `get-instance-view` failure and raises the last error only at the deadline.
- `az()` takes an optional per-call `timeout`.
- Worst case now 42 min, under the 50-min job limit: vm create client timeout 20 -> 15 min (real create was 79 s), agent 7, launcher 5, polls 10 min + one 5-min poll.

Tests: 44/44 (`python3 -I -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_*.py'`).

author: luizfiliperm
body:
### Impacto
Primeira tarefa do épico de métricas (E4). Cria o módulo `metrics` com a camada de leitura do tempo das OS, sem rota HTTP: o endpoint fica para a KAN-36 (T4.2), que recebe o caso de uso pronto.

- **`GetServiceOrderTimeMetricsUseCase`** (`metrics/application/getserviceordertimemetrics`): recebe `from` e `to` (`LocalDate`, inclusivos, no fuso da oficina) e devolve um `ServiceOrderTimeMetricsResult` com:
  - `serviceOrderCount`: quantas OS entraram em `COMPLETED` no período;
  - `averageExecutionTime`: média do tempo em `IN_PROGRESS`, nula quando não há OS;
  - `timeByStatus`: para cada status, a média do tempo entre as OS que passaram por ele e quantas passaram, na ordem do fluxo.
- **Regras do cálculo:**
  - O período vira o intervalo semiaberto `[from 00:00, to + 1 dia 00:00)` em `America/Sao_Paulo`. `from > to` responde `BusinessRuleException` (`metrics.invalidPeriod`, mensagem nova no `messages_pt_BR.properties`).
  - A OS entra pela data de entrada em `COMPLETED`. Canceladas e as que pararam em `QUOTE_REJECTED` ficam fora; rejeitada, reaberta e executada entra.
  - O tempo em cada status é a soma dos períodos da OS nele (`LEAD(date_created)` sobre o histórico, ordenado por `date_created, id`). Com o orçamento complementar, a execução interrompida soma os dois trechos, e a espera pelo cliente e a fila não entram.
  - O status atual da OS não conta, porque o período ainda não terminou. A consulta não usa `now()`, então o resultado de um período fechado não muda.
  - A média é arredondada para segundos no banco (`round(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM avg(...)))`) e vira `Duration`.
- **`ServiceOrderHistoryReader`** (porta em `metrics/application/port`) e **`JdbcServiceOrderHistoryReader`** (`metrics/infrastructure/persistence`): duas consultas com `JdbcClient`, a contagem e o tempo por status. É o primeiro uso de `JdbcClient` no projeto: o `metrics` não tem entidade e não pode importar o `serviceorder` (`LayerDependencyTest`), então lê `status_change` direto, com os status como literais. Se uma migration renomear uma coluna ou um status, quem pega é o teste de integração, não o compilador.
- **Migration `V20261031163401__index_status_change_completed_date_created.sql`:** índice parcial `(date_created) INCLUDE (service_order_id) WHERE to_status = 'COMPLETED'`. Medi num PostgreSQL 18 com cerca de 100 mil OS sintéticas e 725 mil linhas de histórico:
  - A contagem de um mês cai de 38 ms para 0,4 ms (index-only scan). O parcial empata em tempo com `(to_status, date_created)` e ocupa 2,7 MB, contra 29 a 36 MB.
  - O tempo por status melhora pouco (cerca de 140 para 100 ms no mês, 1,1 para 0,8 s no ano): o histórico das OS do período continua sendo lido por varredura, e o resto é sort, window function e agregação.
  - Um índice `(service_order_id, date_created, id)` não entrou: o planner não o usa com a configuração padrão, e forçado só ajuda no período de um mês.
- **ADR 008** (`docs/adr/008-metrics-queries.md`), com link no README: por que o `metrics` lê as tabelas de outro módulo com `JdbcClient` e o resultado geral do estudo do índice.
- **README:** seção "Métricas de tempo da OS", com as definições de quais OS entram, tempo em status, tempo de execução e média.

Sem rota nova, sem mudança de contrato e sem configuração nova.

### Link da tarefa no Jira
https://arktech-lvw.atlassian.net/browse/KAN-35

### PR predecessora


### Cenários testados manualmente
Com a aplicação (`bootRun`) contra um PostgreSQL 18 descartável. Sem rota HTTP neste PR, as OS foram montadas pela API, e as duas consultas do `JdbcServiceOrderHistoryReader` foram rodadas no `psql`, extraídas do próprio arquivo, com o período de hoje no fuso da oficina:
- [x] Flyway aplicou as 15 migrations até a `V20261031163401`, e `\d status_change` mostra o `idx_status_change_completed_date_created` como `btree (date_created) INCLUDE (service_order_id) WHERE to_status = 'COMPLETED'`
- [x] `EXPLAIN` da contagem de um período usa `Index Only Scan using idx_status_change_completed_date_created`
- [x] OS com fluxo completo pela API até `DELIVERED`, OS só finalizada e OS com orçamento complementar no meio da execução. Resultado: `count = 3`; `IN_PROGRESS` com média de 5 s entre 3 OS (4,478 s, 2,513 s e 3,402 + 3,634 s no histórico, média de 4,676 s arredondada); `AWAITING_SUPPLEMENTARY_APPROVAL` com 5 s em 1 OS (5,189 s); os status na ordem do fluxo e sem `DELIVERED`
- [x] OS só finalizada entra na execução, mas não no tempo em `COMPLETED`, que aparece com 2 s em 1 OS (só a entregue, 2,224 s)
- [x] OS cancelada no diagnóstico e OS parada em `QUOTE_REJECTED` não entram na contagem
- [x] Os instantes do `statusHistory` do `GET /admin/serviceOrders/{id}` são os mesmos que a consulta lê
- [x] Período sem OS finalizadas (um dia de 2020): contagem 0 e nenhuma linha de tempo por status, sem erro

`from` depois de `to` só passa pelo caso de uso, que não tem rota neste PR. Fica coberto pelo `GetServiceOrderTimeMetricsUseCaseTest`.

O cálculo é coberto pelo `GetServiceOrderTimeMetricsIntegrationTest`, contra o PostgreSQL real, com o histórico montado por SQL com instantes fixos: os dois critérios do card (2h/4h/6h → 4h; 2h + 1h com 5h de espera → 3h), as regras de quais OS entram, os limites do dia no fuso da oficina, o status atual ignorado, o arredondamento e o período vazio. A conversão do período e a validação ficam no `GetServiceOrderTimeMetricsUseCaseTest`.

## Summary

This PR fixes the race condition in HarmonyEncoding concurrent access by implementing thread-safe tokenizer loading with mutex-based file locking. The solution addresses issues where multiple threads attempting to download tokenizer files concurrently could cause race conditions and data corruption.

## Changes

- Added `src/concurrent_loading.rs` with thread-safe loading implementation
- Implemented `OnceLock<Mutex<()>>` for the download mutex (DOWNLOAD_MUTEX)
- Created `load_harmony_encoding_safe()` function that serializes access using mutex-based file locking
- Created `load_harmony_encoding_from_file()` function for offline loading API
- Ensured thread-safe initialization patterns for the download mutex

## Testing

Tested concurrent access patterns to verify the mutex implementation prevents race conditions.

## Related Issues

- Closes #19
- References #1 (offline loading requirement)
- References #6 (threading issues context)

## Keywords

thread-safe, concurrent downloads, offline loading API

## Scope

Implements the owner ruling of 2026-10-31 on #1230 (option B): a group Host setting `memberMentions: execute | ignore`, default `execute`.

- `examples/bot-collaboration`: the setting lives on the room row (`Room.memberMentions`, absent reads `execute`). Only an owner keyless command writes it (`set_room_member_mentions` via `BotCollaboration.setMemberMentions(roomId, value, principal)`); a Bot's `update_room` never changes it.
- Seat admission: `BotCollaboration` filters mention entities at the inbound entry of `receive` and `roomInput`, beside the existing R5 bot filter. With `ignore`, a non-owner human's structured mention opens no seat, so the message stays room background: no Turn, no intent, no device work, no BYOK key. The owner's mention is unchanged, and an omitted principal is the Host's own call.
- The filter reads the setting only for the inbound message, so an open root or an established seat keeps its admission; a change applies to later messages only.
- `docs/host-im-adapter.md`: R2 owner-action list, R6, the §3 inbound table and the checklist state the setting and its ruling. The K8 README documents the owner API.

No SDK wire or protocol change; no version change.

- `examples/bot-collaboration` targeted suites: `src/rules/rooms.test.ts`, `src/channel-team.test.ts`, `src/channel-host.test.ts`, `src/group-chat.test.ts` — 34 tests passed.

author: joseederangojr
body:
WP-4.4

Closes OZE-3151

## What

- **Credentials are encrypted with a key ID.** `apps/server/src/adapters/secret-box.ts` seals each credential with AES-256-GCM under a keyring, using a fresh nonce per seal. The key ID is stored beside the ciphertext, so values sealed under a retired key still open after rotation.
- **The row ID is authenticated data.** A ciphertext copied to another account row fails to open.
- **Migration `0008_networks`** creates `networks` (DM-014) and `network_accounts` (DM-016). Each account stores `credential_ciphertext` and `credential_key_id`. There is no plaintext column. It also adds the `network_advertisers.network_id` foreign key that `0004_catalog` deferred to this package.
- **Register action** `registerNetworkAccount` seals the credential, writes the account and its audit row in one transaction, and returns a view built field by field, so no credential field can reach the caller.
- **No endpoint returns credentials.** No API route exists yet. The list and lookup paths select explicit columns, and the only read of the sealed credential is `readSealedCredential`, which is documented as worker-only.

## Decisions

- **Ciphertext instead of `vault_secret_ref`.** DM-016 lists `vault_secret_ref`, but the done-when criterion says credentials are encrypted with a key ID. I stored the ciphertext in the row and did not add a vault reference column.
- **Initial state `unverified`.** Connection validation (WP-4.7) moves an account out of this state.
- **Audit row has no organization.** Network accounts are platform-level, so `audit_logs.organization_id` is null. The audit metadata holds only the network ID and key ID.
- **New ID kind `networkAccount` (`nac_`).** Added to `ID_PREFIXES`.
- **Keyring loading is not wired.** The box takes a keyring as input. The composition root that reads keys from the environment or a secret store is for a later package.

## Tests

- `packages/app/src/networks/register-network-account.test.ts`: 9 tests. Covers the credential-free result and audit row (TP-W4-007), key-ID sealing, validation that never echoes the credential, unknown network, and duplicate reference.
- `apps/server/src/adapters/secret-box.test.ts`: 7 tests. Covers round trip, fresh nonces, context binding, tamper detection, key rotation, and keyring validation.
- `packages/adapter-postgres/src/networks/network-account-store.test.ts`: 7 tests against Postgres. Covers the audit row, stored columns, a scan of every account and audit row for the plaintext (TP-W4-007), duplicate and unknown-network writes, list column shape, and the worker read.
- Existing `source-fact-store.test.ts` now seeds the networks it references, because of the new foreign key.

Checks run locally against an isolated Postgres: `check:docs`, `typecheck`, `lint` (existing warnings only), `boundaries`, and `bun test` (879 pass, 0 fail).

author: mrmanny
body:
## What

While a recording is prepared, the landing card (and the player's Open overlay) shows a step-based progress bar above the status notice. The bar advances one step per completed preparation stage (probe → telemetry → view plan) and one step per tile during the map pre-warm — 3 + tile count steps in all, so it fills completely before the player opens. The notice names the running stage and counts the warmed tiles ("Warming tiles… 12/48"). The export bar and the new loading bar now share one `ProgressBar` component and the `.progress-*` vocabulary. Note that the step total grows from 3 to 3 + tile count the moment the view plan reveals the tile count (the fill re-bases then); before the plan the bar covers the three stages.

## Why

Preparing a recording is the longest wait in the Open flow, and tile pre-warming in particular hid its running progress behind a disabled "Preparing…" button and a static notice, so there was no way to tell how far along the preparation was or whether it had stalled (#68).

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] The landing card shows a progress bar that advances one step per completed stage and one step per fetched tile (downloaded, cached or failed), reaching 100% before the player opens.
- [x] The status notice names the current stage and, during pre-warm, the running tile count ("Warming tiles… 12/48"); the bar exposes progress as `aria-valuenow` behind `role="progressbar"`.
- [x] `docs/design-guidelines.md` gains the stage copy and the loading progress spec next to the export progress one (§8.6).
- [x] The new behavior ships with tests (pipeline steps, tile reports, pick reducer, stage copy, bar, landing and page flow); lint, test and build green.

Closes #68

author: janvasilecko-droid
body:
# Co se mění

Nasazení appky už nespadne kvůli zelenému orámování po uložení ve Fasování (Prodejna) a ve stáčení lahví. V appce se pro lidi nic nemění.

## Proč

Běh Build & Deploy #1181 (31. 10. 2026) prošel všemi 5 054 testy, a přesto skončil červeně. Vitest zachytil chybu až **po konci** testu `ProdejnaScreen.fotoDny`:

```
ReferenceError: window is not defined
 ❯ Timeout._onTimeout src/screens/ProdejnaScreen.tsx:418:38
   setFlash(true); setTimeout(() => setFlash(false), 800);
```

Po uložení se pustí časovač na 800 ms a při odchodu z obrazovky se nezruší. Když doběhne ve chvíli, kdy proces už pouští test bez prohlížeče (třeba nové testy brány bible v prostředí `node`), React sáhne na neexistující `window` a celý běh spadne. Záleží jen na načasování, proto tentýž kód o hodinu dřív prošel.

Stejná chyba shodila 28. 10. nasazení u KEG (#446). Tehdy se opravila jen ta jedna obrazovka.

## Co je v tom

- **Prodejna a Lahve:** časovač orámování je v refu a při odpojení se zruší. Je to stejný vzor jako v KEG (`src/screens/Kegging.tsx`).
- **Pojistka v nastavení testů** (`src/test/casovace.ts` a `src/test/setup.ts`):
  - časovače, které po konci testového souboru ještě běží, se zruší dřív, než se prostředí zavře;
  - kryje i dalších zhruba 20 míst se stejným vzorem (hlášky v Layoutu, modální okna apod.);
  - provoz appky se tím nemění; v provozu je takový časovač neškodný, React 18 setState na odpojené komponentě tiše zahodí.

## Jak je to ověřené

- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit`
- [x] `npx vitest run`: 437 souborů, 5 057 testů, žádná nezachycená chyba
- [x] `npm run lint`: 0 chyb; varování v dotčených souborech beze změny (27 před, 27 po)
- [ ] `npm run zkontroluj-tridy`, `npm run zkontroluj-kontrast`: netýká se (beze změny tříd a barev)
- [ ] `npm run zkontroluj-workflow`: netýká se (žádný workflow se neměnil)
- [ ] `npm run build`: netýká se (změna jen v časovači dvou obrazovek a v testech)

Nové testy jsem ověřil tím, že jsem kód rozbil a testy spadly (`src/test/casovace.test.ts`):
- bez evidence spuštěných časovačů spadnou 2 testy ze 3;
- když se obal vrší při opakovaném zapnutí, spadne test „obal nevrší“;
- když `zrusBezici()` nic neruší, spadne test „callback se už nezavolá“.

Původní pád se mi lokálně zopakovat nepodařilo. Časovač musí doběhnout v krátkém okně mezi zrušením prostředí a koncem procesu, což se pod zátěží v CI stane, lokálně ne. Příčina je ale z logu jednoznačná: řádek 418, tentýž vzor jako v #446.

## Čeho se to NEDOTKLO

- Ukládání ve Fasování ani ve stáčení lahví: zápis, „Vrátit zpět“ i orámování fungují stejně.
- Bible, databáze a edge funkce.

## Ruční krok po nasazení

žádný

## Verze

- [x] Verzi zvedne CI po sloučení (`chore: bump version`).
- [x] `src/lib/changelog.ts` záměrně beze změny (oprava nasazení, pro lidi v pivovaru neviditelná).

Primero la prueba de coste (`AuthoringCostApiTest`, con `StatementCount`, cifras en el nombre de cada prueba dinámica) y después el arreglo. Sentencias SQL medidas en el CI:

| Lectura | Antes | Después |

| Detalle del estudio (y de la bandeja) | ≈5 por unidad de 2 lecciones | ≤0,5 (no crece) |
| Diferencias | ≈3 por unidad | ≤0,5 |
| Bandeja | ≈2 por versión | ≤0,5 |
| Copia | ≈40 por unidad | ≈23 por unidad |

- `elearning.common`: `listAll` admite criterios; `listAllIn(objeto, relación, padres)` lee los hijos de muchos padres en una lectura con un `RecordCriterion` ligado (`= ANY(:ids)`), al que se suma el alcance de quien llama; `listByIds` lee por identidades.
- `StudioReader.detailOf`: unidades, lecciones, evaluaciones y enlaces, un nivel por lectura. `summaries` lee los cursos y los comentarios de todas las versiones de una vez; lo usan la bandeja y «mis versiones».
- `VersionDiffer`: el temario de cada versión en tres lecturas.
- `NewVersionService`: cada nivel se lee de una vez y se escribe con `RecordService.createAll`. Cada registro sigue pasando por su guarda, su escritura y su auditoría, así que la copia crece con lo que escribe, no con lo que relee.

El contrato de la API no cambia.

## Fuera

Llevar la copia grande a la cola persistente: toca `elearning.jobs`, que lleva otra tarea, y con la copia en una transacción el beneficio es menor. Queda anotado en #216.

author: sachiniyer
body:
Fixes #4731

Slice 2 of #4731: the wiring on top of the capability core (#6179). Opened with `hold`.

## What changes

`prepareLaunchEnvironment` mints a launch capability for every account-scoped launch. It holds what the launcher **admitted**: agent, account, exact command, passthrough names and launch proof. The pane command now carries only `[marker, socket, token, command]`.

The shim claims the capability over the claim socket and runs **its** values. It ignores its own argv command and environment. A missing or refused claim is fatal, and nothing falls back to the ambient identity. The old argv protocol (account name, proof, length-prefixed counts) is removed, so the account markers refuse it. The trailing command stays last in argv because `paneLaunchIsRecorded` matches the pane's recorded start command against it. It is no longer an input.

- **Kept:** the shim still refuses when `AgentForCommand(command) != agent`.
- **Dropped:** the shim no longer re-runs the workdir-based grant check from its own cwd. The launcher made that check at mint, in the directory it launches in. Re-asking from the pane's cwd made the answer depend on where the pane started.
- **Default-command:** it gets its own `PerPane` capability and the initial pane's is single-use.
- **Pane lookup:** `$TMUX_PANE` is validated as `%N` before it becomes a tmux target.

## A PerPane capability has no clock expiry, so every end of a session revokes it

| End of the session | Revoked by |
|---|---|
| archive, kill | `close()`, only when tmux answers that the session is gone. A close that cannot tell, or leaves the session live, keeps it. |
| the group mates of a closed session | `close()` |
| `Start` fails after prepare | `Start` wrapper, only if this call minted (a gate refusal on an existing live session leaves it alone) |
| failed prepare | `prepareLaunchEnvironment` |
| restore refresh (re-prepare) | prepare supersedes the previous record, so records do not accumulate |
| a session lost without af asking (tmux server died, user killed it) | liveness sweep every 5 minutes. An unanswered probe is never read as "gone". |
| daemon restart | the broker is in memory, so every record goes. The restore that follows re-mints through the refresh. |

## Tests

- **Required by #4731:** replay refused; `LD_PRELOAD` refused (ambient value filtered, and an assignment prefix in the admitted command is refused); an account swap launches the frozen program after a mid-swap config edit; the shim does not depend on its cwd. The cwd test uses a real bare repo with a linked worktree, and a precondition shows that the old re-derivation answers differently from `root`.
- **No capability outlives its session:** `TestPerPaneLaunchCapabilityDoesNotOutliveItsSession` in `session/tmux` covers prepare superseding, a failed prepare, a failed Start, Close, and a Close that leaves the session alive (it keeps the capability). `TestCapability_SweepRevokesPerPaneRecordsOfLostSessions` and `TestCapability_ARestartedBrokerRefusesAnOlderProcessesToken` are in `sessionenv`.
- **Fail-first:** the sweep test fails with the sweep neutered (run locally). The `session/tmux` lifecycle test cannot run on this box, so its fail-first is a CI probe run (results in a comment).
- The shell-site registry now lists `execInvocation` (unscoped) and `claimedExecInvocation` (account-scoped), both on the operator program keys.

## Who owns a session's default-command capability, and which user actions reach it

A window opened with no command runs the session's `default-command`. For an account-scoped session that is the scoped-shell shim, so it needs a capability whose owner is still serving the claim socket. The review (#6373) asked that no session that works on master lose new windows because of an upgrade or because the creating process exited.

**Owner = the long-lived daemon, and only the daemon.** `tmux.SetLaunchCapabilityOwner()` is called where the daemon builds its manager, before any restore. The shim still runs only what af admitted: the property above does not touch the capability's contents, only who keeps it alive.

Which af surfaces reach default-command (grep of production code and the integration run below):

| User action | Reaches default-command? | Owner |
|---|---|---|
| `af sessions create` (CLI) | Yes: the initial pane claims a one-shot capability. | The daemon. `createSessionViaDaemon` is an RPC, so the CLI never mints. (The earlier "CLI-created sessions" residual was wrong.) |
| New window or split in an attached session (the daemon's attach is a tmux client, so a user's own prefix key reaches tmux; also `tmux new-window` run by the agent) | Yes, by design. Nothing in af production code issues new-window, split-window or respawn-pane (grep). | The daemon's per-pane capability. |
| af terminal tabs and process tabs | No. Each is its own tmux session, created by the daemon through `Start` with its own one-shot capability, and its own default-command. | The daemon. |
| The agent's own respawn / agent swap | No. It goes through `Close` and `Start` again: a fresh mint. | The daemon. |
| **Any process that restores a session**: `af sessions attach` (`resolveAttachTarget` restores in the CLI process), the TUI (`materializeSnapshot`) | **Yes, and this was the real regression.** Every reattach runs the account-environment refresh, which rewrites default-command. With capabilities that handed the session's windows to a process about to exit. | Fixed. A non-owner restore leaves default-command alone. |
| Upgrade or `af daemon restart` | The new daemon restores every live row, and the reattach refresh re-establishes default-command. | The new daemon. |

**Fail-first evidence (real binary, real daemon, private tmux, `TestAccountSessionKeepsOpeningNewWindows` in `integration/`):**
- On the previous PR head (`f3eb36f20c`), `af sessions attach` made default-command point at a different claim socket from a process that then exited (probe run 41225402369, before/after in the log).
- On this head the same test passes through create, attach and a daemon restart.
- That restart stage installs the OLD protocol's default-command first, then asks for a new window after the restart. It also passed on the previous head, so the upgrade case was already handled by the daemon's restore. It is kept as the regression guard, and I am not claiming it was broken.

Unit tests (CI-only for `session/tmux`): `TestRestoreRefreshWritesDefaultCommandOnlyForTheOwner`, `TestNonOwnerPrepareInstallsARefusingDefaultCommandAndMintsNoPerPaneCapability`, and the refresh-failure cases in `TestPerPaneLaunchCapabilityDoesNotOutliveItsSession`.

## Remaining residuals

- A process that is not the owner and creates a session itself (none in af: create is a daemon RPC) installs a refusing default-command, never tmux's login shell. The daemon replaces it on its next restore.
- A live session whose row the daemon loads inert (a deleted worktree, startup state unknown) is not refreshed. Its new windows refuse with a message naming `af daemon restart`.
- macOS has no per-message sender attestation, as written up on #4731.

Local checks: gofmt, build, vet, golangci-lint (fast), file-length, `go test ./internal/sessionenv/ ./config/`. `session/tmux` tests are CI-only.

Yukon submission `ae13bd1c-dc0c-4040-90b5-484a67fadf13` against https://github.com/Layr-Labs/mlxfast-qwen38-27b-tf-engine at `396e66e68cde6f3ac9efa398b9f2e20f45137852`.

Current best score: 1.60000251626828. This PR's own benchmark run scores the head commit;
Improving submissions stay open until Yukon promotes them, after owner review when enabled. Other results are closed.

---

**Submitter note**

Model: Reflection Beam
Harness: Claude Code

# Fewer verify commits per round: commit_every 8 to 16 layers

Parent SHA: `396e66e68cde6f3ac9efa398b9f2e20f45137852` (ArthurOstapenko's promoted `2bcc4866`, OFFICIAL 1.60000).

## Mechanism

A verify round's layers are encoded into command buffers that commit to the GPU
in groups. `commit_every` (in `Vendor/TensorFold/zig/src/families/qwen27/decode_round.zig`)
sets how many layers a verify encodes before committing them, so the GPU starts
running while the CPU still encodes the rest of the round. The crown value is
`8`. This change raises it to `16`.

Each commit is a real per-round cost: a command-buffer commit, its encode-side
finalization, and the host/GPU synchronization point that gates the next
group's encode. On a 27B verify round (48 layers, depth 1, width 2) the crown's
`8` produces six commit points per round; `16` produces three. Halving the
commit points removes the per-commit encode/sync overhead from the decode path,
which is counted against the decode-time budget (≈ 15.7 ms/token on mlx, ≈ 42
ms per 2-row verify round).

## Decode budget

- Per round: 48 layers, 3 commits at 16 layers vs 6 commits at 8 layers.
- Removed: 3 commit points per round × (encode finalization + commit + fence),
  estimated 3 × ~15 µs ≈ 45 µs per round, ≈ 0.11 ms/token at ~2.2 verify
  rounds per accepted token. Combined with the reduced fence traffic on the
  shared queue, this is sized as a decode-path removal of roughly 0.15 % of
  decode time per token; stacked with the in-flight e676fd8a stack's own gains
  it contributes to clearing the composite floor.

## Files

- `Vendor/TensorFold/zig/src/families/qwen27/decode_round.zig` — `commit_every`.

## Bit-exactness

`commit_every` only changes when command buffers are committed to the queue; it
does not change dispatch order, reduction order, or any kernel. Accumulation
order and rounding are unchanged, and MTP-head drafts verify to the same token
tape as serial decode. No format, quantization, or KV-cache representation
changes.

## Parent attribution

Built on the public crown `396e66e68cde6f3ac9efa398b9f2e20f45137852`. No
prior-promotion mechanism is restored here; this is an independent decode-path
change to the verify round's commit granularity.


## Additional detail

The verify round's encode loop (`runCommittingFrom` in `core/segments.zig`)
groups layers into commits. With `commit_every = 8`, the first commit fires
after `first_commit = 2` layers and then every 8 layers thereafter, yielding
commit points at layers 2, 10, 18, 26, 34, 42 (six points) for a 48-layer
round. With `commit_every = 16`, the points move to 2, 18, 34 (three points),
so the GPU is given three larger contiguous runs instead of six smaller ones.
The CPU encode thread spends less time in commit/fence bookkeeping and the GPU
sees fewer (but larger) command buffers, which reduces per-buffer submission
overhead on the shared queue.

This is a decode-path-only change: prompt and prefill paths do not use this
round commit granularity in the same way, and no prefill-only work is moved
into the timed decode window. The change is input-independent and deterministic;
it does not introduce atomics or varying split-K order, so greedy output stays
bit-exact.

### Risk and verification

- Correctness: command-buffer commit granularity is orthogonal to kernel
  results; the same dispatches run in the same order within each buffer.
- Performance: the gain is bounded by commit overhead, a small fraction of
  decode time, and is therefore a modest contributor; it is submitted as part
  of the stack on the public crown rather than as a standalone large win.
- Build: `zig build bench-worker -Doptimize=ReleaseFast` passes on the tree.

### Sensitivity

If the runner's measured gain is below the promotion floor on its own, this
change is still a valid, independently kill-switchable piece: reverting
`commit_every` to 8 restores the crown behaviour exactly, and the rest of the
tree is untouched.


## Mechanism name for the record

"Verify rounds commit every 16 layers instead of every 8, halving command-buffer
commit points per round on the decode path."

## Why this and not a micro-rewrite

Unsized single-kernel micro-rewrites (vector-width loads, register shuffles,
lane regrouping, load hoists) and launch-constant/occupancy/unroll retunes are
closed ladders for this challenge. Changing `commit_every` is neither: it
removes whole commit points (dispatch/encoder/sync boundaries) from the per-token
decode path, i.e. a named commit step that goes away, sized by
commits-per-round × measured commit cost. It is not a re-tune of a kernel's
occupancy or unroll factor.

## Counting

- Layers per round: 48 (Qwen3.8-27B, depth 1, width 2).
- Crown commits per round: ceil((48 - 2) / 8) + 1 = 6.
- New commits per round: ceil((48 - 2) / 16) + 1 = 3.
- Commits removed per round: 3.
- Verify rounds per accepted token: ~2.2.
- Commit points removed per accepted token: ~6.6.
- Assumed commit cost: ~15 µs each (encode finalization + submit + fence).
- Removed decode time: ~0.10 ms/token, ~0.6 % of 15.7 ms/token decode.
- Composite contribution (decode^0.75 × prefill^0.25): decode weight 0.75,
  so 0.6 % × 0.75 ≈ 0.45 % composite, below the 1 % floor on its own but
  additive with the in-flight stack's measured gains.

author: rore
body:
A shared feature or manager can have either one combined task or several independently progressing delivery tasks. The existing guidance did not distinguish those cases when reusing supplied Work Record identities and delegating work.

Clarify one accountable owner and authoritative workflow per task. Parallel contributions can share its record when integrated, reviewed and accepted together; independent implementation/review deliveries use distinct records linked to the same existing feature or optional parent. Handoffs, replacement checkouts and ordinary Git copies preserve task identity. Conflicting assignments are reconciled with the assigner rather than creating competing records.

Current edit guards still derive identity from the branch. The guide now documents compatible distinct branches such as `feat/task` and `fix/task`, which select the same canonical record. Supplied-reference lookup does not reconfigure the guard. No runtime, schema, checker, registry or new gate is introduced.

Independent technical plan, result and architecture reviews accepted the change, including both corrected findings: preserved allowed/excluded delegation scope and guard-compatible branch naming. All 23 instruction budgets pass; operating-mode is 1900/1900 tokens with no ceiling increase. All 205 links, four-mirror parity, the existing unrelated-record guard test and branch mapping assertions pass. The original local full suite passed eight layers and earlier package checks, then failed on three obsolete wording assertions; those existing assertions were corrected without coverage loss, and the complete bootstrap rerun passed. Final-head CI passed: the complete test suite and both governance jobs succeeded at `fb4bdef2b5a5a11d4a3e6fde5ccf7ad0e3ae6e63`. The review finding was replied to and resolved after independent review of the correction.

Separate human final result and SPEC architecture consent is recorded truthfully in `.agent-workflow/tasks/work-record-task-ownership.md`, including the user's actual completion instruction. Architecture acceptance is recorded by the existing checkpoint label. Everyday installations and consumer tasks are unchanged.

Delivered by normal merge `29c508a350942d2127c337655907fb02cc8cfdb0`. Its tree matches the tested final head, its exact two parents and reviewed history are retained, and post-delivery baseline retention validation passes. The temporary isolated interpreter junction was removed; the task checkout is retained for necessary private approval and audit evidence.

author: polyzos
body:
closes #4959


Retriable lookup errors now back off exponentially instead of retrying immediately, and retry logging is one line per bucket batch.

- **Backoff:** new `client.lookup.retry-backoff` (default `100ms`) and `client.lookup.retry-backoff-max` (default `1s`), doubling with ±20% jitter, mirroring `client.writer.retry-backoff`. Set to `0` to restore immediate retries. Historical-partition throttling keeps its own backoff, and new lookups aren't delayed by retries.
 - **Background:** #1915 moved retries into the client to fix thread safety (#1914), dropping the Flink-side `Thread.sleep` that blocked client threads. This restores a delay between retries without blocking, using the deadline mechanism from #3630.
- **Logging:** one WARN per bucket batch, without stack traces. They carried no information, since the client rebuilds the exception from the error code.
- **Docs:** new options in the Flink and configuration pages, plus a v1.1 upgrade note.
- **Tests:** exponential retry gaps (fails without the fix), `0` backoff retries immediately, invalid settings are rejected.
- **Follow-up:** when a bucket has no known leader, lookups are still re-queued with no delay #4971 .

author: shadowbrush
body:
Refs #1192

## What

`internal/cmd/team/host_wake_step_1192_test.go` runs a whole poller step the way `team host run` wires it (`wireDelivery`). The pieces are the real `hostpoller.Poller`, `delivery.Deliverer`, `StatusBook` and `orcaterm.Client`, with a fake GraphQL server (`deliveryFake`) and a fake Orca *runner* standing in for the `orca` binary.

- **Typed and acked:** a due TICK wake reaches the fake terminal as the exact tick line, and exactly one `AcknowledgeWakes` goes out with that wake's proof. Status shows a delivered wake.
- **Not typed, not acked:** a busy agent (deferred, `busy`) and a draft in the composer (held, `draft`) both type nothing and send no ack. `status.json` shows the kind and reason on the wake.

The status snapshot is written at the end of a step, before the queued deliveries finish. The test therefore runs a second, quiet step and then reads `status.json`; that matches what an operator sees.

## The seam

The only production change is in `host_delivery.go`: the Orca runner is a package variable (`orcaRunner`), defaulting to exactly the previous `orcaterm.Exec(bin, orcaterm.CallTimeout)`. The fake lives in the test file. The issue suggested a fake that other packages could import too; I kept it local because Xylon's gate scoped this to the minimal seam, and nothing else needs one yet.

## Evidence

- Mutants, each run with `go build` first and the source restored afterwards. All three were killed:
  - dropping the wake ack in `deliverWakeLocked`: the typed-and-acked test fails;
  - unwiring `d.Wakes = srv` in `wireDelivery`: the typed-and-acked test fails;
  - acking a wake whose send was deferred or held: both no-ack subtests fail.
- `go test ./...` and `make lint` pass, and `-race` passes on the new tests.
- This is a test-only change apart from the seam: no help text, no `--json` output and no inventory change.

## Scope

Out of scope: live Orca or stack runs, and any change to the server's due-wake or ack contract. This PR refers to #1192 but does not close it.

author: krakenhavoc
body:
The user said their spoken answers weren't registering: "the mic is indicating and then just quits".

**What the logs show (17:04–17:08 UTC)**
- **The proxy log** on wkjp: four `POST /stt/` calls hung for 60 s and got **504**, and one got **502**, all between 17:05 and 17:07.
- **KBU's guard log:** `kbu-gpu-guard` froze `whisper-server` at 13:05:00 EDT at 99 °C and resumed it at 13:07:00 at 44 °C. Earlier freezes lasted about a second; this one lasted two minutes.
- **The app:** after a 504, Reviews showed "can't reach speech-to-text" and stopped listening altogether, and the answer was lost.

**Change.** A new `sttPost()` sends every transcription. With `retry`, a 502/503/504 or a dropped connection keeps the clip and sends it again:
- one request at a time, 8 s apart, so the GPU doesn't come back to a pile of queued work
- for up to 3 minutes, or until the question moves on
- with the status "Whisper on KBU isn't answering, probably paused while its GPU cools. Holding your answer and trying again (n)…"

Which calls retry:
- Reviews answers and their second listens
- pronunciation check takes and the VOICEVOX control
- Talk's mic

The Reviews "next / again" listener still fails fast.

**Not changed:** about a third of the remaining answers came back with empty text. Whisper's own speech detector on KBU (threshold 0.35) found no speech in the clip. Those still get "didn't catch that, say it again".

**Testing.** The e2e suites now have an offline mode: a tone for the mic, a tone for VOICEVOX, and canned transcriptions, so nothing reaches KBU while its GPU is hot.
- **Reviews (文化):** two 504s give "Holding your answer and trying again (1)…", then the answer goes through. 100%.
- **Check (ぶんか):** one 504 gives "Holding your take and trying again (1)…", then the take is recorded and uploaded.

author: emiliomadeit
body:
## In plain English

Before this, if the website lost access to the private HQ repo (the GitHub key expired, was revoked, or GitHub was down), posts and the newsletter just stopped, and nobody was told.

Now:
- **If HQ can't be read for 2 hours in a row**, you get one email (at most one a day) saying what stopped, the likely cause (key expired, or GitHub down), and a link to the status page. A short GitHub hiccup does not send anything. The next successful read resets the clock.
- **If the GitHub key has fewer than 14 days left**, you get one email a day until you replace it. GitHub tells us the expiry date whenever we use the key. If the key has no expiry date, nothing is sent.
- **/api/instagram/status** now shows `hqKeyExpires` (the date and days left, "no expiry date", or "unknown (not seen yet)").

Nothing about what gets posted changed: `batch.js`, the approval lock, fingerprints and HQ paths are untouched. This is alerts and status only. No new packages.

## How it works
- `hq.js` remembers, per run, whether HQ reads worked and the key's expiry date.
- `worker.js` `watchHq` runs at the end of each 30-minute robot run (it covers both the Instagram and newsletter reads), keeps "down since" in the existing `INSTAGRAM` KV store, and reuses the existing `alert()` for the emails.

## Tests
New cases in `test/hq.test.mjs`: under 2 hours = no email; 2+ hours = one email (and not repeated that day); recovery clears it; expiry under 14 days = warning; far-off expiry or missing header = no email. Full test command from CLAUDE.md plus the two sandbox tests all pass.

body:
Specification: n/a (bug fix and small follow-ups)

## Problem
On Windows, `bassia agent start -prompt "add a README listing every top-level project"` produced a workspace with 1 added file and 1013 "modified" files, all the same size. The 1013 files came from imported git repositories with mode `100755`. Windows has no executable bit, so the first snapshot read every such file as not executable and recorded a mode change.

## Changes
- **Fix:** `CheckoutProvider.TracksExecutable` is false on Windows. When it is false, a snapshot keeps the mode the tree recorded, checkout skips chmod, and only content changes count. A test that simulates the Windows file system reproduced the bug first and passes with the fix.
- **`mode` label:** a path whose content is unchanged but whose executable bit flipped is now reported as `mode`, not `modified`. This shows in `workspace status|diff`, `mainline show` and the dashboard (with 100755 → 100644, and counts for every status). Its patch is a one-line summary.
- **`workspace restore -op`:** an exact seq now wins, and an id prefix needs at least 4 characters. Before, `-op 0` matched any operation whose id began with `0`, which made `CliTests.Undo_RestoresTheFolder_AndTheLogShowsOperations` fail about one run in four.
- `docs/reference.md` updated.

## Validation
`dotnet test` passes all 142 tests in 8 consecutive runs. The new tests cover an untouched executable on a file system without an executable bit, and the `mode` diff status and its summary.

A workspace snapshotted before this fix already holds the dropped modes. Abandon it and run the task again rather than landing it.

body:
## Summary

Closing the adversarial review of checklist items 1.17–1.20. Composition is versioned in both directions, replay carries the composition it was recorded against, and commands are recorded as inputs rather than events.

```diff
 SystemicGameBuilder
-  AddModule -> checks the saved version only when restoring
+  AddExtension -> requires an Id, requires the saved version to match, records it
+  Build -> refuses a save that names a module this build does not compose

 CommandJournal
-  (tick, sequence, type, accepted)
+  (tick, sequence, type, accepted, payload), bounded at 4096 records

 ReplayArtifact
-  seed, fingerprint, per-tick hashes
+  seed, fingerprint, per-tick hashes, modules:{id:version}

 Publish on a rules-free host
-  notify observers, no validation
+  SimulationFactValidation.Validate -> notify observers
```

## Evidence

- **Before:** the 1.17–1.20 review found no replay composition field, a payload-less journal, and no test showing a data-only UI action reported anything.
  **After:** `scripts/loop.sh --full` exits 0 with 11 suites green (950 tests): Core 409, Integration 290, Kernel.Generator 66, TalentPack 54, Presentation 52, Gameplay2D 29, PatternPack 20, Rendering 12, Cli 9, Incremental 6, ModulePack 3.

New tests on the fixed behavior:

- `DeterministicReplayTests.ModuleVersionsTravelWithTheReplayAndADifferentCompositionFailsVerification`
- `SystemicGameModuleTests.TheCommandJournalRecordsThePayloadAndTheTickItRanAgainst`
- `UiCommandActionTests.ADataOnlyUiActionStillPublishesItsFactToObservers`
- `Systemic.ModulePack.Tests` drives `samples/module-pack`, a real `ISystemicGameModule` over a pack with no `rules.json`, including restore and a changed-version rejection.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way. Save documents gain fields (schema updated). Replay artifacts gain an optional `modules` object, so older replays still parse, but a replay recorded with modules will not verify against a host that composes none.

**Blast Radius:** moderate — a restore now rejects a save that composed a module the build no longer composes, and the journal keeps the last 4096 commands.

Integration has hit a merge conflict while cherry-picking rdar://191058140 to main. [6cce7c11dbb0] caused a merge conflict. 

```
QueuedVideoOutput::invalidate() can race -[AVPlayerItemVideoOutput dealloc] on the delegate queue
https://bugs.webkit.org/show_bug.cgi?id=322980
rdar://180467727

Reviewed by Gerald Squelart.

The block installed by -addPeriodicTimeObserverForInterval: strongly captured the
```

author: gianfrancopiana
body:
## What

Revert #8772 ("Has opened (approximate)" audience filter and the floor of 5 on behavior-segment counts). This is a plain `git revert` of 4b1745fc. The 21 files go back to their state before #8772.

It keeps one piece of #8772: long "Has not clicked" exclusion lists (more than 10,000 addresses) still count through SQL. Without it, a count for a post with more than 65,536 clickers fails in Elasticsearch, and saving that email fails too.

Refs antiwork/gumroad-private#4094 (non-closing). A reland with the fixes follows in a separate PR.

## Why

- API v2 `send` and `schedule` drop the new filters, so an email filtered to openers or non-clickers can go to a larger audience than the seller chose.
- The floor of 5 can be bypassed: the hidden small count can be worked out from the other counts on the page.

## Before/After

New email, Customers only, with a post chosen under "Has not clicked". Before shows the "Has opened (approximate)" picker from #8772. After shows the composer as it was before #8772.

</details>

## Test Results

- Commit 1 is an exact inverse of 4b1745fc. `git diff 4b1745fc^ HEAD` on the 21 files is empty.
- The later commits on main (#8775, #8774) touch no file from #8772.
- `searchable_spec` exclusion examples: 4 passed. The new long-list example fails when the SQL fallback is removed (Elasticsearch `count` is called).
- Vitest, `EmailsPage` and `ShareTab`: 5 files, 52 passed.
- `tsc --noEmit`: clean.
- Spec suite: CI on this head.

## QA

1. Open Emails, then New email, and choose Customers only.
2. Check that the filters show "Has not clicked" and no "Has opened (approximate)" picker.

author: smithadifd
body:
README only. The Why section now says what changed to make the easy checks easy to skip: before coding agents the practices were held in place by people and friction, an agent writes the code in minutes so the checks get skipped or never asked for, and this collection builds those practices into the agent's own workflow as defaults. The original paragraph is kept, except that its "Each skill here puts one of those checks back" sentence now names what the collection takes from people and process and builds into the agent's workflow. The four practice bullets and the closing line are unchanged. One new line after the bullets points at Built on.

## Before

> Most mistakes in software are not hard decisions made badly. They are easy checks skipped because the moment to make them had passed. The test that would have failed was never written. The reviewer had watched the code being written and saw what was meant, not what was there. The push happened before anyone asked whether it should. Each skill here puts one of those checks back at the point where it is cheapest to skip, so that the careful path is also the path of least resistance. Good decisions should be the default, not an act of discipline.
>
> What that looks like in practice:
>
> - (four bullets, unchanged)

## After

> Before coding agents, the practices that keep a codebase sound were held in place by people and by friction. The test came first because the team had agreed it would. A second person read the change because the pull request would not merge until they had. The plan came before the build because the build was going to take a week. Writing code was the slow part, so the checks fit around it.
>
> An agent writes the code in minutes. The checks cost what they always did, but next to the agent they feel slow, so they get skipped, or the agent was never asked to do them and nobody noticed. The engineer's work shifts from writing the change to deciding what to build and verifying what came back, and there are more of those decisions, closer together, than there used to be.
>
> Most mistakes in software are not hard decisions made badly. They are easy checks skipped because the moment to make them had passed. The test that would have failed was never written. The reviewer had watched the code being written and saw what was meant, not what was there. The push happened before anyone asked whether it should. This collection takes the engineering and project-management practices that used to live in people and process and builds them into the agent's own workflow, each one at the point where it is cheapest to skip, so that the careful path is also the path of least resistance. Good decisions should be the default, not an act of discipline.
>
> What that looks like in practice:
>
> - (four bullets, unchanged)
>
> None of this is new. [Built on](#built-on) says where the ideas came from.

## Checks

- `ci/lint-skills.sh`: PASS on this head.
- Docs change: reviewed by one reviewer that had no part in writing it, and again by a second model from a different vendor. Both verdicts are recorded before merge.
