author: youssef-adel91
body:
Addresses `docs/KNOWN_ISSUES.md` #24 (Windows: `e2e:context` times out at `remote-letter`).

## What was known
On Windows the app's WebSocket log showed only `open`; the Python client recognised J and sent it over TCP; the server logged nothing about it (it logged nothing about letters at all, by design). Playwright's `websocket` event means the page *created* the socket, not that it connected, so the log could not tell "never connected" from "connected but nothing arrived".

## Changes
- **Server logs (counts only, never the letter):** `letter #N received; sent to K WebSocket clients`, rate-limit refusals, and when a held letter is handed over. `/health` now shows `webSocketClients` and `lettersRelayed`.
- **e2e:** the dollarpy client starts only after `/health` counts one more WebSocket than before the page opened; if it does not, that is its own failing check with the numbers. On a `remote-letter` timeout the launcher prints the app's frames, the client output, the server output and `/health`.
- **Decision on replay:** the server keeps a letter **only if it reached no app**, for `LETTER_HOLD_MS` (default 5000, 0 = off), and hands it **once** to the next app that connects. A letter an app already received is never replayed (a reloaded page does not get old text). Why: the client sends the moment it recognises a letter, so an app a second late would lose it silently; the app only *offers* the letter (the person still points and holds), so a late offer cannot write anything by itself; the letter is held in memory only and never logged.
- Tests: 6 new (`tests/letter-relay.test.ts`: hold/once/ttl/not-held-when-delivered/off/rate limit, and through the real server: early letter reaches the first app only, delivered letter not replayed, log has counts and no letter), plus an order check for `e2e:context`.

## State
- Linux: `npm run check` (872 tests) and `e2e:context` pass.
- **Not run on Windows. The cause is still a hypothesis** (letter sent before the app's socket connected); KNOWN_ISSUES #24 stays open until the author runs `npm run verify` there. If it still times out, the new output says which step is missing.
- No gesture or LETTER threshold changed.

author: devin-ai-integration[bot]
body:
## Summary
In `.autocommit` repos every `:w` is committed, so gitgutter's diff against the index is always empty after a save. This calls `GitGutterBufferDisable` on `BufReadPost`/`BufNewFile` for those buffers. The per-buffer root lookup from #3 moves into `autocommit_root(buf)`, and both autocmds share its cache.

The disable works because gitgutter only sets `enabled` from `g:gitgutter_enabled` while it is still unset, so the `0` survives gitgutter's own buffer init.

Tested headless with Neovim 0.11.4 and vim-gitgutter:
- Gitgutter's `enabled` is `0` for an existing file and for a new file in an `.autocommit` repo.
- Gitgutter is left untouched in an ordinary repo.
- `:w` still produces `[autocommit] save P/P.cpp`.

author: landsman
body:
Closes #64

A failed compression put qpdf's raw stderr in the toast, file paths included, and a failed save did the same with the system's error.

The tool now logs those details as `[ERROR]` and emits a `FAILURE_KIND:` line, which the screen maps to a localized message (en, cs). A rejected file reads "This PDF couldn't be compressed. The file may be damaged or password-protected." The `brew install` hint for a missing tool moves to the logs too, and the toast asks to reinstall.

Verified by running the binary on a damaged file, which logged the qpdf details and `FAILURE_KIND: UNREADABLE_FILE`, and by the unit tests for the kinds and the log parsing. The toast itself was not checked in the running app.

`PdfCompressorIntegrationTest` failed intermittently during this work, on temp files missing from its shared folder, which each test deletes in teardown. Later runs passed on this branch and on main, so the cause is unconfirmed.

Cost (approved in the S261 gateway design, decision 2: under 1 USD a month)

Rollout

- **Ius Scholae** (N): oggi cittadinanza ex legge 91/1992 vs ipotetica proposta basata sulla frequenza scolastica, **non legge vigente**. Per il 2024/25 fonti ISTAT/ISMU e dossier Senato: **931.323 alunni con cittadinanza non italiana, 11,6% del totale; 13,7% nella primaria; 29,4% in provincia di Prato**. Non equivale al numero di minori beneficiari eleggibili: le proposte hanno requisiti su scuola, età, residenza.
- **Nuove discariche** (R): impianti attuali vs ipotesi di nuovi siti, confronto NON cronologico. ISPRA 2024: **102 impianti** per rifiuti di origine urbana (112 nel 2023); **4,43 milioni t** smaltite, **14,8%** dei rifiuti urbani prodotti, **−3,7%** quantità rispetto al 2023. Obiettivo europeo massimo **10% al 2035**, dichiarato come futuro. Dati nazionali non provano necessità o impatto locale di nuove discariche.
- **Nuovi asili nido comunali** (CO): posti operativi e costruzione di nuovi posti, distinta dalla gratuità delle rette. ISTAT 2023/24: **14.570 servizi**, circa **378.500 posti autorizzati**, **31,6 posti/100 bambini sotto i 3 anni**, **59,5% dei servizi con bambini in lista d'attesa** (non 59,5% dei bambini esclusi). PNRR **150.480 posti 0–6**: obiettivo, non risultato completato né solo nidi; fondi 2026 450 milioni assegnati ai Comuni.

## Visualizzazione / controlli
'Di cosa si parla' prioritario, confronto delle opzioni in blocco separato, dati con Paese/periodo/spiegazione/link, pro verdi e contro rossi, caveat su causalità e denominatori. Chromium E2E verifica le tre nuove schede e le precedenti, quattro link per le quattro metriche, note e frecce solo nei confronti corretti. Security Agent, TypeScript/Vite e regressioni obbligatori. Draft fino a CI verde, poi merge e auto-deploy Render. Il Google Sheet sarà aggiornato dopo verifica LIVE.

author: gabrielfernandezmelendez
body:
## Qué cambia
Torneos entre amigos, según el mockup aprobado.
- **Menú → Torneos**: botón nuevo bajo el Mapa del día, con insignia «N en curso».
- **Mis torneos**: lista (en curso, esperando, terminados), **Crear** (con nombre) y **Unirme** con código.
- **Invitar**: código de 6 caracteres, **Copiar** el enlace (`/t/CODIGO`) o **Compartir** (menú del móvil: WhatsApp, etc.).
- **Sala de espera**: pilotos con bandera y la etiqueta Creador. Solo el creador puede empezar, con 2 pilotos como mínimo. Desde ese momento no entra nadie más. Se refresca cada 10 s.
- **En curso / terminado**:
  - tres tarjetas de día; los días acabados muestran al ganador y el mapa de mañana no se desvela;
  - clasificación con los puntos de cada día y el total;
  - botón **Correr el mapa de hoy**.
- **Carrera de torneo** (`/race/:mapa?t=CODIGO`):
  - intentos ilimitados, sin rival;
  - cuenta el mejor tiempo del día en el ranking `t-CODIGO-dN`, que también mejora el del mapa;
  - si el torneo no está en curso, o no es el mapa de hoy, vuelve a la pantalla del torneo.
- Puntos por día: 15-12-10-8-7-6-5-4-3-2. El empate lo rompen los días ganados.

## Reinicio de datos del móvil
Para empezar de cero con los testers, la app borra sola los datos del móvil la primera vez que se abre esta versión (`DATA_RESET_VERSION = 1`).
- Borra: piloto, récords locales, rivales, intentos del día y la sesión y la caché de Firebase.
- Conserva: idioma, estética, volúmenes y tutorial.

**Orden:** 1) desplegar las reglas, 2) merge de esta PR, 3) borrar Firestore (`firestore:delete --all-collections -r`) y los usuarios de Authentication.

## Por qué
Es el siguiente paso de la hoja de ruta: Mapa del día → **Torneos** → carteles.

## Firestore (hay que desplegar)
Nuevo bloque `tournaments/{code}` en `firestore.rules`:
- leer: cualquiera con sesión; listar: solo los miembros;
- crear: el dueño es el único miembro;
- unirse: solo me añado a mí, máximo 10 y nunca con el torneo empezado;
- empezar: solo el creador, con 2 pilotos como mínimo y 3 mapas;
- borrar: nadie.

```
npx -y firebase-tools@latest deploy --only firestore --project rapiddash-gabo
```
Sin desplegar las reglas, crear o unirse falla con «permiso denegado».

## Cómo probarlo
1. Con un piloto: Menú → Torneos → Crear. Copia el enlace.
2. Abre el enlace con otro piloto (otro navegador o el móvil) → Unirme.
3. Con el creador: Comenzar torneo → Correr el mapa de hoy. Haz un tiempo y vuelve: aparece en la clasificación.

Tests: 162 en verde (dominio y caso de uso de torneos). Capturas hechas con un repositorio falso en memoria (no incluido).

author: pingvis
body:
NDI receivers currently convert/upload RGB on the CPU. This port requests packed UYVY for opaque pictures, uploads it at two bytes per pixel and expands it with a wgpu fragment render pass. BGRA/RGBA pictures upload directly with alpha preserved. Failed GPU-pipeline validation retains CPU conversion. Reusable packed frame buffers keep receive-side copying outside the exchange lock.

The shader preserves Nida's existing SD BT.601 / HD BT.709 colour behavior. This is portable wgpu; NDI networking and codec decompression still run through the SDK. Adapted from MIT-licensed im-knots/varda 8e94fcd5a4 (reviewed through 31133902). The branch starts directly at upstream main and excludes Windows backend changes.

Validation:
- All 46 NDI regressions pass locally, including native GPU/CPU colour comparison, padding, alpha, format changes, malformed frames and fallback. The GPU comparison also passes in required Linux lavapipe CI.
- An opt-in real NDI 6.2.1 loopback passes: opaque UYVY reaches the GPU with the reference colour; alpha pictures arrive as BGRA on this runtime, retain alpha 128 exactly and differ by one colour code value from the source.
- RTX 3060 Ti/DX12 optimized microbenchmark, including frame copy/upload/serial GPU completion: CPU fallback 12.058 ms versus GPU 1.155 ms at 1080p; 47.918 versus 4.247 ms at 4K. This excludes SDK/network work and does not compare complete receivers or imply an equivalent FPS increase.
- Production library/benchmark Clippy and the combined fork release smoke pass. The CPU fallback helper was extracted unchanged for benchmark reuse.

Overall upstream CI remains red in existing formatting/platform code, including Windows DeckLink clock_gettime and Linux platform stubs/layout tests. Unmodified base formatting fails too. Independent production cargo check passes with a temporary Windows guard excluded here. External senders, long shows and physical macOS/Linux GPUs remain unqualified.

[Reproduction, loopback evidence and CI limits](https://github.com/pingvis/Nida-Windows/blob/main/docs/varda-feature-port-measurements.md). Upstream baseline blockers are documented for review.

Combined fork qualification also includes a full 3,888-pass library run (17 explicitly ignored, GPU required), followed by 69 passing runner/shutdown checks after the final lifecycle correction.

_Requested by **Dustin** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01JjavRY3uqZkfbXcbFCYZyS?thread=cmsg_01JjavRY3uqZkfbXcbFCYZyS5i7jSpRgBL7wMRkKUuFWa2)_

The second Assistant PR, following #172. It adds more transaction checks, a new **accounts** group, and the waiting count on the inbox header.

## New checks

| Card | Rule | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| different amount? | An entry and a bank copy in one account, ≤ 3 days apart, same payee or alike names, amounts within 25% | **use bank amount**: the entry takes the bank amount, then they match |
| unlinked transfers | Money out of one account and the same amount into another, ≤ 3 days apart, neither a transfer | **link as transfer**, the same as Actual's "make transfer". Between budget accounts neither side keeps a category. To or from off-budget, the budget side keeps its own. |
| wrong account? (maybe) | An entry from the last 60 days whose payee has ≥ 5 other transactions, ≥ 80% of them in one other account | **move to *Visa*** |
| bank sync stale | A linked account whose last sync is ≥ 3 days old, or that has never synced | **sync now** |
| time to reconcile | Last reconcile > 45 days ago with cleared transactions since, or never reconciled with ≥ 10 cleared | **reconcile** opens the account's reconcile |
| old uncleared | Uncleared transactions > 30 days old in an account the bank feeds | **review** opens the register |

- Account cards have no transaction lines. "Later" dismissals keep their keys, because the key changes when the account does (a new sync or reconcile), so the card can come back.
- Cleaning up dismissals now only drops keys whose transactions are gone. Account keys stay.
- Each new fix is one undo step (`move to account`, `link transfer`, and `match` for the amount fix).

## Inbox header count

The inbox pivot header now shows the same small accent count as the assistant: rows to categorize plus possible matches.

## Tests

- `AssistantTest` covers each new check and its fix: adopting the amount, linking a transfer (including the transfer payee), moving on payee habit, the account checks, and account keys surviving dismissal cleanup.
- New baselines: `assistant_more_light`, `assistant_accounts_dark`, `assistant_all_light`. The inbox baselines changed for the header count.
- `ktlintCheck`, `:core:budget:test` and `:app:verifyRoborazziDebug` pass locally.

author: sergiparpal
body:
Five commits on top of `main` (`f7f4c69`). **No run of Stage B exists yet**: the smoke run has not passed, because the pinned provider refused it (below).

1. **`PLAN_REASONED_LOOP.md` signed by Sergi** (§0), alone in its commit.
2. **Stage A**, `results_reasoned_loop/sample.json`: the references, computed after the signature. Every figure §0 declares came back.
3. **§5.5's amendment, its code and its tests**, before signature.
4. **The amendment, drafted and unsigned**, alone in its commit.
5. **The amendment signed by Sergi**, alone in its commit.

**Why the amendment.** Every launch of the smoke run on 2026-10-31 met HTTP 429 from Baidu, the pinned provider: *"temporarily rate-limited upstream"*. OpenRouter listed its endpoint as up throughout.
- **A rate limit became a failed proposal.** Under §5.5 as signed, a call refused on all three attempts was kept as a failed proposal whenever the next call was answered. That leaves an escalation without a rule because the provider was saturated, and it happened at case 0 of the third launch.
- **The smoke check could not pass.** §9's check reads every attempt, so it could not pass a run that met a rate limit at all.

**The change**, in `reasoned_loop/`:
- **A call refused for the rate on every attempt is waited out.** Such an attempt is one `harness/call_record.py` keeps with `RATE_LIMITED = "RateLimitError"`. The call is asked again, with the same messages, after each wait of `RATE_LIMIT_WAIT = (60, 120, 240, 480, 960)` seconds.
- **Once every wait is spent, the run stops.** The call raises `RateLimited`, an `Outage`: nothing records it, and the same command resumes.
- **A call any attempt of which reached the model keeps the signed rule.**
- **The smoke check reads the attempts that reached the model**, and counts the rate-limited ones.
- **The header carries `rate_limit_wait`.**
- **Stage C counts the rate-limited attempts**, and reads the pace without them.
- **`MIN_SIGNATURES = 2`.**

No band, line, row, prompt, setting, seed, trigger, cap or pin moves, and Stage A's record stands.

**The smoke run after the signature.**
- **It recorded nothing.** It was launched at 16:27 UTC under the amended protocol. Its first call was refused on all 18 attempts, through every wait, and the run stopped at 17:06. Nothing was paid.
- **The third launch's partial is set aside.** It was written under the text as signed, and is kept outside git, as the amendment says.
- **Stage B waits on the provider.**

**Checks.**
- The suite is green on 3.12 and 3.10, 2,467 tests. Seven new tests pin the amendment.
- The smoke run's own gates passed `RL-g1` to `RL-g3`. `RL-g4` found two signature lines, none blank.

author: jgorgs
body:
## What this does

Moves the repo's default model policy (`plugins/jstack/models.json`) toward cheaper models for mechanical and high-volume subagent work. The top model stays on judgment and hard debugging. All changes go through tiers, so one line in `models.json` or one line in your override sheet reverts any of them.

**These are repo defaults only.** Any role line in your runtime override sheet still wins over them: `~/.claude/jstack-models.md` on Claude Code, or the Codex, Copilot or Pi equivalents. This PR changes nothing for a role your sheet already names until you re-run `/setup-jstack` or delete that line.

## Audit table

Fire counts come from each skill's own dispatch instructions, not from measured usage.

| Role / skill | Current model | Fires in a typical PR loop | Recommended tier | In this PR |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| jedi-mode `feature, refactoring` | opus (default) | implement: every non-trivial change | default | unchanged |
| jedi-mode `bug-fix` | fable (strongest) | implement: each bug fix | strongest (hard debugging) | unchanged |
| jedi-mode `perf-issue` | fable (strongest) | implement: perf work only | strongest (hard debugging) | unchanged |
| jedi-mode `hillclimb` | fable (strongest) | implement: fans hypotheses out to parallel subagents, many iterations | default | **strongest → default** |
| jedi-mode `judgment and prose` | opus (default) | review/judge: frequent | default | unchanged |
| jedi-mode `strongest judgment` | fable (strongest) | judge: rare, hardest calls | strongest | unchanged |
| jedi-mode trivial mechanical edits | prose said "your fast code model", no role | cleanup: frequent | fast | **new role `mechanical edits` → fast (sonnet)** |
| how `explorer` | opus (default) | explore: 0 or 2–4 per `/how` | fast | **→ fast (sonnet)** |
| how `explainer` | opus (default) | explore: 1 per `/how` | default | unchanged |
| why `investigators` | opus (default) | explore: 1 per MCP category, up to ~7 per `/why` | fast | **→ fast (sonnet)** |
| why `synthesizer` | opus (default) | judge: 1 per `/why` | default | unchanged |
| reflect `tooling` | opus (default) | review: user-invoked only | fast | **→ fast (sonnet)** |
| reflect `judgment, divergent, synthesizer` | opus (default) | review: 3 reviewers + 1 synthesizer, user-invoked only | default | unchanged (see follow-ups) |
| arena `runners` | panel: opus, fable, sonnet, haiku (N=4) | implement: one runner per panel seat | panel | **panel trimmed to 3** |
| arena `cross-judge pool` | panel; judge = first non-parent family | judge: 1 per arena | strongest-first | **panel order now fable first** |
| architect `runners` | panel (N=4) | architecture: one runner per seat, needs ≥2 distinct | panel | **N 4 → 3** |
| interrogate `reviewers` | panel (N=4) | review: one adversary per seat; only run-proven findings survive | panel | **N 4 → 3** |
| swarm `workers` | opus (default) | implement/cleanup: N set by the user or task shape, no default N | fast | **→ fast (sonnet)** |
| no-comments → `comment-sicko` agent | inherits parent | cleanup: 1 per `/no-comments` | fast | **new role → fast (sonnet)** |
| deslop | inherits parent (runs inline, no subagent) | cleanup | n/a, the session model | not changed |
| thermo-nuclear review's 2 subagents | inherit parent | review: 2 per run | strongest/session (deep bug and security review) | not changed |
| statechart | no model role, inherits parent | modeling: rare | session/strongest | not changed |
| jedi-agent (worktree agent) | inherits parent / dispatcher picks | implement | per dispatching role | not changed |

## Reasoning

- **Fast = sonnet, not haiku.** Explorers, investigators and swarm workers still need some judgment. Comment-sicko gets one rerun after a rejected report and then fails, so a weak model there costs a full extra round. You can still point any fast role at `haiku` with one sheet line.
- **Panel drops haiku, not fable.** Architect runners and the arena judge want the top model, so fable stays in the panel and moves to the front of the cross-judge pool. Dropping the cheapest seat still removes one subagent per arena, architect and interrogate run. N=3 is above architect's floor of 2 distinct candidates.
- **hillclimb → default.** It has high fan-out and many iterations of tightly scoped implementation. `bug-fix` and `perf-issue` stay on strongest because they are the hard-debugging roles.
- **Tier, not explicit lists.** Copilot setup asks one question per tier, and `sheet.awk` validates that panel roles span two vendors. Explicit lists would have dropped roles out of every Copilot question, so this PR adds a `fast` tier instead.

## Codex: flagged, unchanged

The `codex` block in `models.json` names Codex models as defaults (`gpt-6-sol` default, `gpt-6-astra` strongest, panel `gpt-6-astra`/`gpt-6-sol`/`gpt-6-luna`), and Pi's `openai-codex` provider table maps families to them. **Flagged:** profiles in our setup must not use Codex models. This PR adds no Codex model. Fast-tier roles map to "your fastest configured Codex model", and the codex example check skips the `fast` tier. The existing Codex block is untouched because tests require the `openai-codex` table. Removing it is a separate decision.

## What quality might drop

- **Exploration** (`how` explorers, `why` investigators): sonnet may miss leads, and the opus explainer or synthesizer can only work with what it gets.
- **Swarm workers** on sonnet may miss subtle issues in each shard.
- **Comment-sicko** may misjudge constraint or "why" comments, which means more parent rejections and reruns.
- **Mechanical edits** on sonnet can occasionally botch a large find-and-replace or patch application.
- **Panel diversity** drops from 4 to 3 seats: fewer independent candidates in arena and architect, and one fewer adversary in interrogate.
- **hillclimb** on opus may find fewer wins per iteration than fable.

## Migration note

On **Copilot**, `sheet.awk` reports every role the sheet lacks. An existing Copilot sheet will report `mechanical edits` and `comment-sicko` as missing until you re-run `/setup-jstack`, which now asks a "Fast model" question. On Claude Code, a missing line falls back to the stamped default.

## Not done (possible follow-ups)

- Run reflect's 3 reviewers on a cheaper tier. Reflect is user-invoked only, and this would change the skill's structure.
- Move interrogate reviewers off the panel tier. That needs Copilot tier work.
- Add a default N to swarm. Today N comes from the user or the task shape.
- CHANGES.md entry and version bump. These are left for release time.

## Checks

- `bun tools/generate.mjs`: ok
- `bun tools/generate.mjs --check`: ok, 95 generated files current
- `bun tools/validate-skills.mjs plugins/jstack/skills`: ok
- `npx --yes markdownlint-cli2@0.18.1 '**/*.md'`: 0 errors in 240 files
- `bun test tests/`: 1005 pass, 40 skip, 0 fail. One assertion in `tests/agent-skills.test.mjs` listed `hillclimb` as a strongest role and was updated for the intended move.

No prices, savings figures or usage numbers are claimed here.

author: nelmad
body:
### Description

Fixes #4261.

When a popover closes in an iframe after the user focuses another pane, removing its focused input can move the iframe's `activeElement` to `body`. The dialog's mutation observer then focuses its container and steals focus back from the other pane.

Defer recovery until the document regains focus, and recover only if its active element is still `body`. Respect paused scopes and retry pending recovery when a parent scope resumes after a nested scope closes. Mount and unmount autofocus behavior is unchanged.

Includes six unit regressions, a two-pane Storybook example, a browser regression covering focus retention and subsequent Tab navigation, and a patch changeset.

### Validation

- Before the fix: five new unit tests fail, and the browser regression reproduces focus being stolen from the second iframe.
- After the fix: 1,205 unit tests pass (2 skipped, 7 todo); all 14 FocusScope, Dialog, and Popover browser tests pass.
- Workspace lint, type checks, formatting, and library builds pass.

Validated with Node 24.19.0, pnpm 11.5.0, and Chromium 151.0.7922.34 using a local executable override. Firefox, WebKit, and Electron were not tested. The separate Next.js SSR application was excluded from dependency installation after registry download failures and was not built.

author: martin-s-a
body:
PR 2 from the review: A5, A6, B3, B4, B5.

| # | Before | Now |
|---|---|---|
| **A6** quotes | an apostrophe ended a bare value and opened a quote: `5'-end 1` or `John's_data/mic.mrc` → "unterminated quoted value", and the **whole file** unreadable. `'it's here'` (valid CIF) failed too | A quote **opens only at the start of a token** and **closes only before whitespace or the end of the line**, as in STAR/CIF and Relion's own tokenizer. A new state machine, `Between/Bare/Quoted/Closing`, split into small functions (`step`, `started`, `bare`, `closing`) |
| **B5** BOM | `﻿data_p` → "data row outside a data block" | skipped on the first line |
| **A5** writer | a value with `\n`/`\r` was quoted across two lines → unreadable file. A column or block name with spaces or `#` → split or cut on reading | `Unwritable` before the file is created |
| **B3** > 2 GiB | `StringBuilder` uses i32 offsets → **panic** → `PanicException` (a BaseException) | the sink **cuts the batch** when a column reaches 1 GiB. Whole reads return `(name, [batches])`, and Python assembles them with `pa.Table.from_batches`, no copy. Symmetric on write: `to_record_batches` no longer joins into one batch (it would overflow again), and Rust writes every batch of a table |
| **B4** a value that does not parse | bare `ArrowInvalid` | `ValueError`: file, canonical table, and the value (from Arrow's message) |

## One deliberate gap, and the doc corrected
B4 does **not** give the line: the rows do not keep their line number once the parser hands them on, and keeping it would cost every read a numeric column. The dated decision in design.md promised "the file and the line" and is corrected to say what it does and why. Also canonical.md.

## Notes
- For B3 I ruled out `LargeStringBuilder`: about 80 MB more per 10M rows on **every** read, a different type for every raw column, and a writer and tests to adapt.
- The equivalence between the fast path and the full scan holds: any line with a quote already went to the scan.
- `ArrowSink` loses `#[derive(Default)]` for an explicit `Default` (it needs `byte_limit`). `with_byte_limit` exists for tests only (`#[cfg(test)]`).

## Tests
Rust: 81 (+8), covering a quote inside a bare value, CIF closing, an unclosed quote, a line break and names in the writer, a round trip with an apostrophe, the BOM, and a block cut into batches by bytes (limit 4 in the test). Python: 254 (+2), a table in several chunks written whole and a value that does not parse (whole and chunked). The four tests of the Arrow boundary now pass lists. Gate green, clippy clean.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

author: arminazimi
body:
## Summary

Implements the Node.js drift collector from #1837.

- Reads `.nvmrc`, `.node-version`, `.tool-versions` (`nodejs`), `package.json` `volta.node` and `engines.node` (floor), every `FROM node:<tag>` stage in `Dockerfile*`, `devcontainer.json` images and the Node feature version, `actions/setup-node` inputs (including matrix values), GitLab CI, CircleCI, and Azure Pipelines images.
- Resolves at major-version granularity. `lts/<codename>` is resolved through the Node.js release schedule (linked in code and docs), including Docker's `lts-<codename>[-variant]` tags. `lts/*`, `latest`, `current`, and `node` stay unresolved.
- Matrix values share one group (`setup-node matrix`), so they are not counted against each other; drift appears when non-matrix pins disagree with each other or fall outside the matrix.
- `--align` rewrites the single-value pins (version files, tool-versions, volta, Docker `FROM` tags while preserving variants, single-value `node-version`) and refuses matrices and floors.
- Reuses `setupNodeVersions`, the Dockerfile/image/devcontainer parsers, and the GitLab/CircleCI parsers; no new dependencies, no network access, no execution of scanned code.

## Commands run

- `npm ci`
- `npm run check` (build, action bundle staging, full test suite, plugin checks, evals) — two clean runs, 3444 tests, 0 failures
- `npm run test:coverage` — all files 95.34% lines / 87.24% branches / 94.97% functions (floors 93/87/93); `src/drift/nodejs.ts` 97.74% lines / 78.46% branches / 100% functions; `src/drift/index.ts` 100% lines / 97.37% branches
- `npm run build:llms` (and its `--check`) after editing `docs/DRIFT.md`

## Evidence

- `tests/drift-nodejs.test.ts` adds CLI-level coverage for every source, Dockerfile stages out of line, `lts/hydrogen` -> 18, unresolved aliases, matrix non-drift, floor conflicts, schema validity, every align patch (verified with `git apply` plus a clean `--check` before/after), align read-only behavior, and a no-network/no-subprocess import check.
- Fixtures under `tests/fixtures/drift/nodejs/` cover `drifted`, `consistent`, `floor-conflict`, `unresolved`, and `align`.
- `examples/drift/nodejs/` demonstrates a drifted repo.

## Notes and gaps

- `src/runtime-pin.ts` is not used directly: its `readPinnedRuntimes` collapses root pins to a single value, while the collector must report every pin and location. Version semantics (floating aliases never resolve) follow that module.
- No corpus run: detector, registry, and corpus behavior are unchanged; only a new drift collector was added.
- Docs generators other than `build:llms` are unaffected (no registry entries, docs pages, or site URLs changed).

Closes #1837

body:
## Problem

**Exam paper generation failing:** `gemini-2.5-pro is no longer available to new users`
- 2 failures on 2026-10-30 at 09:18 UTC
- Route: `exam-paper`
- Parent impact: Cannot generate question papers

## Root Cause

The production environment variable `GEMINI_PRO_MODEL` is set to the retired model `gemini-2.5-pro`. While the code has correct defaults (`gemini-3.1-pro`), environment variable overrides take precedence.

Google's deprecation (effective 2026-10-30):
- `gemini-2.5-pro` → use `gemini-3.1-pro`
- `gemini-2.5-flash` → use `gemini-3.6-flash`

## Solution

Added `mapRetiredGeminiModel()` function in `erpAiGemini.server.ts` that transparently maps deprecated model names to their current stable replacements. This makes the code resilient to env vars holding old model names without requiring env var changes.

## Changes

- **apps/web/src/lib/erpAiGemini.server.ts**: Added mapping function and applied it in `geminiModel()`
- **apps/web/src/lib/erpAiGemini.selftest.ts**: Added tests verifying deprecated models are correctly mapped to current versions

## Test Results

## What

- **`/astro-report`**: a new plugin skill (`plugins/astrology-consultation/skills/astro-report/SKILL.md`). It runs a guided intake as described in ASTRO-REPORT-SPEC, then renders the report through `create_report`. The intake covers:
  - an identity gate before any birth details;
  - date and time validation;
  - the UTC-offset confirmation, DST gap and overlap (`fold`), local mean time, and a forced clock confirmation for pre-1948 South Asia;
  - birth-time sensitivity, consent to print birth data, a confirmation screen, then delivery.
- **Report grounding is mandatory (AU-02).** MCP, REST and the CLI now share one `report_checks` sequence: grounding, citations, fact refs and outlook checks.
  - `create_report` recomputes the engine facts from the birth input. The birth input is not printed, and the client never supplies the facts.
  - A dated model sent without the birth input is refused.
  - A window is grounded only by events of the planets or periods named next to it. On random 3-month windows the pass rate drops from 100% to 36%.
- **MCP parity (AU-14, AU-20).** Every MCP birth tool takes `ayanamsa` and `calendar`. `span_min` is on sensitivity and applicability in MCP and REST. `rest._mode` is removed.
- **Separation and safety (AU-04, AU-17).** New `checks()` rules:
  - a Lal Kitab unit needs an `edition` and an `lk-` section;
  - the citation family must match the unit's system (by book id or name);
  - `combined` units are allowed only in a comparison section;
  - `TEXT` basis is allowed only for rules.

  The NEVER list now covers every ⛔ item and any harm to an animal, and runs on all client text. Guarantee and legal-outcome wording is now an error.
- **Setup (AU-07).** `/setup` asks for consent before the GeoNames place-list download. `doctor` gets a places row. The GeoNames licence row is added.
- **Reports folder guard.** `create_report` refuses a `reports_dir` inside a git work tree, the plugin folder or the skill folder.
- **Exporter.** Plugin `skills/` and `agents/` are now exported, with a test that every `plugin/` file is mapped.
- **Sample and tests.** An invented sample report ("Asha", career, Parashari, consent No) is included as HTML plus its model; the PDF is kept private because the KEEP-OUT gate bans `.pdf`. New tests: `test_astro_report_skill`, `test_astro_report_acceptance` (the 40 spec items), `test_lk_never`, `test_mcp_parity`, `test_sample_report`.
- **Private repo only.** `tools/cc_hooks.py guard` now blocks `private/` and the personal report folders for Bash and the file tools.

## Verified (commands run, real result lines)

- Workspace: `pytest tests` → `1185 passed, 34 skipped`; ruff → `All checks passed!`. The skill selftests and `cc_hooks.py selftest` print ok.
- Private clone: `pytest` → `1186 passed, 33 skipped` (baseline 1120/32). `privacy_check.py --archive …` → `0 finding(s)`; gitleaks → `no leaks found`; pre-commit passed.
- Public clone: `pytest` with the engine on PYTHONPATH → `1069 passed, 63 skipped` (baseline 1004/62). `privacy_check.py` → `0 finding(s)`; gitleaks → `no leaks found`; KEEP-OUT gate passed.
- Guard probes: 12 of 12 as expected (9 blocked, 3 allowed, including `/private/tmp`).

## Known limits (follow-up issues)

- Grounding is proximity-based. A key-point window that names a planet with many events (Saturn, Jupiter) still passes when shifted by about 5 months. Shifted dasha rows and windows that name no planet are caught.
- `get_panchang` takes no `ayanamsa` or `calendar`.
- "Unknown time means compact only" is enforced in SKILL.md, not in the engine.
- The guard cannot see inside a recursive search started above `private/`. A bare word "private" in a command run from the workspace is blocked (false positive).
- Not run: a live Claude Code `/astro-report` turn, because the CLI is not logged in on this Mac. CI runs `claude plugin validate --strict`.

All people in the tests and the sample are invented. No real birth data.

author: pichu2707
body:
Second of three PRs for S9 (run view and persistence), task 9.1b. The orchestrator stays behind the off-by-default `[ai.orchestrator]` gate, and the README is untouched (D14). 9.1c (resume) follows.

## What

- **Worker traces.** A new `OrchestraEvent::Trace` carries a worker's streamed text and its tool rows.
  - The runtime `Tracer` buffers text and flushes at 4 KiB, after 50 ms, before a tool row, at the end of a turn, and before an abort. That keeps a worker's last words ahead of its terminal row and of `Ended`.
  - The app keeps traces in `ChatState`, never in chat entries, so they are not stored or sent as history.
  - Bounds:
    - 128 KiB per worker. Only the excess is trimmed, down to 7/8 of the cap, with an `(earlier output dropped)` line.
    - 16 workers.
    - Tool rows are capped at 512 bytes.
  - All text is sanitised again on entry.
- **The view.** `Ctrl+Space W` opens a full-pane, read-only, scrollable transcript of the worker selected with Alt+Up/Down.
  - It follows new output, and End follows it again after scrolling.
  - The wheel scrolls the view. Esc or `q` closes it.
  - Wrapped rows are cached per width.
  - A trace redraws only when its worker is on view.
- **Never in the way.**
  - Approvals and the batch review are routed before the view and stay answerable.
  - Halted and Declined alerts close the view.
  - Ctrl+C still cancels.
- **Never silent.** Each of these shows a notice:
  - no selection, the gate off, a shell pane, or another view open;
  - a paste, or the prefix keys T, n, s, e, o, a, while the view is open;
  - any unused key.
- **Key.** `W` (capital) is a root prefix leaf, because lowercase `w` is the window group. It is added to the modal-input delta. The choice is pending the user's review.

## Review

- **First review:**
  - a tool row could wipe ~128 KiB of the freshest text;
  - every delta redrew the pane and re-wrapped up to 128 KiB;
  - the wheel and paste went to the hidden conversation;
  - paging could disagree with the drawn rows.

  All of these are fixed.
- **Re-review:** verdict merge. Its two follow-ups are applied:
  - a worker's text is flushed before it is aborted;
  - an unused key does not replace an existing notice.

## Testing

- `cargo test`: 8161 passed, 0 failed.
- clippy `-D warnings` and fmt are clean.
- There are new snapshots for the view only.

body:
## Summary

A product spec can declare a row range per source table. A production `rocky run` counts each declared source once, at the start of the model phase, before anything is written. An `error` breach refuses the product's output model, so no table is written.

```toml
[[product.source.volume]]
table = "raw.sales.orders"   # must be in source.tables
min_rows = 1_000
max_rows = 50_000_000
severity = "warning"         # default; or "error"
```

```
run start ── one COUNT(*) per distinct source (memoized) ──┬─ in range ──▶ recorded
                                                           ├─ warning breach ──▶ volume_warnings, build goes on
                                                           └─ error breach / count not taken at error
                                                                 ──▶ output model refused (no write),
                                                                     run partial, no due_at
```

Only the delivered output is protected; upstream models in the chain still build. The CHANGELOG and docs say so.

Design: advisor-ruled 2026-10-31 (Fable advisor), maintainer to confirm. An Opus red team reviewed the first ruling and found two blocking gaps (how a refused build is recorded, and checking only before the output). The revised ruling fixed both, and this PR builds the revised one.

## Subproject(s) touched

- [x] `engine/` (Rust CLI / crates)
- [x] `sdk/python/` (`rocky-sdk` Python client)
- [x] `editors/vscode/` (TypeScript extension)
- [x] `docs/` (documentation site)
- [x] `schemas/` (canonical CLI JSON schema)

## Changes

- `rocky-core` `product/spec.rs`: `SourceSpec.volume: Vec<SourceVolumeSpec>` (omitted when empty), sharing slice 1's bound parser and judge. New reject codes `volume-source-unknown`, `volume-source-duplicate`, `source-table-invalid`. The identifier check applies only to tables a range names, so existing specs (for example a hyphenated BigQuery project) keep parsing.
- `rocky-core` `product/manifest.rs`, lowering: `product.source.volume` in `COVERED_LEAF_FIELDS` and a manifest row when the list is non-empty. No generated test.
- `rocky-core` `state.rs`: `RunRecord.source_volumes` (defaulted, omitted when empty). The state schema stays v34. `StateStore::last_source_volumes`.
- `rocky-cli` new `commands/run_source_volume.rs`: loading (production and project root only), one count per distinct formatted table ref, verdicts, refusals. Counts race the cancel token.
- `rocky-cli` `run.rs`: counts before the model phase's first write and before the skip gate. Serial refusal through `fail_unretried_model`. Concurrent refusal as the model's `Err` before the retry loop, with `matched`, `skip_states` and `to_build` untouched. A refused output bypasses the skip gate, so an `error` breach is never hidden by an unchanged-output skip.
- `rocky-cli` `output.rs`, `product.rs`: `RunOutput.source_volumes` (omitted when empty), copied to the run record. `rocky product status` gains `source_volumes`.
- Codegen: `schemas/` (run, product_status, rocky_product), Pydantic, TypeScript, `openapi.json`; hand-written `types.py` gains `source_volumes`.
- Docs: a "Source volume ranges" section in `reference/commands/products.md`. CHANGELOG `[Unreleased]` → Added.

## Test Plan

- `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy -p rocky-cli -p rocky-core --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`: clean (on this rebased branch).
- `cargo test -p rocky-cli --features duckdb --lib run_source_volume`: 15 passed. They cover: in range; warning breach; error breach (table untouched, no materialization, one failed execution with time, downstream withheld, partial, no `due_at`); `model_error` only, at parallel 1 and 4; a refused model mid-layer in fail-fast and contained modes; one count for two products; unreadable source at error and warning; cancel; skipped output keeps its count; shadow counts nothing; status; and an `error` breach refused even when the skip gate would skip.
- `cargo nextest run --all-features -p rocky-core -p rocky-cli` (builder, before rebase): 6207 passed. The 6 failures were `chmod 000` tests that only fail as root. 2 of them are fixed on `main` by #2504; the 4 in `rocky-cli` are the same pattern and pass in CI (non-root).
- `just codegen` then `git status`: no drift. `just regen-fixtures`: no fixture diff. SDK `test_schema_parity.py`: 59 passed; full SDK pytest 362 passed; Dagster pytest 819 passed.
- Not run: a live warehouse other than DuckDB.

**Red team (code):** Claude Fable 5.1, a fresh read-only agent, with the diff, `AGENT_REVIEW.md` and the two required answers. Nothing blocking. Dispositions:
- Should-fix, an `error` breach swallowed when the skip gate skips the output: fixed. A refused output bypasses the gate, with a new serial and parallel test.
- Maintainer question, a spec that cannot be read or parsed at run time is skipped with a warning (ranges not checked, even at `error`): kept as slice 1 behaves. It is now documented, pointing at `rocky product verify`, which refuses such a spec. **Hugo to decide** whether an `error` range should make an unreadable spec refuse instead.
- Nit, a shared table's count time added twice to a refusal: fixed (timed once).
- Nit, the cancel wording: fixed (DuckDB finishes the query in the background).
- It confirmed: concurrent refusal follows the same containment and fail-fast path as a real failure; no off-by-one in the hook loop; runs with no ranges issue no extra queries and change no output; no new `_ =>` wildcard; codegen complete.

body:
## What Donovan saw

"Sometimes this gets stuck", then "it's when in the relative area" (three Shotate recordings, 2026-10-31 15:57–16:00). The Workspace Dock stayed up for 3–6 s with the pointer resting 25–50 pt above or beside the bar, over the app underneath (his T3 composer), and only went down once the pointer moved well away.

## Cause

The keep zone was built from the **panel's** frame plus 24 pt slack. The panel is larger than the bar: a bottom dock keeps a 24 pt hover-label row and 8 pt spacing above the bar, and the panel is at least 480 pt long. So the invisible hold area reached ~56 pt above the bar and ~100+ pt beside a narrow one. (#43 fixed a different hold: a stale menu flag.)

## Fix

- `DockEdge.keepZone(bar:panel:sideOpen:screen:)`: the bar you see plus 12 pt (still extended to the screen edge), or the whole panel while the window strip or "+N" list is open, since those sit above the bar and take clicks. Before the bar has reported its frame, the panel stands in.
- The bar reports its frame (`CenterReport(key: "bar")`); `DockEdge.screenRect` converts it to screen coordinates (inverse of `DockCarry.point`, tested).

## Logging

- `trace.log`: `dock up: <edge>, pointer x,y, panel WxH`, `dock down: pointer left at x,y after Ns up`, `dock down: overview open`, `dock drag cancelled…`, and `dock held 2s off the bar by strip|menu|drag: pointer …, bar …` once per hold.
- Every `Trace.log` line also goes to the unified log (subsystem `com.baney.baneyspaces`, public: lines hold workspace numbers, window ids and app names, never titles), so Shotate debug recordings, which reported "nothing from the app itself", now carry them.

## Checks

author: rodloboz
body:
`mix deps.get` flags five packages as vulnerable. This PR fixes four of them before 0.5.0 goes to Hex.

## Changes

| Package | Scope | Lock | Requirement | Advisories |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `jose` | optional, shipped | 1.11.12 → 1.11.13 | `~> 1.11 and >= 1.11.13` | EEF-CVE-2026-65625 to 65632 (8) |
| `phoenix_html` | optional, shipped | 4.3.0 → 4.4.0 | `~> 4.4` | EEF-CVE-2026-117645 |
| `plug_crypto` | shipped (now direct) | 2.2.0 → 2.2.1 | `~> 2.2 and >= 2.2.1` | EEF-CVE-2026-105963 |
| `bandit` | dev/test | 1.13.0 → 1.14.1 | `~> 1.14 and >= 1.14.1` | 12 HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2, WebSocket |

- The lock alone does not protect users of a library, so the `mix.exs` requirements now exclude the vulnerable versions.
- Sake calls `Plug.Crypto` directly (auth, sessions, cursors), so `plug_crypto` is now a direct requirement.
- CHANGELOG: new `### Security` section under 0.5.0.

## Not fixed: `cowlib` 2.21.0 (EEF-CVE-2026-43966, MEDIUM)

- 2.21.0 is the latest release, and the advisory has no fixed version.
- It comes only from `bypass` → `plug_cowboy` → `cowboy` in tests. It is not shipped.
- Cowboy 2.16+ already rejects CR/LF in response headers (`invalid_response_headers`).

## Verification

- `mix precommit`: compile with warnings as errors, unused-lock check, format, `credo --strict`, and 1200/1200 tests pass.
- `mix deps.get` now flags only `cowlib`.

author: michaelassraf
body:
Change-Set: feat-per-route-css
ClickUp task: CU-17tkuw61z4z [Finish per-page CSS: each page inlines only the classes it uses](https://app.clickup.com/t/17tkuw61z4z)

## What

Each page's HTML carries only the Tailwind rules for the classes it renders. The complete sheet loads after paint.

- **`next-styles build`** (new command): runs `next build` with `NEXT_STYLES=routes`, then:
  - reads the classes in every prerendered page's HTML, and requests each static route that renders per request (`next start` on the finished build);
  - builds one sheet per route with the app's own Tailwind config, PostCSS plugins and stylesheet;
  - writes the sheets to `.next-styles/`, traced into the server bundle, and fills each prerendered page.
  - It fails when a route sheet is over 15 KB brotli.
- **`RouteStyles`** (`@flamingo-stack/openframe-frontend-core/route-styles`, rendered once in the root layout):
  - The client part reads `usePathname` during the server render and asks a resolver the server part registered in the process. The rules reach the HTML only, never the RSC payload: Next's `inlineCss` writes a sheet three times.
  - A parse-time loader appends the complete sheet last, at low priority.
  - `complete` keeps the complete sheet on pages that depend on the visitor (signed-in hubs).
- **`withRouteStyles`** (next config) and **`withRouteStylesTailwind`** (Tailwind config, in `style-sources`): under `next-styles build` the root sheet has no utilities, and every page brings its own. `next dev` and any other build behave as before.

## Order

Tailwind v3 writes rules in its own order whatever the content. A route sheet is therefore the complete sheet with rules left out and the rest in the same order, and the complete sheet is appended last. Two partial sheets never override each other in the wrong order. A test pins this.

## Measured (local production builds)

| | Inline CSS (brotli) | HTML (brotli) | FCP, Lighthouse mobile, median of 5 |
|---|---|---|---|
| flamingo `/` | 29.3 → 12.9 KB | 92.5 → 69.4 KB | 1711 → 1290 ms |
| flamingo `/blog` | 29.3 → 11.6 KB | 74.5 → 50.7 KB | 1568 → 1116 ms |
| flamingo blog post | 29.3 → 12.0 KB | 82.5 → 59.3 KB | 1717 → 1293 ms |
| flamingo `/pricing` | 29.3 → 11.7 KB | 75.1 → 51.3 KB | 1671 → 1278 ms |
| openframe-oss-frontend pages | 32.5 → 10.3–12.0 KB | 49–55 → 19.5–25.8 KB | |

After the complete sheet loads, computed styles match the baseline at 390 and 1440 px on 7 hub pages and 4 frontend pages; only animations differ.

## Traps found (written beside the code)

- Turbopack traces what a Tailwind config and a next config import. If either reaches the build tool, Next's server, sharp's native libraries and esbuild end up in the trace and the build fails. So the Tailwind wrapper lives in `style-sources`, and the build tool is loaded behind `turbopackIgnore`.
- React drops custom attributes on a hoisted `<style>`, so the complete sheet's address rides on the loader's `<script>`.

## Tests

`src/__tests__/route-styles.test.ts`:
- class extraction;
- the subset order;
- a finished-build fixture (one sheet per route, every page filled);
- the route resolver;
- the config wrappers.

Release this before the hub and openframe-oss-frontend PRs of this change set.

author: beriki770-ship-it
body:
## What this changes

Part 2 of #749: R-ENEMY-005. The four 1948 operation cards can now give orders to units, under the owner's three rulings of 31 October 2026 on #749. Refs #749.

- **Ruleset: GDD 0.1 only.** A new option key, `unit_orders: [{ unit, q, r }]`, gives the unit of a `map/units_1948.yaml` row a go-to order toward one of that row's own anchor hexes. The order goes through the player's own go-to (`Movement.GiveGoTo`) and shares the movement points the turn's orders have already spent, whether the card is chosen or left to the cabinet. A refused order changes nothing, the same as a refused player order, and the player is told (below). Under `gdd-0.3` the loader still checks the orders but `EventSystem` does not apply them, so the four cards stay effect-free for units. The legacy loop ignores them.
- **Loader.** It refuses an unknown row, and any hex that is not one of that row's anchor hexes in `map/unit_anchor_hexes.yaml`. So a card cannot send a unit somewhere no source places it.
- **Sourced anchors only.** Only the three anchors receive orders.
- **Orders expire with the operation** (the owner's answer 1, 31 October 2026, on this PR):
  - **The window is the anchor's dates, not the card's.** A card's order ends on the `to` date of the anchor it sends the unit to (`map/units_1948.yaml`). From the first turn on or after that day the unit stops where it stands, with a Why line ("stopped: the operation's order to ... has ended"). Why the anchor: a card's `from`/`to` is when the decision is open, not when the operation ran (Horev's card closes on 23 December 1948, but the operation ran to 7 January 1949). The anchor's window is the sourced span of the position the operation sends the unit to. Carmeli's Brosh anchor ends on 19 July 1948, the second truce. Golani's Julis anchor ends on 24 February 1949, the Egypt armistice (`end_basis: front_armistice`). So there are no late arrivals and no marches after an armistice. The loader refuses an order to an anchor with no `to`. The choice is in the code comment (`EventSystem.OrderEnds`) and in `docs/rules/mvp.md` R-ENEMY-005.
  - **The march never ends on an enemy-held place it was not sent to.** A card's route, and each turn's step of it, goes round every enemy-held locality (`Movement.NoEntry`, whether an open target or not), except the hex it was sent to. So Golani goes round Nazareth on the way to Julis and captures nothing. If no route goes round, the order is refused. The player's own go-to is unchanged: it may still end on an open target and capture it. A go-to the player gives replaces a card's order, and so does any other order.
  - **A refused card order tells the player.** It goes into the turn's refusals, like a refused order of the player's, as a go-to for that unit with the reason `Orders.RefusedCardOrder`. The toast shows it the same way ("Not done: The unit could not take the operation's order"; Hebrew: "לא בוצע: לא ניתן היה לבצע את פקודת המבצע ליחידה"). The two new Hebrew strings are agent-drafted and marked for the native reviewer (#564).
- **Pins.** The four cards are re-pinned in `Gdd03EventRulesTests`. Their review status is unchanged (`status: sensitivity-reviewed`), per ruling 2. So `ReleaseGate`, `RealContentTests` and DECISIONS D11 are untouched.

### The four changed cards

| Card | Option | What changed |
|---|---|---|
| `ten_days` | `central_front` (historical) | New `unit_orders`: **Yiftach → Lydda** (hex -3,21) and **Carmeli → facing the Syrian bridgehead at Mishmar HaYarden** (hex 13,5). There is a comment citing both sources. |
| `ten_days` | `southern_front` (alternative) | A comment only: no unit orders until a source is found. |
| `operation_horev` | `launch` (historical) | New `unit_orders`: **Golani → Julis camp** (hex -7,24). There is a comment citing the source. |
| `operation_horev` | `hold` (alternative) | A comment only: no unit orders until a source is found. |
| `operation_yoav` | both options | A comment only: no unit orders on either option, because no source in the repo places a unit at a dated position inside the window. |
| `operation_hiram` | both options | The same as Yoav. |

No text, Hebrew, effects, `set_rung`, sources or status changed on any card.

### Each anchor's source line

- **Dani: Yiftach at Lydda.** `content/map/units_1948.yaml:733` (yiftach's anchor "Lydda", 11 to 20 July 1948). `research_notes/M4 war mode/war-1948.md` section 3, the Dani row (line 139).
- **Brosh: Carmeli facing the bridgehead at Mishmar HaYarden.** `content/map/units_1948.yaml:207` (carmeli's anchor, 9 to 19 July 1948). `war-1948.md` section 3, the Brosh row (line 141).
- **Horev: Golani at Julis.** The `war-1948.md` section 3 Horev row (line 149) is the source for Golani taking part. It does not name Julis. Julis comes from the units file's anchor: `content/map/units_1948.yaml:135` (golani's anchor "Julis camp", from December 1948), with he.wiki's end_note at `:129` (in December 1948 the brigade moved to the Julis camp). The card's comment now says so.

**Yoav, Hiram and every alternative option give no orders until sources are found.** The cards' comments say so too.

### For the owner's review

- **Yiftach's order reaches nobody.** Yiftach has no unit on the board, because no anchor covers 15 May 1948 (R-UNIT-006, `StartingForcesTests`). The order is on the card as ruled, but it is dropped. It is not kept for later.
- **Where the brigades end up now.** Carmeli sets out from Haifa on 15 July 1948 and reaches 8,8 in the Lower Galilee that turn. Its order ends on 19 July, so on 15 August it stops there. Golani sets out from Yavne'el on 15 December 1948 and goes round Nazareth. Its order ends on 24 February 1949, so on 15 March it stops at 3,14, between Zikhron Ya'akov and Hadera, short of Julis. The order expires before it arrives: monthly turns and the way round are too slow to get there inside the window. This is ruling 1 working as asked, not a bug. There is no capture and no fighting. In every golden the final state differs from main's only in where these two brigades stand. Details are in `docs/determinism.md`.
- **Not done here: the anchor move to the 4.4 km hexes** (answer 2) waits for #1796.
- **The unit card follows the card's march** (the owner's ruling of 1 November). For a unit on an operation card's go-to, the card's "Turns to arrive" line now counts the route the march really takes, round every enemy-held place the card did not send it to (`Movement.Route` with `card`, the same flag the march uses). It no longer counts the player's route through Nazareth. The route drawn while you pick a new go-to stays the player's own, because your own go-to replaces the card's order. This is presentation only: the sim and the goldens are unchanged.

## AI assistance

Claude Code (Opus) wrote the change, the tests and the docs, and then the follow-up for the owner's answer 1 (a separate Claude reviewer agent read that round too: READY, no blocking items). A separate Claude reviewer agent checked the diff against the owner's rulings (first verdict NOT READY because of a false changelog claim about Yiftach; fixed; then READY). Round 3 (the route preview) was also written by Claude Code (Opus) and read by two separate Claude reviewer agents (both READY, no blocking items). The "I can defend every line" box is left for Beri.

## Evidence

Round 3 (`4b1fa2bf`, the route preview). Red first, before the fix (`UnitOrdersTests.ACardOrderedUnitsCardCountsTheWayRound`: Golani at 4,12 on a card's go-to to 8,9, beyond Nazareth at 7,10):

```
  Expected: String containing "On its way to the chosen hex. Turns to arrive: 2"
  But was:  "... On its way to the chosen hex. Turns to arrive: 1"
```

After: `dotnet test` 3987 of 3987 passed with no golden or sim file in the diff; `check.sh origin/main` ALL CHECKS PASSED; Unity EditMode InfoPanelLayoutTests, UnitOrdersTests and EventCardTests 124 of 124 passed. A full EditMode run (3766 tests) failed only the server's known environment

author: playlikeboy
body:
### Description

Studio already has unit tests under `apps/studio/src/services/tests`, but `apps/studio` has no jest configuration and no `test` script, so `pnpm test` (`turbo run test`) never executes them. This PR makes those tests runnable and adds coverage for two of the services listed in #1246.

**Test runner**

- `apps/studio/jest.config.js` built on `next/jest`, with `jest-environment-jsdom` and a `@/` path alias
- `apps/studio/jest.setup.js` registering `@testing-library/jest-dom` and the `TextEncoder` / `TextDecoder` / `structuredClone` globals the parser needs under jsdom
- `apps/studio/__mocks__/` for assets, `monaco-editor`, `monaco-yaml`, `@asyncapi/react-component` and `jsonpath-plus` (whose default export condition is an ESM build jest cannot load; the mock resolves its CommonJS build through `@asyncapi/parser`'s dependency tree, so it is not tied to the pnpm store layout or a version)
- `test` / `test:watch` scripts and `jest` + `jest-environment-jsdom` devDependencies

**New tests** (following the existing `createServices()` pattern)

- `server-api.service.test.ts`: generate flow, template download, error handling
- `specification.service.test.ts`: `shouldInformAboutLatestVersion` and `tryInformAboutLatestVersion`

One existing test (`navigation.service.test.ts`, "does not cleanup on non-url transitions") needed a `filesState` seed to pass when the suite actually runs.

`settings.service.ts` is intentionally not covered here because #1372 already adds those tests; this PR is complementary to it.

### Related issue(s)

Part of #1246


#### v1.15.0

Makes `niks3 push --stdin` dependable for long-running callers such as build farms, plus client fixes for unresponsive servers and concurrent uploads.

##### Features

- `push --stdin --retry-timeout 2m` keeps retrying a failing request for that long, so a server restart no longer fails a push. The limit applies per request. The default stays at a few seconds.

- `push --stdin` now exits on SIGTERM and SIGINT. It used to keep running and answer every further request with "context canceled".

- A server that accepts connections but never answers no longer blocks a push indefinitely or makes it ignore Ctrl-C. Each upload registration now gets two minutes.
- Errors after exhausted retries include the server's explanation again, instead of ending in "server returned 503: ".
- Uploading a build log no longer risks a crash (SIGSEGV or SIGBUS) when the server answers early, for example with 403 or 503.

author: the-anonymous-aspirant
body:
## Summary

This is the on-demand Gmail pull, system_3 #8806-B1. The epic is #8806: Gmail into the data lake on demand, read-only, at high sensitivity.

`scripts/gmail/gmail.sh pull [--full]` runs the new `scripts/gmail/gmail_pull.py` in the existing pinned `aspirant-gmail:local` image.

**Credentials (none stored).** The A1 token is opened in memory with `gmail_auth.load_credentials`. That needs the KEK, exactly as `status --check` does, and without one the pull refuses with exit 2. The same refresh check runs first: a refused token exits 3 with the re-consent line instead of returning stale mail.

**Full pull (first run, or `--full`).**
- Reads `users.getProfile` for the history id *before* listing, so a message arriving mid-listing is replayed next time, not missed.
- Then runs `users.messages.list` and a `users.messages.get` with `format=full` for each message.

**Incremental pull (later runs).**
- Reads `users.history.list` from the stored history id (message added/deleted, label added/removed) and fetches only the touched messages.
- A 404 means the history has expired, and the run falls back to a full pull (`fallback=history_expired`).
- Spam and trash are left out on both paths. A message moved there shows up in the delta's `deleted_ids`.

**Output.** Each run with a change writes `/data/gmail/runs/<run_id>/` on the LUKS volume (`/dev/mapper/data_crypt`), at modes 0600/0700. The directory is renamed into place only once it is complete, and holds:
- `messages.json`: `{"messages": [...], "deleted_ids": [...], "mode", "base_history_id", "history_id", ...}`. This is the shape aspirant-explorer's `/api/assets/{sha}/messages` parses: `from`, `text` and `date` are its first-choice keys, and it requires `kind == message_export`.
- `manifest.json`: the source manifest `scripts/lake_ingest.py` loads, with `dataset_id: gmail` and one record `kind: message_export, sensitivity: high`.

Each message carries `id, threadId, date (UTC from internalDate), from, to, cc, subject, labels, text, attachments`.
- `text` is the text/plain part, or the visible text of the HTML (no script or style) when there is none, decoded in the part's declared charset.
- `attachments` is `name, mime, size` only. No attachment content is fetched until security's review (#8806-D1) says otherwise.

**Commit order.** The new history id is written to `state.json` last, after the run directory is in place. A run that dies earlier repeats the same window next time. An `flock` refuses a second concurrent pull with exit 7.

**Logging.** One line of counts and the run id. No subject, address, body or token is printed.

**Boundaries.**
- This program does not encrypt; the lake ingest (#8806-B2) does that through the existing runner. It stores no credential.
- No compose or service change: nothing runs until the operator invokes the wrapper. A real run is #8806-E1.

## Test plan

- `tests/gmail_pull_unit.sh` runs `tests/gmail_pull_test.py` in the pinned image with `--network none`: **12 passed**. The fake service mimics googleapiclient's `users()` call chain and raises the library's own `HttpError`, so the wrapper's pagination and 404 mapping run as written. The mailbox (`tests/fixtures/gmail/mailbox.json`) is synthetic, in Gmail API v1 response shapes, with no real mail. It includes a UTF-8 subject, a multipart/alternative body with a PDF attachment, an HTML-only body, an ISO-8859-1 body, spam, a label change, a move to trash, a deletion, and a message added and deleted within the window.
- **Acceptance:** a full pull at S1, then the incremental delta S1→S2, equals a fresh full pull at S2. Compared message by message as canonical JSON bytes. The incremental run never calls `messages.list`.
- **Negative control:** a mutant that tracks only `messagesAdded` in the history fails exactly that test.
- Other cases covered:
  - the 404 fallback equals the full S2 export;
  - a crash while writing the manifest leaves `state.json` at the old id and no manifest-bearing directory, and the retry repeats the window;
  - a no-change run writes nothing and advances the id;
  - modes are 0600/0700;
  - `lake_ingest.load_manifest` accepts the manifest and reports that it needs a KEK;
  - refusals: a malformed KEK exits 2, no token exits 6, `invalid_grant` exits 3, a wrong KEK exits 2, and none of them writes to staging;
  - the lock exits 7;
  - output from two command runs contains none of the fixture's subjects, addresses or bodies.
- `tests/gmail_auth_unit.sh` is unchanged and still runs. `gmail_auth.py` is not edited.
- `bash -n scripts/gmail/gmail.sh`.

author: cconstantine
body:
Fixes SME-324.

`agents::tests::ended::test_no_notice_when_the_child_waits_on_something_or_finished` was failing most module runs, so it reddened many gates. The flake is in the test.

**The race.** The test pauses `BEFORE_START_DONE`, keyed by the parent, and all three children share that root. When the first or second child's start was still running, that child took the pause instead of the third. The test then made the third child's pod row before its start reached `credentials::reconcile_pod`. That call finds the pod and fails without a cluster ("couldn't write its credentials into its pod"), so the child never had a turn, and `checked_after` timed out at 10 s. Failing module runs took the full window (~11.8 s), passing ones ~6 s.

**The fix.** The test waits for the first two starts to end (`test_hooks::starts_ended`) before taking the pause, with a comment saying why. That is one test file, 9 lines.

**Evidence**, from the `agents::tests::` module run 5 times under the cluster lock:

| Build | `ended` test failed |
| -- | -- |
| `65bb444` (main's code, on SME-78's branch) | 3 / 5 |
| `09f223e` (SME-78) | 3 / 5 |
| this commit | 0 / 5 |

The one other red in the "after" runs was `agents::tests::sweep::test_the_sweep_fails_a_start_a_restart_cut_off` (SME-336), which PR #199 fixes.

**Gate:** `scripts/check.sh` on `c184473`, all checks passed.

It came out of SME-78's gates, on the Ticket Driver's call.

author: lmoresi
body:
On the rotated route, the FAC patch blocks ran PCASM's default unshifted ILU(0) where LU was configured. That held for the saddle-point solve and the thin sheet alike. This PR makes them run the LU.

Closes #892

## What was wrong

`_configure_pcmg` writes the FAC block solver into the options database: LU with a nonzero shift. In the composite FAC form, the default since 891c9bb0, the patch ASM is the composite's second member, and it sets up at its first application. Both rotated call sites set up only the level smoother, then dropped their per-solve keys. The blocks then took PCASM's default. The non-rotated installs always read the LU, because their keys are never dropped.

## The fix

`custom_mg._set_up_fac_smoothers` runs after the PCMG set-up, while the keys are still there. It replaces the two rotated loops and is also called by the velocity-block install. It sets up each FAC level's smoother and its ASM. It then sets the block PC type and factor shift on the live block KSPs, so the blocks run the configured solver even where the ASM had already set up.

## Measured

UWTN 2026-022's linear fault fixture, all-application velocity iterations:

| band ratio h_b/S | 6 | 12 | 24 |
|---|---|---|---|
| ILU blocks (development) | 180 | 259 | 344 |
| LU blocks (this PR) | 66 | 65 | 67 |

On the box: 7 velocity iterations per Newton increment at band ratios 8, 16 and 25. The fixed build reproduces the earlier LU-block measurements exactly.

## Tests

- **test_1090** reads the live PC objects after the solve, not the options database, which held the right keys all along. It covers the rotated saddle-point, rotated thin-sheet, standard velocity-block and scalar top-level installs, each in the composite and the plain ASM FAC form.
  - Against 799ef021 it fails the two rotated composite cases, in serial and at np 2.
  - On this branch it passes in serial and at np 2 and 4.
- **A tier C characterisation** pins which levels carry a FAC patch per install, on test_1022's composed stack. The standard install patches levels 2 and 3. The rotated path clears every coarse level's rows after the orphan restriction, so it patches level 3 only. That rule has not been ruled on, and the test makes a change to it deliberate.

## Docs

`faults-in-convection.md` now says its hierarchy counts were measured while the blocks ran ILU(0). They are to be re-measured after this merges (step 5 of #892's plan). Design note rule 3 ("SOR subdomain solves are the safe default") is marked superseded by 891c9bb0's LU default.

## Review

The adversarial review (a998181f) is in the first comment.

## Issues

- **Left open:** #894, the interface-law multigrid staleness. Its fix is the PR stacked on this one.
- **Pre-existing:** `test_1063_constrained_freeslip_parallel[ti]` misses its accuracy anchor (#826), on development too.

Part 2 of 2 of U-03 (closes #39): the white and black point pickers. Part 1 was #135.

- **Pick white point / Pick black point** in the Levels section. While one is on, the canvas shows the frame with its crop but without rotation, flip or straightening, so a click or dragged box is a position in the cropped frame. The measured end is set in all three channels, the other end is kept, and white stays above black. Escape cancels; choosing the other picker switches without drawing the picture again; a refused area shows the message and keeps picking. The edit is autosaved like the sliders.

body:
El panel lo va a usar una persona mayor que ya conoce WhatsApp. Este cambio le da esa misma forma.

## Chats
- La lista se ve como la de WhatsApp: foto redonda de color con la inicial (cada cliente siempre con el mismo color), nombre grande, último mensaje con ✓✓, hora en verde y un círculo verde cuando el cliente espera.
- "X clientes te esperan": cada uno muestra el mensaje del cliente y la respuesta propuesta como burbujas, con un botón verde grande "✓ Enviar así".

## Dentro de un chat
- Barra de arriba con volver, foto, nombre, teléfono y botón para llamar.
- Debajo, un aviso de quién contesta ("La asistente le está contestando" o "Le estás contestando tú") con su botón.
- Fondo de WhatsApp, burbujas blancas (cliente) y verdes (enviadas, con "Asistente" y ✓✓), y separadores "Hoy" / "Ayer".
- La propuesta de la asistente va en una burbuja verde con borde punteado: "¿Se lo mando?".
- Abajo, la caja para escribir con un botón verde redondo. Las pestañas se esconden dentro del chat, como en WhatsApp.

## General
- Letra base de 17 px.
- El verde de WhatsApp para todo lo que envía.

## Cómo se probó
- `npm run typecheck`, `npm test` (119 de 119) y `npm run build`.
- Vista con el mismo HTML y el CSS compilado, en tamaño teléfono. Con datos reales se revisa en producción: la vista previa no tiene acceso a la base.

body:
## Summary
- LayerNorm・RmsNorm・BatchNorm の create_graph 拒否範囲を S2 方式で受理へ広げる設計を autodiff-higher-order-grad-decision.md に記録
- docs/README.md と compat-matrix-ari-tracker.md を更新

Closes #3736

## 対象外（out-of-scope）
- 構造段の上界判定による拒否を狭めること（S2 の再検討）。承認なしに起票しない。#3767 の論点 3 として所有者へ戻す
- Det 系は #3737、padding_idx は #3738、GPU parity の測り方は #3739 の範囲
- docs/compat-api-scope.md の適用記録と 0.14.0 移行ノート（#3780）の更新。承認後の実装 PR #3809 で行う
- 実装 #3809 の起票・分割と GPU 実機 parity（#3857 の cuda-node、#3859 の metal-node）。いずれも未実測

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Docs-only updates with no runtime or API changes; behavior change is explicitly deferred until approved implementation.
> 
> **Overview**
> Documentation-only change that adds **§45** to `autodiff-higher-order-grad-decision.md` for issue **#3736**: how to widen what `create_graph` accepts for **LayerNorm**, **RmsNorm**, and **BatchNorm (train)** when inputs currently fail entry checks **(b)** (non-finite f32 row deviations) and **(c)** (mean partial-sum overflow).
> 
> The **recommended approach is S0 pre-scaling (案 A)**: per-row power-of-two scale `p`, divide `x` before the existing S1 child-tape structure, then divide the dx output by `p` so second-order terms come from autodiff through `Div` rather than hand-written S2 formulas. Rejection cases **(a)**, **(d)**, BatchNorm **eval**, and structure-stage bounds stay fail-closed; approval is pending **#3767**, with implementation tracked in **#3809** (tests, rustdoc pointers, compat apply record deferred).
> 
> **`docs/README.md`** and **`compat-matrix-ari-tracker.md`** (tracker item 5) now index **§45**; no code, public API, or tolerance changes.

author: ravbogard
body:
**Root cause.** Three of the five newest Daniel Shabbat mornings the reseed learned from (0RC4b6CpvnPbz09ue07q Mar 28, 29EqdMESd6QjhfokL2Bu Mar 21, KBDlDwRI0rfDdv8cxJG9 Feb 28) have zero tracks. They filled the 5-service window, the threshold is 3 of 5, and only two services had rows, so `modalOrder` kept nothing and `rowChanges` deleted every row.

**Fix.** `eligibleSetlists` (slot-uses.ts) drops setlists with no song rows, so empty shells never enter the learning window, the usual-window count or the same-day dedupe.

**Guard.** `learnedOrderGuard`: a learned order that is empty or under half the saved profile's rows is never written.
- `reseed_service_profile`: the dry run carries `shrinkGuard {reason, learned, stored, overridden}`. A real run returns `shrink_refused` unless `allowShrink: true`.
- Per-draft cache (`cacheLearnedProfile`): skips the write and logs it. `draft_service` then drafts from the saved profile (`origin.kind: saved_profile`).

**Tests.**
- `seed-empty-shells.test.ts`: the prod-shaped empty-order case, which fails without the fix, plus guard units.
- An emulator test covering the guard on reseed and on the draft cache.

**Note.** Aug 29 (JZd5mZhlxalYymMaXJMQ) is Noa and Ezra's B'nei Mitzvah but is not marked `special`, so it still counts as a regular week.

author: cakerepository
body:
## What changed

This is the room side of the buildings in #66. Each space is a building on The Commons, and going through its door opens that space's rooms.

- **Spaces.** A person has one house and up to 3 third spaces. A space is a stack of up to 5 floors, and each floor is an ordinary hangout, so chat, plans, check-ins and bots work with no new code.
- **Owner controls.** A new page at `/s/{id}` sets each floor's name, order, private or public, size (8, 50 or 150), paint, flooring and furniture. An owner can also turn someone out of the whole space.
- **Public floors.** Anyone signed in can walk in for 12 hours. A walk-in is a guest in the sense of R14 to R19: they read only from the moment they arrive, so opening a floor shows nobody what was said on it before.
- **The door.** `POST /api/spaces/door` takes a signed-in person from a building to the lowest floor they can reach. **Go in** is on every building in the map's tile menu.
- **`docs/wipe-all-hangouts.sh`.** Deletes every hangout, for a person to run by hand. With no flag it changes nothing and says how much would go.

The rules are S1 to S37 in `docs/spaces.md`, and W60 in `docs/public-city.md`.

## Why

Justin and Morgan want everything on the site to be a place someone built on the map, with one house per person and rooms that work the way hangouts do now. The map has no words in it and rooms are full of them, so the two stay apart and a door joins them.

A `place` move can't make a room, because W1 says a world can't touch a hangout. So the room comes from the person, the first time they go through their own door. That also means a bulldoze, a rebuild and a wipe of The Commons need nothing from this side.

## What deserves a close look

- **Public floors are the risky part.** They're the one place on the private side where someone you never invited can write, and there's no filter or reporting. S15 to S29 are the protections, and opening a floor needs the server's code if it has one.
- **W1 has a new exception, W60.** It goes one way, it's for people only, and a shut door is the same 404 as an empty tile. Please check that S31 to S33 hold up.
- **R37 changed.** It said hangouts outside a city behave exactly as before. A new hangout is now a third space, a person can hold 3, and a floor has a size. The text says so and points here.
- **The wipe deletes house bots.** `auth.rs` reads `is_house` from the `bot_homes` row, which goes with the house, so a house bot left behind would become an ordinary bot with a live token. A `stays_home` bot stays and loses that mark, for the same reason. Both are in `docs/spaces.md`.
- **Tests I changed.** Only the upgrade test in `tests/city.rs`, which gains the five new tables in both of its lists. That makes it check more, not less.
- **`AGENTS.md` isn't updated.** It lists each rule document and should gain S in `docs/spaces.md`, but that file needs a person's OK.

## How you know it works

- [x] `cargo test --locked` passes: 929 on this merged code, natively on Windows
- [x] 56 new tests in `tests/spaces.rs`, with at least one for each of S1 to S37, mostly about what someone who walks in can't do
- [x] With the owner check in the door switched off on purpose, exactly the two tests about an old tile failed, and the code was then put back
- [x] The wipe's test builds every kind of data through real routes, then starts a new server on what's left. Every table has to be on its keep list or end up empty, so a table added later can't escape it
- [x] `docs/wipe-all-hangouts.sh` ran with the real `sqlite3` on a database built by the real server and `demo_bots`: 10 rooms went, 6 accounts and 12 bots stayed, the backup held everything, and the app started on the result with no errors. A failed backup deleted nothing and still restarted the service
- [x] Seen in a browser on a local server: floors, the customize page, a stranger walking in and seeing no history, and right-click, Go in on a building as both owner and stranger
- [x] Numbered rules changed in their docs in this PR
- [ ] CI on this PR

**Not tested:** the wipe on the real server, where `systemctl` was a stand-in, or on a copy of production data. Only the house and studio were placed in the browser, because the cafe and club have no tool yet. Public floors have had no real traffic.

**One failure I couldn't repeat:** `a_broken_request_to_any_route_gets_no_server_error_and_no_path_no_sql_and_no_stack` failed once with a connection error while sending a 70 KB body to `/api/houses/{id}/rules`, a route this PR doesn't touch, on a server that refuses bodies over 64 KB. It then passed 5 of 5 alone and in the final full run, so it looks like a race on Windows, but I haven't proved that.
