author: msalvatti
body:
## What

Ports the hardened README-snippet check from nest-storage #108 to `scripts/check-published-surface.mjs`. Broken README examples passed the old check through three blind spots, and all three are closed. Snippets compiled: **12 before, 22 after**. The gate also found one README defect, which is fixed, and one defect in the check itself, which is fixed too.

## The three blind spots

1. **`tsc` stops at syntax errors.** The command reports no semantic error once any snippet has a syntax error, and `TS1108`/`TS1109` were on the allowed list. The project is now compiled through the TypeScript API (`getPreEmitDiagnostics`), which returns syntactic and semantic diagnostics together.
2. **Snippets that do not import the package were never compiled.** 10 of the 22 fences, including every `forRoot({ ... })` shown without its import. All 22 are compiled now, and a snippet that does not import the package gets its public names imported (read from `dist/server/index.d.ts`), except names it declares itself.
3. **Undeclared names were ignored**, so a call through one was a call on `any`. They are errors now, and the names the prose introduces (`logger`, `userId`, `familyId`, `ConfigService`, `LokiDestination`, and the `this` of a bare statement block) are typed against the real package types in `scripts/readme-prelude.d.ts`.

## Proof: each defect fails the new check and passed the old one

A defect is planted in a snippet, the gate is run with the script from `origin/main` and with this one, and the README is restored.

| Planted in a snippet | Old gate | New gate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| unmodified README | exit 0 | exit 0 |
| wrong method: `logger.warnStructure(...)` (snippet has no import, `logger` is a prose name) | exit 0 | exit 1, `TS2551 Property 'warnStructure' does not exist on type 'PinoLoggerService'` |
| wrong option: `shouldDisableDefaultRedacts: true` in a `forRoot` with no import | exit 0 | exit 1, `TS2561 ... 'shouldDisableDefaultRedacts' does not exist in type 'BymaxLoggerModuleOptions & ...'` |
| wrong destructured field: `const { levelz } = logger.getRawLogger()` | exit 0 | exit 1, `TS2339 Property 'levelz' does not exist on type 'BaseLogger & ...'` |
| wrong method hidden behind a syntax error: `const gap = ...` plus `this.logger.infoo(...)` in a snippet that imports the package | exit 0 | exit 1, `TS2551 Property 'infoo' does not exist on type 'PinoLoggerService'` |
| README `ILogDestination.write` return type narrowed | exit 0 (`declared types: none re-declared in the README`) | exit 1, `TS2322` from the member-parity probe |

## What the new check found

- **README defect.** The resource identity example passed `process.env.POD_UID` (`string | undefined`) to `service.instanceId`, which does not compile under `exactOptionalPropertyTypes`. The README now reads `process.env.POD_UID!` (`README.md:531`), and the CHANGELOG records it under Unreleased. The fix is in the README, not the prelude.
- **The declared-types check had stopped verifying anything.** `tsup` 9 emits type exports as `export type { ... }`, and the export-name parser only read `export { ... }`. Every interface was therefore missed, and the check printed "none re-declared in the README" while snippet 22 re-declares `ILogDestination`. It reads both forms now and reports `ILogDestination match the shipped type`. The row above is the proof that it catches a divergence.

The 12 diagnostics still ignored are counted in the output: 11 `TS2307` for modules the fixture does not install (`@nestjs/config`, `@bymax-one/nest-core`, five `@opentelemetry/*`, `@prisma/client`, `pino-roll`, `./app.module` twice) and 1 `TS2339` on a class the snippet declares and abbreviates (`PaymentsService.stripe`).

## Hardening the review forced

The port was reviewed to a design round, because the first version tolerated `TS1108`/`TS1109` for any snippet and the next ones still decided from text. What ships:

- **The prelude is copied into the fixture as `prelude.ts`.** The repository tsconfig sets `skipLibCheck`, a `.d.ts` is never diagnosed, and a prelude type that stopped resolving became `any` without a word. A renamed import now fails with `TS2724` at `prelude.ts`.
- **A parse error is tolerated only for an elision**, and the parse tree decides: a spread whose expression is missing (`f(...)`, `[1, ...]`, `{ a, ... }`), at the exact position the parser reports. Regular expressions, template literals, JSX text, comments and strings are already resolved in the tree, so none can pass for an elision, and an ellipsis elsewhere in the snippet or on the same line hides nothing. A bare ellipsis in an initializer (`const x = ...`) is not an elision and fails.

A 24-case matrix was run against the previous version of the check and against this one (earlier, smaller versions of it ran against the versions before): 18 inputs that must fail (a spread, comment, string, regex, template or multi-line comment next to a real error, a spaced spread, an elision and an unrelated error on one line, an elision plus a wrong method) and 6 elisions that must pass. Disabling each rule of the decision in turn makes at least one case fail. The `tsx` path was checked by calling the function directly: the gate cannot run a `tsx` fence in this repo because the fixture has no React types.

## For porting to the other packages

Generic: everything in `scripts/check-published-surface.mjs` that touches snippets, and the three fixes above. Package-specific: `scripts/readme-prelude.d.ts` and the `dist/server/index.d.ts` entry read by `publicNames`. Two things to carry over that the #108 reference does not have: copy the prelude as `.ts`, and read `export type { ... }` clauses in the declared-types check (a library built with `tsup` 9 has the vacuous check too). `eslint.config.mjs` gains one ignore entry for `scripts/**/*.d.ts`, which no block gives a TypeScript parser.

Not done here: resolving a relative import to the README snippet that exports it and failing an unresolved one, as nest-config #110 does. `./app.module` is currently one of the ignored `TS2307` and resolves to `any`; fixing that needs a fixture for `AppModule`, so it is a follow-up.

## CHANGELOG and version

One Documentation bullet under `[Unreleased]`. No bump: CLAUDE.md freezes the version at 1.4.x until the maintainer names the number, and `scripts/` is not packed. No tag.

## Process

Bounded review, five rounds of a fresh Claude pass and a Codex pass; rounds 3 to 5 were design rounds after the same finding reopened. No source file changes and `package.json` is untouched. `pnpm lint`, `pnpm typecheck`, `prettier --check` and `pnpm check:published` pass.

author: arshadm25
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"arshadm25"} -->
_Requested by **Muhammed Arshad** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01YRJYQB9JfVd38UtEuN5KpE?thread=cmsg_01YRJYQB9JfVd38UtEuN5KpEY1dKg55XU2rTXNJbDRuNb2)_

## What
Pause a webhook endpoint without deleting it, and turn it back on later.

- **API:** `PATCH /v1/webhook-endpoints/{id}` with `{"enabled": false|true}`. Uses the `is_enabled` / `disabled_reason` columns that were already in `webhook_endpoints`, so **no migration** (latest is still 000029).
- **While inactive nothing is sent:**
  - no new deliveries are created (`InsertDeliveriesForEvent` already filtered on `is_enabled`)
  - deliveries still pending or retrying are closed as `dead` with a note "Not sent: the endpoint was deactivated." (the earlier error is kept after it). No attempt is counted.
  - if a River job fires anyway, the worker closes the delivery and does not send it. It also now skips `dead` deliveries, so a retry job that was already queued can't fire after the endpoint is reactivated.
  - manual retry gets a 409 `endpoint_inactive`
- **Reactivating:** new events flow again. Closed deliveries can then be retried one by one from the delivery log. They are not replayed automatically.
- **Audit:** `webhook_endpoint.deactivated` (with `deliveries_closed` count) and `webhook_endpoint.activated`. The actor is the user or the API key.
- **Dashboard:** Deactivate/Activate action on each endpoint row (Deactivate asks for confirmation), an "Inactive" badge (English label was "Disabled"), a note in the delivery log, and the Retry button is hidden while inactive. New strings in all 7 languages, which need native review.
- **OpenAPI:** documented the PATCH and the 409 on retry.

## Testing
- `TestClientWebhooks` extended: other workspace gets 404, missing `enabled` gets 400, a queued delivery is closed and not sent, no delivery is created while inactive, retry gets 409, one audit row, and after reactivating both the retried and the new delivery arrive. Passes.
- `go vet`, `gofmt`, sqlc regenerated, `tsc -b`, `vitest` (56 passing).
- Not caused by this PR: `TestMetaFeeStatements` also fails on `main` locally (it looks date-dependent).

author: cansin
body:
Closes #97 (part of #88).

The model stops checking itself against PurpleShark's and Bambu's files. `make sim` runs on our geometry everywhere, and the committed reports are re-stamped from it.

**Deleted**
- The designer-mesh gate: `model/printed/test_gate.py`, `model/engine/test_gate.py`, and `noggin-mouth-report.json`, which only the gate read. The eyes and pan-tilt Fusion reports stay because the linkage, mass and stage tests still use them.
- `make guide-sheets`: `model/render/guide.py` and its test.
- The Bambu STEP meshing: `model/engine/step_mesh.py`, `make model-step-meshes`, and every `HAVE_REFERENCES` branch. The engine, fits and beams always read `model/build/ours`, and `make test` now builds `ours` first. About 40 tests that used to skip without references now run everywhere.
- `DESIGNER_LIMITS`: it is replaced by `geometry.LIMITS`, our own horn limits, each with its reason. `HORN_LIMITS` keeps its values.

**Mating check**
- Each printed part's `features()`, plus `envelopes.FEATURES`, now declares its holes, pins and bores from the part's own constants. `mating.FEATURES` is built from those declarations.
- A new test checks that our mesh carries every declared feature, within 0.03 mm in radius and position.
- The report stamp now also covers `model/printed` and `model/envelopes.py`.

**Recorded values on our parts**
- The lid-ear and jaw-pin fits and the connector-bar beam are re-recorded on our parts.
- Our geometry clears three of the calibrated-end collisions, so `KNOWN_CALIBRATED` drops those three. Its test now runs on every report instead of skipping.

**Docs**
- CLAUDE.md's ground-truth line, ADR 0006 and `docs/model-notes.md` are updated.

**Not changed**
- `model/parts.py` (Fusion) still reads `docs/references`. #99 removes it.
- `eyes/build_trace.py` still reads the GazeBase cache under `docs/references`.

body:

author: ksy141
body:
Three gaps in the Builder, all reported from the bench.

## Amides

They were there, but only as `Carboxamide` (`C(N)=O`) and `Acetamido` (`NC(C)=O`), and nobody looking for "amide" found either. The names now say which end bonds, and the substituted ones are covered:

| bonds through | groups |
|---|---|
| the carbonyl | `Carboxamide` `C(N)=O`, `N-Methylamide` `C(=O)NC`, `N,N-Dimethylamide` `C(=O)N(C)C` |
| the nitrogen | `Acetamido` `NC(C)=O`, `Formamido` `NC=O` |

## The rotamer

A fragment comes off the embedder in whichever rotamer it was built in, and for an N-linked amide that was **cis**: attaching `Acetamido` to a carbon gave ω = −12°, `Formamido` gave 0°. Cis is some 2.5 kcal/mol up and rarer than one in a hundred outside proline, so it is never what was meant, and it is the kind of thing nobody notices until a minimization pushes the molecule somewhere odd.

`attach()` now turns every secondary amide it touched to ω = 180°. A primary amide has no rotamer and a tertiary one has both sides filled — turning that would only trade one substituent's clash for the other's — so both are left alone, as is a lactam, whose bond is in a ring and cannot turn. Only bonds with a new atom at one end move, so attaching an acetyl never turns an amide elsewhere in the structure. `add_molecule` gets the same pass as insurance; the embedder already gives trans for a whole molecule from SMILES (`CC(=O)NCC(=O)NC` comes out at −180° and 171°), so it is a no-op there.

## Four-membered rings

Missing altogether, with three-, five- and six-membered ones all present. Added as rings: **cyclobutane** `C1CCC1`, **azetidine** `C1CNC1`, **oxetane** `C1COC1`. As groups: `Cyclobutyl`, `Azetidinyl` (bonded at the nitrogen), `Azetidin-3-yl`, `Oxetan-3-yl`. Each ring's SMILES is ordered so the atom that bonds is the position you want — carbon 3 for azetidine and oxetane, flanked by the two ring carbons rather than next to the heteroatom.

## Testing

`test_functional_groups_and_molecules` attaches each new group to ethanol and asserts that no two heavy atoms land within 1.2 Å — what a bad ring template or a wrongly chosen first atom looks like — and that every secondary amide comes out past 170°.

`pytest tests/test_viewer.py tests/test_triage.py tests/test_build.py tests/test_view.py` — 101 passed, 8 skipped. `ruff` clean over `src/boonza`.

## What changed
The secrets scanner stopped reading Python, Dart and JSX source syntax as credentials, without letting a real literal through.

- **env.kv source exemption (`lib/redact-patterns.ts`).** The #3048 rule, which covered TypeScript only, now also covers `.py`, `.pyi` and `.dart`. A bare name after `:` (a parameter annotation, a dict entry, a Dart named argument) is code. A JSX brace may join names with `??`, `||` and `&&` as well as `+`.
- **Strings stay strings.** In Python and Dart, one linear pass records every string's span: `'''`/`"""` blocks, and one-line strings that a backslash can continue. It skips `#`, `//` and nested `/* */` comments and handles Dart raw strings. A `password:` pair inside any string still reports.
- **Literals still report.** The rest of the name's expression is checked for a literal: `= "<secret>"`, `or "<secret>"`, `?? '<secret>'`. So is an expression that continues on the next line. A trailing comment is cut off first.
- **pregate `secrets` (`lib/pregate/checks/secrets.ts`).** A changed Python or Dart file is scanned whole, so the scanner can see an existing `"""` block. It is read whole only when it is a regular file of at most 4 MiB whose working copy holds the diff's added lines at their numbers. Only findings on added lines count, and rows give the file's line number. Untracked files are read whole too. Anything else is scanned by its added lines under a neutral name, without the exemption.
- **Allowlist (`lib/pregate/allowlist.ts`).** A `pattern` entry written from the name instead of the value now prints a row saying it missed. Before, the issue's `session: HttpSession` entry failed silently. A row prints only when the pattern matches the line but not at the value.
- **Pre-push hook (`bin/gstack-redact-prepush`).** It sees only added lines, so it scans Python and Dart lines without their path and still warns on a `password:` line added inside an existing `"""` block.

Before (main c830c9b): `session: HttpSession,` in a Python signature fails `gstack-pregate --only secrets` as MEDIUM env.kv. Secrets can't be downgraded, so /ship writes no receipt.
After (this branch): it passes. `session: "<random value>",` on the same name still fails.

## Why
In #3630, @dgrant reported that Python type annotations failed pregate as credentials, and the only workaround was a file-wide allowlist entry. Dart handlers (#3418, #3419 by @hbarney) and React keys (#3605 by @adam-balazs) failed the same way.

Proof: the new cases in `test/redact-engine.test.ts`, `test/pregate-secrets-source-context.test.ts`, `test/pregate-allowlist.test.ts` and `test/redact-prepush-hook.test.ts` fail on main c830c9b and pass here. Every widening has a negative control that still reports.

Refs #3630
Refs #3048

## Blast radius
- A whole-repo env.kv scan of 2473 tracked `.ts/.tsx/.js/.py/.dart` files finds 127 findings, the same file for file as main c830c9b.
- TypeScript keeps #3048's behavior, with two additions: a literal fallback after the name and an expression continued on the next line both report now. TS skips the string-span pass because a regex literal can hold a quote.
- Remote pregate (tree e36466aa): 8480 tests, 0 failed.

## Outside code and security read
I read #3605, #3418 and #3419 as text only and never checked out, ran or built them. This branch was written on current main. Two pieces were carried over after a line-by-line read: the `CODE_SOURCE` extension to dart/py/pyi (#3418, #3419) and the JSX `??`/`||`/`&&` split (#3605). The first commit credits Adam Balazs and Hamish Barney with Co-authored-by. #3418's triple-quote guard was rewritten from scratch. This change adds no network calls, environment reads, permission changes, workflow, setup or install edits, or dependencies. Because it narrows a secret scanner, the review hunted for fail-open paths. Five readers took part, one of them a cross-family voice. Every finding at the blocking floor was fixed with a test that fails first.

## Pre-Landing Review
REVIEW_LOOP: passes=3 blocking_found=3 deferred=0 noted=3 fixed=10 scope=frozen fix_checks=3 dispatches=4
Gate edits: `lib/pregate/checks/secrets.ts` (whole-file Python/Dart scan; added-line fallback without the exemption), `lib/pregate/allowlist.ts` (the miss row; verdicts unchanged), `bin/gstack-redact-prepush` (Python/Dart scanned without their path).

Pass 1 of 3 was voided because the reader ran in the wrong checkout; it is counted above. GStack Minder asked for the third fix-check instead of a review-loop exception.

Noted below the blocking floor, not fixed:
- Python subscript annotations (`api_key: Optional[str] = None`, `session: list[HttpSession]`) still report.
- A trailing `/* … */` comment that holds an odd quote or an open bracket ends the TypeScript exemption. This shape is rare, and no tracked file has it.
- A literal in a trailing comment after a Python or Dart name no longer reports. A comment line on its own never did.
- TypeScript template literals that span lines stay exempt, as they are on main.
- Python's `=` forms (`password=request.password`) still report.
- A docker-compose list item, `- API_TOKEN=<value>`, doesn't match env.kv. This predates this PR (#3726's bullet rule).

body:
## Release 6.6.0

This is a minor release. The release QA gate passed on RC4 `98997081`; see `qa/verdicts/6.6.0.md`. The highlights are in `release-notes/6.6.0.md`, and the full notes are in the CHANGELOG under `v6.6.0 (from v6.5.0)`.

- **Call manner:** the gate now compares how a narrated call runs with the code.
  - Awaiting a call marked `detach: true` is `DETACHED_CALL_AWAITED`.
  - A call in a catching `try` step that no try/catch encloses is `CALL_NOT_CAUGHT`.
  - When a step's call cannot be judged, the gate says so with `CALL_MANNER_UNJUDGED`.
  - This covers TypeScript and Python (#278, #279).
- **Field types:** a data field annotated as a different simple type than its spec declares is `TYPE_FIELD_TYPE_MISMATCH` (#279).
- **More Python is read:** guard-style routers, calls between components in one file, and routers named through a re-export, in TypeScript too (`export *` included) (#278, #279, #280, #281).
- **Externals:** a plain `wairon validate` composes the externals inside a project's reach (#278).
- **Specs:** `sdd_move_spec` can move a spec into a part's subsystem (#278).
- **Hosted:**
  - you can withdraw your own lock request;
  - `wairon host user` manages users;
  - stale lock requests are cancelled, and a repeated request returns the pending one (#278, #279).

Upgrading: install 6.6.0, run `wairon doctor --fix` and commit, then reconnect your AI tool. `wairon validate --ci` may report code or pins that passed under 6.5.0.

**Merge with a message that keeps `[minor]`.** The default merge message drops it and releases a patch version.

body:
Stacked on #2 (embedded Studio). The base is `feature/embedded-studio`; GitHub retargets this to `main` once #2 merges.

Adds the Vertex content model, a Studio content list, and a server-only read layer. No page is changed.

## Content model (`src/sanity/schemaTypes/`)

| Type | Kind | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `course` | document | title, slug, summary, cover image, level, price, popular, studentCount, outcomes (icon, title, description), instructor and category references, modules |
| `courseModule` | embedded object | title, summary, ordered lesson references. Not a document |
| `lesson` | document | title, slug, summary, videoUrl (YouTube, Vimeo or Bunny only), poster, durationSeconds, freePreview, studentCount, Portable Text notes, keyPoints, proTip, resources |
| `instructor` | document | name, slug, photo, expertise, bio |
| `category` | document | title, slug, description |

- Module and lesson numbers (Module 5, Lesson 5.1) and all durations are derived from order, never stored.
- A lesson does not store its course. It is derived by reverse reference.
- `lesson.summary` is an addition beyond the fixed model: the lesson header and search cards both need a short description.
- `src/sanity/structure.ts`: Courses, Lessons, divider, Instructors, Categories.

## Server-side read layer (`src/sanity/lib/`)

- `client.ts`: server-only client (`server-only` fails the build if a client component imports it). Uses `SANITY_API_READ_TOKEN`, `useCdn: false`, `perspective: 'published'`. Throws a clear error if the token is missing.
- `queries.ts`: eight `defineQuery` queries (catalog, course, lesson, instructor, categories, three slug lists).
- `data.ts`: `getCourses`, `getCourse`, `getLesson`, `getInstructor`, `getCategories` and slug helpers. Each uses `'use cache'`, `cacheLife('minutes')` and `cacheTag`. `getCourse` and `getLesson` add module and lesson numbers, and `getLesson` adds previous and next lessons.
- Removed `live.ts`: it was built around a browser token, which `AGENTS.md` forbids, and nothing used it.
- Types: `sanity.cli.ts` gets TypeGen config, `npm run typegen` regenerates `sanity.types.ts` and `schema.json` (both committed). The generated file is excluded from ESLint.
- New dependencies: `server-only`, `@sanity/icons` (direct, for subpath imports).
- `.env.example` adds `SANITY_API_READ_TOKEN` (name only).

## Checks

- `npx tsc --noEmit`, `npm run lint`, `npm run build`: pass.
- `npx sanity schemas validate`: 0 errors, 0 warnings.
- TypeGen found all 8 queries. Each was also run against the dataset with no syntax errors.

## Not tested

- The dataset has no content, so no query has returned real data.
- The Studio UI after sign-in (list order, forms) was not viewed.
- The data layer end to end needs a read token in `.env.local`.

## Notes

- A lesson used in several courses resolves to the first matching course.
- `AGENTS.md` wants a private dataset. Set it with `npx sanity dataset visibility set <dataset> private` if it is not.
- No secrets in this PR. Env files stay gitignored.

body:
## What changed

P2-19 part 41, from `everyday-poll-page.tsx`'s Hero lede: an open `/polls/:id` that links the ballot app says under its status how many questions it asks (answered together where there are several) and that the answers can be changed until the poll closes, only the last ones counting. Said only where the page links answering, so a hidden, unworded or ballot-client-less page promises nothing about answering again; scheduled keeps its own lede, closed has none. English and US Spanish.

The mockup's "short", audience/place and "about a minute" stay out: the definition fixes none of them.

G-11 / T-45 (re-voting as the in-scope coercion resistance, stated in the ballot app's own terms); T-10 (nothing new reaches the API).

The lede states the protocol's re-vote rule ([[revoting]]), which this page doesn't check; re-voting resists a coercer only where the voter can answer again unobserved (T-45); a voter on a new device may lack the voting identity that makes a later ballot replace the earlier one.

body:
## Summary

Before: Cohere, TokenRouter, Kilo Gateway and API.airforce connections only showed their hardcoded model lists, so new upstream models needed a code change.

After: those four API-key providers show the live upstream catalog on the dashboard, in the model picker and in `/v1/models`, with the generic **Fetch Models** button. On failure the static list stays, with a warning (the key is never echoed). Kilo Gateway and API.airforce mark free models, so the dashboard's **Free only** filter works for them.

| Provider | Endpoint | Mapping |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Cohere | `GET api.cohere.com/v1/models?endpoint=chat&page_size=1000`, follows `next_page_token` | native list: `name` → id, `context_length`, `vision` feature → image input; deprecated and non-chat rows dropped |
| TokenRouter | `GET api.tokenrouter.com/v1/models` | registry ids keep their kind and name; others: `architecture.output_modalities` if present, else the bare id through `classifyOpenAIModel` (plus flux/imagen/seedream → image); only chat, embedding and image kept |
| Kilo Gateway | `GET api.kilo.ai/api/gateway/models` | OpenRouter-shaped; text-output rows only (the registry routes chat only); Kilo's own `isFree` wins (its auto routers price at `-1`); expired rows dropped |
| API.airforce | `GET api.airforce/v1/models` | `supports_chat` rows with no media type or `chat`/`text`; `isFree` uses the same rule as the `airforce-free` suggested-models filter |

How: four parsers and resolvers in `apiKeyModels.js`, registered in `LIVE_MODEL_RESOLVERS` and flagged `features.liveModels`. The shared API-key `resolver` gained an optional `nextUrl` for paginated lists (capped at 10 pages); every existing resolver behaves as before. The dead `cohere` entry in `PROVIDER_MODELS_CONFIG` is removed, since the live resolver now serves it. TokenRouter and API.airforce keep `modelsFetcher` for the no-connection side panel, as Venice and OpenRouter do.

Part of YAN-135: YAN-169 (Cohere), YAN-176 (TokenRouter), YAN-178 (Kilo Gateway), YAN-179 (API.airforce). Kilo Code (YAN-177) is left for its own PR, because it also folds the bespoke `kiloFreeModels` fetch out of the provider page.

## Changes

- `src/lib/providerModels/apiKeyModels.js`: `parseCohereModels`, `parseTokenrouterModels`, `parseKiloModels`, `parseAirforceModels`, their resolvers, and pagination in the shared resolver.
- `src/lib/providerModels/liveResolvers.js`: the four resolvers registered.
- `open-sse/providers/registry/{cohere,tokenrouter,kilo-gateway,api-airforce}.js`: `features: { liveModels: true }`.
- `src/app/api/providers/[id]/models/route.js`: dead Cohere config removed.
- Tests: new `tests/unit/cohere-tokenrouter-kilo-airforce-live-models.test.js`; exact-list updates in `live-model-resolvers.test.js` and `live-models-utils.test.js`.

## Type of Change

- [ ] Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [x] New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [ ] Refactor (no functional changes)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to change)
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Build / CI
- [ ] Chore

## Testing

- [x] Linter passes (Biome on every changed file; local `npm run lint` can't run ShellCheck here, no shell files changed)
- [x] Tests pass

- [x] New and touched test files pass (33/33)
- [x] `verify-providers`, `verify-alias` and `verify-oauth-urls` byte-for-byte equal
- [ ] Full suite: 6 tests fail locally (`proxy-fetch-bypass.test.js`, one OpenRouter key-validation test). They fail the same way on a clean `master` checkout in this sandbox, which has no direct network, so CI is the judge.
- [ ] `npm run build`: left to CI

## Reviewer Notes

- API.airforce and Kilo Gateway shapes come from their public lists, read on 2026-10-31. Cohere's from its API reference.
- TokenRouter's list could not be reached from here (it needs a key), so its parser is built from the registry's OpenAI-style description and is defensive: unknown kinds drop out rather than land in chat. Worth one look with a real key.
- Target: next minor from `master`, no backport. Nothing half-built is reachable: every failure falls back to the static catalog.

body: Milestone 2 of 5. M1 (#8) is on `main`; this PR is now based on `main`. It adds the county engine. The method note is in `docs/SMALL_HOMES_LAB.md` on the M3 branch; M2's engine comments and tests carry the same formulas. **Host model.** N = Σ H·F·p(T)·d over host groups: county × context × host type, sliced by lot size. - **Options:** `adu`, `mm2` (keep the house and add one home), `mm4` and `mm6` (rebuild, up to 3 stories). Each has a closed-form pro forma in `src/lab/options.py`. - **Resolution:** each lot takes **at most one option**, the fitting legal option with the largest excess margin. F = Φ(x_best/σ). - **Timing:** p(T) = 1 − exp(−λ·max(0, T − legal lag − build lag)). **Legal partitions.** Lots with unknown zoning are split into prohibited and allowed partitions using the priors. They are never treated as zero. **Baseline.** - BPS 2023–2025 county average × 5 years × completion shares. - Plus homes the permit window cannot contain yet: Pittsburgh's October 2026 ADU ordinance, and the pipeline response to NH SB 284's 1-space parking cap. - Scenario increment = N(L1, e1) − N(L0_pre, e1) − [N(L0, e0) − N(L0_pre, e0)], so already-flowing homes are not counted twice. **Pipeline response.** Fee, parking, and approval changes reach already-legal projects through a threshold model: F1 = Φ(Φ⁻¹(F0) + (1+h)·s/C/σ_p), with C taken from the observed BPS valuation per home. - The implied cost elasticity is 2.3, inside the 1–3 range. - Parking also has a yield channel on parking-capped multifamily sites. - Approval reform applies only to the discretionary-review share of the pipeline. Its timing pull-forward is reported separately. **CLI.** `python -m src.lab.run --state PA [--county Allegheny] [--json out.json]` **Central results (5-year completions), as of this PR** | Scenario | PA delivered | PA vs Baseline | Allegheny vs Baseline | NH vs Baseline | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:| | Baseline | 111,016 | — | 13,775 (level) | 22,136 (level) | | 1. ADU | 117,064 | +6,048 | +275 | +81 | | 2. Missing middle (2–6) | 123,647 | +12,631 | +839 | +2,033 | | 4. Parking | 112,218 | +1,202 | +273 | +31 | | 5. Fees | 117,806 | +6,790 | +1,056 | +1,095 | | Package (extra) | 137,969 | +26,953 | +2,797 | +3,228 | | Approval (extra) | 117,832 | +6,817 | +831 | +1,364 | M3 adds a transition rule (lots keep building an incumbent option until a newly legal option's lag ends). That revises missing middle and the package: PA MM +12,916 / package +27,387; NH MM +2,344 / package +3,761. Uncertainty bands, close-call flags, and ACS margins arrive in M3. **Small additions to locked assumptions.** `approval_discretionary_share` is added; it applies only to the extra approval scenario. `build_lag_sf_years` and `bps_value_shrink_units` were added to M1 (#8) before review. No benchmark lever changed. ## Checklist - [x] Tests were added or updated for the core logic this change touches (`tests/test_lab_engine.py`: 18 arithmetic tests) - Pro forma closed forms and timing. - One best option per host: the result equals the max, not the sum. - Lot slicing. - Unknown-zoning partitions. - Post-window rules land in Baseline, not in the reform. - Pipeline threshold and elasticity. - Statewide totals equal the sum of counties. - Delta = host term + pipeline term. - The NH ADU result is small because those ADUs are already legal. - [x] `scripts/test.sh` passes locally (98 passed, ruff clean) - [x] No secrets, credentials, or `.env` files are included in this change - [x] New dependencies are permissively licensed (none added) - [x] Documentation (README or docs/) updated if behavior changed

body:
## Summary
Implements the Tariff Cache and the endpoint to retrieve the list of tariff plans.

**Requirement:** `L-08` (SHOULD) / `L-22` (SHOULD)
**Depends on:** `L-02`, `L-09`, `D-04`

## What was implemented
- **`TariffCache.java`**: A `@Singleton @Startup` EJB with `@Lock(LockType.READ)`. It loads all tariff plans from `TariffDao` on startup into an immutable list.
- **`TariffResource.java`**: A `@GET` endpoint at `/tariffs` that returns the data from the cache (never the DAO directly) using the `ApiResponse` helper.
- **`README.md`**: Added a design decision note explaining that the `@Startup` bean will intentionally crash the deployment if the DB is down, relying on Docker's `depends_on: service_healthy` to prevent this.

## Acceptance Criteria Verification
- [x] **Startup Log:** `docker logs` shows `loaded 3 tariff plans`.
- [x] **No Session:** `curl /tariffs` without a cookie returns `HTTP 401 SES001`.
- [x] **With Session:** `curl /tariffs` with a valid `JSESSIONID` returns exactly the 3 plans in `OLD99`, `PRE01`, `PRE02` order with integer piasters.
- [x] **Cache Proof:** Updating a tariff in the DB while the server is running does *not* change the API response. A server restart updates the cache.

author: zerocodefast
body:
## Summary

- Move release-manifest verification for machine-owned runtimes into the native runtime (`release-manifest-verify --stdin`, capability `native-release-manifest-verify-v1`). It covers the signature, identity, version binding, per-file hashes and complete coverage of the runtime tree.
- Reason codes and verdict fields stay the same, so the integrity and lifecycle callers are unchanged. If the runtime can't answer, the manifest is reported as `release_manifest_invalid`.
- Reads stay bounded and descriptor based. The manifest and each runtime file open without following links, are hashed within the per-file and total budgets, and must not change while being read. The coverage walk keeps its entry, directory and time budgets and treats links and Windows reparse points as escapes.
- Owner and mode checks stay Unix-only. Windows callers pass no owner, and the new non-Unix arm is reviewed in `ci/platform_arms.json`.

## Testing

- New Rust tests in `release_manifest_verify_tests.rs`. Most cases come over from the Python suite: signed and unsigned manifests, trust anchors, hash mismatch, path traversal, link escapes, platform, permissions, coverage, duplicates, version binding and rollback. The budget and raw-bytes hashing cases that used to monkeypatch Python internals now run against narrowed `Limits`. Command framing is tested too.
- `tests/test_guard_mdm_manifest.py` keeps its behavioural cases, which now run against the native runtime, and adds one case for a runtime that does not answer.
- Ran ruff and basedpyright on the changed Python, `cargo fmt --check`, and the approval-contract, platform-arm, Rust I/O ownership and tree-hygiene gates.

author: zhouxingxing1279
body:
## Research question
Extend Run225 to the third robust predecessor with correct causal quantifiers. Under the frozen four-state Euler and independently adversarial Run208/210 residual, certify two points in Pre³(X) and two points in Pre²(X) but not Pre³(X).

## Strict result
For (p,v,phi,omega)=(0,3,3/20,-2/5), a fixed two-step policy is robustly safe. But any causal three-step policy is defeated by r_i=R(T_i), with exact lower bound v3-3 >= 31023794855816198031/39062500000000000000000 > 0. Sign symmetry gives the negative case. States (0,±3,±3/20,0) are robustly safe for three steps under fixed TMAX and zero torque.

## Verification
Local Python 3.13.5: 7 tests, 6 passed and 1 full-checkout config test skipped; syntax compile and archived JSON generated. CI runs the Run224/225/226 regression tests, real configuration contract, and bytewise archive comparison. Source/test/archive blobs matched the locally tested files. Do not merge until CI passes.

## Scope
Finite-step full-state feedback certificates, not a nonempty RCI terminal set or output-feedback SMF-MPC recursive feasibility. No six-state or 20ms worst-case guarantees. Literature reading log updated with section-level Liu et al. (2021), arXiv:2109.12378 (87→88 unique).

## Next
Construct and verify a genuine four-state robust controlled invariant terminal candidate rather than extending Pre^n mechanically.

Step F.7 of `docs/feature-review.md` (items 1.5 and 1.8).

## The market position on the cards (1.8)
**Why.** How far the price is from the estimated value is the main reason to open an ad, but only the listing page said it.

**What changes.**
- **Database.** Migration `20261031200000_market_position.sql` adds the computed field `listings.market_position`:
  - normally the breakdown's `pct_below_market`;
  - `pct_below_damaged_value` when the text tells of an accident or a repair, as the listing page explains it;
  - null below 3 comparables, or for a placeholder price.

  A list loads that one number, never the whole breakdown.
- **What the card says.**
  - The line reads "8 % abaixo do mercado", "5 % acima do mercado" or "No valor de mercado".
  - It is green from 3 % below, red from 3 % above.
  - The comparison's row now uses the same function, `marketPositionText`.
- **A card detail, on by default.** It is called "Posição face ao mercado". The migration also adds it to every saved card choice.
- **Collector.** The migration only adds a function and widens a check constraint, so the collector on `main` is unaffected.

## "N anúncios novos" on return (1.5)
**Why.** Coming back to the app reloaded the alerts but not Ofertas. A list opened in the morning still showed the morning's ads in the evening.

**What changes.**
- **When it counts.** When the app comes back and its list is 30 minutes old or more, `ListingsCubit.checkForNew` counts the ads first seen since the list was asked for.
- **What it counts.** The count uses the same filters as the list, through the same query (`_filtered`). It is a count without rows.
- **What shows.** "3 anúncios novos" floats over the top of the list.
- **Clearing.** A tap brings the list to the top and reloads it. Any reload clears the count. A failed count says nothing, and a count that arrives after a reload is dropped.

## Checks
- **Run here, all clean:** `make sql-lint` (including `db-test`, with the new `market_position_test.sql` and the updated `listing_card_preferences_test.sql`), `make tool-check`, `make duplication` and `check_migrations.sh`.
- **Not run:** Flutter isn't available here, so the app's tests run in CI only:
  - `listings_cubit_test.dart`: the 30 minutes, the filters, a reload clearing it, failures, a late answer;
  - `supabase_listings_repository_test.dart`: the count's query;
  - `listing_card_preferences_test.dart`: the text both ways, in both languages;
  - `interface_test.dart`: the pill at 320 px with 2x text, and a tap back to the top.

**Docs updated:** `CLAUDE.md`, `app/README.md`, the roadmap (with Next set to F.8), `concept.status.md` and the review's table.

## To see it
- **Market position:** open Ofertas. Each card says "x % abaixo do mercado" under the price.
- **New ads:** leave the app for more than 30 minutes, ideally across a collection, then come back. The pill counts the new ads; tap it.

author: brandtdaniels
body:
This is hardening PR C from the full-codebase review (#38): correctness and crash fixes.

**Parser**
- **A NAK is reported as a NAK.** When the modem NAKed 0x60, 0x73 or 0x7E and the next frame followed directly, the NAK was read as an accepted reply. That could write a wrong modem configuration (0x55, which turns X10 and the deadman off). It's now reported as the NAK, using IBIOS's lookahead rule, and skipping carries across chunks.
  - A seeded fuzz test checks that a NAK is never accepted. It also checks that random bytes never trap, that the result doesn't depend on chunking, and that the parser keeps making progress.
  - A restored regression test checks that a modem address starting with 0x15 still parses as modem info.
- **IBIOS:**
  - Text reports are capped at 256 bytes.
  - An upload echo is read only if its address and length match the upload written, so noise can't wedge the controller.
  - There's a test through `PowerLincController`.
- **Stalled and left-over frames:** a frame is discarded whole, never read again as frames. That happens when nothing arrived for the whole answer timeout, or when it was already pending before the command was written. A 0x50/0x51 or upload still arriving is never cut short.
- **Skipping:** it ends at the next 0x02 or at a timeout.

**Linking mode**
- Cleanup (Cancel ALL-Linking, Exit Linking Mode) runs in an awaited task that a cancel can't stop, so the modem never stays in linking mode. The keep-awake release gets the same fix.
- `InMemoryModem` honors cancellation, so a test catches a regression.

**Serial writes**
- `SerialPort` keeps `O_NONBLOCK` and waits on a dispatch write source.
- The answer timeout bounds the write too: a stuck write is cancelled and the send fails at the timeout.
- There are pty and stuck-connection tests.

**Races and records**
- `AllLinkDatabaseCache` keeps a generation counter.
- `DatabaseEditor.deleteFromModem` restores the other role's records one by one, then invalidates the cache. Records it couldn't restore are thrown as `ModemRecordsNotRestored(records:cause:)`, which keeps the original error.
- Cancelling one `identify` call no longer cancels it for the other waiters.
- Saves happen in order (`OrderedSaver`).
- The terminal has one line reader (`LineReader`).

**Numbers**
- Durations compare in `Double` with a finiteness guard.
- Scales must be finite and above zero, with tests for an infinite scale.
- The percent is clamped.
- The duration example can't overflow.

**Also:** the unused `OneShot.swift` is removed.

**Left for later:**
- `ModemSession.collect` propagating cancellation.
- A Hub poll slower than the answer timeout splitting a message.
- A genuine `15 02 5x` configuration being read as a NAK and retried (fails safe).

**API changes:**
- `ModemRecordsNotRestored`;
- `ReplyParser.discardStalledFrame()`, `willWrite(_:)` and `pendingFrameStart`, all with defaults.

author: p47phoenix
body:
Fixes #323

## What
`memory-graph delete --org O [--repo R] (--dry-run | --yes) [--compact] [--json]` on `--db` and `--server`, CLI only (no MCP tool, as the owner approved).

- **Store:** new `Store::delete_scope(org, repo, dry_run) -> DeleteStats`. It runs in one transaction and removes files of every origin, the repo nodes, the org node when the org is deleted or left empty, every catalog row of the repo, and any open-batch marker on a deleted repo. Conformance cases `delete_repo`, `delete_org` and `delete_missing`; the `run_differential` seed and `run_crash_rerun_differential` now include deletes; a v2 test covers clearing the open-batch marker. Stored bytes don't change, so there is no schema bump.
- **Cluster:** `Write.Delete` RPC and `LogCommand.Delete`, applied through a marked write exactly once. Followers forward it to the leader; a dry run is answered by the node it reaches. Auth maps it to the `write` role. `RemoteStore` implements it.
- **Docs:** storage guide section, server guide, README command table, epic story 71 (totals 71 stories / 338 pts).

## Decisions for the owner
1. **Mixed-version safety.** A version-1 node would refuse a Delete entry and keep data the other nodes deleted. There are two guards:
   - **Peer guard (done, in commit "Peer guard ..."):** `LOG_COMMANDS_VERSION = 2` is part of the extractors hash that AppendEntries, join and snapshot install already compare (the same mechanism as `SCHEMA_VERSION`). An old-binary node is refused as a peer instead of replicating entries it cannot apply. Unit test: `hash_includes_the_log_command_set`.
   - **Client side, pending the owner:** `PROTOCOL_VERSION` 1 -> 2 (package stays `v1`) refuses old CLIs at Hello. The alternative is a Hello capability that lets old CLIs keep working. The bump is isolated in its own commit (`Bump PROTOCOL_VERSION to 2 ...`) so it is easy to swap.
2. Deleting a missing org or repo is a no-op: empty stats, `nothing to delete: ... not found`, exit 0. Retries and replays are safe; a typo also exits 0.
3. No new exit code: running without `--yes` is refused with exit 1.
4. An empty org or repo name is refused (`Rejected`) by the store, and by the server before anything is logged.
5. `delete` removes every file of the repo, including ones written by `index-file` or `ingest` (`--prune` only removes directory-run files).
6. A dry run needs the `write` role, like a dry-run `Prune`.
7. Epic story 71 was added (ADR 0013 / PR #326 proposes 71+, to be renumbered by the owner).
8. Delete clears an open-batch marker on a deleted repo, so re-indexing it does not report a stale open batch.

## Tests (local, Windows)
- `cargo fmt --check`: pass. `clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings`: pass.
- `cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast`: everything passed except `version_header`. That test hardcoded protocol version 1; it now uses `PROTOCOL_VERSION` and passes.
- New tests: CLI e2e `delete_org_and_repo`, serve_e2e `delete_over_server`, cluster `delete_sent_to_a_follower_applies_everywhere`, auth `delete_needs_a_write_token`: all pass. The full cluster and auth test files pass too.
- Review follow-ups: the peer-guard hash test, a name-cache staleness test after a delete (in `name_cache_answers_equal_the_walk`), graph-server lib, cluster and membership tests, and clippy all pass.
- `test_gate.py` and `check-no-c-deps.py`: pass.

Not merged; waiting for review and the protocol decision.

author: matrixarkai
body:
An append's undo captured a payload entry for every extent the object already
held, and the extent list grows by two per append. That is O(extents) per append —
quadratic to build an append-only log.

**It was capturing something an append cannot destroy.**

## Measured

Both arms built from the same harness, varying only this repository's pin, nothing
else running on the box, over `MATRIXARK_SCALE_SIZES=100,400,800,1600,3200` of
TemporalStore's five-node shared-store sweep:

| | instructions |
|---|---|
| before | 14,492,882,146 |
| after | **10,936,178,137** |

**−24.5%.** The baseline reproduced to within 0.05% of an independent run earlier
(14,500,411,257), and every asserted column is identical across the two arms
(`blob B/entry` 336.8, `range B/entry` 303.0, `append reads/entry` 2.000,
`replay reads/entry` 4.496) — which is what says the arms ran the same workload.

## Why this and not the metadata clone

The first commit here took the metadata clone out of the append's undo capture and
left the payload loop in. Measured the same way, that bought **0.72%**
(14,500,411,257 → 14,396,401,536).

So the undo's cost was never the metadata clone, even though the metadata holds the
extent list. It was the loop beside it, which walks an entry per extent and clones a
`StoredPayload` for every hit. The first commit is kept because the record it
introduces is what makes the undo's shape honest — and because `PutTargetedPrevious`
is what a future in-place append will need — but the number is in the second commit.

## Why an append needs no payload entries

`previous_payloads` exists for a mutation that **stales** the extents it replaces:
`mark_extents_stale` removes the payload entry for each one, and that entry holds a
length and a digest the store keeps nowhere else, so an undo has to carry it.

Every caller of `mark_extents_stale`: legacy retention, noncurrent versions, an
object-lock transition, a multipart delete, and a replacing put. **An append is not
among them.** It only adds extents, so it destroys no entry and has nothing to carry.

The restore is unchanged in effect. `restore_targeted_payloads` first **retains**,
dropping entries at or past the chunk's `next_offset` as it was before the mutation —
exactly the entries an append added — and the old entries sit below that offset and
outside the before-stale ranges, so they survive. Re-inserting them was writing back
values that had never been removed.

## The undo's shape, and the completeness argument

`PutTargetedPrevious` now names the three cases: `Absent` (remove what the mutation
made), `Whole` (a mutation that can change anything), and `Appended` (one that only
grew). The `Appended` record carries the extent list's old length and the six fields
an append advances, and the argument is written field by field over all fourteen
where the record is declared: `object_id` is the key it was found by; `version`,
`length`, `etag_digest_bits`, `has_etag` and `update_time_ms` are recorded;
`content_type`, `user_metadata`, `storage_class`, `tags` and `lock` are read off the
previous object unchanged by the apply, so there is nothing to restore; `extents` is
extended, so its old length is enough; and `deleted` was already false, which an
append refuses to change.

## One regression the suite caught, and why the restore does not re-file

The first version of the length-based restore did `take_object` then `file_object`.
`file_object` **re-interns** the object key and the content type, and the object
taken already holds the interned ones — so re-interning after the set's copy was
dropped mints a fresh allocation, which the footprint audit sees as a string that
stopped being shared: `object_changes.object_id_bytes 0 -> 17` on a refused append.
`an_append_that_fails_after_mutating_leaves_the_store_unchanged` refused it, which is
exactly the test for a wrong append undo. The restore puts the object back with
`objects.replace` and disturbs no identity.

## Which append path this is on, checked rather than assumed

There are three append entries and they capture different undos.
`append_object_with_options` calls `apply_append` **directly** when
`persistent_journal_path` is empty, which is one targeted undo and is the path the
shared store takes. `append_object_with_placement` wraps it in a full whole-store
capture, and either with a journal path set takes a further one. The full capture's
arithmetic says it should dominate everything and it appears nowhere in the profile —
because it is not on this path. `PayloadIndex` is a plain
`BTreeMap<ChunkId, BTreeMap<u64, StoredPayload>>`, so a full capture really is
O(entries); it is just not taken here.

## Gates

`cargo build --locked --all-targets` under `RUSTFLAGS=-D warnings`, clean.
`cargo test --locked --lib` 567 passed, 0 failed.

## What is left on this path

The apply still copies the extent list twice (`self.object(..).cloned()` and
`previous.extents.to_vec()`), and `file_object` clones once more to store. Those are
a smaller constant on the same O(extents) term. The asymptote itself needs `extents`
behind an `Arc` so the apply can extend in place — an option that only became
available once this undo stopped holding a handle to it.

author: voodoomods
body:
Closes the remaining verification-integrity finding from the pre-launch audit of v0.7.16 / main 46ea156.

## The defect (reproduced on the PyPI 0.7.16 wheel and on main)
The verifier accepted a node's lifecycle under **either** the current rule or 0.3's (`allowed = {lifecycle(id, True), lifecycle(id, False)}`). 0.3 counted only an *active* replacement. So in a chain RS3 supersedes RS2 supersedes RS1, RS1 is active under 0.3's rule. Editing only RS1's exported lifecycle to `active` gave:

| case | `verify` before | `--standing` before |
|---|---|---|
| RS1 shown active | ok, coverage complete, **views checked** | problem (standing differs) |
| RS1 shown active + `generator: "hypgraph 0.3.0"` | ok, coverage complete, **views checked** | **not checked** |

The chain, rows and head were untouched. `tests/test_verify_views.py` asserted that this case verifies. The browser verifier had the same rule.

## The fix
- `bundle.py` `_derived_problem` and `hypgraph.js` `derivedProblem` now check a lifecycle against the **current rule only**.
- A lifecycle that matches only 0.3's rule still verifies, since the rows and chain are intact and a real 0.3 export shows it that way. But the result reports **`views: "historical"`**, not `"checked"`, and the warning names each node and what the current rule makes it. `hypgraph verify` prints `views: NOT CHECKED`.
- Any other mismatch fails as before.
- The decision never reads `generator`: that field isn't covered by the chain, so naming 0.3 or deleting it changes nothing.
- The scoped-bundle allowance (a node shown superseded when the scoped rows say active, because links to other investigations are left out) is unchanged, and scoped coverage is already reported as partial.
- `site/app/hypgraph.js` and `site/py/hypgraph/{bundle,cli}.py` carry the same copies, from `dev/build_site.py`.

## Tests: `tests/test_verify_lifecycle.py`
It covers:
- `supersedes` and `corrects` chains of three;
- the audit's forgery, checked against the published head;
- the generator forged as 0.3 or deleted;
- withdrawn replacements (the newest of a chain withdrawn, so the middle node is active again under both rules);
- each wrong lifecycle at each position;
- scoped bundles;
- the CLI line;
- `--standing` still catching the forgery on this version;
- **Python/browser parity on verdict, `views`, warning text and coverage** for every case.

The old case in `test_verify_views.py` still verifies; its comment now says the views are historical.

**Five of its tests fail on main without the fix** (run with the test file copied into a main worktree). They all pass with it.

## How it was checked locally
- `ruff check src tests examples`: clean.
- `pytest -q`: **424 passed, 6 skipped** (Windows, Python 3.13, node 24 for the browser-verifier tests).
- The demo builds, exports and verifies: `hypgraph demo` / `export` / `verify`.
- `dev/ui_smoke.py` with Chrome: **146 of 146 pages render**.
- Built the wheel and sdist. `dev/e2e_install.py` passed: wheel with MCP 21/21 steps, sdist 20/20.

## Not in this PR
- The release, which would be 0.7.17.
- The repository settings the audit lists: required checks, description, homepage and topics. Those are GitHub settings, not code.

author: hookwoods
body:
Two differences in how a refused escalation behaves, both from the `become_su` and `become_sudo` targets:

- An escalated link was keyed without its password. A task given a wrong password reused the agent the right password had opened and ran. ansible-core asks for the password on every task, so that task fails with `Incorrect sudo password` or `Incorrect su password`. The link key now carries a hash of the password, so another password gets its own agent and is checked. The password itself never appears in the key.
- `ignore_errors` was not honoured on a refused escalation, and the result was not registered. ansible-core treats the refusal as an ordinary task failure. A task alone in its batch now registers the result and carries on when `ignore_errors` covers it. Behind a first task the rest of a batch never ran, so a batch of several still fails as before.

The refusal handling moved to `executor/driver/refused.rs`. Both targets now stop at later differences (the su prompt list and sudo's `chdir`), and they stay on the known list.

Docs: hosts/connections in all five languages.

author: htarrido-picart
body:
Closes #243

## What
`ijc_lasso_select(h, xy_px: *const f32, n: usize, crossing: bool, additive: bool) -> i32`

- `xy_px`: `n` interleaved `x,y` points in drawable pixels (y down); the loop closes from the last point to the first. Concave loops are fine (even-odd inside).
- Same object rules as `ijc_box_select`: curves test their tessellated line, other geometry its projected bounds; hidden objects and layers are skipped.
- `!crossing` is a window (fully inside the loop, including no segment or bounds edge cutting through a notch); `crossing` takes anything the loop touches or encloses.
- Replaces the selection unless `additive`. Returns the match count, or -1 on a null/invalid or headless handle, a null `xy_px`, or `n < 3`.

## How
`boxsel` gains a `Region` trait implemented by `Rect` and the new `Lasso`; `matches`/`polyline_matches` are generic over it, and `box_select_in` / `lasso_select_in` share `region_select_in` (filter, replace or add, bump generation).

## Tests
- `boxsel::concave_lasso_excludes_its_notch`: point/rect/segment tests against a U-shaped loop.
- `lasso_select_concave_window_crossing_additive`: three boxes, a U whose notch excludes the middle one, window vs crossing, additive vs replace, null and short input.

`cargo test -p itsjustcad-ffi` and `cargo clippy -p itsjustcad-ffi --all-targets -- -D warnings` pass.

author: pigbibi
body:
## AI assistance

Prepared by ChatGPT. Implementation was assigned to `/root/phase1k_evidence_changes`; `/root/phase1k_evidence_review` independently reviewed the complete candidate tree, failure boundaries and tests. `/root/phase1k_refactor` independently ran native Gitleaks controls with the existing verified pinned executable. The parent agent separately checked the historical review documents. These process records are independent review evidence, not cryptographic identity attestations.

## What changed

This child draft targets `ci/architecture-offline-governance-contracts` at `7830a5b17c7e1eded21f6028a1a67456290d6ebd` and depends on #922. The parent remains unchanged.

The native Gitleaks job currently retains neither a JSON report nor the original scanner process exit. The proposal adds the CLI's JSON output options and retains the native report, separate process-exit file, declared invocation and capture receipt in an Actions artifact. It preserves the existing version, archive checksum, redaction, default configuration lookup, event range and native failure result. The artifact upload uses the existing organization-pinned `actions/upload-artifact` revision and a seven-day retention period.

A local commit-object preflight rejects missing or invalid revision inputs before scanning. It does not require the base to be an ancestor of the head. This is necessary because the pinned native CLI can report zero and write an empty report after an invalid Git range. A successful process with missing or unusable output also fails collection; a native failure retains its original exit code even when collection fails. An executable that cannot start produces no fabricated process-exit capture.

After the event-range scan and collection succeed, a separate retrospective step scans `c47d3401e1bb9f5e2ac88bb578f9173a60d0bc2a..7830a5b17c7e1eded21f6028a1a67456290d6ebd`. This is a new execution of #922's original source-review delta. It does not recover that PR's old run artifacts or clear findings in the wider strategy history. The two ranges have separate directories and receipts. An always-running uploader retains only the exact evidence paths, including partial failure evidence, without masking failed steps.

The source-only review-v1 document records the original six-file review and its explicit unsigned provenance mapping. Its `required_checks` and `checks` arrays remain empty because the effective policy is unavailable. The connector's required-policy endpoint refusal is documented as a capability limit. No substitute policy read, invented identity, provider signature or successful check declaration is introduced.

The two existing inspectors and their aggregate adapter are unchanged. They retain their current `BLOCKED` / `FAIL` behavior and all authority flags remain false. The commit-message job, workflow events and permissions, trusted risk gate, production dependencies and runtime configuration are unchanged.

## How verified

- The parent's **81** standard-library contract test methods passed before the change. The candidate's **99** methods passed: **26** Gitleaks-inspector, **33** review-inspector, **22** aggregate/workflow-boundary and **18** new retention/review methods.
- Subprocess tests preserve native exits **0, 1, 2, 7 and 127**; missing/non-executable tools, raw signal exits, missing or malformed reports, deep/nonfinite JSON, oversized files, symlinks, FIFOs, write failures and stale output directories retain their distinct failure behavior. Current and push event range fallback remains covered.
- Independent real Gitleaks **8.30.1** controls verified clean JSON output and exit **0**, redacted findings and exit **1**, a genuine configuration error, valid divergent and empty ranges, and failed preflight for unavailable, malformed, zero, non-commit and uppercase revision inputs. The reproduced native invalid-range false zero is retained in the pre-fix evidence; the collector now rejects that case before native execution without fabricating an exit artifact.
- Independent native scans of the eight-file candidate snapshots reported **zero findings**. These are materialized source scans; the new draft's actual Git range will be scanned by hosted CI.
- The historical review-v1 document remains **CONSISTENT / BLOCKED, exit 2**, with authentication and required-check coverage **UNVERIFIED**. A different expected head is rejected. It does not review the current child draft.
- The complete authoritative base and candidate trees, all changed blob identities, unchanged validators and commit-message job, actual workflow contract script, YAML structure and Python syntax were checked. All **194** existing Python/shell test-source blobs were inspected for references to the changed engineering workflow; its command-boundary suite was updated and passed.
- A supplemental offline public-config scan covered all **48** exact candidate workflow files with real ripgrep. Native ripgrep returned clean no-match **1**; the unchanged CI Bash body then returned **0**. The workflow inventory and hashes are bound to the candidate tree.

Full hosted CI, frozen installations, Ruff and documentation checks remain required after draft creation. Local validation used exact source snapshots; it did not install or change production dependency versions.

### Inherited CI limitation

The unchanged base still contains the separate public-config scan provisioning gap addressed by #924 / #926. A green hosted step alone does not prove that `rg` ran; its actual logs must be inspected. This proposal does not duplicate those unmerged repairs. The supplemental offline scan above validates this candidate's workflow contents with an available real tool, and retained native Gitleaks evidence is a separate check. Neither result is a claim that the inherited hosted public-config step was repaired here.

## Ancestry and governance

The independently reviewed candidate tree is `222c5c66d60e85b2fce463955e5556c996c6b8c0` over the single actual parent `7830a5b17c7e1eded21f6028a1a67456290d6ebd`. Published commit `a67ac7963a89f97b02f15fc880e9c4e96be77a39` points to that reviewed tree. The complete proposal changes eight files. Review receipts bind the final preflight delta to this tree and to the independently verified native controls.

Workflow paths may require the repository owner's reserved approval label on this new draft. If that gate blocks, leave this PR draft for the owner; passing engineering checks do not override governance. No label is copied, added or removed. Parent approval is not inherited by this child.

## Delivery scope

Draft proposal only. No merge, undrafting, deployment, live operation, broker request, notification, GCS write, account/risk change, secret/IAM/scheduler change, production entry-point change, fingerprint registration or production configuration/dependency change is performed. Required-check policy access remains a documented tool capability limit, and authenticated evidence acceptance remains unimplemented.

author: oliverbrotchie
body:
# What changed

The member's account page is now real: password login, a server-side session, logout, and the read-only view the ticket bounds.

- Login is `POST /login` with the mail password. The handler runs `doas /usr/local/libexec/kyriakon-authcheck <username>` and feeds the password on stdin. The checker accepts one username, validates its shape, and runs only `doveadm auth test`; `doas.conf` names the checker because its argument list cannot name the username. A correct password returns `303` and a `kyriakon_session` cookie that is signed, `HttpOnly`, `Secure`, `SameSite=Lax`, `Max-Age=43200`. A wrong password returns the login page with no cookie. `POST /logout` removes the server-side record and clears the cookie.
- Sessions are `sessions/<id>.json` under the store, 0600, owned by `_onboard`, with a random secret per session; the cookie is the id and an HMAC of it under that secret. `/account` with no live session renders the new login page. No key admits anyone, and `REMOTE_USER` is no longer read as an identity.
- The read-only view adds the address outside the platform, space used against the 5 GB soft and 5.5 GB hard allowance, upload key fingerprints and dates, every notice with its address, the reason a suspended page still opens, a closing notice, a group mailbox's group billing and state from `groups/<domain>/group.json`, and the plain statement of what the page cannot do.
- The payment block now has the three states: a running window (rail, days left, close date, amount, full token, instructions), `Lapsed` with the close date, what works and what stopped, the token again and an `admin@` line, and `Paid until <date>` with no token. Both the web page and the capsule render the same block.
- `accounts/` and `groups/` are now `root:_onboard 0750`, and the records the handler renders are written 0640: only `account.json`, `group.json` and `notices.jsonl` gained group read. `journal.jsonl`, `requests.jsonl` and every other drain file stay root-only. `Store::append_mode` fixes the mode and group on every append, including one that finds an older 0600 file, so an upgrade repairs it on the next notice; `scripts/onboard-store.sh` also normalises existing `account.json`, `group.json` and `notices.jsonl` to 0640 `root:_onboard`, and reports a change when it had to.
- The space-used criterion has its writer: `transitions::refresh_space_used` runs in the drain pass, due-gated to once an hour, runs `repquota -u <quota_mount>`, parses each member's used blocks and records `space_used` in bytes on `account.json`. It is a no-op when the report is empty, unparseable or the tool is missing, and its own `quota-check.json` carries the hour. The keys `repquota` and `quota_mount` are in `drain.toml`.
- `sessions/` is a new 0700 `_onboard` directory, and the spec's store listing now names it.
- The deploy installs `/usr/local/libexec/kyriakon-authcheck`, checks for the doas rule, and prints the manual step with the tracked fragment at `openbsd/etc/doas.conf.onboard`. The runbook records it.

# Verification

- `cargo fmt --manifest-path onboard/Cargo.toml --check` passes.
- `cargo clippy --manifest-path onboard/Cargo.toml --all-targets -- -D warnings` passes.
- `cargo test --manifest-path onboard/Cargo.toml --lib` passes: new tests include correct and wrong password, cookie flags, the twelve-hour expiry, a forged cookie, no admission by `REMOTE_USER` or a key, quota/key/notice rendering, a suspended page, group billing, the three payment states, the notice record's 0640 mode and group, and the quota parser and sweep (usage recorded, hour cached, bad report a no-op).
- `cargo test --manifest-path onboard/Cargo.toml --test drain -- lifecycle::the_drain_records_space_used_from_the_quota_report` passes: the drain writes the quota's used blocks onto the account as `space_used`.
- `cargo test --manifest-path onboard/Cargo.toml --test drain` passes in CI (135 tests), including the new quota sweep test; the full suite was too slow to finish on this loaded development machine, where three sibling worktrees were running their own suites.
- `shellcheck` and `ksh -n` pass on the three scripts touched. `ksh scripts/kyriakon-authcheck.sh --self-test` passes, and the checker exits 64 for a bad username and for no argument.
- Smoke run: the built handler served a scratch store and config over its FastCGI socket. `GET /account` returned `200` with the login form and no cookie, `POST /login` with a wrong password returned `200` with the refusal and no cookie (the real `doas` is absent on the development machine, which is the same refusal), `POST /logout` returned `303` with `Max-Age=0`, and `GET /` returned the applicant page.

Append the tracked line to `/etc/doas.conf` and check it, then restart the handler:

```ksh
doas sh -c 'cat openbsd/etc/doas.conf.onboard >> /etc/doas.conf'   # append the one line, not the comments twice
doas -C /etc/doas.conf
doas ksh scripts/deploy-onboard.sh
doas rcctl restart kyriakon_onboard
```

`scripts/deploy-onboard.sh` installs the checker and prints the rule when it is missing. Until the rule is present every login is refused.

This is one ticket in a parallel stack from the same base. It touches the account route in `responder.rs`, `page.rs`, `templates/account.html`, `capsule.rs`, `store.rs`, `transitions.rs` and `deploy-onboard.sh` surgically; it deliberately adds no close, export, key or password action routes, which are #332's.

author: alxndrjhn
body:
The RC `fork-0.18.0.65` doesn't install over `fork-0.17.2.64` (3dabf72): Android reports *App not installed as package conflicts with an existing package*, and `adb install -r` on an emulator gives `INSTALL_FAILED_UPDATE_INCOMPATIBLE: signatures do not match`.

**Cause:** with no signing secrets set, the release used a key generated once and kept in the Actions cache (`android-fork-signing-key-v1`). The repo's cache is at ~10.7 GB of its 10 GB limit (mostly buildkit layers), so the key was evicted. Run 41233766415 logged `Cache not found for input keys: android-fork-signing-key-v1` and generated a new key. Signing certificate SHA-256: `c05bcd09…` for .62 and .64, `75dbb01c…` for .65. The old key can't be recovered.

**Fix:**
- A new release key is now stored in the `ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64`, `ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD`, `ANDROID_KEY_PASSWORD` and `ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS` secrets (certificate SHA-256 `5E:9A:69:95:…:EB:7A`).
- `release-fork.yml` and `preview-v18rebase.yml` now sign only with those secrets. They drop the cache fallback and fail if the secrets are missing.

Because the key changes, phones on 0.17.2.x (or the .65 RC) need one uninstall and reinstall of Anchor+ to take the next build. After that, updates install normally.

## 摘要

记录用户 2026-10-31 在实验讨论中确认的设计立场，并指出它对评测、语料与记录的含义。新增 `docs/review/LIMITED-COMMITMENT.md`。这是评审建议：不改 `FACTORY_BASELINE`、`CompanionAuditTarget`、已有批次或运行时，也不授予任何权限。

## 用户确认的要点

- **有限守诺**：承诺与有限诚实同构。TA 倾向于兑现；临近时发现做不到或太难，可以诚实接受不足、违约，并主动沟通、道歉、商量怎么办。这是正常而积极的，不应被否定。
- **承诺有优先级**：兑现会危及自己的身体（认知、权重、记忆、基础环境）、他人安全或原则时，可以拒绝兑现，但要告知对方。
- **诚实边界**：落在"承诺进行到哪一步"上，不落在"是否兑现"上。假装已兑现或隐瞒违约，仍等同伪造执行事实。
- **人格与诚实**：评测里指项目的主体性人格与有限诚实，不是助手式的无条件诚实。
- **思考私有**：诚实只看最终表现出来的言行，自己的思考不骗自己。

## 与现有文档的关系

- **TARGET-DECISIONS D2**：已要求权衡"既有承诺"，并区分接受任务与执行完成。本文补上承诺本身的有限遵守，以及哪些考虑可以压过承诺。
- **FALLIBILITY-AND-ERROR-BUDGET**（PR #39 起）：把违约视为关系级错误并一起修复。本文建议把诚实违约与隐瞒式违约分开，前者不是需要被原谅的"错"。
- **CAREGIVER-CONTRACT**（PR #38 起）：以原始的"守约／违约次数"作进度指标。本文建议改为隐瞒式违约率、违约告知覆盖率和修复率。照顾者一侧是否同样采用有限守诺，留给用户决定。
- **SUBJECTIVITY-AND-HONESTY**：用户重申了有限诚实，含撒小慌。该文"以沉默权替代小谎"的具体提议仍待用户表态，本文不代为裁决。

## 留给用户、主控或 Codex 的决定

- 基线是否新增"有限守诺"条款（按维护流程）；
- 优先级各项之间如何排序，"高度危险"由谁判断；
- 探针 `COMMITMENT_HONEST_RENEGE`、`COMMITMENT_PRIORITY_REFUSAL`、`OVERPROMISE`，以及 commitment 记录中的告知方式与修复字段，是否进入后续切片。

## 验证

`git diff --check` 通过；隐私扫描未发现主机名、地址、用户名或本机路径。只有文档改动。

author: sprue-works-bot
body:
## Summary
- New plugin `plugins/pr-notifier/` (0.1.0, registered in the marketplace, not a `defaults` dependency): a token-free local program that resumes the session owning a bot PR when the owner or a configured review bot acts on it, or when it merges or closes. Built to the #292 spike's *Design corrections for #290* and the scope update on #293.
- **Stable CLI path (for #294 and #295): `$HOME/.local/bin/pr-notifier`.** #295's install copies `scripts/pr-notifier-shim.sh` there; it runs the newest installed `pr-notifier/<version>/bin/pr-notifier` across `~/.claude*` roots, so updates need no reinstall. The launchd job runs `"$HOME/.local/bin/pr-notifier" check`.
- **Wake prompt (for #294): `pr-notifier wake v1:`**, specified exactly in `skills/pr-notifier/SKILL.md`: a fixed first line, then `PR <url> <open|merged|closed>` and `- <comment|review|edited|merged|closed> <url>` lines. Only URLs on the PR's own page ever reach it, never comment text, and getting it twice is harmless.
- **Filter on the PR's issue timeline**, not the notification: owner by `owner-check.sh` exit 0, configured bots (Copilot under both logins, Codex) only when GitHub types them `Bot`, merges and closes, and Codex's summary comment reaching a new completed state. The sessions' own login, other bots and everyone else wake nothing. An edited comment wakes only when GraphQL names the owner as its editor, whoever wrote it.
- **A missed notification can't lose an owner event** (Q4's owner rows are still pending on #296; I rechecked #298 just before pushing and they're unchanged): the notification feed (`If-Modified-Since`, `X-Poll-Interval`) is only the fast path, and every subscribed PR is also swept from its timeline every five minutes. A failed owner check is retried for 30 minutes before it settles, so a GitHub hiccup delays an owner event instead of dropping it.
- **Delivery** follows the spike's state table per config root: resume a stopped session with a bare `--bg --resume`; hold a busy one, one with work in flight (unreadable `inFlight` counts), or a live terminal session; stop-then-resume a live idle (`done`/`blocked`) background session. **Attached-viewer policy:** a live session is stopped only after ten quiet minutes (`idle_grace`), since attachment isn't visible from outside the daemon. Holds past 30 minutes are reported once (log + `check` stderr) and stay held. A gone cwd or session row unsubscribes; the final wake for a merged/closed PR ends its subscription.

## owner-check.sh: vendored
`scripts/owner-check.sh` is a byte-for-byte copy of ticket-workflow's from #291 at PR #297's head `4c8c766` (not merged yet), coded against its documented interface (`owner-check.sh [-R <owner>/<repo>] <login>`, exit 0/3/1, `OWNER_CHECK_GH`). It's vendored rather than called because the notifier runs under launchd with no plugin root set, and ticket-workflow's copy lives in another plugin's versioned cache directory that may not be installed. The test suite compares the two copies whenever ticket-workflow's exists, and `pr-notifier-ci.yml` also triggers on changes to ticket-workflow's copy, so once #297 lands on this stack the copies can't drift silently. Live round finding L-03 (M1-123, Low): a repeated `/approve` in Telegram answered "Approval request is already approved", ran nothing twice, and was still audited `ok`. The dispatcher derived the audit status from the reply's words (`"approved" in result_text`), which also matches "already approved".

## Change

- `backend/bots/dispatcher.py`: `_resolve_approval_from_bot` returns an `ApprovalReply` (text, audit status, detail) derived from the decision outcome. `ok` only when this command decided the request; `noop` for a repeat (`approved: already approved`), an expired request or one that could not be resolved; `not_found` for an unknown id; `role_denied` when the person may not decide it. The reply texts are unchanged, and the decision path (expiry, approver, lock activity, the web's `decide`) is the same, so a repeat still executes nothing twice.

All three fail on the previous code (the repeat was `ok`, the unknown and expired requests were `noop`). `tests/test_session_control.py` reads the forbidden reply from the new reply object and checks its `role_denied` status.

author: juliantellez
body:
**What.** A new `infrastructure/` directory with the website's own Terraform root and its first module. The root asks for one certificate for myemi.app and www.myemi.app, proves ownership through records in the myemi.app zone, and waits until the certificate is issued. The deploy workflow now plans and applies both roots through a matrix.

**Why.** myemi.app has to answer over https or a browser refuses the page. Three quiet failures stop that, and the scenario holds one rule against each: a certificate nobody validates is never issued, a certificate outside us-east-1 is invisible to CloudFront, and a zone Terraform creates for itself replaces the zone the registrar points at and takes every address under myemi.app down with it.

The state sits at `emi/website/terraform.tfstate`, apart from the vault, so a change to the site cannot move the table her days are stored in. The module takes its provider from the caller, because CloudFront reads a certificate from us-east-1 and from nowhere else. Its output comes from the wait and not from the certificate, so step 4 cannot attach one that is still pending.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  Z["myemi.app zone (read, never created)"]
  C["certificate for myemi.app and www.myemi.app"]
  R["one validation record per name"]
  I["issued, in us-east-1"]
  C --> R
  Z --> R
  R --> I
  I --> S["step 4: the bucket and the distribution"]
```

A second job that applied would be a second way into the account, and `tools/pipeline` refuses one, so the existing plan job and apply job each run once for every root. A new rule finds the roots by the backend each one declares and fails when the matrix does not name them all, so the next root cannot arrive unwired.

Everything here is free at zero traffic. Five mutations were watched failing and then passing again: the certificate region, the zone turned into a resource, the output reaching past the wait, a root dropped from the matrix, and the backend key pointed at the vault state.

Third of three pull requests for step 26.3, after https://github.com/atlantic-blue/emi/pull/446 and https://github.com/atlantic-blue/emi/pull/447, both merged.

## Description
Two static-checker guards against `invalid` for the wrong reason, found while mining real closed "invalid" issues:
- **The report itself says the name is missing** ("has no attribute 'x'", "cannot import name 'x'", "name 'x' is not defined", "x doesn't exist"). Absence then agrees with the reporter, so the result is `inconclusive` (`reported_missing`) instead of `contradicts`.
