author: aljopro
body:
Entry 9.4 — the WebGL2 replayer draws AD-3's whole command union, and the agreement with `core/raster` is proved on the committed kit and on **every gating row of `golden/ledger.json`**.

## Evidence, from the lane's own log

- **16/16 committed vectors exact** (was 3): fill, blits with key/tint/blends, both R-15 tint remaps, the alpha-0 skip, row order, the Bresenham line (shallow and steep), the rectangle outline (thick and thin), the ellipse outline and filled, the `.iso` projection, a legacy bitmap-font run and a TrueType run. Blend cases are exercised; the bound allows one unit but all of them measure **0**.
- **19/19 gating ledger rows exact** through WebGL2 — 12 authored scenes and 7 closing baselines, the largest 307 commands — and every row is **pixel-identical after `flush()`**.

## What changed

**The pixels a GPU cannot derive come from the core, not from a second implementation.** `linePixels`, `rectOutlinePixels`, `ellipsePixels`, `isoSourceOffset` (`core/raster/shapes.ts`) and `textInk` (`core/raster/text.ts`) were extracted from the reference rasteriser, which now plots exactly those; the replayer draws one one-pixel quad per point. That refactor moved **no** goldens: `pnpm golden` 20 rows, `pnpm closing` 8/8, core 2247/2247.

**Text.** Legacy cells keep the reference's forward cell mapping, the italic shear and bold's second ink; TrueType keeps `getGlyphRaster`'s coverage and per-glyph offsets. Coverage 255 is a plain write, any other coverage is the reference's integer coverage blend. A family the game does not ship draws in `DEFAULT_FONT_ASSET` — the substitution the engine already makes before it rasterises. Without it the Basic sample presented four blank labels; the constant moved to `core/raster/text.ts` and the engine imports it.

**Two presentation defects fixed by it.** A tiled blit uploads only the tile it names: a 589-tile `.tst` is wider than `MAX_TEXTURE_SIZE`, and an incomplete texture samples as black — which is how Caoquest used to present a wrong frame with **no** diagnostic. And a frame clears to transparent black like the reference's zeroed buffer, so a covered pixel's alpha is the command's rather than the canvas's.

**AD-33 as pure geometry.** `presentationFrame`: `letterbox` scales by an integer factor and centres, `expand` shows 1:1 with a black surround. The draw list is always drawn at its logical resolution.

**Harness seams.** `TracerResult.textures` so a replayer can draw the same scene; `ClosingFrameWithDrawList.pixels` so a replayer is compared with the engine's own screen (the closing oracle, AD-4) rather than with a rasterisation that differs where the engine substitutes a font.

**The lane.** A conformance spec over all 16 vectors and an agreement spec over all 19 rows, each replayed twice with a cache flush between (AD-27, G4 rule 3). The page reports the worst channel and the pixel it happened at, never a bare boolean. `render-webgl2` gains its own `tools/no-skips` group and `unit` shard over its two pure leaves.

## Gates

`pnpm typecheck` (including the page's own project), `pnpm lint`, `pnpm graph` (539 modules), `pnpm provenance`, `pnpm licence`, `pnpm fixtures:test` (99), `pnpm no-skips:test` (12), `pnpm test:strict` (2512/2512, none skipped), `pnpm closing` (8/8), `pnpm golden` (20 rows), `pnpm browser:test` (4 passed).

No golden, state hash, draw hash or baseline PNG moved.

Fixes #929

body:
## Intent

The fleet's machine admission (bin/fm-machine-resources.py with config/machine-admission.json, consumed by fm-spawn and fm-capacity) refuses new workers when the memory PSI full average over 60 seconds exceeds 5 (memory_full_avg60_max). On 2026-10-31 the laptop used 6 of 26 GB with 20 GB available (largest process Milvus at 627 MB) and still refused workers, and the server refused at PSI full 5.5 with 9.6 GB available. PSI full spikes come in short bursts when 4 to 6 workers run test suites at once, and refusals land on those peaks, so machines refuse workers while mostly idle. The owner asked whether the laptop is really short on memory; it is not. The owner approved upstream fixes to github.com/ashkonmousavi/firstmate under the same consent as earlier fork fixes: one pull request into the fork's curated branch. Required: admission must reflect real capacity, by reading a window that ignores short test bursts, or by limiting concurrent heavy test runs per machine instead of refusing new workers (choose the smaller change that works), and the change must be shown to reduce refusals against real free memory.

## What Changed

- Add optional `memory_full_avg300_max` admission checks alongside a configurable avg60 burst ceiling, preserving avg60-only behavior for existing policies.
- Record admission verdicts, PSI windows, available memory, and policy hashes in a rotating best-effort log.
- Add regression coverage and configuration guidance, plus documented real-machine replay comparisons showing fewer refusals with ample available memory.

✅ Low: The opt-in pressure window preserves existing capacity gates and legacy policy behavior, and the prior fixes are supported by the current source.

author: willington123
body:
## Para qué
Una tienda equivale a un número de WhatsApp API. Un portafolio puede tener varias cuentas de WhatsApp y varios números (uno por producto). Cada tienda debe ver solo sus mensajes, sus cuentas publicitarias y sus creativos.

## Problema que corrige
Una app de Meta tiene **una sola URL de webhook**. La URL por tienda (`/api/whatsapp/webhook/<tienda>`) **descartaba** los mensajes de los demás números de esa app. En un portafolio con 3 números, solo una tienda recibía mensajes.

## Cambios
- **Webhook único `/api/whatsapp/webhook`:**
  - Reparte cada número a su tienda.
  - Acepta avisos firmados con la clave de la app de la tienda dueña del número, además de las claves de la plataforma. Si la firma no coincide, se ignora el aviso.
  - Acepta el token de verificación de cualquier tienda. Integraciones ahora muestra esta URL.
- **URL antigua por tienda:** reparte los otros números de la misma app (misma clave secreta) a sus tiendas.
- **Un número por tienda:** al conectar, si el número ya está en otra tienda se rechaza y se dice en cuál.
- **Reutilizar la conexión de un portafolio** (`GET /api/integrations/whatsapp/numbers`, `POST /api/integrations/whatsapp/reuse`):
  - Lista las tiendas del usuario con conexión propia y todas las cuentas de WhatsApp y números del portafolio (vía `owner_business_info` → `owned_whatsapp_business_accounts`), marcando los que ya están en uso.
  - Conecta el número elegido copiando el token y la clave cifrados.
  - Requiere ser dueño o administrador de las dos tiendas.
- Al conectar se suscribe la cuenta de WhatsApp a la app (`subscribed_apps`).
- Las tiendas nuevas abren Integraciones con una guía de qué conectar.

## Pruebas
- Portafolio: 21/21. Cubren conexión manual y suscripción, URL única, fuentes reutilizables, cuentas y números del portafolio, números en uso, número fuera de la cuenta, reutilizar entre cuentas de WhatsApp, rechazo de número ocupado, otra persona sin acceso, reparto por número en la URL única, firma incorrecta, URL antigua que reparte, tokens de verificación y bandejas separadas por tienda.
- Regresiones: fase 2 47/47 (se actualizó la URL esperada), anuncios 10/10, aislamiento entre tiendas 59/59.
- `tsc` y `next build` OK.

## Para el usuario
En cada app de Meta, la URL del webhook debe ser `https://konnexa.lat/api/whatsapp/webhook`, la misma para todos los números.

author: akbarhoja
body:
Canvas’s syllabus file resolves through a signed storage URL and a CDN redirect. This operator-only P0 diagnostic reads at most two selected courses, samples two assignment details per course, and retrieves one configured PDF through one manually validated storage-to-CDN hop. It reuses the reviewed core probe; it does not implement the P1 collector.

The v5 manifest adds the exact `cdn.inst-fs-iad-prod.inscloudgate.net` host and observational `webRequest` permission alongside the institution and original file host. A temporary response-header listener matches the active request URL, GET method and own extension initiator. Every fetch uses manual redirects, omitted file-host credentials/referrer, bounded time/bytes, and exact destination validation. No arbitrary follow mode, request modification, cookie export, persistent source storage or cloud upload. Identity checks fence the whole report and run before the CDN hop. PDF MIME/signature and a private SHA256 comparison identify the separately saved local sample; PDF text extraction is a separate local check.

Operator-reported live v5 evidence: 7 courses discovered, 2 selected, assignment lists of 22/23 with 12/9 instruction bodies; 4 assignment details read with no rubric criteria observed; one discussion view sampled. The configured PDF read 398346 bytes through one hop, passed signature validation and matched the local sample. This passes bounded PDF retrieval, not full academic collection, positive rubric access, account-switch coverage or unattended browser operation. The popup remains explicitly `partial_probe`/`probe_output_not_acceptance`.

Validation: 64 local Node cases pass; 685 disposable backend cases passed before the live run, with two existing warnings. Ruff, formatting and diff checks pass. M’s scoped review found a Windows child-script path issue: the regression now uses `fileURLToPath`; Windows re-review is requested and is separate from local macOS evidence. Current follow-up changes do not alter the installed runtime.

Claim: #104 / coordination #4. Stacked on #105 (`codex/p0-local-access`). Private scope, signed URL values, local PDF/hash and prepared package remain ignored; none are published. P0 stays open for remaining evidence/review and separate baseline/interfaces/WhatsApp gates. Outlook is optional and paused. No deployment, paid model call, live upload, send or P1 ownership change.

author: khromov
body:
Linux verification ahead of 0.4.0 (#57). Everything in 0.4.0 works on Linux except what is fixed here. **Merge this before #57** so the fixes ship in 0.4.0.

## Fixes

| Problem on Linux | Fix |
| --- | --- |
| **The title bar shrank from 34 to 26 px** when app content overflowed the window, and everything below jumped 8 px when content started or stopped fitting. GNOME Wayland only. Older than 0.4.0. | `flex-shrink: 0` on the bar |
| **The window had no app id.** `docs/shipping.md` tells Linux users to add a `.desktop` file, but `app.identifier` never reached the window, so `WAYLAND_DEBUG` showed no `set_app_id` and X11 had no `WM_CLASS`. A desktop had nothing to match that file by. | `identifier` now becomes `appId`; an explicit `appId` wins |
| **`test:automation-live` failed at its screenshot**, which the Linux addon can't take. | The screenshot step is skipped on Linux |
| **`consume` and `bun:consume` failed at the starter's headless test**, so a scaffolded app's build never ran on Linux. | The test step is skipped on Linux |
| **Docs were silent:** `screenshot()` and `GPUIX_SCREENSHOT` don't work; the picker rejects without a portal; bounds reads stall on a minimized Wayland window. | Added to `docs/`, `starter/AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md` |

The window now takes `identifier` from `app` on every platform, but only Linux uses it: GPUI's `set_app_id` does nothing on macOS or Windows. I read that in the local `../gpuix` checkout, which lags native 0.11.

**CI, which you may want to review separately (`2f7ec8a`):** Linux is added to the `consume` matrix, and the `linux` job now runs `test:bundle`, `test:compile` and `test:automation-live` under `xvfb-run` with Mesa's software Vulkan, on both runtimes. Until now no CI job ever launched a Linux window. This wasn't strictly asked for, so drop it if you'd rather not carry it.

## What was verified

Ubuntu 26.04 VM with GNOME 50 and Mesa software rendering, on `origin/main` plus these commits.

**Display environments:** the real session on Wayland (`wayland-0`) and XWayland (`:0`), Xvfb, and a private headless GNOME Wayland session. Not every check ran in every environment.

| Area | Checks | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Static | `typecheck`, `lint`, scaffolder `npm pack --dry-run`, binding load | pass |
| Tests that can run on Linux | `test:bundle`, `test:compile` on Node 24, Node 26 and Bun | pass |
| `test:automation-live` | Node 26 and Bun, in all four environments | pass |
| `gpuix-svelte/build` | `npm run compile`; scaffolded apps from the packed tarball; a path with a space and a `’`; `render_hot`, missing-icon and computed-value errors | pass; binaries launched on X11 and Wayland |
| `consume`, `bun:consume` | Node 24 and 26 | pass |
| `Scroller`, plain and virtual | wheel, thumb drag, overlay removal, content growing and shrinking, Node and Bun, X11 and Wayland | pass |
| `Scroller` idle redraws | same matrix | 0 frames/s; plain mode also follows a maximize on Wayland |
| `prompt_for_paths` | real portal with the GTK backend | app stays usable behind it (reads 25–45 ms); Escape gives `null`; choosing gives the path |
| `prompt_for_paths` without a portal | unreachable D-Bus | rejects; app keeps running |
| `read_native`, closing | WM close on a busy window | exit 0 in 12 of 12 runs, Node and Bun, X11 |
| `<canvas>` | real window | paints as a div, with its child, and warns |
| `render()`'s `app.name` | real window | used as the title when `title` is missing |
| Examples | all eight on Node, X11 and Wayland | no errors; 0 frames/s idle except those that animate on purpose; X11 screenshots checked by eye |
| Title bar | real window | Close exits 0; Maximize works; with overflowing content, GNOME Wayland screenshots show 26 px on `main` and 34 px here |
| `.desktop` matching | private GNOME session with a matching `.desktop` file, `main` against this branch | GNOME's window tracker reports `window:N`, "Unknown" and a generic icon on `main`; `com.example.gpuixdemo.desktop`, "GPUIX Demo App" and the file's icon here |
| `demo` (four windows), `demo:web --build-only`, `docs` | | pass |

## Not covered

- **Headless suites:** `TestGpuixRenderer` doesn't exist on Linux, so they can't run here, including the new check in `test/titlebar.ts` and all of `test/dialog.ts` and `test/scroller.ts`. This PR's macOS and Windows CI runs them. I reproduced the title bar bug and the fix in a real window, using the same fixture.
- **Web:** built only, not run in a browser.
- **Desktops:** KDE and other non-GNOME desktops weren't tried. Everything ran on Mesa software rendering (`libEGL` warnings in the logs come from that), not a real GPU.

## Review

A separate review of this diff found no defects. It ran the Linux-runnable checks and compared the native claims with `@gpuix/native` 0.11.0's source. Its two low-priority notes are left alone because neither is a defect of this PR: `app.name` doesn't set macOS's `appName`, so the Hide and Quit menu items show the window title (older than this PR, and macOS only), and the header comment in `test/bundle.ts` doesn't mention `window_options_for` (cosmetic).

## Known, left alone

- **Stall while minimized on Wayland:** `getElementBounds`, `getElementsAt` and `getAutomationTree` block JS for 2 s and throw, because a minimized window gets no next frame. `read_native` hides the throw but not the wait, and `automation` reads fail the same way. Nothing in `src/` polls these any more, so this only affects apps that do; it comes from native and is now documented.
- **Shutdown log:** a commit racing the window closing can log `commit failed: … UI thread is not running` (seen once in 12 closes). The exit code is still 0.

body:
Adds a native Qt Widgets installer for the independent Yūrei image, reusing existing shrine artwork. Screens cover disk selection, accounts, explicit whole-disk erase confirmation, installation output and the result.

The backend receives passwords over stdin and binds the request to disk size/device number. It rejects mounted/read-only/live-medium targets, rechecks capacity before writes and prevents concurrent installations. It enables SDDM, the temporary greeter or console boot according to the image contents.

Verified at 22779cad1a1f4865c35c8fa34ed03bcfbb5daf07: real C++ compilation and Qt model tests; all six previews; repository/package/theme checks; disposable UEFI installation against the pinned pre-Qt ISO, installed-disk-only boot, password login, root/EFI mounts and sudo. Evidence: https://github.com/Subuwu97/Yurei-OS/actions/runs/41253627942.

Latest head d0a072b84c72f4fc4ff5df0258eff734540af0b6 incorporates main's Direct3D build fix and Qt runtime checks. The bootstrap accepts an explicit use_pc manual input, restricted to owner dispatches on main/Qt/installer refs. Other runs use GitHub-hosted runners; the legacy YUREI_RUNNER variable is unused by this revision. The PC preflight checks runner identity, sudo, KVM, ext4 build storage and actual Windows free space. Installer branch builds are on demand; pushes no longer launch another full bootstrap.

The full image workflow requires all six GUI previews to render inside the actual live guest before the GUI stdin/device-protocol install and reboot test. Successful installer-branch builds retain the ISO/checksum for three days. Branch builds do not publish releases.

Remaining release checks: compositor/mouse interaction and desktop authentication/cancellation inside the Qt-enabled image. Offscreen previews do not cover those. UEFI whole-disk ext4/systemd-boot only; no manual partitioning, dual boot or encryption.

The Qt base is now merged upstream, so this PR targets main. This work does not push to main.

_Requested by **Ralf** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01VajHxoMpjg2u43YzaGY7La?thread=cmsg_01VajHxoMpjg2u43YzaGY7LaRZ3riACaDRVnmTV8cs8ebg)_

ROADMAP "Missing for daily use", item 7. Built as a module of amadeos-system, as Ralf decided.

## New module `taskmanager` (package `amadeos-taskmanager`)
- **Programs**: one line per program window with status (Running, Minimized, Not responding), workspace, CPU, memory and disk of its process tree. You can Switch To a window (across workspaces too), End Program (SIGTERM, then Force End after 5 s) or Show Processes.
- **Processes**: a tree or a flat list. Sort, search and All users. You can end a process or its tree, force end, pause or continue, set the priority, open the program folder, copy the command line and see properties. Other users' processes, and raising priority, go through `pkexec`.
- **Performance**: the last 60 s of CPU per core, memory and swap, network and disk. A click enlarges one graph. Speed 1/2/5 s or Paused.
- Everything comes from `/proc`, tested against a fake `/proc` tree. Single instance through a Unix socket. 5 languages, and Help opens User's Handbook chapter 59.

## Window manager
- Pings the active window every 2 s, and every window asked to close (`_NET_WM_PING`, now in `_NET_SUPPORTED`). If a window does not answer within 5 s:
  - its title gets "(Not Responding)",
  - the property `_AMADEOS_NOT_RESPONDING` is set,
  - `amadeos-taskmanager --not-responding WIN` asks Wait / End Program / Open Task Manager.
  The mark clears and the dialog closes once the window answers again.
- **Ctrl+Shift+Esc** and **Ctrl+Alt+Delete** open the Task Manager.
- Limitation: AWT answers the ping on its toolkit thread, so a Java program with a blocked event thread is not marked. It can still be ended from the Task Manager.

## Checks
- `:wm:test` and `:taskmanager:test` are green.
- In `:base:test`, only the 4 `PamAuthenticatorTest` cases fail in my container. That class is unchanged here; only `X11EwmhHelper` changed in base.
- Tried under Xvfb with the amadeOS WM: both keys, a stopped client getting marked and unmarked, End then Force End, all three tabs.

Follow-ups: the image package list and User's Handbook ch. 59 (amadeos), and the dev handbook chapter (amade-commons).

author: centdix
body:
## Summary
Running the backend tests from inside a webmux pane disconnected the live dashboard's terminals. `terminal-adapter.test.ts` was killing the real `wm-dash-5111-*` tmux sessions that the dashboard's terminal WebSockets are attached to.

Root cause: `setTerminalAdapterDependenciesForTests()` resets every dependency the caller doesn't pass back to the real implementation. The interrupt and send-prompt tests mock only `spawnTmuxProcess`, so in those tests `spawnSyncCommand` was the real one. The `afterEach` then called `cleanupStaleSessions()`. With `PORT` unset, that listed sessions on the real tmux server and ran `tmux kill-session` on every `wm-dash-5111-*`.

## Changes
- `backend/src/__tests__/terminal-adapter.test.ts`: added a `setFakeDependencies(overrides)` helper. Any dependency a test doesn't override gets an inert fake (unexpected PTY spawns throw, tmux and sync commands are no-ops, sleep resolves immediately). It's applied in `beforeEach` and used by every test in place of `setTerminalAdapterDependenciesForTests`, so nothing in the file can reach the real tmux. Production code is unchanged.

## How it was found / verified
- A watcher polled the live tmux server and logged whenever a `wm-dash-5111-*` session disappeared.
- Before the fix, running test files one at a time showed `terminal-adapter.test.ts` killing the live session every time, and no other file did.
- After the fix, the live session survived 3 runs of the file plus the full backend suite.
- `bun test` (backend): 617 pass, 0 fail
- `bun run check` (backend): passes

## Test plan
- [ ] With the dashboard open on a worktree terminal, run `cd backend && bun test` from a webmux pane. The terminal stays connected.

author: rar9
body:
## Problem

`GHSA-g3hv-75wg-m249` (moderate) — minimatch has a potential denial of service via globparts amplification. Affected: **< 11.0.1**.

Our lock pulled `minimatch@10.2.6` through `ts-morph@^28.0.0 → @ts-morph/common@0.29.0`, which declares `minimatch: ^10.0.1`. **10.2.6 is the last 10.x release**, so no patched version exists inside that range — a cross-major bump is the only remedy short of dropping ts-morph.

The repo gate `scripts/security/scan-osv.ts --strict` fails on this advisory today (`❌ pkg:npm/minimatch@10.2.6 — GHSA-g3hv-75wg-m249`), i.e. the OSV check is red on `next`.

## Implementation

- `package.json`: override `"minimatch": "^11.0.3"` in the existing `overrides` block (bounded to 11.x, so a future 12.x cannot slip in unreviewed) (same convention as `fast-uri`, `brace-expansion`, …).
- `bun.lock`: regenerated → `minimatch@11.0.3`.
- `sbom.json`: regenerated via `bun run audit:sbom` (722 components) — the OSV scanner reads the SBOM, so a stale SBOM would report the old version.

**Compatibility check for the major bump:** the only consumer, `@ts-morph/common@0.29.0`, calls the exported function `minimatch(path, pattern)` only (`dist/ts-morph-common.js:1199`, `:1287`). None of the APIs removed in v11 are used (`makeRe()`, `Minimatch#regexp`, `MMRegExp`, `AST`, `debug`, `maxExtglobRecursion`). The repo has no direct `minimatch` import, and `ts-morph` is a devDependency, so the override does not leak into `create-sveltycms` consumers.

## Benefit / verification

- `bun run scripts/security/scan-osv.ts --strict` → **722 packages, 0 affected, gate passed** (was failing).
- `bun audit` → only `deepmerge@4.3.1` (low, dev/build-time, already suppressed by the scanner).
- ts-morph functional probe: `addSourceFilesAtPaths(['src/**/*.ts','!src/**/*.d.ts'])` → 1023 files; `scripts/lint/lint-tenant-api.ts` (ts-morph based, full scan 1023 files) → exit 0.
- `ADAPTER=node COMPILE_ALL_ADAPTERS=true bun run build:verbose` → build OK (1m31s).
- Pre-commit chain on CT200: format+lint, lint-staged, risk audit (incl. OSV), component interactions, SBOM sync all ✔; the only failing stage is the Redis-backed `cache-service-l2-contract` suite (needs `TEST_REDIS_URL`/Docker, not available in that checkout) — unrelated to this change.

Rollback: revert this commit (override line + regenerated lock/SBOM).

author: ram0ng1
body:
<!-- O título em inglês deste PR, para as notas do release em inglês (as que vão para o discuss.flarum.org). Sem ele, vai o título do PR. -->
EN: Backup downloads are streamed through Flarum's response pipeline

## O que muda

O download de backup escrevia o arquivo direto na saída do PHP e chamava `exit`. Isso pulava o resto da pilha de middlewares e não dava para testar: um teste chamando a rota encerrava o próprio PHPUnit. O motivo era não carregar o arquivo na memória, mas o Flarum 2 já resolve isso desde o 2.0.0: o `Flarum\Http\Emitter` transmite em pedaços (`SapiStreamEmitter`) toda resposta cujo corpo é um `CallbackStream`.

- **`FileRangeStream`** (novo, `src/Http`): um `CallbackStream` legível sobre uma faixa do arquivo. O emitter lê o arquivo em pedaços de 8 KB, então nem um backup de vários GB passa pela memória.
- **`DownloadBackupController`** devolve uma resposta PSR-7 normal, sem `echo`, sem mexer em buffers e sem `exit`. Continuam iguais os headers (`Content-Disposition` com nome em UTF-8, `Accept-Ranges`, `X-Accel-Buffering`, `nosniff`, `no-store`), o `Range` com resposta 206 e a proteção do caminho por `StoragePaths::backupFilePath()`.
- **`DownloadTest`** cobre o arquivo inteiro, uma faixa no meio e os últimos N bytes. Os três falhavam antes da mudança: o `exit` encerrava o processo do teste.

### Verificação

- Suíte inteira: 34 testes de integração e 42 unitários. PHPStan sem erros.
- No servidor real com `memory_limit=64M` (abaixo do tamanho do arquivo), um backup de 200 MB baixou inteiro, com SHA-256 idêntico ao do disco. As faixas `bytes=100000000-100000099` e `bytes=-10` voltaram com 206, `Content-Range` certo e os bytes exatos do arquivo. Nenhum erro de memória.

### Sobre o restante do relatório que motivou este PR

- **"Rotas com `{id}` leem o parâmetro da query string":** falso positivo. O `RouteHandlerFactory::toController()` do Flarum 2 junta os parâmetros da rota aos da query antes de chamar o controller, e o próprio core lê assim. No fórum de teste, exportar (`/exports/{id}/tick`), baixar e apagar por `{id}` funcionaram.
- **`sodium_memzero` depois da cópia em base64:** a cópia é o retorno de `generateKeypair()`, mostrado uma vez para o admin colar no `config.php`. Fica como está.
- **`ExportJob` com `Connection` concreta:** já recebe a interface injetada e estreita com verificação, porque o dump precisa de `getDriverName()`. Já está documentado no código.

author: aclater
body:
Closes #37. This replaces the per-PR figures in `docs/performance.md` with one fresh round on the release code, as #37 asked ("be sure to update perf stats when we do the docs refresh"). The layout from #52 is unchanged. It also adds a separate NAS section with #21 part 1's figures.

## How the round was run
- **Code:** `main` at 49f114c (includes #53; scarletbook 0.5.0), in the two release builds: generic (`-C target-cpu=x86-64`) and x86-64-v3.
- **Gate first:** both builds passed the DSF gate, **93/93** tracks identical, and hashed all 93 WAV files.
- **Timing:** under `benchlock`, means of 3.
- **Quiet machine:** each part waited until the load average had stayed under 2 for 5 minutes.
  - The cleanroom VM was shut off all night. Its load was still recorded with the exact match `pgrep -f '^/usr/bin/qemu-system.*guest=scarletbook-cleanroom'` (fields 14+15), and was 0 throughout.
  - A watcher looked for compilers and fuzzers every 2 s during each part and saw none. A part disturbed by either would have been redone.
- **Scripts:** copies of the earlier agents' scripts, with only paths, names and the VM match changed:
  - B/bench.py: straight reads, WAV seeks, metadata;
  - pin050/bench.py: in-process seeks;
  - lat/bench2.sh: local and NFS seeks, cold and warm;
  - seek041/conc.py: concurrency;
  - c/tagcost.sh: DSF tag walk;
  - mounttime.sh;
  - D/meas/run27.py: SMB, client- and server-side.

  On top of those: scarletbook's own `bench decode` 0.5.0, `seek_latency`, and `cargo bench --bench pcm` pinned to one core.
- **Reruns:** four parts failed at once on the first pass, all from bugs in my driver; the machine was never involved. They were fixed and rerun on a quiet machine:
  - decode and tags: a shell function wasn't exported;
  - mount: an unmount failed as busy, and the leftover mount then held the lock;
  - SMB: the client container didn't exist yet.

  Only valid runs are published.

## What changed against the previous published figures
- **DSF straight read against `bench decode`:** 1.36x / 1.37x / 1.50x (DST stereo / plain DSD / DST 6 ch.). It was 1.43x, from a loaded machine with scarletbook 0.3.0 (#4). The 6-channel area, and the v3 build's DST stereo, sit right at the 1.5x line.
- **WAV against DSF:** 1.07x / 1.23x / 1.17x (was 1.09 / 1.20 / 1.16 in #42).
- **Local cold seek through FUSE:** 2.1 ms DST, 1.5 ms plain DSD (#25 measured 1.4 and 0.5). The new means include a few slow seeks of up to 5.8 ms; the fastest plain DSD seeks took 0.29 ms. WAV seek 2.7 ms (was 1.8).
- **Converter:** 308x real time (was 305x); wide filter 149x (was 147x).
  - SSE2 only: 247x and 108x.
  - **New finding:** v4 is now slightly faster than v3 for the 30 kHz filter at 176.4 and 352.8 kHz (2–4 %), and slower everywhere else (up to 22 %). v3 stays the default.
- **The x86-64-v3 build:** converts at the same speed as the generic build, whose AVX2 code is chosen at run time. It reads DST areas **10–18 % faster** because scarletbook's DST decoder is compiled for AVX2 too. The README's v3 line now says this instead of the earlier claim about conversion CPU.
- **NFS, client-side:**
  - cold first touch 21.9 ms plain DSD (was 18.6) and **36.9 ms DST (was 26.8; worst single seek 64.7 ms, over the 50 ms target)**;
  - with a warm seek index, 1.8 / 2.3 ms (was 2.0 / 2.7).

  The first-touch figures depend on the NAS's disks and on which positions it last cached.
- **SMB, client-side:**
  - cold 4.3 / 5.3 ms (was 5.2 / 6.1);
  - **with a warm seek index, 2.4 / 2.6 ms (was 3.4 / 3.6)**. This now meets the target for plain DSD, because images stay open between reads (#35).
- **SMB, server-side:** DSF 4.8 / 5.7 ms, WAV 5.4 / 6.1 ms (was 4.7–5.5).
- **Concurrency:** the local worst read is 36.2 ms (was 27.0), within 50 ms. **On NFS, players' worst reads are 75–170 ms (was 19–120)**: reads of parts of an image the NAS takes from its hard disks. This is marked "not met".
- **Memory:** peak 169–356 MiB (was 168–342).
- **Mount, listing and tags:**
  - mount of the NFS library: 0.12 s for 154 images (was 101 ms for 138 images);
  - header and tag walk of 186 files: 113 ms (was 84);
  - DSF tag walk: 0.09 s (was 0.07), with the same 342 calls and 20.7 MB.
- **NAS section, from #21 part 1 (i5-1235U):** cold seek DSF 7.7 ms, WAV 11.2 ms; 6-channel DST is CPU-bound at about 40x real time; peak memory 307–396 MB.
- **Server-side NFS, and SMB from a NAS's hard disks:** measured on the NAS after the v0.1.0 tag (#21 part 2). This machine has no rootful container runtime, which NFS-Ganesha needs.

## Kept from earlier PRs, and labelled as such
- The #47 comparison with scarletbook 0.4.1's seeking.
- The #40 both-threads v4 measurement.
- The History table: one line per improvement, each against its own before.

## Docs
`docs/performance.md` is rewritten. The new figures also go into README.md (deployment latencies, the v3 build), docs/user-guide.md (memory, tag walk), docs/deployment.md and docs/design.md. No code changes.

author: bhekanik
body:
## Problem

To do and Updates remained bold after a row was inspected because their tone followed the source email's READ flag. Seeing a row is not the same as reading its email, finishing a task, or letting go of an update.

## Behavior

- Opening a row's email or details/peek marks that exact row revision seen. Selecting a row or fetching a list does not.
- Unseen rows are bright and bold; seen rows are normal-weight grey even while unfinished. Selection is background-only.
- New task content, folded mail, corrected facts and tracker transitions become unseen. An old acknowledgment cannot hide a newer revision.
- Account-scoped local state survives restarts and portable backup/restore. No provider flags or completion state are changed by the acknowledgment.
- IPC, bridge, CLI (`mxr modes seen`), TUI and MCP (`mxr_mode_row_seen`) share the preview-capable operation. Older payloads without a revision remain compatible.
- D190 supersedes D189; guides and generated bridge contracts follow.

## Validation

- Store suite: 534 passed, 2 ignored, including persistence, account/mode isolation and backup/restore.
- Daemon regression tests cover seen-but-open tasks, source READ independence, stale peeks, new folded mail, tracker transitions, malformed requests and reopening tasks.
- Web suite: 267 files, 1922 tests passed; typecheck and lint pass.
- TUI suite: 1,285 unit tests plus all integration/snapshot tests passed, including uniform selection without reverse video.
- MCP suite: 34 passed, including preview-by-default and explicit confirmation.
- Extended the existing Updates browser journey to verify a real peek persists across reload without letting go.

Additional local validation is complete: the scoped Rust gate, `cargo build -p mxr`, 99 protocol tests, 150 bridge unit tests and 9 bridge integration tests pass. The extended Chromium Updates journey passes, including peek persistence, exact let-go selection and complete undo. Browser screenshots cover calm unfinished rows and background-only selection in dark and light themes (`~/Desktop/mxr-read-state/`).

The unchanged dependency audit initially failed on newly reported moderate build-tool advisories. With the user's approval, narrow `glob` and `minimatch` overrides update those transitive tools; the production web build and moderate-or-higher audit pass without suppressions, and generated API types are byte-for-byte unchanged. The full web suite was rerun successfully against the worktree's locked installation. Five low-severity audit findings remain below the existing CI gate.

Review follow-ups are validated: 33 focused daemon tests (including Now revision parity and account scoping), all 6 CLI help tests and updated help snapshots, and 150 focused web tests pass. Production web build, typecheck, lint and the scoped Rust gate pass. Peeks/details acknowledge opening transitions only, including when new revisions arrive while still open. Now decorates the same exact revisions, and ledger queries are bounded to displayed rows rather than account history. All review threads have been answered.

The PR is ready and awaiting the full required CI suite on the final correction.

## Migration

Schema 106 adds a separate exact-revision seen ledger. Existing rows start unseen; this deliberately does not backfill from provider read flags.

author: objeck
body:
`ubuntu-latest` became 26.04 between 16:09Z and 18:31Z on 2026-10-31 (the same workflow logged `Image: ubuntu-24.04` at 16:09Z). The linux-x64 build then links `libopencv_*.so.410` and `libmbedtls.so.21`, where `core/release/runtime_deps.json` records `.so.406` and `.so.14`, so "Declared runtime dependencies match the build (POSIX)" failed master CI on a docs-only commit (#1479).

It is not only a CI problem: a release built on that image would ship binaries that Ubuntu 24.04 and older cannot run. v2026.10.2's linux-x64 was built before the change and is unaffected.

This pins the three linux-x64 matrix legs (`ci-build.yml`, `release-build.yml`, `nightly-hardening.yml`) to `ubuntu-24.04`, matching the arm64 legs and `release-deb.yml`. Moving to 26.04 should be a deliberate change that updates `runtime_deps.json` and the install instructions together.

Other `ubuntu-latest` jobs (tools, docs, summaries) are unchanged; they do not produce shipped binaries.

Test: `python tools/cicd/test_nightly_contract.py` passes. CI on this branch is the real check.

Closes #1479 once master is green.

author: a-canary
body:
Slice 1 of wb-rf4: the deterministic, fail-closed leak gate every sanitized synthetic task must pass before leaving the host (harness-bench is pre-public; 9router models read these tasks).

**Usage:** `bun bin/leak-gate.ts [--denylist F] [--allow-no-gitleaks] <file-or-dir>...`

- exit 0: no hits
- exit 1: hits as `file:line:rule  snippet`; every match is redacted in the snippet, and gitleaks hits print `[REDACTED]` with no line content
- exit 2 (fail closed): denylist missing or empty, gitleaks missing (unless `--allow-no-gitleaks`), gitleaks error, no files, or a bad flag

**Rules:**
- `deny`: private-name denylist, case-insensitive whole word (`-` counts as part of a word). It is loaded from outside the repo, by default from the operator's private vault. 49 terms seeded locally and none committed.
- `ipv4`: any address except 127.0.0.1, 0.0.0.0 and the RFC5737 documentation ranges
- `tailscale-ip`: addresses in 100.64/10
- `email`: any address except example.{com,org,net} and the .test/.example/.invalid/.localhost domains
- `home-path`: `/home/<user>` and `/Users/<user>` paths
- `gitleaks:<RuleID>`: gitleaks run with the host-side `bin/gitleaks.toml`

**Receipts:**
- `bun test bin/leak-gate.test.ts`: 5 pass, 0 fail. Coverage: each rule fires on its fixture, matched values are never printed, a clean fixture passes, a missing or empty denylist exits 2, and snippets are redacted.
- Gitleaks missing from PATH: exits 2 (checked by hand).
- Prototype `2026-10-31-task-draft.json`: 0 hits, exit 0.

Not in this PR: the sanitizer itself (MODEL case → synthetic task), the verify FAIL/PASS check, and delivery.

body:
Season-wide participation questions need a known state and correct side for every game. This read-only tool checks manifest-bound runtime inputs and applies existing participation guards to each observed final team game, separating played, explicit DNP, exact-game other-side association and unknown. Unknowns suppress the missed total. Unusable identity metadata rejects before any unverified historical fallback.

Reciprocal team-game rows and exact catalog date/finality define the requested population; nullable legacy venue fields cannot silently discard games. Populated venue contradictions, missing/duplicate/nonreciprocal sides and source/identity conflicts still reject. Missing keys are unresolved qualification keys: contradictory existing evidence may need repair rather than new collection. No independent complete-season or injury/tenure claim.

The existing LeBron17-game structured request is rebased to the already-published generation. It requests34pinned original TraditionalV3+SummaryV3JSON bodies for exact keys only, without assuming all17areDNP or initiating acquisition. author: lalalune
body:
Notes-only PR for lane `w15a25-cto-o2tfg3repay`. This wave-15 lane was continued in wave 16 and targets `admin_cto::execute` at 0x22a10. It changes no program source.

**Result: no landable change.** Main is still the best zero-loss measurement: 0.67376, 3,124 slots, 27,400 B.

| | before (main 9120883) | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| admin_cto ratio / slots / bytes | 0.67376 / 3,124 / 27,400 | unchanged (notes only) |
| normalized / raw | 1034 / 1034 | unchanged |

## What this adds

1. **A fast oracle for `validate`'s inline decisions** (`tools/reduce.py` + `tools/vbfi.py` + `tools/thr.py`).
   - It reduces the 35 MB capture to `validate` plus its callees, 3.5 MB.
   - It prints validate's block frequencies at the start of its own inliner visit, per `to_string` site, plus the cost and threshold for each site.
   - It runs in about 3 s, against about 2.5 min for the full pipeline. On `m0` it gives the same decisions as the full pipeline.
2. **Why main inlines 307 and 312.**
   - At validate's visit, 307 is at 0.0283 and 312 at 0.0287, where the cold limit is 0.02.
   - The non-holder arm gets 0.1509. That flow is the threaded hr=0/!holder edge (0.0703) plus a 50/50 re-test of `holder` at the split (0.0806).
   - The BPI facts behind this are the bool zero heuristic (62.5 % to the error), 50/50 for `holder`, 50/50 for the `if let Some` range form, and 37.5 % for `memcmp == 0`.
3. **Trigger table.**
   - The 289 spellings `if st.holder_reward{if !holder{..}}`, `holder==false` and `if holder{}else{..}` make 307 and 312 cold. Each gives the original's exact outline pattern and its lddw count of 86.
   - All three collapse to M 1,410 at 27,008 B.
   - `!holder` (B1) misses the threshold by 10 % (0.0220).
   - `unwrap_or(false)` makes execute's visit inline 307 and 312 again.
4. **Why the triggers collapse.**
   - The raw-IR emulation of the trigger (`Ie2`) gives the same bytes class as the source trigger (27,008 B, M 1,410).
   - Threading alone, with no outlining (`Ie2i`), also collapses (M 1,423).
   - The `!holder` spelling without threading, plus forced O, costs only -14 M. That row is `T289hb_O`.
   - 326 inlined at validate's visit is harmless, even +5 rfj (`Io326`).
   - One visible symptom is execute's `args=&(new,)` copy, which survives as `%_45.sroa.5 [32 x i8]`. Forwarding it (`X1` = `Tfwd`) recovers only 138 M.
   - The rest is a global register-allocation reassignment starting at the first instruction.
5. **O-repay grid on tf_g3 with forced outlining.**
   - Otf_g3 alone is M 2,199. b01 costs -439 M (1,760), the same as its -428 on main. b02 is 1,765.
   - Fa collapses (1,402), and b02+Fa gives 1,362.
   - True LCS and Mperm are in `NOTES.md`. The room on O cannot be bought back with these pieces.

Ledger: approach `o2tfg3repay`, keys `0x22a10-w15-9120883-o2tfg3repay-{grid,trig,irexp}-*-v1`.

author: ettiennehugo
body:
Ettienne: "Just make it use the Multicharts enum".

## Change (`_VolumeProfileFuturesBase`)
- `string McBidAskChartTypeName = "VolumeDelta"` (parsed with `Enum.Parse`) is now `protected ChartType McBidAskChartType { get; set; } = ChartType.FootPrint`. Live Check 9a shows that the enum has no `VolumeDelta` member, so the old default always switched the tier off. The P-BA1 unknown-name warning is removed.
- Request: for `FootPrint` it uses `Resolution.CreateFootPrint(res.Type, (int)res.Size, CumulativeDeltaChartType.ASK_TRADE_BID_TRADE, FootPrintChartType.BID_ASK_VOL, false)`, because MC support says Data2 stays null otherwise. Any other chart type sets `res.ChartType` directly.
- The loader no longer uses reflection or string member names. It reads the typed `result.Data2` (`BarPriceLevels[]`), `result.RTData2` (`BarPriceLevels?`), `bpl.Levels` (`PriceLevel[]`), `bpl.Time`, and `PriceLevel.Price` / `UpVolume` / `DownVolume`.
- Journal diagnostics, each line logged once:
  - every `DataLoadedEvent` with its `IsCompleted` value;
  - the history `data2(n|null)` and `levels(n)`, and the RT `rtData2` level count;
  - any caught exception with its type and message.
- `m_mcHistoryDone` is set when `IsCompleted` is true even if parsing failed, so `OF McBidAsk loaded bars(0) ... chartType(FootPrint)` still prints.
- The `OF McBidAsk loaded` line now includes `chartType(..)`.
- The spec, base-class spec, live-check sheet (PDF regenerated) and engines manual are updated. Older `specs/engines-manual-v*.md` snapshots are left as they were.

## Evidence for each typed member
| Member | Source | Status |
|---|---|---|
| `ChartType.FootPrint` | Live Check 9a enum dump | confirmed |
| `IDataLoaderResult.Data2 : BarPriceLevels[]`, `RTData2 : BarPriceLevels?` | MC .NET Programming Guide v1.1 §4.7.4 p72 | confirmed |
| `BarPriceLevels { Bar, PriceLevel[] Levels, Index, Time, TickID }` | PG §4.7.4 p75–76 | confirmed |
| `PriceLevel.Price / UpVolume / DownVolume` | MC forum t=52737 (MC support sample code) | names confirmed by the sample; **types not documented**. The code casts with `(double)`, which compiles for double or decimal. |
| `Resolution.CreateFootPrint(EResolution, int, CumulativeDeltaChartType, FootPrintChartType, bool)`, `CumulativeDeltaChartType.ASK_TRADE_BID_TRADE`, `FootPrintChartType.BID_ASK_VOL` | MC forum t=52737 | **forum only**. Not in the PG; the signature and the size type (`int`) are unconfirmed. |
| Up = Ask traded and Down = Bid traded under `ASK_TRADE_BID_TRADE` | inferred from the enum name | **unconfirmed (P-BA2)**. Verify in Live Check 9. |

If any of these fails to compile in the MC editor, the error will name the exact member to fix. There is no fallback to strings.

## Other string-based lookups (not changed here)
On MultiCharts types:
- `_CustomSignal.Strategy.CS:1304` `tickBarMember`: `Bar` "Time"/"Close"/"TotalVolume"/"Volume"/"Ticks" through GetProperty/GetField.
- `_VolumeProfileFuturesBase.Strategy.CS:809` `barMember` (from `flowTick`, l.797): the same `Bar` member names.
- `_InstrProbe.Strategy.CS:144` `get(o, prop)`: probe that reads properties of MC objects by name.

On our own types (listed for completeness):
- `Enum.Parse`: `_StructuralTargetPatterns.Indicator.CS:143`, `_StructuralTargetPatterns.Strategy.CS:305`, `_EconomicCalendar.Strategy.CS:690`.
- `Enum.TryParse`: `_EventCalendar.Function.CS:1307/1318/1322`, `_PortMM.Function.CS:191`.
- `GetField`: `_MarketBreadth.Strategy.CS:388` (own `Entry`).
- `GetProperties`: `_CustomSignal.Strategy.CS:2162` (own inputs).

No `GetMethod`, `InvokeMember` or `dynamic` usage.

## Tests
All 22 suites are green. The C# 7.3 syntax check is clean, and the stub type check shows no change in errors. I added the typed `Data2`/`RTData2`/`BarPriceLevels`/`PriceLevel`/`CreateFootPrint` to the type-check stubs (/workspace/tools, outside the repo). There is no unit test for the loader: it is callback-only MC API with no pure logic to extract.

## Import order
`_VolumeProfileFuturesBase` (F7), then recompile and re-add any derived signals (e.g. `_DeltaDivRevFuturesLELX`).

## Analyst review #2 applied
- **Up/Down mapping:** the `OF McBidAsk loaded` journal line now ends with `mapping(UpVolume=AskTraded DownVolume=BidTraded UNVERIFIED)`.
- **History diagnostic:** one line at completion with cumulative `batches / nullData2Batches / data2Bars / levels` (it used to show only the first batch's counts).
- **`flowTick`:** `barMember` reflection and its `MemberInfo` fields are removed. It now reads the typed `Bar` members:
  - `Bar.Close` is confirmed in PG v1.1 §4.7.4, DataLoader example (`m_EURAUD[index].Close` on a `List<Bar>` filled from `Result.Data`).
  - `Bar.TotalVolume` is confirmed in MC forum t=13113 (`tickBuckets[index].Sum(tick => tick.TotalVolume)` over DataLoader `Bar[]`).
  - The member types (DateTime/double) are assumed. The code casts with `(double)`.
  - The old `Volume`/`Ticks` name fallbacks are dropped. Only `TotalVolume` is used.
- **Not touched:** the `_CustomSignal:1304` and `_InstrProbe:144` reflection.

## Held items: RESOLVED from Ettienne's API dump of his MC install
- `CreateFootPrint(EResolution based_res_type, UInt32 based_res_size, CumulativeDeltaChartType, FootPrintChartType, Boolean disp_as_percentage)`. `res.Size` (UInt32) is now passed without the `(int)` cast. The final `false` is `disp_as_percentage`.
- `CumulativeDeltaChartType {NOTHING, ASK_TRADE_BID_TRADE, DELTA_UP_TICK_DOWN_TICK}` and `FootPrintChartType {BID_ASK_VOL, TOTAL_VOL, DELTA_ASK_BID_VOL}`.
- `Data2` is `BarPriceLevels[]` and `RTData2` is `Nullable<BarPriceLevels>`, so `BarPriceLevels?` is correct. The `BarPriceLevels` struct is {Bar Bar, PriceLevel[] Levels, int Index, DateTime Time, uint TickID, uint TotalRes}.
- `PriceLevel` is a struct with double fields Price/UpVolume/DownVolume and a double TotalVolume property. The `(double)` casts are removed.
- `Bar` is a struct: DateTime Time; double Open/High/Low/Close; float Up/Down/Unchanged/TotalVolume; uint TickID/TotalResolution; ETickTradedSide TickTradedSide; ETickTradedSideEx TickTradedSideEx; bool EndOfSession. This confirms `Bar.Time`. The redundant `(double)b.Close` is removed. `TotalVolume` keeps an explicit float-to-double `(double)`.
- The test stubs now match these exact types.
- **Still UNVERIFIED:** the UpVolume=AskTraded / DownVolume=BidTraded mapping. The journal still flags it.

**Note for later (not changed here):** `Bar.TickTradedSide` and `Bar.TickTradedSideEx` exist. They are a typed option for the tick loader's aggressor side, to evaluate in a separate PR.

Tests: all 22 suites green (Calendar 780, Profile 58, SessionClock 68, OrderFlow 68, Avwap 46, Daily 44, Dvp 605, Event 553, Gate0 148, Gmm 43, InstrProbe 29, LevelStudy 30, Mtf 9, PortMM 132, PriceAction 79, RegimeGate 146, Regime 46, Roll 59, Tick 15, Tod 19, VpHelper 250, Xmkt 12; 0 failed). Stub type check: no change vs main.

author: awantika-m
body:
Closes #50

## What this PR does

Hardens claim extraction against untrusted reports:
- The model sees only the first 16 KiB of the report (`MAX_REPORT_CHARS`); `Extraction.truncated` records the cut.
- The report is fenced between marker lines with a random per-call boundary (`secrets.token_hex`, redrawn if the report contains it) and the prompt states it is data.
- Model answers are validated against that same cut copy; symbols must be whole identifiers. The regex path still reads the whole report, unchanged.

**Real Gemma finding:** on an injection report, `gemma3:1b` returned the injected `rm -rf ~` as the repro command and `pwned` as a name; they were kept because they literally appear in the report (validation only blocks strings that are not in it). The extracted repro command is never executed by any code path — only `--repro` / the Action's `repro` input run anything; a follow-up adds a cross-cutting regression test for that. Truncation is not yet shown in the markdown/JSON report.

## Models the product uses in this PR

`gemma3:1b` via Ollama (claim extraction)

## AI coding assistants that helped write it

Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5)

## How we tested it

Test-first: 7 of 9 new tests failed before the change (the two pure-injection tests already passed thanks to the existing literal-in-report check). Fake-model tests cover truncation, boundary collision, fake JSON and instructions inside the report. One real gemma3:1b run on an injection report (result above). Full suite: 344 passed, 81 skipped.

author: vibdev
body: OA-41: swipe a sidebar thread to close it. Builds on OA-40 (#49, merged as f8384d8); this PR is one commit on `main`. ## Summary ```diff close-thread.tsx sidebar rows only (OA-40) the keyboard's way to the same actions + swipe.tsx wheel deltaX (trackpad) · pointer events (touch, pen) + .swipe-actions [Delete…][Mark done], revealed from the right + .swipe-row translateX(-offset) +swiping.ts pure: resisted · pullFor · settle · shown ``` ```text pull left 0 → 76px row follows 1:1 → Mark done pull past 76px half speed up to 152px → Delete… (still asks: same deleteClicked as the menu) past 152px barely moves let go rests at nearest of 0 · 76 · 152; swipe back → 0 ``` - **Scrolling and back gestures stay the browser's.** Axis lock comes after an 8px slop. A mostly vertical move is never taken, and touch rows set `touch-action: pan-y`. A rightward swipe on a closed row isn't `preventDefault`ed, so the browser's back gesture survives, and touches within 24px of the left edge are ignored. - **Taps and focus:** - The click that ends a touch swipe does nothing. - A tap on an open row closes it. - Escape closes it and refocuses the row's link. - Only one row is open at a time. - **Reduced motion.** With `prefers-reduced-motion` the snap has no transition. The row still tracks the finger, since that is direct manipulation. - **Keyboard.** The same actions are in the row's context menu (Menu key or Shift+F10, from #49). Revealed buttons are tabbable; hidden ones are not. - **Telemetry.** `via` gains `"swipe"` on `thread.marked-done` and `thread.deleted`. ## Evidence | Before (#49): right-click or keyboard only | After: trackpad swipe past the first stop | |---|---| | | | | First stop: Mark done | Touch, first stop (390) | Touch, further: Delete (390) | Delete from a swipe still asks | |---|---|---|---| | | | | | I drove Chrome with Playwright on the fixture server, with `wheel` deltaX for the trackpad and CDP touch events in the 390px drawer. Playwright needs an ffmpeg download for video, which I didn't add, so these stills stand in for one. ```text short trackpad swipe → rests at 0 ✔ held → follows (-78); let go → first stop -76, [Mark done] tabbable ✔ further: -81,-86,…,-151,-153,-155,-156,-158,-159 (resistance) → -152 ✔ swipe back → 0 · vertical wheel → 0 · deltaX:1 then vertical → 0 ✔ rightward wheel on a closed row: defaultPrevented = false ✔ Mark done from a swipe → leaves Needs you; telemetry via "swipe" ✔ Delete… from a swipe → confirm dialog → deleted; via "swipe" ✔ touch: first stop -76, no navigation; further -152; tap closes, no navigation; vertical drag → 0 ✔ second row opened → first closes · Escape → closed, focus on the row's link ✔ prefers-reduced-motion: transition-duration 0s ✔ closed row: overflow visible (focus ring and current outline whole) ✔ ``` `web/test/swiping.test.ts` covers the model: following, resistance, `pullFor` inverting `resisted`, settling, and a done thread's single stop. `server/src/close.test.ts` gains a test for `via: "swipe"`. `pnpm check` (rebased on f8384d8): exit 0, `ℹ tests 924 · ℹ pass 924 · ℹ fail 0`. Reviewers on this commit: the security review found nothing. The correctness review raised three Important issues, all fixed: - `overflow: hidden` clipped the sidebar's focus rings, so the row now clips only while open or moving; - the wheel locked its axis on the first event, so deltas now add up past the slop first; - the click swallow could close a just-opened row or eat a later keyboard activation. Its three nits are fixed too: focus after an action, a second finger, and one open row at a time. ## Merge Danger **Door:** two-way. Web only, plus one more allowed value for an optional telemetry field. No migration. **Blast Radius:** sidebar Every sidebar thread row is wrapped. A broken gesture could take a scroll or a click in the sidebar, which is what the checks above cover. The inbox and the group page are unchanged. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

`demarches-page.test.ts` expected a task due 2026-11-01 to read « dimanche 1er nov. », but `nextTaskDay` compares with the real date. author: vitto
body:
Magma writes the rules of composition of its design language as files beside the patterns, `agents/patterns/<id>.md` with `kind: foundation` (magma-design-system/magma#1189): rhythm on `main` since magma-design-system/magma#1206, the other five in magma-design-system/magma#1217. This pull request gives them a place in Foundation and lets the site take them when a release of `magma` ships them. It has to be merged **before** that release, as magma-design-system/magma#1197 asks: today Typography says the style `h1` is the title of the page, and the domain `titles` says `h3`.

## What changes

- **A group Composition** in Foundation, after Design: Rhythm, Density, Actions, Titles, Surfaces, Widths and alignment (Ritmo, Densità, Azioni, Titoli, Superfici, Larghezze e allineamento). Decided on 2026-11-01 against the six inside Design, nine items in one group (`plan/CONTENT_STRUCTURE.md`).
- **One page per domain, generated** from the installed `magma`, at `/foundation/<id>/`: the whole file as the agents read it (principle, when to use it, what decides it, cases, always true, situations, accessibility, Magma gaps, decisions with the link to each comment). The header says where it comes from, as the component pages do; the Italian pages show the same English text with the note that the packages are documented in English only.
  - `loadDomains` (`src/lib/magma.mjs`) reads the folder beside the package's `AGENTS.md`; the collection `src/loaders/domains.ts` renders each body, without its `h1` and the notes for maintainers; links between domains become links between pages.
  - Order, icons and labels: `DOMAINS` in `src/lib/nav.mjs`. A domain the package ships and the list lacks **fails the build**, as an unknown usage file does for the components.
- **The cases at work.** Magma ships a preview for each case of a domain, the stage that shows the rule working (the pilot is `widths`, in magma-design-system/magma#1217). The page of the domain shows them after its table of cases: a heading with the id of the case, the stage (`PreviewStage.astro`, with its handles, Reset and "Open in a new tab") and the line of what to try under it, in English on the Italian pages too. The table of contents lists them under Cases.
  - `loadDomains` reads `agents/patterns/previews/<id>/` with the domain (the keys `try`, `height`, `whole-page`); a preview with nothing to try, or of a case the domain does not have, fails the build. The loader renders the body in two parts around the previews, cut at the `h2` after Cases.
  - Each runs alone at `/docs/example/domain/<id>/<case>/` (`src/pages/example/domain/[domain]/[case].astro`), as Magma's `render_preview` runs it: the words in Italian, an inset of 600, none for a stage that is a whole page (`whole-page`, the case `widths/page`, whose bar and gutter start at the edge).
- **The landing page** shows the group in cards (`DomainCards.astro`, `PageCards` with `domain`), and its table of contents lists it (`src/route-data.ts`, Starlight route middleware: the heading is written by a component, so Starlight does not see it).
- **Prose tables**: the tables of a domain have two to six columns of prose. With every cell on one line, or with the long ones at the phrase measure (50ch), every table of Rhythm scrolled sideways in the content column. A cell longer than 30 characters now wraps at the measure of a title (`PROSE_CELLS_FIELD` in `src/lib/markdown-tables.mjs`, only for these texts): the tables of two and three columns fit, those of five and six scroll as the API tables do.
- **Typography**: "Picking a style" follows the domain `titles`: `h3` for the title of a page of an application (in the tag `h1`, once), `h5` for a section and a dialog, `h6` for a part and a group of fields; `h1`, `h2` and `h4` have no role there. The rule "the tag says the structure" keeps its reason and points to Titles. **Color** points to Actions after "a view has one primary action". `DomainLink.astro` links while the installed magma ships the domain, and writes the text alone before, so no page links to a page that is not built.

## Verified

- `astro check`: 0 errors. `npm run lint`: clean. Prettier: clean.
- `npm run build` with magma 2.9.0 (no domain): no group, no cards, no entry in the table of contents, Typography and Color without links, no page of a preview.
- `npm run build` with the `magma` of magma-design-system/magma#1217, unpacked from its `npm pack` tarball (no `npm link`): the twelve domain pages (six per language) in the sitemap. With its `styles` and `design-tokens` packed too, since the previews take the widths from their tokens: the five pages of the previews of `widths`, and on the page of the domain, in English and in Italian, the five previews, their headings and their entries in the table of contents.
- In headless Chrome at 1440 px: the text and the form end at 532 px, the window of the dialog is 580 px, the bar and the page start on one edge; at 375 px the short fields and the fields of the dialog go one under the other; `page` opened alone at 1600 px stops at 1280 px, centred. (In the hidden Browser pane of Claude Code the frames keep their first height: it fires no ResizeObserver.)
- In the dev server, in the browser: the navigation with the group, a page in English and in Italian (Titoli, with the note), the cards and the table of contents of the landing page, the link from Typography to Titles, the tables of Rhythm and Actions.

## After the release

Renovate brings the release of `magma` that ships the domains, and the group appears with it; nothing to change here. The site does not read the patterns from the package yet (#89): the patterns and blocks stay as #93 writes them.

author: motebit-agent
body:
## Why

`@motebit/verify` was the last open commitment in `coverage-graduation.json`. Its `target_date` is 2026-11-30. From that date, `check-coverage-graduation` (drift-defense #130) fails CI hard if the package's live vitest thresholds miss the target. Coverage was 60/52/47/58 (statements/branches/functions/lines) against a target of 85/80/85/85. This PR closes the gap with real tests. The date, the target and the coverage includes are untouched.

## Evidence

| Axis | Before (measured / floor) | After (measured / new floor) | Target |
|---|---|---|---|
| Statements | 59.94 / 58 | 96.91 / 94 | 85 |
| Branches | 51.83 / 50 | 94.64 / 92 | 80 |
| Functions | 47.36 / 47 | 100 / 100 | 85 |
| Lines | 57.95 / 56 | 96.99 / 94 | 85 |

**Coverage tests**
- 55 new tests, for 189 in total. They run the real `main()` in-process through a helper that captures stdout, stderr and the exit code. Only the real verifier and crypto code runs, and fixtures are signed with the real signers.
- The tests cover:
  - help, version and usage exit codes;
  - strict-by-default and `--lenient`;
  - every `--expect` and I/O error path;
  - `content-artifact` (header and file forms, every mismatch, execution-ledger v1.1 inner receipts);
  - `approval-decision` (every verdict, pin and malformed shape).
- Proof the tests bite: `packages/verify/src/__tests__/cli-main-in-process.tampers.mjs` breaks one CLI behaviour at a time, and **11/11 RED**.
- The entry is recorded as `GRADUATED 2026-10-31`, like its five sibling entries. `pnpm coverage-graduation` exits 0.

**Gate self-test**
- Closing the last open entry made the `check-coverage-graduation` probe in `check-gates-effective` vacuous. It had worked by back-dating a real short entry.
- The probe now injects a synthetic overdue entry (a 2020 date, target 101), so it bites whatever the real manifest holds. The gate stays alive for future money and identity packages.
- Full `check-gates-effective`: **260/260**.
- `pnpm check`: all 160 drift defenses pass.

## Review

- No source changes to `packages/verify`. All changes are in tests, the vitest thresholds, the graduation entry, the probe and one doctrine sentence (`coverage-graduation.md`: all six entries graduated).
- New floors sit 2 points under the measured values, following the repo's CI-margin precedent. Functions stay at 100.

## Deferred

- 16 branches are unreached and listed in the commit message, not excluded. They are defensive guards that argument parsing makes unreachable, non-`Error` throw arms, and fallbacks for fields the verifiers always set.
- A source fix for the ledger: in `content-artifact` and `approval-decision`, a manifest with a missing or non-string key under `--producer-key` throws a raw `TypeError`. It fails closed with exit 2, but not with the named error `packages/verify/CLAUDE.md` rule 5 asks for.

author: rhamenator
body:
Fixes #125.

`events-fetcher.js` used the bot host's local timezone to build the six-week Firestore query window. Under UTC, its upper bound excluded a late Saturday event that was still within Saturday in Lansing. This switches the bound calculation to `America/Detroit` with `moment-timezone`, preserving the query shape. A test exercises the actual fetcher query across the fall DST transition and asserts both bounds.

## Verification
- Node 24.21.0, `TZ=UTC npm test`: 66 specs, 0 failures.
- Node 24.21.0, `TZ=America/Detroit npm test`: 66 specs, 0 failures.
- `npm run lint`: pass. `npm run test:legacy`: 10 commands passed. `git diff --check`: pass.
- Personal test Firestore project `lansing-codes-test-staging`: created a temporary event at `2026-12-06T02:00:00Z` (Saturday 9:00pm Lansing), froze the fetchers' clock at `2026-10-31T22:00:00Z`, and ran both versions with `TZ=UTC`. The fixed fetcher returned the event; the original fetcher omitted it. The test deleted the document in `finally`, and a separate read-only check found zero temporary `codex-fetch-window-` documents remaining. No production service, Slack post, or Heroku dyno was used.

This PR targets `fix/lansing-event-reply-time` (#122), which targets `security-fixes` (#100). That includes the separate fix for the pre-existing UTC format-time test failure, allowing the full UTC suite to pass. Retarget/rebase as those PRs merge and rerun CI. Production host timezone and deployed behavior remain unverified.

author: gbourgeat
body:
The fourth hardening wave: what the triage of the points the audit left unproved confirmed in the runtime packages and the generated client, one commit each, every one with its `changes/` entry.

- **aspects (breaking, `To move`):** `cached` keeps its entries per tenant, unless the caller says `shared: true`, through a new `scope` of the aspect runtime the composition templates and the example give. Concurrent calls of two tenants no longer share one call. Work under an elevation neither reads nor writes the cache.
- **auth:** `keycloakAuthenticator` takes access tokens only: a `typ` other than `Bearer` is refused (`To move` for a spec that signs its own tokens).
- **http:** field access holds on a status the route does not declare, under the rules of every declared response; its docs say what a rule reaches.
- **cli, generated client:** a path parameter that is empty or a dot segment throws a `TypeError` and sends nothing; the client of the example is regenerated (`To move`: regenerate the clients).
- **kernel:** an erasure runs every rebuild, the first failure is thrown once they all ran.
- **cli:** `privacy/snapshot-sealed`, a value of a snapshot named like personal data is sealed, a warning as the other `privacy/*` rules.
- **docs:** what an erasure leaves in a cache until its time to live, and that the masks of `subjectMasker` need a key store.

Each new spec was seen red without its change. Ran: the suites of aspects, auth, http, kernel, validation, di and testing; the CLI specs touched; `ci:typecheck`; `docs:samples`; lint (0 errors); knip; parity; `check --self` (962 fixtures); `ci:arch`; the three plugin validations; three generated stacks, `biome format` clean and `init --force` without a diff. Not run: the whole suite with its floors and the end-to-end shards, which this CI runs.

author: slealq
body:
Fixes #84 for Create and Edit. Train and Vision are out of scope.

## Changes
- **History on the image:** each created or edited image keeps its exact prompt, model name, settings, seed, charged cost, LoRA details and inputs in the order sent to the provider. The history is copied onto the library image, so deleting the generation, an input or a LoRA can't remove it.
- **Input copies:** the worker saves an 800px copy of each input. Failures here never fail a job.
- **Viewer:** a How it was made panel. Live inputs open the real image, and deleted ones show the copy with a note. Labels: No longer offered, Deleted, Partial history. Images list what they were used to make.
- **Delete warning:** single, batch and folder deletes say how many images used the image. Deletion now runs as a background job, and images hide from the grid immediately.
- **Older images:** the API builds a partial history from the generation record until the backfill runs, so nothing disappears from the viewer. `backend/scripts/backfill_image_history.py` hasn't been run on DEV.

## ⚠️ Deployment order
**Run migration 057 on DEV before merging, not after.** `Image` and `GeneratedImage` now map a `history` column, so with new code on the old schema every image query returns a 500. The migration is additive (two nullable columns, one table, one enum value), so the current deployed code keeps working on the new schema.

## Verification
- `ruff check backend scripts/sync_data.py`: passed
- `pytest` on this branch: 952 passed
- `npm run lint`: no errors. `npm run build`: compiled
- Migration 057 upgrade, downgrade and upgrade on a throwaway pgvector Postgres: passed
- Real Postgres scenarios: LoRA renamed and deleted, generation deleted, input deleted, retired model, owner isolation on the used-by count, live partial history, and account deletion with cascades
- Backfill `--dry-run` ran on an empty database only
- Playwright at 1440×900 and 3440×1289 against a mocked API: clicking a live input opens that image, deleted inputs have no link, the warning shows the right count, and a deleted tile hides in under 50ms

## Not verified
- Real Azure storage, real Celery workers and real model calls
- The backfill against real data
- That `charged_cost` fills in on a real run. The code path was read, not exercised, so this needs checking on the first DEV run.
- The local Docker stack wasn't rebuilt

author: linuxnow
body:
Minor release 0.28.0, the wave that closes this repo's open list.

New faces, each with closed-form oracles at the nine rates, a golden, sabotages and fuzz seeds. Each runs in the console's strip or return at no latency; the plugin faces and the picker follow from these.
- clipper: drive, ceiling, softness. Console: last insert before MAIN on a drum or bus strip.
- upward: an upward compressor over omx_dyn's UPWARD law. Console: a talk strip, a low lav, a quiet speaker on a conference bus.
- glue: a bus compressor from the comp slot's detents. Console: a group or MAIN; parallel on a drum group.
- loudlevel: a leveler to a LUFS target over omx_loudness. Console: a speech or playback strip, MAIN, a stream feed.
- balancer: four bands walked toward a target spectrum. Console: slow tone correction on MAIN or a group, a playback strip.
- spring: a spring reverb. Console: an FX return on a guitar or vocal aux.

Also new:
- mix/omx_slew.h: a gain that crosses a declared time, not one block (#235), with closed-form oracles and digests at the nine rates and the engine's loop written out as a reference, bit for bit at quanta 64, 256 and 1024.
- MIXMATRIX_PERIOD_SHARE and make bench-mixmatrix: 64 x 32 held to 0.2 of the period at the nine rates, 6.5 % measured at 192 kHz.
- tools/clone-check.sh, with a baseline that only shrinks; tools/travel-grid-check.sh. Each carries its sabotage.

Changed:
- The delay face takes the kernel's read taps: resolve() gains fxDelayTaps, tap0Gain, tap0Pan and tap1..3 Factor, Gain and Pan after pingpong (the tap-delay spec, section 3). One tap at unity and centre is the delay that shipped. omx-plugins' delay core must pass the twelve arguments.
- plosive sensitivityDb and popSensitivityDb come up at 16 dB, above the 13.5 and 10.5 dB of steady contrast a buzzy vowel raises. The leveler's table, width's bass mono switch and WIDTH_COMB_GAIN stand as declared.
- comp attackMs steps 0.1 and releaseMs 5, eq notchQ 0.1. Each stepped from its minimum missed its own default or maximum.
- The EQ kinds, the low-pass hand-over and the HRP family tables read their declarations. No value moves.
- omx_eq_matched_pair calls omx_matched_pair; omx_round_half_up replaces three copies in src; the instance faces share one opening and one bypass check (fx/omx_instance_io.h). No digest moves.
- The formerly lines are gone from the headers.
- reverb_return arm E reads its level off the stimulus. With the band read 1 dB low the old arm passed 315 of 315; the new one is red on 9.

Consumers: the step of comp attackMs, comp releaseMs and eq notchQ is what a surface steps by. The plosive's defaults moved. omx-contract's item units hold neither LUFS nor dB/s, so those controls say dB and name the rest.
